2335224.title: PRESIDENT OF INDIA PRESENTS SWACHH SURVEKSHAN AWARDS
2335224.body_html:
President's Secretariat
PRESIDENT OF INDIA PRESENTS SWACHH SURVEKSHAN AWARDS
CLEANLINESS IS NOT MERELY A MATTER OF MAINTAINING THE AESTHETIC APPEAL OF PUBLIC SPACES; IT IS ALSO AN INDICATOR OF OUR HEALTH, SOCIAL CONSCIOUSNESS, AND ADMINISTRATIVE ACCOUNTABILITY: PRESIDENT DROUPADI MURMU
Posted On: 11 NOV 2026 8:52PM by PIB Delhi

The President of India, Smt Droupadi Murmu presented the Swachh Survekshan Awards 2025-26 in New Delhi today (November 11, 2026).

Speaking on the occasion, the President said that a single organization alone cannot achieve the goals of cleanliness. It requires the participation of every citizen, every household, every community, and every city. She underlined that cleanliness is not merely a matter of maintaining the aesthetic appeal of public spaces. It is also an indicator of our health, social consciousness, and administrative accountability. It is a reflection of our habits at home too. 

The President said that every citizen, especially youth, women, Resident Welfare Associations and community organizations, should engage with various aspects of cleanliness. They should share their experiences and report any shortcomings, the resolution of which could help make our cities cleaner and healthier. This should foster an ongoing dialogue between the municipal administration and the citizens, thereby strengthening trust, transparency, and accountability.

 The President said that citizens are the best judges when it comes to assessing the cleanliness of their surroundings. Therefore, the use of citizen feedback should not be limited merely to surveys or rankings. Instead, this feedback should serve as a vital tool for improving municipal services and addressing local challenges.

 The President said that there is a need to develop effective, affordable and safe technologies in the field of sanitation. She was happy to note that various institutions, including several IITs and other scientific research organizations, are actively working in this direction.

 The President noted that several startups have emerged in the sanitation sector. She said that such enterprises can contribute significantly toward solving real-world sanitation challenges while also creating employment opportunities.

 The President said that there is a need to place special emphasis on enhancing the capacities of Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities, as these are the fastest-growing urban centers. They have distinct needs and challenges. Their development should take place within a national framework designed to address their specific problems and challenges. She said planners in Tier-2 cities can learn from the issues faced by Tier-1 cities, and to do so, they should study the experiences of planners in Tier-1 cities.

 The Swachh Survekshan Awards, organized by the Union Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, honours India’s cleanest cities and recognizes their outstanding contributions to Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban.

2335212.title: Sarbananda Sonowal Lays Foundation Stones for Projects Worth Rs 560 Crore at Visakhapatnam Port
2335212.ministry: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
2335212.body_html:
Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
Sarbananda Sonowal Lays Foundation Stones for Projects Worth Rs 560 Crore at Visakhapatnam Port
Sonowal Dedicates Port Promenade in Visakhapatnam to the nation, open for public
New Contracts to employ about 500 local people
Sonowal ties projects to PM Modi's vision of Citizens as Active Partners of development
It opens up the port to the city: Sonowal on the newly inaugurated Promenade
Posted On: 11 NOV 2026 8:38PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways (MoPSW), Sarbananda Sonowal, in Visakhapatnam, dedicated a waterfront promenade at the Visakhapatnam Port to the public and laid foundation stones for four new projects, bringing the port’s package of new works to about Rs 560 crore.

The Rs 19 crore Port Promenade runs about 710 meters (2,330 feet) along the water from the Venkateswara Temple to the International Cruise Terminal and covers about 5.5 acres. The promenade gives residents a regulated, safe place to watch ships and port operations for the first time. "It opens up the port to the city," Sonowal said. "This project is dedicated to the people of Visakhapatnam.”

The promenade has a waterfront walkway and two view decks, one a Titanic-style viewpoint, along with a park, a public plaza, a children's play area, a food court and visitor parking. It was built on existing port land without affecting cargo operations. Its location beside the cruise terminal is also meant to add to the terminal's appeal for cruise passengers.

Sonowal tied the project to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's vision of inclusive development, in which citizens are not just beneficiaries but active partners in building the nation. A port that was once closed to outsiders now invites residents in, he said, and the new terminal contracts will give about 500 local people jobs running its berths.

"Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision is a development in which every citizen has a place and a part to play," Sarbananda Sonowal said. "A port that opens its gates to the people, and gives local youth the work of running its berths, is that vision in action.”

Sonowal also laid foundation stones for three contracts to operate and maintain existing cargo terminals, together worth about Rs 580 crores. They cover the WQ-1 and WQ-1RE berths; WQ-2 and WQ-3; and EQ-3. Operators must mechanise the berths with cranes and conveyors, with environmental controls, and will employ about 500 local people. "Through these projects, VPA will secure assured cargo throughput and achieve optimum capacity utilisation in these berths," Sarbananda Sonowal said.

The Union Minister also laid the foundation stone for upgrading the port's sewage treatment plant from 10 million liters a day to 15 million liters, including a new 5 million-liter plant, at an estimated cost of about Rs 11 crores. Treated water is used for dust suppression, wetting roads and sprinkling at stockpile yards, and the upgrade supports the ministry's Harit Sagar green port initiative.

Sonowal said the port handled a record 91.17 million metric tons of cargo in the 2025-26 fiscal year, about 10% more than a year earlier and its fourth straight year of growth. From April 1 to Oct. 31, cargo rose by 4.44 million metric tons, or 8.88%, over the same period last year. "You must beat last year's target of 10% growth," Sonowal encouraged the port employees as he spoke and interacted with them.

The initiatives were launched as Sonowal is going to speak at the 31st CII Partnership Summit–2026, which the Andhra Pradesh government is hosting on November 12 and 13, which is themed under ‘Navigating New World Order: Trade, Technology, Trust.’

The port has taken up four Public-Private Partnership (PPP_ projects worth about Rs 800 crores, which are under construction and expected to be commissioned by 2027. It has one of the deepest container terminals among India's major ports, with a permissible draft of 16 meters, and is shifting to a landlord-port model to cut vessel turnaround time and logistics costs.

Sonowal credited Prime Minister Narendra Modi's leadership for transforming Indian ports into world-class facilities as the country works toward becoming a developed nation by 2047. He described the day's projects, from a public promenade to a cleaner sewage system, as examples of the Prime Minister's call for development that includes every section of society.

"When citizens are partners and not spectators, development lasts," Sonowal said. "That is the spirit of Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas, Sabka Vishwas, Sabka Prayas, and it is the surest road to a Viksit Bharat by 2047.”

Sonowal also thanked Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu and the state government for their support.

Visakhapatnam Lok Sabha member M. Sribharat, Rajya Sabha member Golla Babu Rao, Andhra Pradesh BJP president P.V.N. Madhav, legislators Ch. Vamsi Krishna Srinivas and P. Vishnu Kumar Raju, and port Chairperson Jasmeet Singh Bindra attended among other officials and employees of the port.

2335207.title: Swachh Survekshan Awards 2025-26
2335207.body_html:
Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs
Swachh Survekshan Awards 2025-26
President of India Smt. Droupadi Murmu Awards the Nation’s Cleanest Cities after the Swachh Survekshan 2025–26
AHMEDABAD (Mentor) – SANAND (Mentee), INDORE (Mentor) - DEPALPUR (Mentee) & TIRUPATI (Mentor) - KUPPAM (Mentee) rank top 3 in ‘Swachh Shehar Jodi category for accelerating urban waste management excellence
NAVI MUMBAI, SURAT & VIJAYAWADA Declared Top 3 in Clean Cities of Super Swachh League
GVMC VISAKHAPATNAM, JABALPUR and LUCKNOW Emerge as India’s top 3 Swachh Shehar in the Million Plus population category
This year awards were given for the first time to Swachh River Front Town, Swachh Coastal Town and Clean Himalayan City,
350+ ULBs jump 500 ranks to move up in Swachh Survekshan 2025-26
Smaller Cities Lead the Change: 1,700+ ULBs with population under 50k Improve Their Rankings Over 2024–25
State-Level Winners to Be Honoured in Award Ceremonies in respective States
Posted On: 11 NOV 2026 8:31PM by PIB Delhi

 Smt. Droupadi Murmu, Hon’ble President of India, honoured India’s cleanest cities at the Swachh Survekshan Awards 2025–26 held at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi, convened by the Department of Urban Development (DoUD), Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA). Winners were felicitated in the presence of Sh. Manohar Lal, Union Minister for MoHUA & Power and Shri Tokhan Sahu, Minister of State for MoHUA. This year 60 national awards have been announced, under 5 categories:

  • Swachh Shehar Jodi (SSJ)
  • Clean Cities of Super Swachh League
  • Swachh Shehar in 5 population categories
  • Swachh River Front Town
  • Swachh Coastal Town
  • Clean Himalayan City
  • State First Swachh City

Speaking at the event, Smt. Droupadi Murmu, Hon’ble President of India, underscored that cleanliness cannot be achieved through the efforts of any single institution alone and requires active participation from all stakeholders. She emphasized the importance of citizen participation, behavioural change, administrative accountability, and sustained public engagement. Highlighting the need to inculcate cleanliness values from an early age, she called for integrating issues such as plastic waste management into school curricula and fostering continuous dialogue with children and youth. The President noted that meaningful progress in sanitation is possible when citizens, local administrations, and sanitation workers work together, and when the on-ground suggestions of sanitation workers and citizen feedback are given due importance. She also appreciated the Swachh Shehar Jodi initiative as a new dimension of collaborative learning, enabling cities to share innovations, test solutions, and support one another in achieving higher standards of urban cleanliness.

Addressing the gathering, Union Minister for Housing and Urban Affairs Shri Manohar Lal said that under the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Swachh Bharat Mission has evolved into a nationwide people's movement, transforming urban sanitation and encouraging greater citizen participation. Highlighting the progress achieved since 2014, he stated that urban waste processing has increased from 16% to 80%, while door-to-door waste collection coverage has risen from 44% to over 96%. He further noted that the remediation of legacy waste dumpsites has freed nearly 11,000 acres of urban land for productive use.

The Hon’ble Minister also encouraged States to conduct Swachh Survekshan competitions at the State level to rank cities and towns within their respective States, fostering healthy competition among Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) and encouraging smaller towns to improve their cleanliness standards.

Shri Manohar Lal highlighted the growing scale and impact of Swachh Survekshan, which has expanded from 73 cities in 2016 to 4,751 cities in 2025–26. He informed that 2.70 crore citizens provided feedback during this year's survey, while over 1,700 smaller cities improved their rankings and more than 350 cities registered improvements of over 500 positions. Emphasising the importance of behavioural change, the Minister said that the real success of Swachh Survekshan lies not merely in improving rankings but in making cleanliness a permanent habit and collective responsibility. He also highlighted the participation of nearly 2.10 crore citizens in Swachhata Hi Seva 2026, the benefits extended to around 17 lakh SafaiMitras through over 33,000 special camps, and the participation of nearly 4 lakh children in Gyan Yatras.

The Minister further highlighted several new initiatives aimed at strengthening collaboration and encouraging excellence in urban sanitation. He stated that under the Swachh Shehar Jodi initiative, 70 mentor cities have been paired with 191 mentee cities to facilitate knowledge-sharing and improve sanitation outcomes. He also referred to the introduction of special award categories for River Front Towns, Coastal Towns and Himalayan Cities, along with recognition across five population categories to ensure wider participation. Highlighting the PRAGATI-50 initiative, Shri Manohar Lal said that 50 cities would be developed as Model Clean Cities through technology-driven interventions and continuous monitoring. Congratulating all award-winning cities, urban local bodies and SafaiMitras, he reiterated the Government's commitment to making cleanliness an integral part of urban life and realising the vision of a Swachh and Viksit Bharat.

Sh. Satendra Singh, Secretary, DoUD, MoHUA, highlighted how Swachh Survekshan has, over the past decade, strengthened the assessment and improvement of urban sanitation services while driving tangible on-ground outcomes under the Mission. Secretary, MoHUA, further mentioned that Swachh Survekshan is much more than an assessment; it is the collective voice of millions of people committed to the vision of a Swachh Bharat. He said, “today is a celebration of the outstanding efforts made by our cities and citizens in advancing the cause of cleanliness.”

The Swachh Survekshan 2025–26 results reflect a strong upward momentum across urban India, with over 350 ULBs improving their position by more than 500 ranks. Smaller cities have emerged as key drivers of this transformation, as 1,700+ ULBs with populations below 50,000 population improved their rankings compared to 2024–25, demonstrating that sustained efforts and citizen participation are accelerating the Swachhata movement across towns of all sizes.

Showing excellence in collaborative efforts and peer-learning, Mentor city Ahmedabad & Mentee city Sanand, Mentor Indore & Mentee Depalpur and Mentor Tirupati & Mentee Kuppam, were declared the top-ranked jodis under Swachh Shehar Jodi award. The Top 3 Swachh Shehar Jodis have been identified based on the combined score of the Mentor City (SS 2024-25 awardee) and its paired Mentee City. It reflects the joint performance and collaborative efforts of both cities under the Swachh Shehar Jodi initiative, thereby recognizing mentorship outcomes along with overall cleanliness and service delivery improvements. The intention of Jodi award is that the best performing cities should handhold cities with low scores to improve their performance. The initiative started after 2024-25 award ceremony with the motive of Each One - Teach One and rooted in India’s timeless Guru–Shishya tradition, where knowledge, experience, and best practices are passed on from one city to another to collectively advance the journey towards urban excellence and cleanliness.

 

Maharashtra’s Navi Mumbai, Gujarat’s Surat and Andhra Pradesh’s Vijayawada emerged as top 3 Clean Cities of Super Swachh League.

Marking the rise of a new generation of clean cities, GVMC Visakhapatnam, Jabalpur and Lucknow emerged as India’s top Swachh Shehar in the million plus population category.

Swachh Survekshan Awards 2025-26 expanded its coverage to include the Hills and Himalayan cities as well as River front and coastal towns. Rudrapur in Uttarakhand, Jammu & Shopian in J&K have been declared as the top 3 Clean Himalayan Cities. Riverfronts, coastlines and water bodies, are an integral part of the natural and cultural heritage. Their cleanliness is essential not only for environmental sustainability but also for the health and livelihoods of communities. In line with the same, the top 3 ranks for the Swachh River Front Town have been bestowed upon Rewa (MP), Bilaspur (Chhattisgarh) & Varanasi (UP) consecutively, while awards for Swachh Coastal Town went to Odisha’s Puri, Kerala’s Alappuzha and Maharashtra’s Ratnagiri.

To recognize and reward excellence across States and Union Territories, the State First Swachh City Award was conferred on 30 top-performing cities. Union Territories have been classified into two categories for awards: (i) Up to 5 ULBs and (ii) more than 5 ULBs.

As part of the 10th edition of Swachh Survekshan, Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) were assessed across 43 indicators covering 10 critical domains, including Segregation, Collection & Transportation of Waste, Solid Waste Management, Visible Cleanliness, Access to Sanitation, Mechanisation of Desludging Services, Ecosystem Strengthening & Institutional Parameters, Used Water Management, Advocacy for Swachhata, Overall Welfare of Sanitation Workers, Citizen Feedback & Grievance Redressal. Over 3,000 trained assessors undertook extensive on-ground evaluations nationwide, supported by real-time GPS-enabled monitoring. From evidence submission to verification, the entire assessment process was conducted through a fully digital, transparent, and rigorously quality-assured framework, ensuring credibility and consistency at every stage.

2335194.title: Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 at Dilli Haat Records Cumulative Sales Cross Rs 73.49 Lakh, Reflecting Growing Public Appreciation for Artisans' Products
2335194.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 at Dilli Haat Records Cumulative Sales Cross Rs 73.49 Lakh, Reflecting Growing Public Appreciation for Artisans' Products
Mela Draws Enthusiastic Public Participation, Celebrates India's Cultural Diversity
More Than 130 Stalls Showcase Traditional Handicrafts, Handloom Products and Indigenous Creations Across Seven Thematic Zones
Daily Cultural Performances, Traditional Music and Folk Dances Create a Vibrant Festive Atmosphere
Posted On: 11 NOV 2026 8:01PM by PIB Delhi

The ongoing Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 at Dilli Haat, INA, in the National Capital, is witnessing enthusiastic participation from citizens, families and young visitors, offering a vibrant celebration of India's traditional craftsmanship, cultural heritage and artistic diversity. The growing public interest is also reflected in the sales recorded during the Mela.

 

A Senior Official in Ministry said the four participating National Corporations under the Ministry of Social Justice And Empowerment, have recorded cumulative sales of approximately ₹ 73.49  Lakh between November 1 and November 10, 2026. The sales reflect the encouraging response from visitors and the increasing market opportunities for products created by beneficiary communities.

The four participating corporations include National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC), National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC) and National Divyangjan Finance and Development Corporation (NDFDC), he said.

Organised by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, the 15-day Mela has emerged as an engaging platform where visitors explore indigenous products, experience regional art forms and connect with the country's rich cultural traditions.

Organised around the theme ‘प्रकाश और परंपरा – ज्योति से ज्योति जलाएँ’, the Mela brings together traditional craftsmanship and cultural heritage through seven thematic zones: कला आँगन, प्रकाश चौक, पूजा पथ, सजावट बाज़ार, घराना, स्वाद चौक and मंच. Each zone offers visitors a distinctive experience, covering traditional crafts, festive decorations, home décor, cultural products and regional culinary traditions.

The Official said the Mela features more than 130 stalls showcasing a diverse range of handicrafts, handloom products, traditional textiles, lamps, festive decorations, home décor items and other indigenous creations.

 

The visitors are enthusiastically exploring the stalls, appreciating the craftsmanship of participating artisans and purchasing products that reflect India's rich artistic traditions, he added.

A major attraction of the Mela is its lively cultural programme organised every evening at the Manch.

Artists and performing troupes from different States are presenting colourful folk dances, traditional music and regional art forms, bringing together diverse cultural expressions on a common platform.

These performances offer visitors an opportunity to experience India's cultural richness and regional traditions while creating a festive atmosphere of celebration and cultural exchange.

The cultural evenings have added a distinctive dimension to the Mela, making it more than an exhibition and shopping destination.

Visitors are enjoying the performances, discovering different regional traditions and experiencing the artistic diversity that reflects India's pluralistic cultural identity.

The Mela provides a valuable marketing platform for artisans and beneficiaries belonging to Scheduled Castes, Other Backward Classes, Safai Karamcharis and persons with disabilities to showcase their products and connect directly with consumers.

The Ministry facilitates their participation by providing free stalls, travel expenses, daily allowances and transportation facilities for their goods, helping them overcome logistical and financial barriers.

The initiative also promotes wider market access through platforms such as Bharat TULIP, which connects artisans with e-commerce opportunities, and Purple Fest, which celebrates the creativity and capabilities of persons with disabilities while encouraging inclusion and equal opportunities.

Since 2022, the Ministry has been organising Shilp Samagam Melas, benefiting more than 1,000 artisans from Scheduled Castes, Other Backward Classes and Safai Karamchari communities by providing opportunities to exhibit and market their products. The initiative aims to encourage self-employment, strengthen entrepreneurship and promote socio-economic empowerment through sustainable livelihood opportunities.

The Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 will continue at Dilli Haat, INA, New Delhi, until November 15, 2026.

Through its combination of traditional products, cultural performances and public participation, the Mela offers a meaningful platform for celebrating India's artistic diversity while advancing the vision of an inclusive and self-reliant India.

2335193.title: INDIAN NAVY AND ROYAL NAVY OF OMAN CONDUCT 15TH EDITION OF BILATERAL MARITIME EXERCISE NASEEM AL BAHR (SEA BREEZE)
2335193.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
INDIAN NAVY AND ROYAL NAVY OF OMAN CONDUCT 15TH EDITION OF BILATERAL MARITIME EXERCISE NASEEM AL BAHR (SEA BREEZE)
Posted On: 11 NOV 2026 7:57PM by PIB Delhi

The Indian Navy and the Royal Navy of Oman conducted the 15th edition of their bilateral maritime exercise, Naseem Al Bahr (Sea Breeze), aimed at enhancing interoperability, strengthening professional cooperation and promoting mutual understanding between the two navies.

During the harbour phase, Subject Matter Expert Exchanges (SMEE) were conducted between specialist teams of the two navies. The exchanges covered key areas of mutual interest, including Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD), Mine Countermeasure Operations and Hydrography. These interactions facilitated the exchange of professional knowledge and operational experience in specialised maritime domains.

The sea phase featured joint operational activities between Indian Naval Ship Surat and Royal Navy of Oman Vessel Al-Mu’azzar. These included joint Visit, Board, Search and Seizure (VBSS) drills and cross-deck operations, providing opportunities for personnel of both navies to practise coordinated procedures and enhance operational interoperability.

Exercise Naseem Al Bahr (Sea Breeze) reflects the close maritime partnership between India and Oman and the shared commitment of the two navies to strengthening maritime cooperation. The exercise also reinforces the Indian Navy’s engagement with regional maritime partners in furtherance of the Government of India's vision of MAHASAGAR (Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions).

2335192.title: INDIAN NAVAL SHIP TRISHUL CONCLUDES PORT CALL AT SAFAGA, EGYPT
2335192.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
INDIAN NAVAL SHIP TRISHUL CONCLUDES PORT CALL AT SAFAGA, EGYPT
Posted On: 11 NOV 2026 7:56PM by PIB Delhi

Indian Naval Ship (INS) Trishul concluded her port call at Safaga Naval Base, Egypt, on 09 Nov 2026, as part of her ongoing operational deployment.

The port call further reinforced the growing India–Egypt defence and maritime partnership , in the backdrop of the 11th India–Egypt Joint Defence Committee (JDC) meeting held in Cairo in Apr 2026 (https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2254773). The 11th JDC meeting provided an institutional framework for advancing defence commitments under the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on Defence Cooperation signed in Sep 2022, following the elevation of bilateral ties to a Strategic Partnership in 2023.

During the visit, the Commanding Officer of INS Trishul called on RAdm MD Abd El Maksoud, Commander, Red Sea Naval Base, Egypt. Discussions covered maritime security in the Gulf of Suez and the strategic significance of the Red Sea. The ship's crew also visited Egyptian Naval Ship ENS Port Said (976), gaining insights into its operational capabilities and the best practices followed by the Egyptian Navy.

The visit further featured reciprocal interactions between personnel of the Indian and Egyptian navies, along with joint diving training activities. These professional engagements provided opportunities for exchange of operational experience, sharing of Best Practices and furthering mutual understanding between the two navies.

The port call reaffirmed the longstanding defence ties between India and Egypt and their shared commitment to maritime security and regional stability. Following completion of the engagements, INS Trishul proceeded for the next phase of her operational deployment.

2335191.title: 8TH EDITION OF INDIA–MYANMAR NAVAL EXERCISE (IMNEX-26) COMMENCES AT VISAKHAPATNAM
2335191.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
8TH EDITION OF INDIA–MYANMAR NAVAL EXERCISE (IMNEX-26) COMMENCES AT VISAKHAPATNAM
Posted On: 11 NOV 2026 7:52PM by PIB Delhi

The 8th edition of the India–Myanmar Naval Exercise (IMNEX-26) is being conducted at Visakhapatnam from 10 to 14 Nov 2026. Myanmar Navy Ship UMS King Sin Phyu Shin arrived at Visakhapatnam on 10 Nov 2026 to participate in the exercise alongside INS Rana and INS Sumedha. The Opening Ceremony was held onboard INS Rana on 10 Nov 2026, marking the commencement of the bilateral exercise.

IMNEX serves as an important platform for advancing maritime cooperation between the two neighbouring countries. The exercise provides an opportunity for both the Navies to exchange professional expertise, enhance mutual understanding and develop greater operational synergy.

The Harbour Phase includes professional interactions, Subject Matter Expert Exchanges (SMEEs), cross-deck visits, sporting engagements and discussions on operational matters. The subsequent Sea Phase will involve coordinated maritime operations, tactical manoeuvres and exercises aimed at enhancing interoperability between the participating units.

IMNEX-26 underscores the enduring friendship and maritime partnership between India and Myanmar. The exercise is aligned with India's vision of MAHASAGAR (Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions) and reflects the shared commitment of both Navies to maritime cooperation and a secure and stable regional environment.

2335187.title: Ministry of Tribal Affairs to Organise National Tribal Literary Festival in New Delhi on 12–13 November 2026
2335187.body_html:
Ministry of Tribal Affairs
Ministry of Tribal Affairs to Organise National Tribal Literary Festival in New Delhi on 12–13 November 2026
Two-day festival to bring together tribal writers, poets, scholars and cultural practitioners; focus on preserving tribal languages, oral traditions and indigenous literary heritage
Posted On: 11 NOV 2026 7:44PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Tribal Affairs will organise a two-day National Tribal Literary Festival on 12 – 13 November 2026 at Silver Oak, India Habitat Centre, New Delhi, as part of the celebrations commemorating Janjatiya Gaurav Divas 2026. The festival aims to provide a national platform for celebrating India's rich and diverse tribal literary traditions, promoting indigenous languages and oral narratives, and recognising the contributions of tribal writers, poets, storytellers and knowledge holders. The inaugural session will be attended by Shri Jual Oram, Hon'ble Union Minister of Tribal Affairs; Shri Durgadas Uikey, Hon'ble Minister of State for Tribal Affairs; Dr. Joram Aniya, Hon'ble Member, NITI Aayog; Shri Chamu Krishna Shastri, Chairman, Bharatiya Bhasha Samiti; and Smt. Ranjana Chopra, Secretary, Ministry of Tribal Affairs, along with other senior officials and distinguished guests.

The Festival aligns with the Hon’ble Prime Minister’s vision of Viksit Bharat@2047 by recognising the knowledge, languages and cultural contributions of tribal communities as vital to India’s inclusive, knowledge-driven and culturally rooted development, and by ensuring that their voices and heritage remain an integral part of the nation’s journey towards a developed India. It will bring together tribal writers, poets, authors, researchers, linguists, academicians and cultural practitioners from across the country to celebrate the diversity of tribal literary heritage.

Tribal literature represents an important repository of India's civilisational and cultural heritage. Rooted in community histories, lived experiences, relationships with nature, traditional ecological knowledge and collective memory, these literary traditions have been transmitted across generations through oral narratives, songs, folklore, storytelling and indigenous forms of expression. However, several tribal languages and their associated literary traditions continue to face challenges relating to documentation, intergenerational transmission and wider dissemination.

Recognising the importance of safeguarding this invaluable heritage, the Festival will explore the rich and diverse literary traditions of tribal communities, tracing the continuum from oral traditions and community memory to contemporary literary expression. The deliberations will cover the significance of tribal folklore, including, ritual songs, myths, folktales, riddles, proverbs, children’s traditions, seasonal narratives and women's oral traditions, as well as the role of oral epics and heroic traditions in preserving community histories and cultural memory.

The festival will feature thematic sessions on tribal literature, poetry, folklore and storytelling, bringing together writers, poets, scholars and practitioners representing diverse tribal languages. Discussions will examine the contribution of oral traditions to multilingual education, language and literacy, including their role in transmitting ecological knowledge, social and ethical values, and cultural identity across generations. Dedicated poetry and story-reading sessions will showcase literary works and creative expressions in different tribal languages, providing an opportunity for tribal authors and poets to share their narratives with a wider audience.

Through these literary sessions, the festival seeks to strengthen the recognition of tribal literary heritage, encourage the preservation and intergenerational transmission of indigenous narratives, and bring greater visibility to tribal languages and literary expressions in India's cultural and academic discourse.

Organised as part of the celebrations of Janjatiya Gaurav Divas, commemorating the birth anniversary of Bhagwan Birsa Munda, the National Tribal Literary Festival seeks to honour the rich cultural legacy and contributions of India's tribal communities. It reaffirms the importance of preserving and celebrating their literary and linguistic heritage as an integral part of India's cultural identity and collective heritage.

2335182.title: Under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and guidance of Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah, Government of India rationalizes Indian visa regime
2335182.body_html:
Ministry of Home Affairs
Under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and guidance of Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah, Government of India rationalizes Indian visa regime
Under Visa regime rationalization, main categories for Visa reduced from 13 to 09 and sub categories from 49 to 23
Indian visa regime rationalization to boost foreign tourist arrivals, enhance medical value travel and foreign student arrivals
Number of fields to be filled in the application forms for all 23 visa sub-categories reduced by 65%–70%, now application process easier, faster, and more applicant-friendly
Changes reduce overlap between visa categories and make framework easier to navigate for visitors, patients, students, researchers, investors and business professionals
Rationalization intends to boost legitimate travel, education, healthcare and economic engagement with India through clearer, purpose-based visa options
Posted On: 11 NOV 2026 7:39PM by PIB Delhi

Under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and guidance of Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation, Shri Amit Shah, the Government of India has simplified its visa regime. The step aims at making it more compact, coherent and responsive to the requirements of foreign nationals visiting India. On 27th August, 2026, the Ministry of Home Affairs reduced the number of main visa categories from 13 to 9 and the number of sub-categories from 49 to 23. This follows the earlier rationalisation undertaken in October, 2025, when the main visa categories were reduced from 22 to 13 and sub-categories from 63 to 49. While considering the simplification of Indian Visa regime, the Government of India studied the Visa system of the developed countries and global standards.

The consolidation of similar purposes of travel is aimed at providing greater clarity and ease in identifying the appropriate visa category while facilitating legitimate foreign arrivals.

Currently e-visa is processed by electronic travel authorization under 13 sub categories. The facility of e-visa is presently available to the nationals of 172 countries.

Visitor Visa: greater flexibility for short and long stays

The erstwhile Tourist Visa has been renamed Visitor Visa, reflecting a broader range of permitted purposes beyond conventional tourism. The category has been organised into two sub-categories, V-1 and V-2, so that applicants may select a visa suited to the nature and duration of their proposed visit.

V-1 Visa: In addition to other eligible visitor activities, it covers short-term activities such as business meetings, medical consultations, wellness retreats, short-duration medical treatment and short-term courses in Indian languages, music, art and craft. It is granted for 30 days with multiple entries.

V-2 Visa: Intended for longer-duration visits, with validity of 1, 5 or 10 years, as specified. It covers the activities permissible under V-1 and mountaineering. For mountaineering, a visa of six months, with multiple entries, will be granted.

By bringing a wider range of short visits under a clearly identified category, the new arrangement makes visa selection simpler for travelers who may combine leisure with business meetings, medical consultations, wellness retreats or cultural learning, short duration yoga programme. The longer-duration V-2 option provides continuity and convenience for eligible repeat visitors, while the specific mountaineering provision addresses the distinct needs of such travel.

Medical Visa: continuity of care and ease of repeat visits

The Medical Visa framework retains separate provisions for treatment under conventional and AYUSH systems. M-1 Visa covers medical treatment other than treatment under AYUSH systems, while M-3 Visa covers treatment under AYUSH systems. M-1 and M-3 Visas, including their e-Visa variants, will be granted for one year as a default option with multiple entries. Corresponding medical attendant visa provisions are also available accordingly M-2 and M-4 Visas will be granted for attendant of M-1 and M-3 visa holders respectively.

This arrangement gives patients greater predictability when treatment involves multiple consultations, follow-up appointments or staged procedures. Multiple-entry validity can reduce the need for repeated visa applications during a course of care, while the distinct AYUSH provision helps applicants identify the appropriate treatment route. The availability of attendant visas also facilitates support by accompanying persons. This will encourage the Medical Value Tourism in India as per  the Prime Minister’s Vision of Heal in India.

Student Visa: clearer pathways for education and research

The Student Visa category has been consolidated into two broad sub-categories. S-1 Visa covers school, graduate and post-graduate education. S-2 Visa covers PhD and research scholars in Indian universities, visiting faculty, foreign research students visiting India for research, scientific and anthropological expeditions, internships and exchange students, among other specified academic activities.

For foreign students enrolled in Indian educational institutions through the Study in India portal, the e-S1 Visa may be granted for up to five years or for the duration of the academic course, whichever is less, with multiple entries. These provisions offer students a more readily identifiable visa pathway and greater certainty for academic planning. Longer validity linked to the course duration can also minimise procedural interruptions and make it easier for eligible students to travel during their studies.

Business Visa: clearer provisions for investment and specialized activities

The Business Visa category has been consolidated into B-1 and B-2. B-1 Visa covers long-term, licence-based business activities, including foreign nationals seeking to establish industrial or business ventures in India. B-2 Visa covers short-term, contract-based business activities, including Production Investment Business, conferences, sports, performative arts and films.

A specific provision has also been made for foreign subject-matter specialists, engineers and technical personnel engaged by Indian companies in activities such as installation and commissioning, quality checks and essential maintenance, production, IT and ERP ramp-up, training, supply-chain development, plant design and bring-up, senior management and technical support, including transfer of know-how, technology and services. Such personnel may be granted a Production Investment Business Visa under the B-2 category through the e-Visa platform. This was earlier granted under e-B4 visa nomenclature.

This differentiation gives businesses greater clarity when planning long-term investments as against short-term contractual assignments. The dedicated provision for technical specialists can facilitate timely deployment of expertise for setting up and operationalising industrial facilities, transferring technology, training personnel and supporting production, thereby improving predictability for companies and foreign professionals alike.

Simpler, purpose-based visa framework

Taken together, the changes reduce overlap between visa categories and make the framework easier to navigate for visitors, patients, students, researchers, investors and business professionals. The rationalisation is intended to support legitimate travel, education, healthcare and economic engagement with India through clearer, purpose-based visa options, subject to applicable eligibility criteria and conditions.

Simplified Visa Application Forms to facilitate Foreign Nationals visiting India

The Ministry of Home Affairs has undertaken a comprehensive exercise to simplify and rationalize visa application forms across 23 categories/sub-categories of Visas. The required filed/column for all 23 categories/sub-categories of Visas have been reduced 65%-70%. The initiative aims to significantly reduce the information required from foreign national, simplify visa form while retaining essential details necessary for visa processing. This will reduce time and effort required to complete application by the applicant as well as it will enhance administrative efficiency by facilitating more focused scrutiny and processing of visa application.

To implement all changes made in Indian Visa Regime, the MHA is updating the IT systems and by year-end, visas will be granted as per new rationalization.

The revised visa framework now comprises nine main categories as indicated below:

S. No.

Main category of visa

Purpose for which granted

1

Business Visa

 

 

Long-term business activities including establishing an industrial/business venture; short- term business activities like participation in sports & cultural/commercial performances, production investment business, attending conferences, shooting of films including documentaries & advertisement films.  

2

Diplomatic Visa

Diplomats including UN Diplomats assigned to India or visiting India and their dependents

3

Work Visa

Long-term employment with Indian companies/organizations, working in NGOs and missionary activities

4

Journalist Visa

Journalists accredited in India

5

Medical Visa

Foreigners visiting India to undergo intensive/indoor medical treatment including treatment under Ayush systems and their attendants

6

Official Visa

Non-diplomatic officials including UN non-diplomatic officials assigned to India or on a visit to India and their dependents

7

Student Visa

School/graduate/post-graduate education, studies in Yoga, Vedic Culture & Indian Music/Dance, Buddhist studies, studies of Indian Languages & Indian knowledge systems, research, internship and exchange students

8

Visitor Visa

Tourism, short-term activities including business meetings, medical consultations & Wellness retreats, transit and mountaineering

9

Miscellaneous Visa

Persons of Indian Origin & their spouses/children, those coming to join various specified institutions like Auroville Foundation, dependents of foreign nationals coming on various long duration visas, stay visa for Afghanistan nationals, Long Term Visa for certain categories of nationals from neighbouring countries and other miscellaneous purposes not covered by any other visa category.

2335179.title: BUILDING A STRONGER AND MORE PROSPEROUS INDIA REQUIRES EFFECTIVE INSTITUTIONS AND PUBLIC SERVANTS: LOK SABHA SPEAKER
2335179.body_html:
Lok Sabha Secretariat
BUILDING A STRONGER AND MORE PROSPEROUS INDIA REQUIRES EFFECTIVE INSTITUTIONS AND PUBLIC SERVANTS: LOK SABHA SPEAKER
TECHNOLOGY MUST BE LEVERAGED TO PREVENT AND DETECT CRIME AND STRENGTHEN INTERNAL SECURITY: LOK SABHA SPEAKER
LOK SABHA SPEAKER INTERACTS WITH IPS PROBATIONERS IN PARLIAMENT HOUSE COMPLEX
Posted On: 11 NOV 2026 7:35PM by PIB Delhi

Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla today emphasised that building a stronger and more prosperous India requires effective institutions and public servants who are responsive to the aspirations and concerns of citizens. He underlined that police officers must maintain constant engagement with the public, communicate with people regularly, and develop a close understanding of their needs and challenges. He said that public trust is the cornerstone of effective policing. He called upon the probationers to earn the confidence of citizens through impartiality, transparency, accessibility and prompt action. He observed that the police must be perceived not merely as an agency responsible for maintaining law and order, but also as a dependable institution that stands with people and safeguards their rights and security.

Shri Birla made these remarks while interacting with a group of IPS probationers at the Parliament House Complex. He called upon them to dedicate themselves wholeheartedly to the service of the people and the nation.

Shri Birla observed that the Indian Police Service offers a unique opportunity to make a meaningful difference in people's lives. He urged the probationers to discharge their responsibilities with a deep sense of commitment, integrity, sensitivity and accountability, keeping public welfare at the centre of their professional conduct.

Highlighting the transformative role of technology in policing, the Lok Sabha Speaker encouraged the young officers to make optimal use of emerging technologies, digital tools, data analytics and modern investigative techniques to prevent and detect crime. He noted that technology-driven policing can enhance operational efficiency, improve responsiveness and strengthen the overall law-and-order framework.

Shri Birla further observed that the challenges facing society are constantly evolving and called upon the probationers to remain open to new ideas, continuously upgrade their professional capabilities, and adopt innovative approaches to policing. He stressed that effective policing must combine technological advancement with human sensitivity and compassion. The Speaker expressed confidence that the young officers, with their professional training, commitment and enthusiasm, would make valuable contributions towards strengthening the country's internal security and building a safe, secure and progressive India.

The interaction provided an opportunity for the IPS probationers to exchange views with the Lok Sabha Speaker and gain insights into the functioning of Parliament and India's democratic institutions.

संविधान सदन के केंद्रीय कक्ष में संसद के अध्ययन दौरे पर आए भारतीय पुलिस सेवा (IPS) के 78वें आरआर बैच (2025 बैच) के अधिकारियों के साथ संवाद किया। भारत की संसद और संसदीय प्रणाली हमारे लोकतंत्र की गौरवशाली पहचान हैं। संविधान विधायिका, कार्यपालिका और न्यायपालिका के दायित्वों को निर्धारित करते हुए न्याय, समानता और बंधुता पर आधारित शासन व्यवस्था का मार्गदर्शन करता है। कानून और नीतियों की वास्तविक सार्थकता उनके प्रभावी क्रियान्वयन में निहित होती है, जिसकी महत्वपूर्ण जिम्मेदारी प्रशासनिक एवं पुलिस अधिकारियों पर होती है। युवा अधिकारियों से अपेक्षा है कि वे संवेदनशीलता, निष्पक्षता और जनसेवा की भावना के साथ अपने दायित्वों का निर्वहन करें। कानून का उद्देश्य केवल व्यवस्था बनाए रखना नहीं, बल्कि प्रत्येक नागरिक के अधिकारों और गरिमा की रक्षा करना भी है। समाज के अंतिम व्यक्ति तक न्याय और सुरक्षा का विश्वास पहुँचाना ही लोकसेवा की वास्तविक कसौटी है। पुलिस सेवा में महिलाओं की बढ़ती भागीदारी भी एक सकारात्मक परिवर्तन है। मुझे विश्वास है कि ये युवा अधिकारी अपनी निष्ठा, दक्षता और मानवीय दृष्टिकोण से राष्ट्रसेवा करते हुए सुशासन और लोकतांत्रिक मूल्यों को और सुदृढ़ करेंगे। @LBSNAA_Official

2335167.title: Achievements made by Ministry of Women and Child Development under Special Campaign 6.0
2335167.ministry: Ministry of Women and Child Development
2335167.body_html:
Ministry of Women and Child Development
Achievements made by Ministry of Women and Child Development under Special Campaign 6.0
Cleanliness activities undertaken in more than 12 lakh field Institutions under the special campaign
 51,090 grievances disposed during the dedicated one-day event as part of special campaign 6.0
Posted On: 11 NOV 2026 7:05PM by PIB Delhi

Ministry of Women and Child Development, including all Autonomous/ Statutory Bodies under its administrative control, had initiated efforts and finalised action plans & targets to implement Special Campaign 6 for improving Swachhata and disposal of pending references from 2nd October - 31st October, 2026. The Special Campaign aimed at promoting cleanliness streamlining work, addressing pending grievances across the Ministry and its Autonomous Bodies.

As part of the implementation phase of Special Campaign 6, States and UTs had organised a dedicated special one-day event on 30th October, 2026 by undertaking the following activities on a large scale with active participation of field-level functionaries and the community:

  • Cleanliness Drives at Field-Level Institutions
  • Effective Public Grievance Redressal and organizing Grievance Redressal Chaupal/e-Chaupals for redressal of grievances received under the schemes of the Ministry through POSHAN Tracker, PMMVY & CPGRAMS portal.

On account of the concerted efforts made by the Ministry as well as State Government functionaries as part of dedicated special one-day event, cleanliness drives & public grievance redressal campaigns were conducted on a large scale in the field institutions functional under the schemes of the Ministry viz. Anganwadi Centres, Child Care Institutions, Shakti Sadans, Sakhi Niwas, Creches etc. As a result of the same cleanliness activities were undertaken in 12,08,313 field institutions located all over the country under the special campaign & 51,090 grievances were disposed during the dedicated one-day event. In addition to the above, 5,51,653 other activities such as plantation drives, handwash messages to beneficiaries of Anganwadi and other field institutions were undertaken in the said institutions.

        Further, the Ministry recognised and appreciated the services of Safai Mitras and sanitation workers for their contribution towards sustaining cleanliness. The Safai Mitras were felicitated with new uniforms and awards as a mark of appreciation for the dedicated services of all Safai Mitras who work throughout the year to maintain a clean and hygienic campus.

2335168.title: Cyber Threats Respect No Borders, Neither Should Cooperation: Union MoS for Communications Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani at ITU PP-26
2335168.body_html:
Ministry of Communications
Cyber Threats Respect No Borders, Neither Should Cooperation: Union MoS for Communications Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani at ITU PP-26
Developing Nations Must Have a Say in Setting Global Technology Standards: Dr. Pemmasani
India's Digital Growth Must Reach Every Village says Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani, Showcases BharatNet at ITU PP-26
Posted On: 11 NOV 2026 7:05PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of State for Communications and Rural Development, Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani, presented India's approach to digital connectivity, emerging technologies and cybersecurity at the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) Plenipotentiary Conference (PP-26) in Doha.

Speaking at the High-Level Discussion on Emerging Technologies, he highlighted India's efforts under Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi to make technology accessible and affordable. With 2.2 billion people across the world still offline, he pointed to India's investment of approximately $15 billion in BharatNet to extend broadband connectivity to rural areas.

He also spoke about Samriddh Gram Centres, a WSIS Prize winner, where villagers can access healthcare, agricultural advice, banking and government certificates. India's work in affordable AI computing, indigenous language AI models, quantum research and 100 5G use-case labs also featured in his address. He called for developing countries to have a greater role in framing global technology standards and spectrum policies.

On the sidelines, Dr. Pemmasani met delegations from Malaysia, Iran and Uzbekistan. Discussions covered cross-border cyber fraud, digital infrastructure security and cooperation in quantum technology.

Sharing India's experience in tackling digital fraud, he said alerts sent to banks had helped prevent suspected financial losses of over ₹5,000 crore.

"Cyber threats do not respect borders, and neither should our cooperation. Learning from each other's best practices makes all of us stronger," he said.

Began my engagements at ITU PP-26 in Doha with the High-Level Discussion on Emerging Technologies. Under PM Shri Narendra Modi ji, India is democratising technology: affordable AI compute for our innovators, AI models in Indian languages, quantum research hubs, and 100 5G labs building talent for the future. With a modern regulatory framework and the Bharat 6G Vision, we are preparing for a future where telecom networks, AI and satellites converge, so that connectivity reaches every remote corner. Called for global cooperation on standards, spectrum and capacity building, so developing nations shape these technologies, not merely adopt them. దోహాలో జరుగుతున్న @ITU PP-26 సదస్సులో అధికారిక కార్యక్రమాలను "ఎమర్జింగ్ టెక్నాలజీస్" పై జరిగిన ఉన్నతస్థాయి చర్చతో ప్రారంభించాము. ​గౌరవ ప్రధాని శ్రీ @narendramodi గారి నేతృత్వంలో సరికొత్త సాంకేతికతను సామాన్యుల ముంగిటకు తెస్తున్నాము. మన యువ ఆవిష్కర్తలకు తక్కువ ఖర్చుతోనే ఏఐ కంప్యూట్, మన భాషల్లోనే ఏఐ మోడల్స్, క్వాంటం పరిశోధనా కేంద్రాలు, అలాగే భవిష్యత్తు కోసం నిపుణులను తీర్చిదిద్దే 100 5G ల్యాబ్‌లను సిద్ధం చేశాము. ​ఆధునిక నియంత్రణ విధానాలు, 'భారత్ 6G విజన్'తో ముందుకు సాగుతూ... టెలికాం, ఏఐ, శాటిలైట్ వ్యవస్థల కలయిక ద్వారా దేశంలోని చిట్టచివరి పల్లెకూ బలమైన కనెక్టివిటీని చేర్చే దిశగా అడుగులు వేస్తున్నాము. ​సాంకేతిక ప్రమాణాలు, స్పెక్ట్రమ్ కేటాయింపులు, నైపుణ్యాభివృద్ధిలో ప్రపంచ దేశాలన్నీ చేతులు కలపాలని పిలుపునిచ్చాము. తద్వారా అభివృద్ధి చెందుతున్న దేశాలు సాంకేతికతలను కేవలం వాడుకోవడమే కాకుండా, వాటి రూపకల్పనలోనూ ముందుండగలవు. #ITUPP26 #IndiaAtITUPP26

— Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani (@PemmasaniOnX) November 11, 2026

Held bilateral meetings with the delegations of Malaysia, Iran and Uzbekistan at ITU PP-26 in Doha. Discussed cooperation on cyber fraud, cybersecurity and quantum technologies, the vital role of the ITU in developing the telecom sector, and the capacity-building support India provides in this field. Cyber threats do not respect borders, and neither should our cooperation. Learning from each other's best practices makes all of us stronger. ​దోహాలో జరుగుతున్న @ITU PP-26 సదస్సు సందర్భంగా మలేషియా, ఇరాన్, ఉజ్బెకిస్తాన్ ప్రతినిధి బృందాలతో వేర్వేరుగా ఫలప్రదమైన ద్వైపాక్షిక చర్చలు జరిపాము. ​సైబర్ మోసాల కట్టడి, పటిష్టమైన సైబర్ భద్రత, క్వాంటమ్ టెక్నాలజీ రంగాల్లో పరస్పర సహకారంపై విస్తృతంగా సమాలోచనలు చేశాము. అంతర్జాతీయ టెలికాం రంగ విస్తరణలో ITU పోషిస్తున్న కీలక పాత్రతో పాటు, సాంకేతిక నైపుణ్యాభివృద్ధి కోసం భారతదేశం అందిస్తున్న బలమైన తోడ్పాటును ఈ సందర్భంగా వివరించాము. సైబర్ ముప్పులను తిప్పికొట్టాలంటే ఉమ్మడి సహకారమే బలం. పరస్పర అనుభవాలను పంచుకుంటూ కలిసి పోరాడాలని నిర్ణయించాము.

2335147.title: From the Margins to Leadership
2335147.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From the Margins to Leadership
Inspiring Journey Of Six Women From Telangana And Delhi Reflect Their Empowerment Through Safer Livelihoods, Entrepreneurship And Community Leadership Under NAMASTE
Posted On: 11 NOV 2026 6:30PM by PIB Delhi

Women engaged in sanitation and waste management are increasingly emerging as entrepreneurs, decision-makers and community leaders, demonstrating how access to institutional support, mechanisation and livelihood opportunities can contribute to their socio-economic empowerment.

The inspiring journey of six women from Telangana and Delhi reflect this transformation, highlighting their determination to move beyond traditional occupational roles and build more secure, independent and dignified futures for themselves and their communities.

In Siricilla, Telangana, five women sanitation workers Anusha Reddy, Kavitha Goud, Swathi Yadav, Srilatha Naidu and Madhavi Kumar (all names changed) had been working as septic tank cleaning helpers under private contractors. Each earned an average monthly income of approximately ₹15,000 while undertaking physically demanding sanitation-related work involving occupational risks and limited opportunities for professional advancement. Despite their experience in sanitation services, financial constraints and limited access to resources made it difficult for them to establish an independent enterprise.

A significant turning point came when the five women learned about the Swachhta Udyami Yojana (SUY) during a locally organised loan mela. Recognising the opportunity to become entrepreneurs, they collectively decided to establish a mechanised sanitation enterprise. With financial assistance under the scheme, they acquired mechanised desludging vehicles and began providing sanitation services under Siricilla Municipal Corporation. This marked an important transition from working as sanitation helpers to collectively owning and managing mechanised sanitation operations.

Through mechanisation, the women moved towards safer and more efficient sanitation practices, reducing their dependence on hazardous manual cleaning methods. Their responsibilities expanded to operating mechanised vehicles, coordinating desludging services and managing their enterprise. The initiative strengthened their economic independence, enhanced their professional confidence and enabled them to take greater ownership of their livelihoods.

Today, Anusha, Kavitha, Swathi, Srilatha and Madhavi are contributing to improved sanitation services while demonstrating the potential of women-led enterprises in the sector.

A similar journey of empowerment and leadership can be seen in Seemapuri, Delhi, through the experiences of Anita (name changed), originally from Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh. After moving to Delhi following her marriage, she began supporting her family by sorting waste alongside her husband, who was engaged in waste picking. Over time, she gained experience in waste management activities and started operating a small scrap shop, contributing to her family's financial stability.

Her journey towards community leadership began when she was mobilised by a Resource Organisation and became associated with a Self Help Group (SHG). Through active participation and commitment to collective development, she gradually emerged as a community leader and became the President of the SHG. Recognising her leadership abilities and experience, a local NGO subsequently engaged her as a Senior SHG Mobiliser and Community Mobiliser, providing her with an opportunity to support other women and waste pickers in accessing information, resources and institutional assistance.

Anita's association with the National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) Scheme further strengthened her journey towards safer working conditions and socio-economic security. Through the scheme, she received occupational safety training, Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) and an Ayushman card, supporting her access to safer occupational practices and healthcare benefits. Her engagement with the NGO also enabled her to earn an additional monthly income of ₹10,000 while continuing her involvement in waste picking activities, contributing to greater financial stability for her family.

Drawing upon her own experiences, Anita now plays an active role in mobilising waste pickers, strengthening community groups and spreading awareness about the NAMASTE Scheme. She sensitises fellow workers about registration procedures, occupational safety measures and available government benefits, helping them connect with formal support systems. Her transition from waste picker to SHG President and community mobiliser reflects how access to opportunities, collective participation and institutional recognition can strengthen women's leadership and enable them to support the development of their communities.

The journey of these six women demonstrate the wider impact of interventions aimed at strengthening the safety, dignity and socio-economic empowerment of sanitation workers and waste pickers. While the five women from Telangana have moved towards collective entrepreneurship through mechanised sanitation services, Anita has emerged as a community leader, supporting fellow workers in accessing information, entitlements and livelihood opportunities.

The NAMASTE Scheme, through its focus on occupational safety, mechanisation, capacity building, social security linkages and livelihood support, is contributing towards the development of a safer and more inclusive sanitation ecosystem. These interventions not only help improve working conditions but also create opportunities for workers to enhance their skills, strengthen their financial independence and participate more actively in economic and community development.

Their achievements highlight how women's empowerment extends beyond individual income generation to include enterprise ownership, collective decision-making, leadership and the ability to create opportunities for others. By transforming their experience and skills into entrepreneurship and community mobilisation, these women are contributing to a more inclusive and dignified sanitation and waste management sector.

From sanitation helpers to enterprise owners, and from waste picking to community leadership, their journeys reflect the transformative potential of financial assistance, mechanisation, occupational safety measures and institutional support.

Through NAMASTE and associated livelihood interventions, the Government of India continues to advance its commitment towards the safety, dignity and socio-economic empowerment of sanitation workers and waste pickers, enabling women to become active contributors to a safer, more self-reliant and inclusive India.

2335145.title: From Financial Barriers to Global Academic Excellence
2335145.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Financial Barriers to Global Academic Excellence
 A Journey Towards Higher Education Through the National Overseas Scholarship
Posted On: 11 NOV 2026 6:28PM by PIB Delhi

The journey of 24-year-old student, Mr. Rahul Dabhade (Name Changed) reflects how access to quality higher education and targeted financial assistance empower talented students from Scheduled Caste communities to overcome economic barriers and pursue their aspirations at prestigious international institutions.

Through the National Overseas Scholarship, the Government of India continues to promote educational empowerment, equal opportunities and inclusive development, enabling deserving students to contribute to the nation's progress through their knowledge, skills and expertise.

Mr. Rahul Dabhade, belonging to the Scheduled Caste community from Maharashtra, demonstrated remarkable academic dedication and determination in pursuing his higher education aspirations. Despite financial and social challenges, he remained committed to advancing his academic journey and building a promising professional career.

Aspiring to pursue postgraduate studies in Construction Economics and Management at a globally reputed institution, he faced significant financial constraints due to the high cost of international education, including tuition fees, living expenses, travel and other academic requirements.

A significant opportunity came in 2025–26 when he received financial assistance under the National Overseas Scholarship (NOS) Scheme of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India. The scheme enabled him to pursue his MSc in Construction Economics and Management at University College London (UCL), United Kingdom, one of the leading universities in the world. The scholarship provided comprehensive financial assistance, including tuition fees amounting to £39,800, a maintenance allowance of £9,900, airfare, visa fees, insurance and other admissible academic expenses.

The financial assistance under the scheme significantly reduced the economic burden associated with pursuing higher education abroad. It enabled him to continue his studies without the risk of discontinuation due to financial constraints and provided access to international academic opportunities. The support also allowed him to focus on his academic commitments and make the most of the educational facilities and learning environment at the university.

With the support received through the National Overseas Scholarship, Mr. Rahul Dabhade is currently pursuing his postgraduate studies at University College London. He is actively participating in lectures, tutorials and other academic activities, gaining valuable international exposure and developing specialised knowledge in construction economics, infrastructure development and project management. The academic experience is helping him strengthen his professional competencies and broaden his understanding of global practices in the construction sector.

The intervention under the National Overseas Scholarship has played an important role in overcoming financial barriers to international higher education and expanding his academic and professional opportunities. Beyond financial assistance, the scheme has enabled him to access world-class education, enhance his knowledge and work towards a promising future in his chosen field.

2335144.title: CHIEF OF THE ARMY STAFF DELIVERS CAVALRY MEMORIAL ADDRESS AT MECHANISED FORCES SYMPOSIUM 2026
2335144.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
CHIEF OF THE ARMY STAFF DELIVERS CAVALRY MEMORIAL ADDRESS AT MECHANISED FORCES SYMPOSIUM 2026
Posted On: 11 NOV 2026 6:27PM by PIB Delhi

General Dhiraj Seth, Chief of the Army Staff (COAS), delivered an address on “Vision for Future Warfighting in the Indian Subcontinent” at the Mechanised Forces Symposium 2026, held at Manekshaw Centre, New Delhi, on 11 November 2026. The two-day symposium, organised by the Cavalry Officers’ Association in collaboration with the Directorate General of Mechanised Forces, brings together senior serving officers, veterans, defence scientists, industry representatives and strategic thinkers to deliberate on the changing character of warfare.

In his address, the COAS highlighted the Indian Army's ongoing transformation to meet emerging operational challenges. He emphasised that transformation goes beyond modern equipment and organisational restructuring, requiring a culture of innovation, technological adaptation and agility, while keeping the Yoddha at its core.

Highlighting jointness and integration as critical enabler of future warfighting, the COAS underscored the need for seamless coordination across Services and domains. He also reiterated the Indian Army's commitment to Aatmanirbharta through indigenous capability development and stronger partnerships with industry and academia.

Reflecting on the evolution of the Mechanised Forces, the COAS described their journey as a testament to the Army's spirit of adaptation. He expressed confidence in their continued pivotal role in future warfare.

The COAS's address formed the centrepiece of the inaugural session, which commenced with a welcome address by Lt Gen Ashok Mehta (Retd), President, Cavalry Officers' Association, and also witnessed the unveiling of the book “Armour 2040: Steel, Silicon & The Future Battlespace”, authored by Lt Gen AB Shivane (Retd). Delivering the keynote address on “Contemporary Mechanised Warfare in the Indian Context”, Lt Gen Prit Pal Singh, Director General Mechanised Forces, emphasised the transition from platform-centric capabilities towards an integrated, network-enabled and autonomous combat ecosystem.

Building on these themes, the symposium will also deliberate on Artificial Intelligence and autonomous kill chains, manned-unmanned teaming, integrated drone warfare, next-generation combat systems and multi-domain mechanised operations. The two-day event will culminate on 12 November 2026 with a valedictory fireside discussion on “Indian Mechanised Forces 2035: Transforming for the Future Operational Environment”.

2335141.title: Government Strengthens Rural 4G Connectivity Through 4G Saturation Project
2335141.body_html:
Ministry of Communications
Government Strengthens Rural 4G Connectivity Through 4G Saturation Project
Number of Villages Without 4G Connectivity Declines by Nearly 75% in Four Years
BSNL’s 18000-plus 4G Saturation Sites Empowering Rural India; 1.86 Crore GB Data Consumption in October 2026
DoT Steps Up Efforts to Ensure 4G Connectivity in Unserved and Remote Villages Across India
Posted On: 11 NOV 2026 6:25PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Telecommunications (DoT) is making sustained efforts to bridge the digital divide and strengthen telecommunications infrastructure across rural, remote and underserved areas of the country. These efforts have resulted in a significant reduction of nearly 75% in the number of villages without 4G connectivity, from 45,180 in 2022 to 11,372 in 2026, marking substantial progress towards expanding digital connectivity across rural India.

DoT’s 4G Saturation Project has played an important role in this expansion. The project was designed to provide 4G connectivity to 24,680 previously unconnected villages, ensuring that people in remote and underserved areas can access reliable mobile communication services and the benefits of digital connectivity. Private telecom service providers have also contributed to expanding rural 4G coverage through their network expansion initiatives.

BSNL’s 18,291 sites commissioned under the 24,680-site 4G saturation rollout plan are carrying substantial data traffic in rural areas. In October 2026, these sites served a maximum of 10,21,048 active users in a day, who together used over 1.86 crore GB (18,659,170 GB) of data, an average of 18.3 GB per user in the month. With about 56 active users per site on average, each site is serving dispersed rural communities that were earlier outside serviceable 4G coverage.

The Government has also sanctioned an additional 26,000 mobile network sites for the next phase of expansion to address the remaining connectivity gaps. Extending connectivity to remote and geographically difficult locations remains a key challenge due to difficult terrain, high infrastructure costs, scattered settlements and the presence of remote tribal habitations. The Department is continuing its efforts to address these challenges through coordinated action with BSNL and other telecom service providers.

Way Forward

Moving forward, the Department of Telecommunications will continue to prioritise the coverage of remaining unconnected villages, particularly in remote, tribal and aspirational regions. The deployment of additional mobile network sites, expansion of network-sharing arrangements and improved utilisation of existing telecom infrastructure will remain important strategies for achieving wider rural connectivity. Greater coordination with telecom service providers and targeted interventions in geographically challenging areas will further accelerate network expansion. These efforts are aimed at ensuring inclusive digital access and enabling rural communities to benefit from digital governance, education, healthcare, financial services and other essential digital platforms.

The Department of Telecommunications remains committed to the vision of a digitally connected India, ensuring that the benefits of reliable mobile connectivity reach every corner of the country and that no village is left behind in India's digital transformation.

2335121.title: From Substance Dependence to Self-Reliance
2335121.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Substance Dependence to Self-Reliance
Journey Of Rajsamand Rajasthan’s Mukesh Towards Recovery And A Dignified Life Through NAPDDR
Posted On: 11 NOV 2026 5:46PM by PIB Delhi

The journey of Mr Mukesh (name changed) reflects how accessible de-addiction services, medical care, counselling and sustained rehabilitation support through NAPDDR, helps individuals rebuild their lives and achieve economic self-reliance.

Through National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR), the Government of India continues to strengthen de-addiction and rehabilitation services, supporting the vision of a healthier society and a drug-free India.

Mukesh, a 39-year-old individual belonging to the Scheduled Tribe community from Rajsamand district of Rajasthan faced significant physical and financial challenges due to substance abuse. The prolonged effects of substance use had affected his physical well-being, causing bodily discomfort and pain in his joints and hands.

Coming from a financially vulnerable family, he had received education up to the high school level. His family also faced difficulties in securing adequate housing and meeting basic necessities. Despite these challenges, he aspired to establish himself professionally and improve the living conditions of his family.

A significant turning point came on 5 March 2026, when he received assistance from the District De-addiction Centre, Rajsamand, operated by Shubhdeep Group Seva Sansthan, under the NAPDDR framework of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India. The intervention provided him with comprehensive support, including medical consultation, counselling, yoga sessions, nutritious meals, clothing and accommodation.

As part of the rehabilitation support, the centre ensured regular and timely meals, daily morning yoga sessions and scheduled medication in the morning, afternoon and evening. Clothing and other essential necessities were also provided free of cost. This structured care and support enabled him to focus on his recovery and gradually work towards rebuilding his life.

With the support received through the centre, he moved towards a healthier lifestyle and greater financial stability. Following his recovery, he became engaged in self-employment and now earns a monthly income of ₹12,000, marking an increase of ₹5,000 compared to his earnings before treatment. His improved financial condition has enabled him to contribute towards household expenses and support his family with dignity.

The intervention under NAPDDR has played an important role in helping him overcome the challenges associated with substance dependence and move towards social and economic rehabilitation. Beyond medical assistance, the comprehensive support provided by the centre has helped him regain stability, pursue self-employment and work towards a more secure future for his family.
