2335115.title: Bharat Parv 2026 Showcases India’s Rich Cultural Heritage and Diversity at Ekta Nagar, Gujarat
2335115.body_html:
Ministry of Tourism
Bharat Parv 2026 Showcases India’s Rich Cultural Heritage and Diversity at Ekta Nagar, Gujarat
Inaugurated by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on 30 October 2026, the festival continues till 15 November 2026 under the theme ‘Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat’
States and Union Territories showcase ODOP products, traditional handicrafts, indigenous art forms and cultural performances
Posted On: 11 NOV 2026 5:43PM by PIB Delhi

Bharat Parv 2026, organised by the Ministry of Tourism, Government of India, in partnership with Gujarat Tourism and with the support of States and Union Territories, is underway at Ekta Nagar, Gujarat, celebrating India’s rich cultural heritage, vibrant traditions and diversity under the unifying theme of ‘Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat’. The festival was inaugurated by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on 30 October 2026, as part of the celebrations of Rashtriya Ekta Diwas, and will continue till 15 November 2026.

The festival brings together traditional arts, handicrafts, regional cuisines, folk traditions, music, dance and indigenous craftsmanship from across the country, offering visitors an opportunity to experience India’s cultural diversity at one destination.

A major attraction of Bharat Parv is the Theme Pavilion, featuring participation from 29 States and Union Territories, Incredible India and Central Cottage Industries. The pavilion showcases more than 100 One District One Product (ODOP) products, along with traditional handicrafts, textiles, paintings, agricultural produce and other distinctive regional products, highlighting the artistic excellence and cultural identity of different regions of India.

The ODOP showcases are a key highlight of the festival, with participating States and Union Territories presenting products that reflect the distinctive skills, traditional craftsmanship and local specialities of their respective regions. From intricately crafted textiles and handloom products to traditional paintings, handicrafts and region-specific agricultural produce, these exhibits offer visitors a glimpse of India’s diverse indigenous products and craft traditions. By bringing locally renowned products onto a national platform, Bharat Parv provides an opportunity to enhance the visibility of regional craftsmanship, promote traditional skills and encourage greater appreciation of products made by local artisans and craftspeople. The Incredible India pavilion further highlights the country’s heritage, culture and festivals through engaging digital interventions.


 

Live demonstrations by traditional artisans are another major attraction, providing visitors an opportunity to witness India’s indigenous craftsmanship firsthand. These include traditional mask-making from Assam, Madhubani painting and Sikki craft from Bihar, Rogan art and traditional paintings from Gujarat, bamboo art from Chhattisgarh, coir-product making from Kerala, Pattachitra painting and silver filigree from Odisha, Aipan painting and Ringaal basket weaving from Uttarakhand, and Sozni art from Jammu and Kashmir. These demonstrations provide a platform for artisans to showcase their skills and introduce visitors to traditional art forms, techniques and indigenous knowledge systems passed down through generations.


 

The festival also features a vibrant line-up of cultural performances representing the diverse folk and classical traditions of States and Union Territories. Visitors are experiencing Kuchipudi from Andhra Pradesh, Bihu and other folk dances from Assam, Garba from Gujarat, traditional folk performances from Haryana, Tholpavakoothu from Kerala, Ravanhatta instrumental music from Rajasthan, traditional dance forms from Tamil Nadu, Santoor performances from Jammu and Kashmir, and Baul folk music and Purulia Chhau from West Bengal, among several other regional performances. These cultural presentations bring alive the music, dance and artistic traditions that form an integral part of India’s cultural heritage.

The Food Court, featuring regional cuisines and traditional delicacies from 23 States and Union Territories, is another major attraction, offering visitors an opportunity to experience India’s diverse culinary traditions. A specially curated Studio Kitchen, managed by the National Council for Hotel Management and Catering Technology (NCHMCT), further enriches the experience through demonstrations highlighting regional culinary practices and traditional food preparation techniques. The Food Court also hosts daily cultural performances from 5:00 PM to 8:00 PM, featuring artists from 10 States each day, combining regional cuisine, music and dance in a vibrant setting.


 

Beyond celebrating India’s cultural diversity, Bharat Parv provides a common platform for showcasing regional products, promoting indigenous art forms and bringing traditional artisans, craftspeople and performing artists closer to audiences from different parts of the country. The festival also highlights the role of local traditions, crafts and cuisine in enriching tourism experiences and showcasing the distinctive cultural identity of different regions.

Bharat Parv 2026 continues to reinforce the spirit of ‘Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat’ by fostering cultural exchange, promoting national integration and celebrating India’s unity in diversity. The festival will remain open to visitors at Ekta Nagar, Gujarat, until 15 November 2026.

2335093.title: INDIAN NAVY TO COORDINATE FIFTH EDITION OF PAN-INDIA COASTAL DEFENCE EXERCISE 'SEA VIGIL-26'
2335093.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
INDIAN NAVY TO COORDINATE FIFTH EDITION OF PAN-INDIA COASTAL DEFENCE EXERCISE 'SEA VIGIL-26'
Posted On: 11 NOV 2026 5:17PM by PIB Delhi

The fifth edition of the Pan-India Coastal Defence Exercise 'Sea Vigil-26' is being held from 11 to 19 Nov 2026, coordinated by the Indian Navy as the lead agency. The exercise will be conducted in two phases: The Coastal Defence and Security Readiness Evaluation (CDSRE) phase from 11 to 17 Nov 2026, followed by the Sea Phase on 18 and 19 Nov 2026.

Exercise Sea Vigil was conceptualised in 2018 to validate the measures instituted to strengthen maritime security in the aftermath of the 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks. Sea Vigil-26 will span the entire coastline and Exclusive Economic Zone of India, and will involve all Coastal States and Union Territories, along with other maritime stakeholders, including the fishing and coastal communities.

The exercise is significant in terms of its geographical spread, the number of participating agencies and units, and the range of its objectives. Assets of the Indian Navy, Indian Coast Guard, Coastal Security Police, Customs and other maritime agencies will participate. The conduct of the exercise is also being facilitated by the Ministries of Defence; Home Affairs; Ports, Shipping and Waterways; Petroleum and Natural Gas; and Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, together with other agencies of the Centre and Coastal states and Union Territories.

Sea Vigil is also a build-up to the Indian Navy's biennial Theatre Level Readiness Operational Exercise (TROPEX). Together, Sea Vigil and TROPEX address the entire spectrum of maritime security challenges, from coastal defence to operations on the high seas.

The conduct of Sea Vigil at the national level provides an opportunity, at the apex level, to assess the nation's preparedness towards Maritime Security and Coastal Defence. Sea Vigil-26 will provide a realistic assessment, and further strengthening of India's Maritime and National Security.

***

2335089.title: PM to visit Karnataka and Gujarat on 13-14 November
2335089.body_html:
Prime Minister's Office
PM to visit Karnataka and Gujarat on 13-14 November
PM to inaugurate, dedicate to the nation, lay the foundation stone and flag off various development projects worth over ₹15,600 crore in Bengaluru
Projects span key sectors including urban mobility, power transmission, renewable energy, petroleum infrastructure, waste management and railways
PM to inaugurate Bengaluru Metro’s Pink Line from Kalena Agrahara to Tavarekere
PM to dedicate to the nation India's largest underground LPG storage cavern in Mangaluru
PM to inaugurate four redeveloped railway stations under the Amrit Bharat Station Scheme - Chamarajanagar, Chikkamagaluru, Sakleshpur and Subrahmanya Road
PM to flag off the Bengaluru-Mangaluru-Madgaon Vande Bharat Express
PM to participate in Golden Jubilee Celebrations of Prashanti Kutiram in Bengaluru
PM to inaugurate COSMOS-Mysuru Planetarium, India's first LED dome planetarium
PM to perform Darshan and Pooja at Ambaji temple in Banaskantha, Gujarat
Posted On: 11 NOV 2026 5:14PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister will visit Karnataka and Gujarat on 13-14 November. At around 10:45 AM, Prime Minister will participate in Golden Jubilee Celebrations of Prashanti Kutiram. He will also address the gathering on the occasion. At around 12:45 PM, Prime Minister will flag off and undertake a metro ride from Tavarekere to IIM Bangalore metro station. At around 1:15 PM, Prime Minister will lay the foundation stone, inaugurate and dedicate to the nation various development projects worth over Rs 15,600 crore in Bengaluru. He will also address the gathering on the occasion

Thereafter, Prime Minister will travel to Mysuru  where, at around 3:30 PM, he will participate in a tree plantation programme at Bharat Vann. At around 4, PM, Prime Minister will inaugurate COSMOS-Mysuru Planetarium. He will also address the gathering on the occasion.

On 14th November, Prime Minister will perform Darshan and Pooja at Ambaji temple in Banaskantha, Gujarat. Ambaji Temple is one of the 51 revered Shakti Peethas.

PM in Bengaluru

Prime Minister will participate in the Golden Jubilee Celebrations of Prashanti Kutiram, the residential headquarters campus of Swami Vivekananda Yoga Anusandhana Samsthana (S-VYASA). On this occasion, he will lay the foundation stone of the Golden Jubilee Administrative Block and launch the S-VYASA Off-Campus at Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala.

Being held from 13 to 23 November 2026 on the theme ‘Towards Viksit Bharat 2047’, the Golden Jubilee celebration marks five decades of institution-building and service. Established in 1975, Prashanti Kutiram was founded with the objective of integrating modern science with India's spiritual wisdom.  It is home to S-VYASA, which was declared a Deemed-to-be University in 2002 and is dedicated to education and research in Yoga.

The programme will also commemorate the birth centenary of Shri Hongasandra Venkataramaiah Sheshadri Ji, a distinguished thinker, writer and organiser born in Bengaluru in 1926. He joined the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh in 1946 and served as its Sarkaryavah from 1987 to 2000. He was among the visionaries behind S-VYASA and his inspiration and guidance played an important role in shaping the growth of Prashanti Kutiram and advancing the institution’s mission over the decades.

Prime Minister will inaugurate, dedicate to the nation, lay the foundation stone and flag off various development projects worth over ₹15,600 crore in Bengaluru. These projects span key sectors including urban mobility, power transmission, renewable energy, petroleum infrastructure, waste management and railways.

Prime Minister will inaugurate Bengaluru Metro’s Pink Line from Kalena Agrahara to Tavarekere, developed at a cost of around ₹3,470 crore. The new stretch will enhance urban connectivity, ease daily commuting, reduce travel time and strengthen public transport facilities in Bengaluru.

Prime Minister will also inaugurate the Transmission Scheme for Integration of Renewable Energy Zones (Phase-II) in Koppal-II and Gadag-II, developed at an investment of around ₹4,450 crore. The transmission system will facilitate the evacuation of approximately 2 GW of renewable energy potential from the Koppal and Gadag regions of Karnataka for onward transmission and distribution to beneficiaries across the grid. He will also inaugurate the Transmission Scheme for the Solar Energy Zone in Bidar, developed at an investment of around ₹1,370 crore. The project involves the establishment of a Bidar Pooling Station and will facilitate the evacuation of 2.5 GW of solar power from the region.

Prime Minister will lay the foundation stone of the Transmission Scheme for Integration of Davanagere/Chitradurga and Ballari Renewable Energy Zones, at an investment of over ₹3,450 crore. He will also lay the foundation stone of the Transmission System Strengthening project for Integration of Additional Renewable Energy Potential at Davanagere and Ballari, at an investment of over ₹1,100 crore.

Prime Minister will dedicate to the nation India's largest underground LPG storage cavern in Mangaluru, constructed at a cost of over ₹850 crore. With a storage capacity of 80,000 metric tonnes, the facility will significantly strengthen India's LPG storage infrastructure. The project also includes a 9.4 km LPG pipeline connecting New Mangalore Port to the main terminal, facilitating efficient transportation and storage of LPG. Prime Minister will also dedicate to the nation the Devangonthi Marketing Terminal of Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Limited (MRPL), Bengaluru. Built at an investment of ₹330 crore, the state-of-the-art facility will strengthen petroleum product storage and distribution infrastructure in Karnataka.

Prime Minister will lay the foundation stone of GAIL's Compressed Biogas Plant at Haralakunte, Bengaluru. The plant will process approximately 300 tonnes of municipal solid waste daily to produce 12.6 tonnes of clean Compressed Biogas (CBG). The project will promote scientific waste management, reduce dependence on conventional fuels and contribute to a cleaner and more sustainable environment.

Prime Minister will inaugurate four redeveloped railway stations under the Amrit Bharat Station Scheme - Chamarajanagar, Chikkamagaluru, Sakleshpur and Subrahmanya Road. The redeveloped stations will offer improved passenger amenities and serve as city centres, promoting local commercial activities and tourism in the region.

Prime Minister will dedicate to the nation the 45 km Bagalkot-Wandal railway line doubling section, forming part of the 284 km Gadag-Hotgi Doubling Project. The section will improve passenger and freight movement, support local trade and facilitate coal supply to the Kudgi NTPC plant.

Prime Minister will also dedicate to the nation the electrification of the 55 km Sakleshpur-Subrahmanya Road Ghat railway section. Passing through one of India's most challenging railway terrains, the project marks a significant engineering achievement. With its completion, the entire Bengaluru-Mangaluru rail route is now fully electrified.

Prime Minister will flag off the Bengaluru-Mangaluru-Madgaon Vande Bharat Express, providing faster and modern rail connectivity between Bengaluru, Coastal Karnataka and Goa. The service will connect key destinations including Hassan, Sakleshpur, Mangaluru, Udupi, Murdeshwar, Gokarna and Karwar before reaching Madgaon, benefiting passengers and boosting tourism in the region.

PM in Mysuru

Prime Minister will participate in a tree plantation programme at Bharat Vann, as part of the ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ initiative. Bharat Vann is an urban afforestation initiative aimed at developing dense, self-sustaining native forests using the Japanese Miyawaki technique. Spread across 17.63 acres, the Mysuru project aims to create a green community asset with over 2 lakh native trees. The project uses natural soil-enrichment materials such as cow dung, compost and Jeevamrut to support the growth of native shrubs, timber, canopy, flowering and fruit-bearing trees. The multi-layered forests will help enhance biodiversity, improve groundwater recharge, reduce dust and air pollution, moderate local temperatures, prevent soil erosion and support carbon sequestration.

Prime Minister will inaugurate the COSMOS-Mysuru Planetarium, marking a significant advancement in planetarium technology and astronomy education in the country. Built by the Indian Institute of Astrophysics (IIA), COSMOS-Mysuru is the first LED Dome planetarium in India. Envisaged as an astronomy education and training centre, it is located on the campus of the University of Mysore at the foothills of Chamundi Hills.

The state-of-the-art facility features a 15-metre tilted dome comprising around 6,150 panels with 4.2 crore individual LEDs. Unlike conventional planetariums that use projectors to display images on a passive dome, its LED panels can be controlled in real time, offering an immersive visual experience and new possibilities for astronomy education.

The Sky Theatre will showcase professionally produced astronomy programmes, along with an in-house film exploring the connection between the history of Mysuru and astronomy. The shows will be available in Kannada, English and Hindi. The centre will also house exhibition halls, a museum featuring astronomy models and artefacts, a lecture hall, a training centre and interactive outdoor exhibits.

The centre's activities will complement the Indian Institute of Astrophysics' research, operation of multi-wavelength telescope facilities across India and in space, development of future astronomical facilities and national-level outreach programmes.

2335080.title: India Strengthens Regional Health Partnerships as First BIMSTEC Health Ministers’ Meeting Unanimously Adopts Joint Ministerial Statement in Colombo
2335080.ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
2335080.body_html:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
India Strengthens Regional Health Partnerships as First BIMSTEC Health Ministers’ Meeting Unanimously Adopts Joint Ministerial Statement in Colombo
Union Health Minister Shri J.P. Nadda Leads India’s Engagement at Historic Meeting; BIMSTEC Countries Adopt Revised Plan of Action on Public Health (2026–2030)
India and Sri Lanka Deepen Healthcare Partnership; MoU Exchanged for 100 Additional Ambulances under Indian Grant Assistance of Approximately USD 5.28 Million
Shri Nadda Announces Indian Support for 50 Medical Kiosks/Health ATMs to Strengthen Primary Healthcare Services in Sri Lanka
India to Host BIMSTEC Centre of Excellence in Traditional Medicine at ITRA, Jamnagar, Gujarat
Union Health Minister Holds Bilateral Meetings with Health Ministers of Sri Lanka and Nepal to Strengthen Healthcare Cooperation
Shri Nadda Highlights India’s Healthcare Transformation and Offers to Share Expertise in Primary Healthcare, Digital Health and Public Health Infrastructure with BIMSTEC Countries
Union Health Minister Interacts with Indian Diaspora in Colombo; Highlights India’s Growing Global Leadership and Strong India–Sri Lanka Partnership
“No Country Should Be Left Behind in Its Pursuit of Better Health Outcomes”: Shri J.P. Nadda
Posted On: 11 NOV 2026 5:05PM by PIB Delhi

In a major step towards strengthening regional health cooperation, the First BIMSTEC Health Ministers’ Meeting held in Colombo, Sri Lanka, today unanimously adopted a Joint Ministerial Statement, reaffirming the collective commitment of member countries to advancing accessible, affordable and quality healthcare, strengthening regional health security and building resilient public health systems across the Bay of Bengal region.

Union Minister of Health and Family Welfare and Minister of Chemicals and Fertilizers, Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda, represented India at the historic meeting, highlighting the country's growing role in advancing regional health cooperation through knowledge-sharing, digital innovation, capacity building and collaborative action on common public health challenges.

The meeting also adopted the Revised BIMSTEC Plan of Action on Public Health (2026–2030), providing a structured roadmap for cooperation in disease surveillance, pandemic preparedness, digital health, traditional medicine, One Health and healthcare workforce development.

India's engagement at the meeting was further marked by significant bilateral initiatives with Sri Lanka, including the exchange of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) for the supply of 100 additional fully-equipped ambulances and the announcement of support for 50 Medical Kiosks/Health ATMs to strengthen primary healthcare services. Shri Nadda also held bilateral discussions with Nepal's Health Minister and interacted with the Indian diaspora in Colombo, reaffirming India's commitment to strengthening its longstanding partnerships in the region.

BIMSTEC Health Ministers Unanimously Adopt Joint Ministerial Statement

Addressing the inaugural meeting, Shri Nadda described the occasion as a landmark in regional cooperation, following the decision taken at the Sixth BIMSTEC Summit in Bangkok in April 2025 to establish a dedicated mechanism for cooperation among Health Ministers of member countries.

He emphasised that BIMSTEC countries share both a collective responsibility and a significant opportunity to strengthen healthcare systems, improve access to quality health services and enhance preparedness against emerging health challenges.

The unanimously adopted Joint Ministerial Statement underscores the commitment of member countries to Universal Health Coverage and Sustainable Development Goal 3, while identifying key priorities for coordinated regional action.

The Statement provides a forward-looking framework for strengthening disease surveillance, emergency preparedness, early warning systems, antimicrobial resistance management, digital healthcare, traditional medicine, climate-related health responses and capacity building.

It also envisages exploring a BIMSTEC Digital Health Framework to promote telemedicine, interoperable electronic health records and the use of Artificial Intelligence in diagnostics and disease modelling.

The meeting welcomed regional initiatives, including the proposed BIMSTEC Regional Centre of Excellence for Public Health in Sri Lanka, the establishment of the BIMSTEC Centre of Excellence on Tropical Medicine in Thailand, and India's initiative to establish a Centre of Excellence in Traditional Medicine.

The Joint Ministerial Statement also welcomed Bangladesh's proposal for a Regional Zoonotic Disease Observatory and Early Warning System and underscored the importance of strengthening coordinated preparedness against cross-border health threats.

India Offers to Share Its Healthcare Expertise with BIMSTEC Countries

Highlighting India's progress towards Universal Health Coverage under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, Shri Nadda outlined the country's comprehensive approach to healthcare, combining expanded primary healthcare services, financial protection, modern public health infrastructure and digital innovation.

He informed the gathering that India has established over 1.85 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs, bringing comprehensive primary healthcare services closer to communities and improving access to preventive, promotive and essential healthcare.

The Minister also highlighted Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY), one of the world's largest publicly funded health assurance schemes, providing annual cashless hospitalisation coverage of up to ₹5 lakh per eligible family and covering over 60 crore people.

Referring to the Pradhan Mantri Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission (PM-ABHIM), he underscored India's investments in strengthening public health infrastructure, disease surveillance, diagnostic capabilities and preparedness for future health emergencies.

Shri Nadda also highlighted the transformative role of technology in expanding healthcare access, noting that India's National Telemedicine Service, eSanjeevani, has crossed 50 crore teleconsultations.

He outlined India's experience under the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM) in building an interoperable digital health ecosystem to improve healthcare accessibility, efficiency and continuity of care.

Reaffirming India's commitment to regional cooperation, Shri Nadda offered to share the country's experience, technical expertise and best practices with BIMSTEC Member States, particularly in primary healthcare, digital health systems and public health infrastructure.

India to Host BIMSTEC Centre of Excellence in Traditional Medicine at Jamnagar

In a significant initiative to deepen regional cooperation in traditional medicine, Shri Nadda announced India's commitment to hosting the BIMSTEC Centre of Excellence in Traditional Medicine at the Institute of Teaching and Research in Ayurveda (ITRA), Jamnagar, Gujarat.

The Centre is envisaged as a regional platform for collaborative research, academic exchanges, institutional partnerships, capacity building and the sharing of traditional medicine knowledge and best practices.

It will also promote evidence-informed approaches, quality and safety standards, and the responsible preservation of traditional knowledge.

The Joint Ministerial Statement welcomed India's initiative, recognising its potential to strengthen regional cooperation in traditional medicine.

India's proposal to host the next meeting of the BIMSTEC Task Force on Traditional Medicine was also welcomed.

Underscoring the importance of collective preparedness, Shri Nadda called for greater regional cooperation under the One Health approach. He highlighted that the approach aligns with Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's vision of “One Earth, One Family, One Future”, rooted in India's ancient philosophy of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam representing India's long-held integrated approach to global health, sustainability and collaborative governance.

The Minister emphasised that that One Health is a shared responsibility and early detection, timely information-sharing and coordinated action are essential to preventing disease outbreaks and safeguarding public health.

India and Sri Lanka Deepen Healthcare Partnership; MoU Exchanged for 100 Additional Ambulances

On the sidelines of the BIMSTEC meeting, Shri J.P. Nadda held a high-level bilateral meeting with Sri Lanka's Minister of Health and Mass Media, Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa, to review ongoing health initiatives and explore opportunities for further strengthening cooperation between the two countries.

In a significant outcome of the meeting, the two Ministers witnessed the exchange of an MoU for the supply of 100 additional fully-equipped ambulances to Sri Lanka's 1990 Suwa Seriya Emergency Ambulance Service.

The initiative will be supported through Indian grant assistance of SLR 1,725.73 million (approximately USD 5.28 million) and is expected to further strengthen emergency medical response capabilities, improve operational efficiency and facilitate timely access to emergency healthcare services across Sri Lanka.

India has been a longstanding development partner in the establishment and expansion of the Suwa Seriya service, having earlier extended grant assistance of USD 7.5 million in 2016 and USD 15.02 million in 2018.

These initiatives supported the deployment of 297 ambulances, which have played a vital role in providing emergency medical assistance, including during the COVID-19 pandemic and natural disasters.

The additional 100 ambulances will further build upon this successful partnership and strengthen Sri Lanka's emergency healthcare network.

India Announces Support for 50 Medical Kiosks/Health ATMs in Sri Lanka

Further strengthening bilateral healthcare cooperation, Shri Nadda announced India's support for the procurement of 50 Medical Kiosks/Health ATMs to enhance primary healthcare delivery in Sri Lanka.

The initiative, involving Indian grant assistance of up to SLR 225 million, forms part of the USD 450 million comprehensive rehabilitation package announced by the Government of India following Cyclone Ditwah, which affected Sri Lanka during November–December 2025.

The Medical Kiosks will be deployed at Sri Lanka's Arogya Primary Health Centres to provide point-of-care diagnostic services integrated with telemedicine facilities.

The initiative is expected to improve access to essential diagnostic services, enable timely medical consultations and strengthen technology-enabled primary healthcare delivery, particularly for communities requiring accessible and efficient healthcare services.

These initiatives reflect India's continued commitment to supporting Sri Lanka's health system and advancing a development partnership focused on delivering tangible benefits to people.

Shri Nadda Meets Nepal's Health Minister; Discusses Stronger Bilateral and Regional Health Cooperation

Shri Nadda also held a bilateral meeting with Nepal's Minister for Health and Food Safety, Ms. Neesha Mehta, on the sidelines of the First BIMSTEC Health Ministers’ Meeting.

The two Ministers held fruitful discussions on deepening bilateral and regional health cooperation, sharing expertise and best practices, and improving access to affordable, accessible and quality healthcare.

The meeting reaffirmed the deep-rooted historical, cultural and people-to-people ties between India and Nepal, which continue to provide a strong foundation for cooperation in healthcare and development.

Guided by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's Neighbourhood First policy, India reiterated its commitment to working closely with Nepal to strengthen healthcare partnerships, promote improved health outcomes and advance shared regional prosperity.

Union Health Minister Interacts with Indian Diaspora in Colombo

During his visit, Shri Nadda also interacted with members of the Indian diaspora in Colombo, acknowledging their invaluable contribution to strengthening the longstanding friendship and people-to-people ties between India and Sri Lanka.

Addressing the gathering, the Union Health Minister highlighted India's remarkable progress over the past 12 years under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, particularly in healthcare, digital innovation, pharmaceuticals, medical research and technological advancement.

He emphasised that India's expanding capabilities offer significant opportunities for strengthening cooperation with Sri Lanka in healthcare, education, digital transformation and economic development.

Shri Nadda highlighted that India's Neighbourhood First and MAHASAGAR policies have further strengthened its enduring partnership with Sri Lanka, reflecting the shared commitment of both countries to regional stability, development and prosperity.

He appreciated the important role played by the Indian diaspora in fostering mutual understanding, enhancing cultural connections and serving as a bridge between the two nations.

A New Chapter in Regional Health Cooperation

The First BIMSTEC Health Ministers’ Meeting brought together Health Ministers and senior representatives from Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Thailand.

The meeting was chaired by Sri Lanka's Minister of Health and Mass Media, Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa.

The unanimously adopted Joint Ministerial Statement reaffirmed the decision to convene BIMSTEC Health Ministers’ Meetings and Senior Officials’ Meetings every two years, ensuring sustained engagement and follow-up on agreed regional priorities. Thailand's offer to host the Second BIMSTEC Health Ministers’ Meeting in 2028 was also welcomed.

Concluding his address, Shri Nadda expressed appreciation to the Government of Sri Lanka for hosting the historic meeting and reaffirmed India's commitment to building a healthier, safer and more resilient BIMSTEC region.

He emphasised that “No country should be left behind in its pursuit of better health outcomes.”

The unanimous adoption of the Joint Ministerial Statement, the advancement of a common regional public health roadmap, India's commitment to hosting the Centre of Excellence in Traditional Medicine, and the significant bilateral healthcare initiatives with Sri Lanka and Nepal mark an important step towards strengthening regional health security and deepening India's healthcare partnerships.

Together, these engagements reinforce India's commitment to translating regional cooperation into meaningful outcomes for people, guided by the vision of inclusive development, shared prosperity and “One Earth, One Family, One Future.”

*****

 

SR

2335052.title: NHAI Debars Bijwasan User Fee Collection Agency for One Month following Misbehaviour with Road User
2335052.body_html:
Ministry of Road Transport & Highways
NHAI Debars Bijwasan User Fee Collection Agency for One Month following Misbehaviour with Road User
NHAI has also issued a Show Cause Notice proposing debarment of the Agency and Owners/ Directors, for a period of one year from participation in future tenders of NHAI
Posted On: 11 NOV 2026 4:33PM by PIB Delhi

Taking strict action against the User Fee Collection Agency, National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has debarred M/s Riddhi Siddhi Associates from participating in any ongoing or future tenders issued by NHAI for a period of one month and imposed a penalty of Rs.15 lakhs on agency, following misbehaviour by its personnel with road users at Bijwasan Fee Plaza on NH-248BB on 05th November 2026.

Considering the gravity of the incidence, NHAI has also issued a Show Cause Notice proposing debarment of the Agency and Owners/ Directors, for a period of one year from participation in future tenders of NHAI. The agency has also been directed to hand over the fee plaza to the new agency on 14.11.2026.

As per the Contract Agreement, the User Fee Collection Agency is responsible for ensuring proper conduct, discipline and behaviour of its personnel deployed at the fee plaza. The incident reflects a gross failure on the part of the agency to ensure discipline, proper supervision and adherence to contractual obligations.

NHAI reiterates its commitment to ensuring safe, secure commuting experience for all National Highway users and maintains a zero-tolerance approach towards any form of misconduct or indiscipline at toll plazas.

2335021.title: Special Campaign 6.0 Concludes with Significant Achievements in Institutionalizing Swachhata and Reducing Pendency in DDWS
2335021.body_html:
Ministry of Jal Shakti
Special Campaign 6.0 Concludes with Significant Achievements in Institutionalizing Swachhata and Reducing Pendency in DDWS
Posted On: 11 NOV 2026 4:09PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti,successfully concluded Special Campaign 6.0 for Institutionalizing Swachhata and Minimizing Pendency in Government Offices, conducted from 2nd October to 31st October, 2026. The campaign focused on promoting cleanliness, improving workplace management, strengthening record management and ensuring the timely disposal of pending matters.

As part of the preparatory activities preceding the campaign, a Swachhata Pledge and Swachhata Quiz were organised on 30th September 2026, followed by a Shramdaan activity at Kalindi Kunj on 1st October 2026, led by Hon’ble Minister of Jal Shakti.

During the implementation phase, a felicitation ceremony titled 'Safai Mitra Samman', along with a health camp for sanitation workers, was organised on 8th October, 2026 to recognise their invaluable contribution and promote their well-being. Further, an in- house painting competition on the theme of Swachhata was organised on 15th October, 2026 to promote awareness and encourage active participation among officials and staff.

Continuing its efforts towards maintaining a clean and hygienic workplace, officials and staff of the Department participated in a cleanliness drive on 28th October 2026 at the Sanitation Park, CGO Complex. The activity involved Shramdaan, including sweeping pathways, collecting litter and clearing accumulated waste from the premises, reflecting the spirit of collective responsibility towards cleanliness.

Significant achievements were recorded in the disposal of pending matters and record management. During the campaign, the Department disposed of 576 Public Grievances and all 29 Public Grievance Appeals, 25 references from Members of Parliament, 3 Parliamentary Assurances and 2 PMO references. Further, 100 e-files were reviewed and closed, contributing to the streamlining of official records and improving administrative efficiency.

The Department also leveraged digital and social media platforms to enhance the outreach and visibility of the campaign. Through these concerted efforts, DDWS reaffirmed its commitment to institutionalising Swachhata as a sustained practice, promoting the dignity and well-being of sanitation workers, improving the working environment and strengthening administrative efficiency through the timely disposal of pending matters.

2335019.title: DGFT prohibits export of Lithium-Ion Battery Black Mass to strengthen domestic recycling and critical mineral recovery
2335019.body_html:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
DGFT prohibits export of Lithium-Ion Battery Black Mass to strengthen domestic recycling and critical mineral recovery
The measure aims to ensure domestic availability of critical minerals, strengthen battery recycling capacity and reduce import dependence
Measure to complement Government’s ₹1,500 crore Incentive Scheme for Critical Mineral Recycling
Posted On: 11 NOV 2026 4:07PM by PIB Delhi

The Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT), Department of Commerce, has prohibited the export of Lithium-Ion Battery Black Mass falling under ITC(HS) Code 85491400. Vide Notification No. 49/2026-27 dated 10 November 2026, the export policy of the item has been amended from ‘Free’ to ‘Prohibited’ with immediate effect and until further orders. The transitional arrangements under Para 1.05 of the Foreign Trade Policy (FTP), 2023, will apply.

ITC(HS) Code 85491400 covers waste and scrap of primary cells, primary batteries and electric accumulators, as well as spent cells, batteries and accumulators, which are unsorted and do not contain lead, cadmium or mercury. The Notification specifically describes the item as Lithium-Ion Battery Black Mass. Black Mass is the powdery material obtained from shredding end-of-life lithium-ion batteries and battery manufacturing waste. It contains recoverable quantities of critical minerals, including lithium, cobalt, nickel and manganese.

Critical minerals are essential inputs for electric mobility, advanced chemistry cell batteries, energy storage, electronics and renewable energy. India depends substantially on imports for several of these minerals. Recycling battery waste is among the quickest and most sustainable ways of developing a domestic supply of these resources. While the country's capacity to recycle battery waste and refine critical minerals from it has grown considerably, it is not being fully utilised due to inadequate feedstock availability. Exports of Black Mass generated in India divert this valuable secondary resource abroad, while domestic recyclers have, in some cases, had to import material to meet their requirements.

The export prohibition is intended to ensure that Black Mass generated in India is recycled and refined within the country. The measure is expected to assure feedstock availability for domestic recycling and refining units, improve their capacity utilisation and encourage further investment and employment in the sector. It will increase domestic recovery of lithium, cobalt, nickel and other critical minerals, thereby reducing import dependence and the associated foreign exchange outgo. It will also strengthen supply chains for battery manufacturing, electric vehicles, energy storage and clean-energy technologies, in line with the vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat. Further, the measure will advance the circular economy and ‘urban mining’, reducing reliance on primary mining, while supporting environmentally sound recycling of this hazardous material within the country in accordance with applicable environmental regulations.

The measure complements the Government's initiatives under the National Critical Mineral Mission (NCMM), including the ₹1,500 crore Incentive Scheme approved by the Union Cabinet in September 2025 to develop recycling capacity for the separation and production of critical minerals from secondary sources such as battery waste and e-waste. Retaining Black Mass within the country will help ensure that the recycling capacity being developed under the Scheme has access to adequate domestic feedstock.

The step is also in keeping with measures adopted by several major economies to retain critical mineral-bearing battery waste and Black Mass for domestic processing.

The Notification is available on the DGFT website, www.dgft.gov.in.

2335012.title: Vice President graces the 105th Foundation Day celebrations of Tamilnad Mercantile Bank (TMB) in Thoothukudi
2335012.body_html:
Vice President's Secretariat
Vice President graces the 105th Foundation Day celebrations of Tamilnad Mercantile Bank (TMB) in Thoothukudi
TMB’s 105-year journey is a testament to its commitment to trust, service and financial inclusion
Banks must support MSMEs, farmers, entrepreneurs and women-led enterprises to realise Viksit Bharat @2047
Posted On: 11 NOV 2026 4:03PM by PIB Delhi

Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today graced the 105th Foundation Day celebrations of Tamilnad Mercantile Bank (TMB) in Thoothukudi, and called upon the bank to aspire to become one of India’s leading private sector banks in the coming years.

Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan graced the 105th Foundation Day celebrations of Tamilnad Mercantile Bank in Thoothukudi today. Congratulating the bank on its remarkable 105-year journey, he highlighted its contribution to India’s economic growth and called upon banks to strengthen financial inclusion, support entrepreneurs, MSMEs, farmers and women-led enterprises, and contribute to the vision of Viksit Bharat @ 2047. Governor of Tamil Nadu Shri Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar, TMB Part Time Chairman Shri K. Ramachandran, MD & CEO Shri Salee S. Nair, Executive Director Shri Vincent Menachery, members of the Board and senior officials were present on the occasion.

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) November 11, 2026

Congratulating the bank on its remarkable 105-year journey, the Vice President recalled its origins in 1921 as Nadar Bank Limited and commended its contribution to the country’s banking sector.He said that, from its humble beginnings, the bank has grown into a major banking institution with 632 branches across 17 States and four Union Territories, serving over 53 lakh customers and recording total business exceeding ₹1.30 lakh crore.

Highlighting the vital role of banks in nation-building, he emphasised the importance of responsible lending and extending financial support to MSMEs, farmers, small traders, entrepreneurs, women-led enterprises and corporates.

The Vice President noted India’s remarkable economic progress and said that the banking sector has a crucial role in realising the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047. He highlighted the transformation brought about by digital banking and UPI, as well as the expansion of financial inclusion, which has enabled more people to access formal banking services.

Commending TMB’s recent performance and technological progress, he urged the bank to continue strengthening cybersecurity, safeguarding customers’ money and personal data, and embracing innovation. He also stressed that the bank should remain rooted in Thoothukudi, its place of origin, even as it expands its national presence.

The Vice President expressed confidence that Tamilnad Mercantile Bank would continue to scale greater heights and establish itself among India’s leading private sector banks.

Tamil Nadu Governor Shri Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar, TMB Part Time Chairman Shri K. Ramachandran, Managing Director and CEO Shri Salee S. Nair, Executive Director Shri

Vincent Menachery, members of the Board and senior officials were present on the occasion.

2335003.title: Vice-President attends Platinum Jubilee celebrations of his alma mater, V.O. Chidambaram College, Thoothukudi
2335003.body_html:
Vice President's Secretariat
Vice-President attends Platinum Jubilee celebrations of his alma mater, V.O. Chidambaram College, Thoothukudi
Vice-President recalls his college days, including participation in the movement against the Emergency and efforts to support the families of those imprisoned
“Students must embrace technology, acquire knowledge and stay away from drugs and harmful habits”: Vice-President
Posted On: 11 NOV 2026 3:54PM by PIB Delhi

Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today attended the Platinum Jubilee celebrations and Alumni Meet of V.O. Chidambaram College, Thoothukudi, as the Chief Guest. The college is his alma mater, where he studied from 1975 to 1978.

Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan graced the Platinum Jubilee celebrations and Alumni Meet of V.O. Chidambaram College, Thoothukudi, today. It was a special occasion for him to return to his alma mater and reconnect with an institution that holds a cherished place in his life.

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) November 11, 2026

He paid floral tributes to the statue of freedom fighter V.O. Chidambaram Pillai on the college campus and inaugurated a commemorative arch marking the institution’s 75th anniversary. He also visited his former classroom and interacted with his classmates from the 1975–78 batch, fondly recalling his college days.

At V.O. Chidambaram College, Thoothukudi, Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan paid floral tributes to freedom fighter Shri V.O. Chidambaram Pillai. https://t.co/FvcGp05N84

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) November 11, 2026

Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan attended the 1975–78 batch Alumni Meet at his alma mater, V.O. Chidambaram College, Thoothukudi. He revisited his old classroom, interacted warmly with his classmates and fondly relived cherished memories of their college days. https://t.co/NRaxStEALq

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) November 11, 2026

Addressing the gathering, the Vice-President recalled how the college, its teachers and the personalities he encountered there shaped his outlook and prepared him for greater responsibilities. He fondly remembered his teachers’ lessons, campus life and the values he imbibed during his student years.

Recalling the Emergency, he spoke about his participation in the movement against it while studying at the college. He also recalled mobilising funds to support the families of those who had been imprisoned during the period.

Paying tribute to V.O. Chidambaram Pillai, he highlighted the freedom fighter’s immense sacrifices, his commitment to workers’ welfare and his enduring contribution to the freedom struggle.

Emphasising national unity, the Vice-President said India’s strength as a united nation safeguards the language, culture and identity of its diverse communities, including Tamil culture. He urged students to strengthen national consciousness while taking pride in their mother tongue. He also encouraged them to learn multiple languages and take Tamil to the global stage.

Highlighting the importance of education in nation-building, he referred to the expansion of higher education institutions across the country and called upon the college to preserve its legacy while embracing new technologies, scientific research and emerging disciplines to make quality education accessible to all sections of society.

He urged young people to develop self-discipline, stay away from drugs and other harmful habits, and contribute to the vision of a developed India by 2047.

The Vice-President expressed happiness at witnessing the growth of his alma mater and said the Platinum Jubilee should mark a new beginning towards greater achievements.

Tamil Nadu Governor Shri Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar, College Secretary Shri A.P.C.V. Chockalingam, Principal Dr. C. Veerabagu, Alumni Association President Shri A.V. Murugesan, college administrators, faculty members, alumni and students were present.

2334998.title: Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN) dismantles clan lab (clandestine laboratory) of mephedrone (md) in Mau, Uttar Pradesh; Seizes 11.7 kg mephedrone, precursor chemicals and laboratory equipment; arrests two suspects under Operation Vajra 3.0
2334998.body_html:
Ministry of Finance
Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN) dismantles clan lab (clandestine laboratory) of mephedrone (md) in Mau, Uttar Pradesh; Seizes 11.7 kg mephedrone, precursor chemicals and laboratory equipment; arrests two suspects under Operation Vajra 3.0
Posted On: 11 NOV 2026 3:51PM by PIB Delhi

The Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN) conducted a significant operation against an interstate drug synthetic network and busted a clandestine laboratory manufacturing Mephedrone (MD) in the Tajopur Industrial Area, Mau, Uttar Pradesh under its Operation Vajra 3.0.

Acting on specific intelligence developed by the CBN MP Unit, a joint team of CBN MP Unit and CBN UP Unit conducted a coordinated operation on 08.11.2026 and successfully identified and busted an active clandestine synthetic drug manufacturing facility.

The operation led to the recovery of 11.7 kg mephedrone (MD) at different stages of processing. The team also seized 20.9 kg 2-bromo-4-methylpropiophenone, a key precursor used in the manufacture of Mephedrone, along with 3.5 kg acetic anhydride and approximately 119.9 kg/L of various chemicals, solvents and processing reagents, including dichloromethane, hydrochloric acid, sodium bicarbonate, sodium chloride and organic amines.

 

 

 

Mephedrone seized at different stages of production

The operation further resulted in the seizure and dismantling of the complete clandestine laboratory infrastructure, comprising industrial grinders and mixers, steel tanks and vessels, heating equipment, glass reaction and distillation apparatus, temperature-measuring devices, voltage balancers and other equipment used for illicit manufacture of synthetic drugs, besides personal protective equipment.

Dismantling of clandestine manufacturing laboratory

During the course of the operation, two persons involved in the illicit manufacturing network were arrested under NDPS Act 1985. Further investigation is underway to ascertain the wider interstate network, source of precursor chemicals, financial linkages and intended distribution channels.

The entire seizure and further proceedings were conducted in accordance with the provisions of the NDPS Act, 1985, following prescribed legal procedures.

The dismantling of the clandestine laboratory has prevented the further manufacture and distribution of a significant quantity of illicit Mephedrone and dealt a major blow to an interstate synthetic drug network.

During 2026, the CBN has busted six clandestine labs till date with seizure of 130.2 kg mephedrone (MD) and 1465.4 Kg/L precursor chemicals. Arrest of 20 suspects have been made in connection to these cases.

The operation reflects the continued vigilance, dedication and commitment of the Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN) towards combating illicit drug trafficking and clandestine manufacturing of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances.

CBN remains steadfast in its efforts to dismantle clandestine drug manufacturing networks, prevent the diversion of precursor chemicals, identify and disrupt interstate trafficking syndicates, enforce the provisions of the NDPS Act, 1985, and contribute towards the national mission of a Nasha Mukt Bharat, Viksit Bharat.

2334980.title: Bureau of Energy Efficiency Organises Webinar and Undertakes Various Awareness Activities During BRICS Sustainable Lifestyle Week 2026
2334980.body_html:
Ministry of Power
Bureau of Energy Efficiency Organises Webinar and Undertakes Various Awareness Activities During BRICS Sustainable Lifestyle Week 2026
Posted On: 11 NOV 2026 3:21PM by PIB Delhi

As part of the observance of BRICS Sustainable Lifestyle Week (BSLW), observed from 1 to 7 November 2026, the Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE), Ministry of Power, organised a webinar on the theme “Energy Conservation” on 2 November 2026. The webinar aimed to highlight the pivotal role of energy efficiency in promoting sustainable lifestyles, reducing energy consumption, enhancing energy security and advancing India's commitment towards sustainable development.

The webinar commenced with the inaugural address by Shri Krushna Chandra Panigrahy, Director General, BEE, who highlighted the significance of energy efficiency as a key enabler of sustainable development and emphasised the need for concerted efforts towards promoting energy-efficient practices across various sectors.

The technical sessions were delivered by eminent experts and representatives from reputed institutions and organisations, including TERI, AEEE, IIT, CLASP and SEforALL, covering a wide range of topics relating to energy efficiency. The deliberations encompassed India's progress and initiatives in the field of energy efficiency, measures for enhancing energy efficiency in industries, and the role of technological interventions in reducing energy consumption. The sessions also provided an overview of India's Standards and Labelling Programme for appliances, highlighting its contribution towards promoting energy-efficient products and enabling informed consumer choices.

Further, the discussions focused on market trends and the impact of behavioural changes on electricity consumption, emphasising the importance of sustainable consumption practices and responsible energy use. The role of Demand Side Management (DSM) in transforming energy efficiency into a flexible grid resource was also deliberated upon, particularly in the context of optimising electricity consumption, enhancing grid flexibility and supporting the integration of renewable energy into the power system.

The webinar witnessed participation from representatives of the Ministry of Power, Central Public Sector Undertakings (CPSUs), manufacturers' associations, industry representatives, domain experts and other relevant stakeholders. The participation of stakeholders from diverse sectors facilitated the exchange of knowledge, experiences and perspectives on various aspects of energy efficiency and the adoption of sustainable practices.

As part of the BRICS Sustainable Lifestyle Week observance, BEE also undertook several awareness initiatives to encourage energy conservation and responsible electricity consumption. These included the Energy Conservation Pledge taken by Shri Krushna Chandra Panigrahy, Director General, BEE, along with BEE officers and employees on 2 November 2026 at the BEE office, New Delhi. Banners and standees carrying messages on energy conservation were also displayed at the BEE office to sensitise employees about the importance of adopting energy-efficient practices.

Furthermore, a Switch-Off Hour was observed from 10:00 AM to 11:00 AM on 2 November 2026, during which employees were encouraged to switch off lights and other non-essential electrical equipment when not in use.

Additionally, BEE conducted a 7 day social media campaign on the theme “Save Energy” under the hashtag #BRICSforLiFE, aimed at disseminating messages on energy-efficient practices and encouraging citizens to adopt sustainable lifestyle choices. The campaign emphasises the importance of individual actions and collective participation in promoting energy conservation and sustainable consumption.

Through these initiatives, BEE reaffirmed its commitment towards promoting energy-conscious behaviour, sustainable consumption and mainstreaming energy efficiency as an integral component of India's sustainable lifestyle initiatives, contributing towards a more energy-efficient and sustainable future.

About BEE

The Government of India set up the Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) on1st March, 2002 under the provisions of the Energy Conservation Act, 2001. The mission of the Bureau of Energy Efficiency is to assist in developing policies and strategies with a thrust on self-regulation and market principles.

A key objective is reducing the energy intensity of the Indian economy. BEE coordinates with designated consumers, designated agencies and other organizations. It recognises, identifies and utilises the existing resources and infrastructure, in performing the functions assigned to it under the Act. The Act also provides for regulatory and promotional functions.

2334979.title: Cabinet approves Continuation of Stand-Up India Scheme
2334979.body_html:
Ministry of Finance
Cabinet approves Continuation of Stand-Up India Scheme
To promote entrepreneurship among Women, Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes
Targets to cover minimum 2.5 lakh beneficiaries
Approval for Credit Guarantee Corpus of Rs.4,111 crore
Posted On: 11 NOV 2026 3:18PM by PIB Delhi

The Union Cabinet, chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, has approved thecontinuation of Stand-Up India Scheme for a period of 5 years upto 31.03.2031. The scheme aims to promote entrepreneurship among Women, Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs) and aims to provide financial assistance to additional 2.5 lakh entrepreneurs in a span of five years. Since its launch in April 2016, the scheme has facilitated loans to more than 2.75 lakh Women/SC/ST entrepreneurs.

Salient features of the scheme:

  • Eligible borrowers: Women, SC and ST entrepreneurs for setting up new/green field enterprises
  • Quantum of Support: The loan can be in the form of either Composite (Working Capital and Term Loan) or Term loan for amounts above Rs.10.00 lakh and upto Rs.1.00 crore (upto 85% of the project cost).
  • Eligible Sectors: Manufacturing, Services, Trading and Agri allied activities.
  • Credit Guarantee coverage: 85% of the loan amount
  • Guarantee Fee: Standard guarantee fee of 0.50 %

Impact:

  • Credit access for women, SC and ST entrepreneurs, enabling enterprise creation and strengthening entrepreneurship across underserved communities, thereby supporting inclusive economic growth.

2334977.title: Cabinet approves continuation of Credit Guarantee Fund for Micro Units
2334977.body_html:
Ministry of Finance
Cabinet approves continuation of Credit Guarantee Fund for Micro Units
Provides credit guarantee for loans extended under Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana
Approval for corpus of Rs.5,000 crore facilitating PMMY loans amounting to Rs.12.6 lakh crore
Posted On: 11 NOV 2026 3:15PM by PIB Delhi

The Union Cabinet, chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, has approved thecontinuation of Credit Guarantee Fund for Micro Units (CGFMU) for a period of five years upto 31.03.2031. The scheme provides credit guarantee coverage to the Lending Institutions through National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company Limited (NCGTC) against default risk.

As on September 2026, more than 60.36 crore loans amounting to  Rs.43.34 lakhs crore have been sanctioned by lending institutions since launch of PM Mudra Scheme. CGFMU which was launched in January 2016 has acted as a major catalyst in enabling the growth of PMMY loans in the country.

Salient features of the Scheme:

  • The purpose of the fund is to provide guarantee to Lending Institutions (LIs) for the following credit facilities:
  • Loans extended to eligible micro enterprises under Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY) upto Rs.20 lakh;
  • Overdraft of upto Rs.10,000 provided by banks under Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) accounts; and
  • Loans granted to Self Help Group (SHG) where portfolio is between Rs.10 lakh to Rs.20 lakh.
  • Guarantee coverage: Linked to the disbursement amount in case of working capital limits and outstanding amount for term loan accounts to reflect the actual risk exposure of LIs.
  • Guarantee Fee: Decrease in guarantee fee from @1% p.a. to @ 0.75% p.a. No change for SHG; continue to pay guarantee fee of 0.25% for the first year and 0.50% in subsequent years.
  • Duration of the Scheme: The Scheme would be applicable to all loans extended under PMMY during the XVIth Finance Commission Cycle i.e. FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31.

Impact:

  • Collateral free loans under Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana has created a whole new generation of entrepreneurs who previously could not avail loans from formal banking system.
  • The extension of CGFMU scheme will enable loans of Rs.12.6 lakh crore over next 5 years
  • The scheme will act as a catalyst to young aspiring entrepreneurs to set up and grow their business.

2334874.title: Prime Minister shares a Sanskrit Subhashitam, highlighting the foundation of a progressive nation's strength and power
2334874.body_html:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister shares a Sanskrit Subhashitam, highlighting the foundation of a progressive nation's strength and power
Posted On: 11 NOV 2026 8:39AM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi shared a Sanskrit Subhashitam today, highlighting that the strength and power of a progressive nation are founded upon penance, religious observances, and the desire for the welfare of all.


The Prime Minister wrote on X;


"भद्रमिच्छन्त ऋषयः स्वर्विदस्तपो दीक्षामुपनिषेदुरग्रे।

ततो राष्ट्रं बलमोजश्च जातं तदस्मै देवा उपसन्नमन्तु॥"


The sages, who wished for the welfare of all and were knowledgeable about heaven, first devoted themselves to penance and religious observances. It was through this penance and these observances that the nation, strength, and power came into existence. All the gods pay homage to such a progressive nation and its strength.

2334873.title: Prime Minister extends greetings to the nation on the occasion of Bhai Dooj
2334873.body_html:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister extends greetings to the nation on the occasion of Bhai Dooj
Posted On: 11 NOV 2026 8:37AM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today extended his heartfelt greetings to the citizens across the country on the auspicious occasion of Bhai Dooj.

The Prime Minister stated that this sacred festival is a symbol of the affection, and deep-rooted warmth of the cherished bond between brothers and sisters. On this auspicious day, he offered his sincere wishes for the happiness, joy, and prosperity of everyone.


The Prime Minister shared on X:
