2334866.title: Bharat Mobility Expo gaining global recognition, third edition to be the second largest such expo in the world: Commerce and Industry Minister Shri Piyush Goyal
2334866.body_html:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
Bharat Mobility Expo gaining global recognition, third edition to be the second largest such expo in the world: Commerce and Industry Minister Shri Piyush Goyal
Shri Piyush Goyal urges mobility industry to tap global markets and expand India's manufacturing footprint
Shri Goyal calls for positioning India as the world's manufacturing hub through global partnerships and export-led growth
India well on track to achieve $1 trillion export target this year; engineering sector records 22 per cent growth: Shri Goyal
Posted On: 10 NOV 2026 9:48PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Commerce & Industry Shri Piyush Goyal today, speaking at the Curtain Raiser of the third edition of Bharat Mobility Global Expo in New Delhi, highlighted the growing stature of the event and the importance of the mobility sector to India's manufacturing and global economic ambitions.

He urged industry stakeholders across the mobility value chain to look beyond the domestic market and tap global markets and export opportunities. He said that complementing India's large domestic market with international markets would enable businesses to achieve economies of scale and become globally competitive in pricing. Expressing confidence in the capabilities of Indian manufacturers, he said that those supplying to Japanese and European automobile manufacturers, as well as the aerospace and defence sectors, had the potential to meet world-class quality standards.

Recalling the initial discussions on the concept of Bharat Mobility, Shri Goyal said that the initiative had brought together different segments of the mobility ecosystem, which had traditionally organised separate exhibitions at different times and locations, often attracting the same set of visitors. He said that bringing the entire ecosystem under one roof had been made possible by the availability of Bharat Mandapam and Yashobhoomi, developed with the vision of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi to make India an international exhibition destination.

The Minister said that Bharat Mobility had demonstrated the strength of a whole-of-Government approach by breaking silos between departments, ministries and States, while also bringing together different industries associated with the mobility sector. These include steel, chemicals, electronics, two-wheelers, three-wheelers, four-wheelers, commercial and passenger vehicles, construction equipment and tyres.

Congratulating industry stakeholders on the success of the second edition, Shri Goyal expressed confidence that the third edition would be even bigger and better, potentially emerging as the world's largest mobility exhibition in terms of both size and visitors, including domestic and international visitors. He said that, depending on the demand for exhibition space and the expansion of facilities, Bharat Mobility could potentially become the largest event of its kind globally.

The Minister urged the organisers and industry to market the event extensively across the world and aim to attract at least 25,000 international visitors out of the expected 10 lakh visitors. He emphasised that the event should go beyond original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) and reach the wider global ecosystem, including tyre dealers, suppliers, auto component manufacturers and the substantial after-sales market.

Shri Goyal said that every segment represented at Bharat Mobility offered significant opportunities for international engagement and sourcing from India. He urged industry stakeholders to identify opportunities across individual sectors and countries, and to look at the entire global value chain. He said that failing to think on a global scale would undermine the considerable effort invested in organising Bharat Mobility.

Shri Goyal said that the only possible bottleneck to India's progress was the mindset and not the country's capabilities. He emphasised the need for industry to recognise and realise India's potential.

Sharing his experience of interactions with international industry leaders during overseas delegations, the Minister said that the interest and enthusiasm for India had been extraordinary. Referring to his recent visit to Japan, he said that the response from Japanese industry had been particularly encouraging, with several companies expressing interest in partnering with Indian manufacturers to serve global markets. He noted that the interest extended beyond small investments, with companies considering billion-dollar investments in India to manufacture products for the world.

He said that European manufacturers, which had traditionally focused on international markets, were increasingly recognising the challenges of competing globally given Europe's manufacturing costs and regulatory burden. Referring to the Free Trade Agreement (FTA) negotiations, the Minister said that market access in India would initially allow European automobile manufacturers to test demand by introducing a limited number of models in the Indian market. Once they identify models with adequate demand, manufacturers could establish production in India, not only to serve the domestic market but also to export to the rest of the world.

Shri Goyal said that manufacturing in India would enable companies to benefit from economies of scale, access the large domestic market and produce vehicles at competitive prices for global markets. This would create significant opportunities for Indian component manufacturers, startups, steel and rubber industries, and other participants across the mobility ecosystem. He urged industry stakeholders to capture these opportunities before other countries did.

The Minister underlined that India's large domestic market was a major advantage in attracting global manufacturing investments. Referring to automobile sales during the festive season, he said that one million cars had been sold during Navratri alone, while around 70,000 cars were sold over the two days of Dhanteras. He said that the scale of the Indian market offered an ideal opportunity for global manufacturers to establish production facilities in India and use the country as a base for serving international markets.

Urging the industry to build on the success of the first two editions, Shri Goyal called for the third edition to be larger in scale, more efficient and more technologically advanced. He said that the first two days of the exhibition had been reserved for businesses, business launches and new product launches, providing an opportunity for companies to showcase their quality and capabilities to the world.

He highlighted that bringing the entire mobility value chain together at one location made the event particularly attractive to international visitors, who could engage with different segments of the industry in a single visit. Recalling his experience as an entrepreneur around 40 years ago, when he visited Hanover to engage with the entire engineering ecosystem, the Minister said that India was now creating similar large-format platforms through Bharat Mobility, Bharat Tex, Startup Mahakumbh and Bharat BuildCon.

He said that these platforms, which bring together entire value chains, enabled India to showcase its capabilities to the world. Referring also to the convergence of India's telecom and electronics industries towards large exhibitions, Shri Goyal said that India was offering the world a scale that it had not witnessed before. He said that the theme "Beyond Boundaries" reflected the spirit of Bharat and the future envisaged for Indian industry.

Shri Goyal reiterated that India's target of achieving $1 trillion in exports this year was sacrosanct and said that the country was well on track to achieve it. Referring to the September export figures, he said that India had already achieved approximately $480 billion, accounting for 48 per cent of the annual target in the first six months. He noted that exports generally picked up in the second half of the year and expressed confidence in the country's export performance.

The Minister said that the October export figures would be shared by the Commerce Secretary on the 15th and indicated that the numbers would be encouraging. He expressed confidence that there would be no looking back thereafter and called upon industry to move beyond incremental growth and aim for greater expansion.

Highlighting the contribution of the engineering sector to export growth, Shri Goyal said that the sector had recorded growth of around 22 per cent. He urged industry to sustain this growth and make it a benchmark for the future rather than treating it as a one-time achievement.

The Minister said that the European Union's 27-nation bloc was expected to open up for Indian businesses at zero duty by March or April, providing further opportunities for Indian exporters in the coming year. He added that India was also negotiating with another seven to eight countries, which would further expand market access. Once these opportunities materialise, India would have preferential access to markets accounting for nearly 75 per cent of global GDP.

Shri Goyal urged industry to act early to capture emerging international opportunities, noting that countries across the world were competing for global markets and investments. He said that the Government had endeavoured to address the aspirations of industry by expanding market access and extending support through various initiatives.

He highlighted the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for the auto component industry and the PLI Scheme for specialty steel. He also referred to the Export Promotion Mission and urged industry stakeholders to make full use of the initiative to strengthen exports, market their products and build their industry brands.

Emphasising the wider significance of the mobility sector, Shri Goyal said that mobility was not merely about economic figures, production numbers or the sector's contribution to the economy, but also about transforming lives and fulfilling aspirations. Referring to World Bank data indicating that 50 crore people had moved out of extreme poverty in India over a period of 12 years, he said that one of the first aspirations of people moving up the economic ladder was to upgrade their mobility and transport.

He said that this transformation was visible in the shift from bicycles to two-wheelers and from two-wheelers to entry-level four-wheelers. As families and individuals moved up the economic ladder, their self-respect, self-esteem and desire to contribute to nation-building also increased. He noted the growth of the new middle class, the rising number of first-time passenger vehicle buyers and the expansion of highways and roads across the country.

The Minister also highlighted the growing attractiveness and affordability of electric mobility and said that the mobility sector would be among the biggest beneficiaries of India's position as the fastest-growing large economy. He called upon the industry to build the entire mobility ecosystem in India and make the country the manufacturing hub of the world, covering vehicles, components and mobility technologies.

Shri Goyal said that India should also emerge as a centre for developing technologies and creating designs, with all talent-driven solutions being centred around the country. He expressed confidence that the potential for growth across the mobility sector was immense and said that India should soon aspire to sell 10 million passenger vehicles domestically, with exports being additional to domestic sales.

Referring to the two-wheeler sector, the Minister noted that annual sales were already around 25 million units, excluding exports. He said that the potential across all segments of the mobility ecosystem was substantial and invited industry stakeholders to be part of India's growth journey by thinking big, planning ambitiously, pursuing collaborations, bringing in new technologies and supporting startups to introduce newer elements into their businesses.

The Minister also indicated that the growing demand for Bharat Mobility could require further expansion of exhibition infrastructure at Bharat Mandapam and Yashobhoomi. He said that exhibition space was likely to be fully booked and that the possibility of returning to temporary hangar facilities could not be ruled out.

He said that the demand witnessed during the third edition would be assessed to plan the next phase of expansion at both venues. The objective would be to provide at least one-and-a-half times, if not twice, the existing exhibition space by the time the fourth edition of Bharat Mobility was organised. He expressed confidence that by then the mobility industry would also be significantly more integrated with the global economy, enabling businesses to expand their international presence and market penetration.

Shri Goyal said that Bharat Mobility presented an important opportunity to showcase India's capabilities and that the country should rapidly establish itself as a global leader in the mobility sector. With production capabilities and competitiveness declining in some other markets, he said, India must position itself as a trusted partner for businesses looking to relocate their operations and manufacturing.

Concluding his address, the Minister said that India would be a harbinger of good news and a torchbearer of a prosperous and developed nation. He expressed confidence in the positive future of the mobility sector and urged industry stakeholders to translate their optimism into action through scale, speed and skill.

He extended his best wishes to all stakeholders for the successful organisation of the third edition of Bharat Mobility Global Expo 2027 and for their continued contribution to India's growth journey.

The third edition of Bharat Mobility Global Expo 2027 is set to be the largest global mobility event, bringing together over 1,750 exhibitors, 11 concurrent shows and an expected footfall of more than 10 lakh visitors across over 2.5 lakh square metres of exhibition space at Bharat Mandapam and Yashobhoomi. The Ministry of Commerce & Industry and the Ministry of Heavy Industries, Government of India, today hosted the Curtain Raiser for Bharat Mobility Global Expo 2027, setting the stage for the third and largest edition of India's flagship global mobility event.

Bharat Mobility Global Expo 2027 to be held from 4–9 February 2027 in Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi and Yashobhoomi, Dwarka, Delhi

Building on the success of the previous editions, Bharat Mobility Global Expo 2027 is set to expand significantly in scale and scope. The forthcoming edition will bring together established automotive sectors as well as emerging areas such as advanced mobility technologies, air mobility, urban mass transit, agri-mobility, batteries and energy solutions, and next-generation transportation systems.

The expansion reflects the evolution of Bharat Mobility Global Expo from a mobility exhibition into a comprehensive global platform representing the entire mobility ecosystem. Under the theme "Smarter Mobility for a Better Tomorrow", the third edition of BMGE will showcase India's capabilities across manufacturing, engineering, technology, innovation and sustainable mobility, while facilitating collaboration among industry, Government, startups, technology providers, academia and international stakeholders.

The Expo will feature a wide range of specialized shows across the two venues.

At Bharat Mandapam, BMGE 2027 will include Auto Expo – The Motor Show 2027, India International Tyre Show 2027, Bharat Battery Show 2027, Mobility Tech Pavilion, India Cycle Show 2027 and the Steel and Advanced Materials Pavilion. At Yashobhoomi, the Expo will bring together The Components & Technology Show 2027, Bharat Construction Equipment Expo 2027, Agri Mobility & Technology Expo 2027, Air Mobility Expo 2027, and Metro & Urban Mass Transit Expo 2027. Both venues will also witness State and Ministry participation, conferences, special pavilions and experience zones, startup showcases, meetings, media facilities and other mobility-related showcases.

The consolidation of these diverse sectors under the Bharat Mobility umbrella will enable visitors and industry stakeholders to experience the complete mobility ecosystem – from vehicles, components and materials to software, batteries, digital technologies, infrastructure and future mobility solutions.

The 2027 edition will place a strong emphasis on the technologies shaping the future of mobility, including electrification, advanced battery and energy-storage technologies, connected and software-defined vehicles, artificial intelligence, automation, advanced manufacturing, sustainable materials and emerging mobility solutions.

Beyond the exhibition floor, Bharat Mobility Global Expo 2027 will continue to serve as an important knowledge-sharing and business-engagement platform. The Expo will feature conferences, leadership sessions, policy discussions, product launches, technology demonstrations, buyer-seller meetings and B2B/B2G interactions, bringing together experts and decision-makers from India and across the world.

Special emphasis will also be placed on enhancing the participation of MSMEs, startups and emerging technology companies. BMGE will provide these enterprises with an opportunity to showcase their capabilities, engage with global OEMs and technology leaders, explore potential partnerships and access new domestic and international business opportunities. International participation in the form of country pavilions and international delegates will be another highlight of the event.

The Expo will also provide a platform for Central Ministries, State Governments, testing and certification agencies, research institutions and other ecosystem stakeholders to showcase initiatives, policies, infrastructure capabilities and programs relevant to India’s rapidly evolving mobility landscape.

Bharat Mobility Global Expo is being developed through close collaboration between Government and industry, with participation from leading industry associations representing the various segments of the mobility ecosystem.

The Curtain Raiser brought together senior Government officials, representatives of supporting Ministries, industry associations, automotive and mobility sector leaders, representatives of foreign Missions and embassies, knowledge partners and other key stakeholders.

With its significantly expanded scale, wider sectoral coverage and increasing international participation, Bharat Mobility Global Expo 2027 aims to further establish India as a key global destination for mobility manufacturing, innovation, technology and investment, while strengthening BMGE’s position among the world’s leading mobility platforms.

For more information about Bharat Mobility Global Expo 2027, please visit www.bharat-mobility.com

2334802.title: Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 at Dilli Haat Records Cumulative Sales of Over ₹ 64.52 Lakh, Reflecting Strong Public Response and Growing Market Opportunities for Artisans
2334802.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 at Dilli Haat Records Cumulative Sales of Over ₹ 64.52 Lakh, Reflecting Strong Public Response and Growing Market Opportunities for Artisans
Mela Showcases India's Traditional Craftsmanship, Cultural Diversity and Inclusive Entrepreneurship
More Than 130 Stalls Showcase Handicrafts, Handloom Products, Traditional Textiles and Indigenous Creations Across 07 Thematic Zones
Union Ministers and Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Visit the Mela and Interact with Artisans
Posted On: 10 NOV 2026 7:27PM by PIB Delhi

The ongoing 15 day Shilp Samagam Mela 2026, being organised by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, at Dilli Haat, INA, in the National Capital, has emerged as a vibrant platform showcasing India's rich traditional craftsmanship, cultural heritage and entrepreneurial spirit.

The Mela will continue until November 15, 2026, that is providing an opportunity for artisans and beneficiaries belonging to Scheduled Castes, Other Backward Classes, Safai Karamcharis and persons with disabilities to showcase and market their products to a wider audience.

The Ministry has been organising Shilp Samagam Melas since 2022. Through these fairs, more than 1,000 artisans from Scheduled Castes, Other Backward Classes and Safai Karamchari communities have benefited from opportunities to exhibit and market their products.

The initiative aims to promote self-employment, encourage entrepreneurship and facilitate the socio-economic empowerment of beneficiary communities.

Organised around the theme ‘प्रकाश और परंपरा – ज्योति से ज्योति जलाएँ’, the two week Mela brings together India's rich cultural heritage and traditional craftsmanship through seven distinct thematic zones. These include कला आँगन, प्रकाश चौक, पूजा पथ, सजावट बाज़ार, घराना, स्वाद चौक and मंच, offering visitors a comprehensive experience of India's artistic, cultural and culinary diversity.

A senior official in the Ministry said the Mela has witnessed encouraging sales since its commencement, reflecting the enthusiastic response of visitors and growing appreciation for products crafted by beneficiary communities.

He said the four participating corporations, namely the National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC), National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC) and National Divyangjan Finance and Development Corporation (NDFDC), have recorded cumulative sales of approximately ₹ 64.52 Lakh between November 1 and November 9, 2026.

He said the sales figures reflect the positive market response to the products showcased at the Mela and the growing market opportunities for participating artisans.

The Ministry facilitates the participation of beneficiaries by providing free stalls, travel expenses, daily allowances and transportation facilities for their goods. These support measures help artisans overcome logistical and financial barriers while enabling them to access new markets and customers.

The Mela showcases a diverse range of handicrafts, handloom products, traditional textiles, festive decorations, lamps, home décor items and other indigenous products through more than 130 stalls.

The exhibition provides an accessible marketing platform for artisans and beneficiaries to connect directly with consumers, expand their market reach and strengthen their entrepreneurial capabilities.

The Mela also provides opportunities for artisans to expand their market reach through initiatives such as Bharat TULIP, which connects artisans with e-commerce platforms, and Purple Fest, which celebrates the creativity and capabilities of persons with disabilities while promoting inclusion and equal opportunities.

The Mela has witnessed visits by Hon'ble Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment, Dr. Virendra Kumar; Union Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri Ramdas Athawale; Union Minister of State for Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, Smt. Nimuben Jayantibhai Bambhaniya; and Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri Sudhansh Pant, along with other senior officials.

During their visits, the dignitaries toured the exhibition stalls, appreciated the traditional craftsmanship and interacted with participating artisans, reaffirming the Government's commitment to promoting inclusive entrepreneurship, economic empowerment and sustainable livelihood opportunities for disadvantaged communities.

A major attraction of the Mela is the series of cultural activities and programmes hosted every evening at the Manch. Artists and troupe performers from different States come together to present colourful folk dances, traditional music and regional art forms. These performances offer audiences a glimpse into India's pluralistic cultural expressions on a single platform, creating a festive atmosphere and fostering regional cultural exchange.

Citizens, families and young visitors are enthusiastically visiting the Mela to explore the diverse range of traditional products, appreciate the craftsmanship of participating artisans and support their efforts towards entrepreneurship, economic empowerment and self-reliance.

The common visitors are enjoying different colours of the Mela, and experience India's rich cultural heritage while supporting the artisans and entrepreneurs contributing to the vision of an inclusive and self-reliant India.

2334785.title: From Financial Constraints to Global Academic Opportunities
2334785.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Financial Constraints to Global Academic Opportunities
A Journey of Excellence Through the National Overseas Scholarship
Posted On: 10 NOV 2026 6:55PM by PIB Delhi

A significant opportunity came through the National Overseas Scholarship (NOS) Scheme of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, for a youngster with financial constraints.

During the financial year 2025–26, Mr Rajesh Shedge (name changed) received financial assistance under the scheme, enabling him to pursue his academic aspirations at University College London.

Coming from Maharashtra, a young student belonging to the Scheduled Caste community demonstrated strong academic commitment and an aspiration to pursue higher education at an internationally reputed institution.

Despite his dedication and academic ambitions, financial constraints posed a significant challenge to his dream of studying abroad. The high cost of international education, including tuition fees, accommodation, travel and other associated expenses, made pursuing postgraduate studies overseas difficult for his family.

Determined to build a career in the field of infrastructure development, project management and construction economics, he aspired to pursue a postgraduate degree in Construction Economics and Management at University College London (UCL), United Kingdom, a globally recognised institution. However, arranging the substantial financial resources required for international education remained a major obstacle.

Under the National Overseas Scholarship, financial assistance was provided towards tuition fees of £39,800 and a maintenance allowance of £9,900, along with airfare, visa fees, insurance and other admissible academic expenses. This assistance substantially reduced the financial burden on his family and enabled him to access quality international education without the uncertainty of arranging funds for essential academic and living expenses.

With the support of the scheme, Mr Shedge  is currently pursuing an MSc in Construction Economics and Management at University College London, United Kingdom. He is actively participating in lectures, tutorials and other academic activities, gaining exposure to international education standards, advanced knowledge and professional practices in the construction and infrastructure sectors.

The National Overseas Scholarship has played a crucial role in transforming his educational aspirations into reality. Beyond financial assistance, the scheme has opened avenues for international academic exposure, professional development and enhanced future career prospects.

Mr Rajesh Shedge’s journey reflects how targeted educational support can help deserving students overcome financial barriers and access opportunities at leading global institutions.

Through the National Overseas Scholarship, the Government of India continues to promote inclusive access to higher education and empower students from Scheduled Caste communities to pursue academic excellence and contribute to the nation's development.

2334780.title: From Occupational Risk to Safer Livelihood
2334780.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Occupational Risk to Safer Livelihood
A New Chapter of Dignity Through the NAMASTE Scheme
Posted On: 10 NOV 2026 6:45PM by PIB Delhi

The journey of 60 year Mr Subramanian (name changed), reflects the importance of ensuring occupational safety, health protection and livelihood security for sanitation workers.

Through the NAMASTE Scheme, access to protective equipment and awareness training has helped him continue his profession with greater confidence, improved well-being and dignity. His experience highlights how targeted interventions under the NAMASTE Scheme are contributing towards safer working conditions, better livelihood opportunities and a more dignified future for sanitation workers.

Mr Subramanian, a sanitation worker from Pondicherry Municipality, belonging to the Scheduled Caste community, had spent over 15 years undertaking the demanding work of sewer and septic tank cleaning. Throughout his working life, he was frequently exposed to hazardous conditions, often without adequate protective equipment or occupational safety measures. Prolonged exposure to hazardous waste resulted in recurring skin infections and respiratory discomfort, affecting his ability to work regularly and maintain his health.

As the sole earning member of a family of four, his health-related challenges placed considerable financial pressure on the household. Frequent medical expenses further strained the family's limited resources, while his modest monthly income of approximately Rs. 12,000 made it difficult to manage household requirements. Despite these hardships, he remained committed to his profession and aspired to continue earning a livelihood with dignity while ensuring his safety and well-being.

A significant change came in 2025 through the National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) Scheme, implemented by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. Under the scheme, he received a comprehensive Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) kit comprising protective overalls, heavy-duty gloves, gumboots, a face mask and a safety helmet. He also underwent awareness training on safe sanitation practices and the prevention of occupational health risks.

The provision of protective equipment and safety awareness brought a meaningful improvement to his working conditions. With better protection against occupational hazards, his health improved considerably, work-related absences reduced and medical expenses declined. Improved health and greater consistency at work also contributed to an increase in his monthly income from approximately Rs. 12,000 to Rs. 16,000–18,000, strengthening his financial stability.

2334772.title: Department of Military Affairs Successfully Completes Sixth Edition of Special Campaign
2334772.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
Department of Military Affairs Successfully Completes Sixth Edition of Special Campaign
Posted On: 10 NOV 2026 6:32PM by PIB Delhi

Department of Military Affairs (DMA) and all establishments under its purview successfully conducted the sixth edition of the Special Campaign from October 2 to 31, 2026, with the active participation of the Defence Forces and Headquarters Integrated Defence Staff (HQ IDS).

The cleanliness drive was undertaken at 8,507 campaign sites identified by the Department. In addition, various organisations simplified a total of 324 rules and processes. Disposal and sale of scrap, including electronic waste (e-waste), generated revenue of approximately ₹89.68 crore. As part of the record management initiative, 5,28,443 physical files were reviewed, of which 16,837 files were weeded out. This resulted in the effective freeing up of 3,53,291 square feet of space, enabling its improvement and alternate utilisation. During the campaign, a total of 2,905 public grievances and 466 public grievance appeals were disposed of. Further, 91 MP references and four IMC references were responded to.

Several innovative practices and noteworthy initiatives emerged from the campaign. The Indian Air Force Station, Tambaram, in collaboration with a specialized NGO, undertook the rejuvenation of nine heritage shallow wells, each approximately 60 to 80 years old. The initiative has resulted in an additional water yield of one lakh litres per day, meeting approximately 11.1 per cent of the Station's daily water requirement. In another significant initiative, INS Shivaji, under the Southern Naval Command, in collaboration with IIT Mumbai, installed a biomass-based gasifier steam cooking system with a foliage processing capacity of one tonne.

As part of the campaign, the Defence Forces and HQ IDS contributed extensively towards promoting cleanliness across military posts, units, stations, establishments and cantonments, while simultaneously undertaking concerted efforts to minimise pendency in official matters. Special emphasis was placed on the timely disposal of public grievances, Members of Parliament (MP) references, Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) and State Government references, appeals and parliamentary assurances.

2334770.ministry: Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers : Department of Pharmaceuticals
2334770.body_html:
Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers :
Department of Pharmaceuticals
PLI Scheme for Medical Devices extended up to 2035–36; Fresh applications invited
Focus on Critical Component Manufacturing
Scheme guidelines made easier and investor friendly for Ease of Doing Business
Minimum Sales Threshold Requirement to Claim Incentive Discontinued
Minimum Investment Requirement Trimmed
Posted On: 10 NOV 2026 6:30PM by PIB Delhi

The Government of India has invited fresh applications under the Production Linked Incentive Scheme for Promoting Domestic Manufacturing of Medical Devices (PLI-MD), which has now been extended up to 2035–36. Approximately Rs 2700 Cr outlay available under the Scheme will be utilized for the purpose. The applicants can submit applications through an online portal, which would be operational in the next 10 days.

Launched in 2020-21, the PLI-MD scheme has led to domestic manufacturing of over 60 high end medical devices and components, including X-ray tubes and detectors, 1.5T MRI, LINAC, CT scanners, mammography machines, Cathlab, orthopaedic and cardiac implants, dialyzers etc till date. The scheme has resulted in production valued at over ₹16,000 crore.

On the basis of learnings in the first phase of the Scheme, a number of simplifications have been done in the eligibility conditions as well as procedure for claiming incentive by the applicants.

The applicants shall be allowed 3 years for setting up their manufacturing facilities in any of the 4 Target Segments (TS) viz. medical consumables, disposables and implants (TS 1), Critical components (TS2), high-end medical devices which are presently at a nascent stage of domestic manufacturing (TS3), and high-end medical devices that are presently only assembled in the country (TS4). The tapering incentive rate would be averaging ~5% for TS1, ~9% for TS2 & TS3, and 6% for TS4. In the Consumables and Disposables segment, the focus shall be on creating manufacturing scale and world class quality. In the TS 3 & 4, priority shall be given for value chain integration, so that there is an overall increase in competitiveness and quality of Made in India devices. The focus on critical component manufacturing under the Scheme, would help achieve value chain integration and also give a boost to the MSME sector.

Under the Scheme, minimum sales threshold requirement to claim incentive has been discontinued, and minimum investment requirement has also been trimmed.  To enhance Ease of Doing Business (EoDB), the scheme guidelines have been made easier and investor friendly.  The applicants shall be free to submit any number of applications in one or more TS and the application window shall remain continuously open over a long period of time.

PLI-MD 2.0 aims to fulfil the vision of Atmanirbhar Bharat and Make in India, develop indigenous supply chains, attract investment, generate employment, improve quality of Made in India devices, reduce price of medical devices, and enhance India's global competitiveness in high-end medical technologies. The objective of the Scheme is to promote deep manufacturing of medical devices, as well as manufacturing of high-end medical equipment like 3T MRI, PET-CT, Ultrasound probes & consoles, high-throughput IVD analyzers etc which are currently not being manufactured in the country.

2334764.title: Odisha charts a National Roadmap for Millet led Agricultural Transformation
2334764.body_html:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
Odisha charts a National Roadmap for Millet led Agricultural Transformation
Dr. M.L. Jat Emphasises Expansion of Millet Cultivation Area to 5 Lakh Hectares with Production Target of 8 Lakh Metric Tonnes by 2047
Two days National Event on Agro-Biodiversity Conservation, Climate-Resilient Agriculture and Sustainable Food Systems Begins in Bhubaneswar
Posted On: 10 NOV 2026 6:18PM by PIB Delhi

A two day national event on agro-biodiversity conservation, climate-resilient agriculture and sustainable food systems was commenced on 10th November 2026 at Bhubaneswar, Odisha, in the presence of Shri Braj Mohan Ram, Governor of Odisha, Shri Kanak Vardhan Singh Deo, Minister for Agriculture and Farmer Welfare, Government of Odisha, Dr. Mangi Lal Jat, Secretary DARE and Director General, ICAR, Dr. Soumya Swaminathan, Chairperson, M.S. Swaminathan Research Foundation; and Shri Sachin Ramachandra Jadhav, IAS, Commissioner-cum-Secretary, Department of Agriculture and Farmers' Empowerment, Government of Odisha, along with eminent agricultural scientists, policymakers and other stakeholders.

The inaugural session marked the formal commencement of event, followed by visit to exhibition stalls and display of agricultural innovations, indigenous crop diversity, millet-based products and interaction with farmers.

Addressing the gathering, Dr Jat emphasised on use of rich agrobiodiversity of Odisha through a greater focus on opportunity crops including millets to address the grand challenges of climate change, soil health, nutrition etc while promoting local food system for one health.

Dr. Jat, also highlighted the success of Odisha Shree Anna Abhiyan and its potential to emerge as a national model for millet-based agricultural transformation. He stressed on the area expansion of millet cultivation from 1.79 lakh ha to 5 lakh ha by 2047 with a production target of 8 lakh metric tonnes. The state achievement in ragi procurement, with 7.5 lakh quintals during KMS 2024-25 and a target of 8 lakh quintals for 2025-26 and importance of conserving indigenous millet diversity, particularly the 163 documented finger millet landraces, and promoting traditional varieties such as Kalia, Bati, Mami and Bharathi were appreciated.

Further, Dr. Jat discussed on scaling up scientific cultivation practices, promoting minor millets such as suan and kangu, developing affordable processing machinery, strengthening FPOs and women's SHGs, and expanding millet-based enterprises and market linkages through ICAR-IIMR, Hyderabad. He also proposed about the strengthening research collaboration between ICAR-IIMR, Hyderabad and for establishment of Centre of Excellence on Millets at Odisha University of Agriculture and Technology.

The event aimed to strengthen institutional partnerships, promote knowledge exchange and accelerate Odisha's journey towards sustainable, climate-resilient and economically viable millet-based agricultural development.

2334759.body_html:
Ministry of Micro,Small & Medium Enterprises
Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) holds Round Table Discussion with CPSEs on Enhancing Procurement from SC/ST MSEs
Posted On: 10 NOV 2026 6:13PM by PIB Delhi

A Round Table Discussion with Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) was held on 5 November 2026 at Dr. Ambedkar International Centre, New Delhi to monitor procurement status of CPSEs on mandated 4% from SC/ST MSEs under Public Procurement Policy of Government. Ms. Mercy Epao, Joint Secretary, Ministry of MSME chaired the meeting. Shri Ajit Chavan, Additional Chief Executive Officer, GeM, Dr. S.S Acharya, Chairman-cum-Managing Director, NSIC and other Senior Officers from Ministry, Department of Public Enterprises and NSIC participated and share their respective interventions to support the SC/ST MSEs.


A total of 30 CPSEs including BHEL, BEL, NTPC, AAI, BEML, Coal India Ltd participated in the Round Table discussion, which centred on the challenges being faced by the CPSEs and sharing of best practices and how to deepen coordination between NSSHOs, GeM and CPSEs.

In her address, Ms. Mercy Epao, highlighted various initiatives undertaken to promote and handhold to SC/ST MSEs under National SC-ST Hub (NSSH) Scheme. This resulted in continuous increase in the share of SC/ST MSEs in public procurement. In FY 2025-26, more than 36 times hike in public procurement from SC/ST MSE since inception of the scheme. She further informed about Entrepreneur Awareness & Special Vendor Development Program (EA&SVDP), a new initiative for creation of awareness amongst SC/ST MSE and to network with CPSEs. She urged CPSEs to formulate internal action plan to achieve the target and also provide support in terms of Vendor Registration/Enlistment Procedure, Product/Service Matchmaking, Regional/Local Connect of CPSEs with SC/ST MSEs and Handholding support.

Shri Ajit Chavan, Additional CEO, GeM, acknowledged the Ministry of MSME’s significant contribution towards empowering small enterprises and achieving key milestones under the public procurement framework. He informed about various measures taken to facilitate SC/ST MSEs in tender participation including identification of SC/ST MSE sellers through dedicated marketplace filters. He emphasized the importance of engaging sellers from diverse sectors, particularly on services and industry verticals to ensure equitable access to procurement opportunities. He encouraged CPSEs to utilize the services of the Nodal Officer appointed by GeM for handholding support.

The Round Table provided an opportunity for CPSEs to interact with best performing CPSEs, to address their gaps/challenges. The discussion also focused on identifying avenues for enhanced collaboration between CPSEs and NSSH through vendor development programs, capacity-building initiatives and digital facilitation support to strengthen procurement from SC/ST and women-owned MSEs.

2334758.title: ‘Nasha Mukt Yuva, Viksit Bharat Quiz’ Records Participation of Over 25,607 Citizens
2334758.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
‘Nasha Mukt Yuva, Viksit Bharat Quiz’ Records Participation of Over 25,607 Citizens
Quiz to Remain Open for Participation Until November 25, 2026
Campaign Reaches Over 35.84 Crore People, Including 14.33 Crore Youth and 11.32 Crore Women
Over 33.57 Lakh Activities Conducted in Educational Institutions; 39.91 Lakh Persons Treated and Rehabilitated; More Than 755 DoSJE-Supported De-addiction Centres Working Across the Country
Over 46.73 Lakh Nasha Mukt Pledges Taken; More Than 2 Lakh Nasha Mukti Mitras Registered
Posted On: 10 NOV 2026 6:07PM by PIB Delhi

The online ‘Nasha Mukt Yuva, Viksit Bharat Quiz’ has witnessed an encouraging response, with total participation crossing over 25,600 citizens as of November 10, 2026. The growing participation reflects increasing public engagement, particularly among young people, in the collective endeavour of building a drug-free India.

The quiz was launched on October 26, 2026, by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, under the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (NMBA). The initiative aims to promote awareness about the harmful effects of substance use and encourage citizens, especially youth, to actively contribute towards creating a Nasha Mukt Bharat.

MY Bharat Quiz QR

A Senior Official in the Ministry said the quiz is being conducted from October 26 to November 25, 2026, and remains open to all citizens.

He said the interested participants can access the quiz through the MY Bharat portal and take part in this nationwide awareness initiative.

Participation Link: https://mybharat.gov.in/quizzes/yuva/detail/Url9dlIwCinQVSf8lwPB9w/

Launched on August 15, 2020, the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan aims to strengthen drug demand reduction efforts through preventive education, awareness generation, treatment, rehabilitation and community participation, he added.

Initially launched in 272 vulnerable districts, the Abhiyaan has since expanded its reach to cover all districts across the country, he further said.

The Official noted that the campaign has reached over 35.84 crore people, including 14.33 crore youth and 11.32 crore women, reflecting the nationwide scale of its awareness and outreach initiatives.

NMBA Mobile App

Under the Abhiyaan, over 33.57 lakh activities have been conducted in educational institutions, while 39.91 lakh persons have been treated and rehabilitated through a network of more than 755 Department of Social Justice and Empowerment (DoSJE)-supported de-addiction centres working across the country, the Official said. The total number of Nasha Mukt pledges taken has crossed 46.73 lakh, with more than 2 lakh Nasha Mukti Mitras registered, he added.

Noting that the Abhiyaan enters its seventh year, the Official said the ongoing quiz seeks to deepen public understanding of the harmful effects of substance use, promote informed decision-making and encourage young people to become active ambassadors of awareness and prevention.

The initiative reinforces the vision of a Nasha Mukt Bharat and Viksit Bharat, recognising the importance of healthy individuals, families and communities in the country's development, Official further said.

Nasha Mukti Mitr Registration QR Code

Giving details, the Official informed that the quiz comprises 20 Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs), which participants are required to answer within 10 minutes.

A participation certificate is generated for every participant who successfully submits the quiz, he said.

He added the participants can also view the correct answers upon completion, enabling them to enhance their understanding of substance use prevention.

Underscoring the importance of this digital initiative, the Official said the Ministry aims to strengthen community participation, encourage responsible choices and mobilise citizens, especially youth, to contribute to the movement against substance use.

NMBA e-pledge QR Code

He said the Ministry encourages all citizens, particularly young people, to participate in the ‘Nasha Mukt Yuva, Viksit Bharat Quiz’ before November 25, 2026, and become active contributors to the collective vision of a drug-free India.

2334756.title: New AIIMS cross 6 crore OPD consultations since 2021-22, expanding access to specialised tertiary healthcare across India
2334756.ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
2334756.body_html:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
New AIIMS cross 6 crore OPD consultations since 2021-22, expanding access to specialised tertiary healthcare across India
22 new AIIMS approved under Pradhan Mantri Swasthya Suraksha Yojana (PMSSY), 18 fully functional institutions providing comprehensive healthcare, medical education and research services
Expansion of AIIMS under PMSSY addresses regional imbalances in affordable and reliable tertiary healthcare, and strengthens medical education and research
OPD consultations at new AIIMS rise from 50.03 lakh in 2021-22 to 144.96 lakh in 2025-26, reflecting increased utilisation of specialised healthcare services
Posted On: 10 NOV 2026 6:05PM by PIB Delhi

The new All India Institutes of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) established under the Pradhan Mantri Swasthya Suraksha Yojana (PMSSY) have collectively recorded over 6 crore Outpatient Department (OPD) consultations in the five-year period since 2021-22, as on 31st October 2026. The achievement reflects the growing reach of these institutions and their contribution to bringing specialised tertiary healthcare services closer to people across the country.

The Government of India has been expanding the AIIMS network under PMSSY to address regional disparities in the availability of affordable and reliable tertiary healthcare. The initiative has also sought to strengthen the country's medical education and research ecosystem alongside the expansion of specialised healthcare services.

Of the 22 new AIIMS approved under PMSSY in various phases, 18 are fully functional. These institutions provide a range of services spanning OPD and Inpatient Department (IPD) care, emergency and trauma services, diagnostics, medical education and research.

The growing utilisation of these institutions is reflected in the year-wise OPD figures. Consultations increased from 50.03 lakh in 2021-22 to 77.95 lakh in 2022-23 and 100.52 lakh in 2023-24, reaching 129.98 lakh in 2024-25 and 144.96 lakh in 2025-26. During 2026-27, the new AIIMS recorded 97.41 lakh OPD patients till October 2026. The cumulative figures across these years amount to approximately 6.01 crore.

The new AIIMS have also expanded opportunities for undergraduate, postgraduate and nursing education, while developing specialised clinical facilities and advanced medical services. Together, these institutions are contributing to the expansion of India's medical education and research infrastructure.

2334740.title: Delhi's River Tourism Begins with the Launch of Yamuna Recreational Cruise Service
2334740.ministry: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
2334740.body_html:
Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
Delhi's River Tourism Begins with the Launch of Yamuna Recreational Cruise Service
Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal  Inaugurates Project in presence of Delhi CM Rekha Gupta
30-seater Electric Vessel launched along Sonia Vihar-Jagatpur stretch; initiative aims to boost Delhi's Sustainable Tourism
Yamuna’s Mythology and Heritage to Come Alive in Spectacular Light and Sound Show
Yamuna Cruise signals a new wave of river tourism in Delhi: Sarbananda Sonowal
Committed to develop Delhi's riverfront as an attractive public destination: Rekha Gupta
Posted On: 10 NOV 2026 5:47PM by PIB Delhi

Delhi took a significant step towards expanding its river-based tourism offerings with the inauguration of its first recreational Yamuna River Cruise service on the Yamuna by Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways Sarbananda Sonowal in presence of Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta at Sonia Vihar here today.

Developed along the Sonia Vihar-Jagatpur stretch, the initiative aims to unlock the tourism and recreational potential of the Yamuna while offering residents and visitors a new way to experience the national capital. The launch also marks another milestone in the Centre's efforts to develop India's rivers as vibrant avenues for tourism, passenger movement and economic activity.

The inauguration was attended by Minister of State for Ports, Shipping and Waterways Shantanu Thakur; Minister of State for Road Transport and Highways Harsh Malhotra; Public Works Department and Irrigation and Flood Control Minister Parvesh Sahib Singh; Tourism Minister Kapil Mishra; Forest & Environment and Industries Minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa and MP Manoj Tiwari, along with senior officials including Vijay Kumar, Secretary, Ministry of Ports, Shipping & Waterways; Rajeev Verma, Chief Secretary, Delhi Govt and Sushil Kumar Lohani, Chairman, Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI) among others from the Central and Delhi governments.

Speaking at the inauguration, Sarbananda Sonowal said the project reflected the government's commitment to harnessing India's vast inland waterways potential under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

“Under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, India's rivers and inland waterways are emerging as important drivers of economic growth, tourism and sustainable connectivity. The launch of Delhi's first recreational cruise service on the Yamuna is another step towards reconnecting people with our rivers and unlocking their immense potential. This launch signals a new wave of river tourism in the city. We are transforming waterways into avenues for tourism, trade and livelihoods while advancing our commitment to cleaner and more efficient mobility. This is an important part of our vision of building a Viksit Bharat,” Sarbananda Sonowal said.

The project features a 30-seater electric cruise vessel offering visitors a scenic experience along an approximately 6-kilometer round-trip stretch of the river. The use of electric-powered vessels highlights the potential of inland waterways for clean and sustainable mobility.

Chief Minister Rekha Gupta said the initiative would add a new dimension to Delhi's tourism landscape and strengthen public engagement with the Yamuna.

“The Yamuna is an integral part of Delhi's history, culture and identity. This recreational cruise service will offer residents and visitors a new way to experience the river while creating fresh opportunities for tourism and local economic activity. Under the dynamic leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, we remain committed to develop Delhi's riverfront as an attractive public destination, with better amenities, sustainable infrastructure and experiences that celebrate the city's heritage,” Rekha Gupta said.

Envisioned as a wider eco-tourism destination, the Yamuna project includes a range of recreational attractions and visitor amenities. A key attraction is a musical fountain featuring a coordinated light and sound show depicting the history and spiritual significance of the Yamuna, including its association with Surya Dev, Yama and the divine leela of Shri Krishna, particularly the legendary Kaliya Daman.

The destination also includes a food court, shopping area, children's play zone and adventure sports facilities, including skating and rock climbing. Modern floating jetties, dedicated ticket counters and online booking facilities, restrooms, waiting areas and illuminated approach pathways have been incorporated to provide visitors with a convenient experience.

The Yamuna has been designated as National Waterway-110 under the National Waterways Act, 2016. The launch of the cruise service marks an important step towards developing the waterway for recreational navigation and river-based tourism in the national capital.

The initiative is part of a wider national transformation of India's inland waterways. Cargo movement on national waterways has increased from 18 million metric tonnes in 2013-14 to 218 million metric tonnes in 2025-26, reflecting the growing role of waterways in the country's logistics network. With freight movement costing an estimated ₹1.06 per tonne-kilometer on waterways, compared with ₹1.41 by rail and ₹2.28 by road, inland navigation offers a cost-effective alternative for transporting cargo.

River cruise tourism is another emerging dimension of this expansion. The number of river cruise vessels offering overnight journeys has increased from five in 2013-14 to 26 in 2025-26. The landmark journey of MV Ganga Vilas, recognised in the Limca Book of Records as the world's longest river cruise. Covering more than 3,200 kms across India and Bangladesh, the journey connected 50 tourist destinations, traversed two countries, five states and 27 river systems.

The Recreational Yamuna River Cruise Service has been developed by the Inland Waterways Authority of India under the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways in collaboration with the Delhi Development Authority, Delhi Tourism and Transportation Development Corporation, Delhi Jal Board and the Irrigation and Flood Control Department of the Delhi government.

2334718.title: Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh Chairs ESSC General Body Meeting, Emphasises Citizen-Centric Science Communication to Showcase India's Scientific Achievements
2334718.body_html:
Ministry of Earth Sciences
Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh Chairs ESSC General Body Meeting, Emphasises Citizen-Centric Science Communication to Showcase India's Scientific Achievements
Union Minister Reviews Major Achievements of Earth Science Institutions in Deep Ocean Mission, Weather Forecasting, Ocean Services and Polar Research
India’s Deep-Sea Exploration Is Advancing with MATSYA-6000 and Indo-French Collaboration, says Dr. Jitendra Singh
Ocean information services, polar expeditions and glacier research expand India's scientific capabilities and public utility: Dr. Jitendra Singh
Dr. Jitendra Singh Proposes Mission-Mode Approach for Polar and Solid Earth Sciences to Accelerate Scientific Outcomes
Posted On: 10 NOV 2026 5:27PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences, and MoS PMO, Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh today chaired the Second General Body Meeting of the Earth System Sciences Council (ESSC), where he emphasised citizen-centric science communication and the need to transform India's scientific achievements into accessible, compelling narratives for the general public.

Calling for greater citizen-centric science communication, the Minister stressed that scientific breakthroughs, technological innovations and research outcomes must be conveyed in simple language that enables ordinary citizens to appreciate their relevance and national significance.

The meeting reviewed the annual reports and audited accounts for FY 2025-26 of the five constituent institutions of ESSC; National Institute of Ocean Technology (NIOT), Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (INCOIS), National Centre for Earth Science Studies (NCESS), Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology (IITM) and National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR). Secretary, Ministry of Earth Sciences, Dr. T. Srinivasa Kumar; Director General, CSIR, Dr. N. Kalaiselvi; Joint Secretary, MoES, Dr. G.R.S. Rao; Additional Secretary & Financial Adviser, MoES, Chetan Prakash Jain; and senior scientists and officials of the Ministry and its institutions attended the meeting.

Dr. Jitendra Singh emphasised that professional communication expertise must complement scientific knowledge to make research and technological achievements more accessible to society. He encouraged greater coordination among institutional communication teams, regular interaction with media professionals and the use of creative formats to communicate scientific achievements, technological applications and public services more effectively.

Reviewing the progress of the Deep Ocean Mission, Dr. Jitendra Singh was apprised of major advances in India's human deep-sea exploration programme, including the development of MATSYA-6000, the country's 6,000-metre depth-rated human submersible. Indian aquanauts successfully completed dives to 4,025 metres and 5,002 metres during the Indo-French expedition aboard the submersible Nautile, marking a significant advancement in India's deep-sea exploration capabilities.

NIOT also reported progress in indigenous ocean technologies, including desalination solutions for Lakshadweep, offshore fish cage technologies, oceanographic instrumentation, deep-sea mineral exploration and ocean thermal energy conversion. These initiatives strengthen India's capabilities in ocean exploration, marine research and sustainable utilisation of ocean resources.

Dr. Jitendra Singh reviewed scientific advances under Mission Mausam and the PRITHVI programme, including developments in the Bharat Forecasting System, advanced numerical weather prediction and atmospheric observation networks.

IITM's research is strengthening weather and climate forecasting through improved modelling systems, expanded observation infrastructure and emerging Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning applications. These efforts are aimed at improving forecasting capabilities and strengthening India's scientific preparedness for weather and climate-related challenges.

The Minister reviewed INCOIS's expanding ocean information and advisory services for fishing communities, coastal populations and maritime stakeholders. Its services include multilingual marine advisories, fishing-related information, swell-surge inundation forecasts and ocean observation products, strengthening the application of ocean science in public service delivery and coastal preparedness.

NCESS presented its scientific contributions in earth sciences, including research on landslides, tectonic processes, ocean structures, atmospheric aerosols and rainfall over the Western Ghats, alongside the development of scientific laboratories and research facilities.

Dr. Jitendra Singh reviewed NCPOR's achievements in polar and ocean research, including the 45th Indian Antarctic Expedition involving 95 members, the 16th Indian Arctic Expedition, glacier monitoring in the Himalayas and scientific investigations in the Southern Ocean.

Research on polar environments, glacier dynamics, ocean-atmosphere interactions and carbon cycling continue to contribute to a deeper understanding of climate change and global environmental processes, strengthening India's contribution to international polar research.

In his concluding remarks, Dr. Jitendra Singh welcomed the suggestions and contributions of members and assured follow-up by the Ministry. He encouraged members to continue sharing ideas and suggestions with him, the Secretary and concerned officials beyond formal meetings, describing the institutions as an extended scientific family working collectively towards advancing India's Earth Sciences capabilities.

2334717.title: Union Minister of State For Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare Shri Ram Nath Thakur participates in Khet Bachao Abhiyan in North 24 Parganas
2334717.body_html:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
Union Minister of State For Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare Shri Ram Nath Thakur participates in Khet Bachao Abhiyan in North 24 Parganas
The Minister emphasises on Natural Farming for Soil Protection and Sustainable Agriculture
Posted On: 10 NOV 2026 5:27PM by PIB Kolkata

Kolkata; November 10, 2026

 

As part of the nationwide Khet Bachao Abhiyan, the Union Minister of State for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare, Shri Ram Nath Thakur participated in a programme organised by the ICAR-National Institute of Natural Fibre Engineering and Technology (ICAR-NINFET) at Subhasnagar, in Swarupnagar Block of North 24 Parganas district, West Bengal.
The programme underscored the Government of India's commitment to protecting agricultural land, restoring soil health and promoting natural farming as a sustainable approach to agriculture. It highlighted the importance of conserving soil resources, reducing excessive dependence on chemical inputs and encouraging environmenta-friendly farming practices for the benefit of the present and future generations.

While addressing the gathering, the Union Minister harped on returning to natural farming and least utilisation of chemical fertiliser, so as to keep the soil health intact. He highlighted natural farming as an important approach to maintaining soil fertility, improving soil health and promoting ecological balance. He also encouraged farmers to adopt climate-resilient agricultural methods, scientific innovations and modern technologies to ensure long-term agricultural productivity and sustainability.

The Minister also stressed on the importance of conserving soil as a living resource and adopting balanced, need-based agricultural input management. He urged farmers to make effective utilisation of Soil Health Cards for informed fertiliser application, improved nutrient-use efficiency and the maintenance of soil fertility. In this regard, he highlighted the role of Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs) in providing technical guidance, practical demonstrations and extension services to facilitate the adoption of sustainable and natural farming practices.

The Union Minister urged the farmers to return to extend processes of farming, including utilisation of organic fertilisers an organic pesticides, to boost natural farming as well as aiding in reaps which are healthy for living.

The event was organised by ICAR-NINFET.
The programme reinforced the central message of Khet Bachao Abhiyan for Ravi crops, going on from October 22, to November 30, 2026 in the entire country- healthy soil is the foundation of healthy crops, sustainable agriculture and farmers' prosperity. Promoting natural farming, conserving soil fertility and adopting environmentally sustainable agricultural practices are essential to safeguarding agricultural resources and ensuring long-term food and livelihood security.

2334716.title: BRIC’s third Foundation Day celebrated at NII
2334716.body_html:
Ministry of Science & Technology
BRIC’s third Foundation Day celebrated at NII
India has potential to lead next biotechnology-driven industrial revolution, says Dr Jitendra Singh
Dr Jitendra Singh calls for stronger industry participation in India’s biotechnology ecosystem
BRIC’s integrated model is accelerating scientific collaboration while preserving institutional autonomy: Dr Jitendra Singh
BRIC and UK’s Centre for Process Innovation sign Letter of Intent to strengthen collaboration in biomanufacturing
Posted On: 10 NOV 2026 5:24PM by PIB Delhi

Speaking today at the third Foundation Day of the Biotechnology Research and Innovation Council (BRIC), held at the BRIC–National Institute of Immunology (NII), Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences, and Minister of State in the Prime Minister’s Office, Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, the Department of Atomic Energy and the Department of Space, Dr Jitendra Singh said that India has potential next biotechnology-driven industrial revolution and called for deeper integration across scientific institutions and greater participation by industry in India’s biotechnology ecosystem.

Dr.Jitendra Singh said the Government had encouraged greater integration among science institutions to overcome silos and improve coordination. The Minister described BRIC as a “joint family” in which institutions pool resources while retaining their identities, independence and autonomy. The arrangement, he said, had reduced procedural delays associated with multiple directorates and approvals while creating opportunities for scientific collaboration. The Minister added that other departments and ministries had replicated the model.

Referring to the sector’s growth, Dr.Jitendra Singh said India’s bioeconomy had expanded from about USD 10 billion when the Government took office to more than USD 195 billion. He said the country’s biotechnology startup ecosystem had grown from around 50–60 startups to more than 11,000, with several showing global potential. The Minister also highlighted efforts to strengthen high-performance manufacturing through biomanufacturing hubs, biofoundries and AI-integrated biomanufacturing.

Dr.Jitendra Singh cited biofoundry hubs in Mohali, Hyderabad, Pune and Thiruvananthapuram, and said international partnerships, including the collaboration with the UK’s Centre for Process Innovation, would support further progress.

The Minister said the Genomics Centre of Excellence had attracted interest from medical institutions, including AIIMS. Dr. Singhsaid that genomics could support the shift towards precision medicine, with institutions beginning to adopt the approach and collaborate. Dr Singh also spoke about the i3C PhD programme, which enables scholars to immerse themselves in research, innovate and collaborate, including through placements in the health and agriculture sectors. He said nearly 200 students had benefited from the programme.

Dr. Singh said the Prime Minister’s Independence Day appeal to young people to explore new opportunities in biotechnology had generated enthusiasm across the sector. He also referred to outreach programmes for school students and the public, and recalled proposing a dedicated mentorship programme to encourage girls to pursue science.

Further, Dr.Jitendra Singh said the Government was opening more avenues for private-sector participation in science and research, drawing on experience from reforms in the nuclear sector. He referred to the Research, Development and Innovation Fund, the Anusandhan National Research Foundation and BIRAC as parts of the wider research and innovation landscape. He said India should be at the centre of the next industrial revolution, which he described as likely to be driven by biotechnology, artificial intelligence and genomics. Unlike earlier industrial revolutions that emerged elsewhere before India adopted their technologies, he said, the country’s biotechnology community had the opportunity to be at the forefront of the next one.

During the event, the Wellcome Trust announced a grant of up to ₹21.7 crore for a five-year immersion training programme for more than 250 iBRIC+ PhD scholars. A Letter of Intent was also signed between BRIC and the UK’s Centre for Process Innovation to strengthen India–UK collaboration in biomanufacturing and support the development of biofoundries.

Winners of the Festival of Sports were felicitated at the event. The iBRIC+ Spotlight Scientist of the Year–2026 awards were presented to Dr Sunil Laxman of BRIC-inStem, Dr Rashna Bhandari of BRIC-CDFD, and Prof.Bhabatosh Das, Professor at BRIC-THSTI

Dr Rajesh S. Gokhale, Secretary, Department of Biotechnology, and Director General, BRIC, emphasized that BRIC’s core vision is to move beyond isolated institutional excellence by unifying India’s 13 premier biotechnology institutions across 11 cities into a decentralised national network. Anchored in the pillars of people, culture, trust and resource allocation, and supported by a lean Secretariat and translational initiatives such as the i3C PhD curriculum and BRIC–BIRAC entrepreneurship programmes, the Council aims to connect laboratory innovation with market applications, advance sovereign technologies, strengthen food and health security, and establish India as a global biotechnology leader with lasting economic and societal impact

The event was also attended by Lt. Gen. (Retd.) Dr MadhuriKanitkar, Member, Prime Minister’s Science, Technology and Innovation Advisory Council (PM-STIAC), and former Vice-Chancellor of Maharashtra University of Health Sciences; Ms EktaVishnoi (IRS), Joint Secretary (Administration), Department of Biotechnology; and Dr Pushkar Sharma, Director, BRIC-NII.

2334712.title: From Financial Constraints to Academic Progress
2334712.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Financial Constraints to Academic Progress
 A Journey Supported by the NFSC Fellowship
Posted On: 10 NOV 2026 5:21PM by PIB Delhi

The journey of Mr. Sayan Rai (name changed) demonstrates how timely educational assistance can help students overcome financial and geographical barriers, access essential research resources and pursue their academic aspirations. It highlights the role of the NFSC Scheme in supporting higher education and empowering aspiring scholars to contribute meaningfully to the academic community.

At 32, Mr. Sayan Rai, a Scheduled Caste research scholar from Darjeeling, West Bengal, is pursuing his Ph.D. with determination and a strong commitment to academic research. His aspiration to undertake quality doctoral research, however, was accompanied by considerable financial challenges. As a full-time research scholar with limited sources of income, meeting academic and everyday living expenses placed a significant burden on him and his family.

Coming from a family where his parents were also supporting the education of his sibling, he faced difficulties in managing expenses related to rent, electricity, accommodation, books, stationery, fieldwork and travel. Limited resources also prevented him from purchasing a personal laptop, often requiring him to depend on borrowed devices and university facilities.

Inconsistent internet connectivity in the Darjeeling Hills further affected his access to online academic resources. Financial constraints also made it difficult to participate in conferences, workshops and seminars.

The National Fellowship for Scheduled Caste Students (NFSC) Scheme has played an important role in supporting his academic journey. Since November 2022, he has been receiving assistance in the form of Fellowship, House Rent Allowance (HRA) and Contingency.

The financial assistance received so far amounts to Rs 18,41,870, helping him meet essential academic and living expenses and continue his doctoral studies with greater confidence and stability.

The support has enabled him to purchase a laptop, obtain a reliable internet connection and acquire books, stationery and other essential research materials. It has also helped him meet conference and seminar registration fees, travel expenses and fieldwork costs. In particular, the assistance has made it possible for him to undertake intensive fieldwork, an important component of his research, while participating more actively in academic activities.

Today, Mr. Sayan Rai is able to devote greater attention to his Ph.D. research with reduced financial uncertainty. The fellowship has strengthened his academic productivity and confidence as a researcher while reducing his dependence on his family for educational and living expenses.

2334710.body_html:
Ministry of Communications
India Post and IndiGo Bring Digital Detox 2.0 to 15 Flights Across 11 Destinations, Spreading Festive Cheer Through Handwritten Postcards
Campaign celebrates the spirit of Diwali by reviving the personal touch of festive greetings in the digital age
Posted On: 10 NOV 2026 5:17PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Posts, Ministry of Communications, in collaboration with IndiGo, organised Digital Detox 2.0, the second edition of its in-flight postcard writing activity, following the enthusiastic response to its inaugural edition. Coinciding with the festive season, the initiative offered passengers a unique opportunity to convey heartfelt Diwali greetings to their loved ones through handwritten postcards.

 

The campaign was conducted across 15 IndiGo flights covering 11 destinations, including Chandigarh, Ranchi, Bagdogra, Delhi, Mumbai, Goa, Pune, Ahmedabad, Kolkata, Varanasi and Jaipur. Passengers were provided with specially designed Digital Detox kits containing postcards, greeting cards and DIY postcards through specially designed Diwali Stickers encouraging them to take a break from their screens and pen personalised festive messages.

Building on the success of its first edition, the initiative sought to revive the tradition of handwritten communication while promoting mindful engagement. By bringing the experience of letter writing to air travellers, the campaign highlighted the enduring charm of personal correspondence in an increasingly digital world.

Passengers warmly welcomed the initiative, sharing their memorable experiences of the campaign. One passenger remarked, “Writing a postcard at 30,000 feet was a wonderful experience and something I will remember for my lifetime.” Another participant shared, “This was my first time writing a postcard. It made me realise how special handwritten messages can be in an age of instant digital communication.” Appreciating the festive touch, another passenger said, “Sending Diwali wishes through a handwritten postcard felt much more personal and meaningful than a digital message.”

 

  

Through Digital Detox 2.0, India Post reaffirmed its commitment to innovative public outreach, celebrating the timeless tradition of connecting people through letters while adding a personal touch to Diwali celebrations.
