2334707.body_html:
Ministry of Home Affairs
Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) successfully concludes Special Campaign 6
Under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and guidance of Home Minister Shri Amit Shah, month-long campaign focused on disposal of pending matters, promoting cleanliness and efficient office management
Campaign also emphasized on addressing public grievances and improving functioning of MHA and its organisations
During the campaign, special emphasis laid on field and outstation offices having direct public interface
A total of 6757 sites were initially identified for the Swachhata campaign, which was subsequently expanded to cover 7,963 sites
147 references from Members of Parliament, 141 references from State Governments, 11,902 public grievances and 1,666 appeals were disposed of
2,19,644 physical files and 30,385 electronic files were reviewed, 78,125 square feet of office space was freed through effective record management and disposal of redundant material
Over ₹10.17 crore generated through the disposal of scrap, out of which ₹2.63 crore through e-waste disposal
Active involvement of CAPFs and other affiliated organisations further strengthened campaign and contributed significantly to its successful implementation
MHA reaffirms its commitment to sustain momentum generated by Special Campaign 6, with emphasis on efficient service delivery, accountability, cleanliness and promoting a positive work culture
Posted On: 10 NOV 2026 5:10PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) has successfully concluded Special Campaign 6 for Disposal of Pending Matters, conducted from 2nd to 31st October, 2026. Under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and guidance of Home Minister Shri Amit Shah, the month-long campaign focused on promoting cleanliness and efficient office management, expediting the disposal of pending matters, addressing public grievances and improving the overall functioning of the Ministry and its organisations. Special emphasis was laid on field and outstation offices having direct public interface.

Under Special Campaign 6, Ministry of Home Affairs achieved significant progress in disposal of pending matters, cleanliness and efficient office management. The campaign commenced with a preparatory phase on 15th September 2026, followed by its implementation from 2nd to 31st October 2026, across the Ministry of Home Affairs and its Attached and Subordinate Offices throughout the country.

The campaign was closely monitored at the highest level, with active participation from all Divisions of the Ministry, Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) and affiliated organisations. Regular progress reports were uploaded on the Special Campaign Portal, hosted by the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG).

A total of 6757 sites were initially identified for the Swachhata campaign, which was subsequently expanded to cover 7,963 sites. The major achievements of the campaign are as follows:

  • Disposal of references and grievances: 147 references from Members of Parliament, 141 references from State Governments, 11,902 public grievances and 1,666 appeals were disposed of.
  • Review of records: 2,19,644 physical files and 30,385 electronic files were reviewed.
  • Space management: 78,125 square feet of office space was freed through effective record management and disposal of redundant material.
  • Revenue generation: Over ₹10.17 crore was generated through the disposal of scrap, out of which ₹2.63 crore through e-waste disposal.
  • Social media outreach: Around 1,200 posts carrying the hashtag #SpecialCampaign6 were shared across various social media platforms, including X, Instagram, Facebook and YouTube, to create awareness and highlight the activities and achievements of the campaign.

As part of Special Campaign 6, a special one-day intensive drive was organised on 13th October 2026, with a focus on accelerating the achievement of campaign targets through coordinated efforts across the Ministry and its Attached and Subordinate Offices. The activities undertaken included tree plantation drives, intensive cleanliness campaigns and weeding out of old and redundant records, along with other initiatives aimed at promoting environmental sustainability, improving workplace cleanliness and ensuring efficient records management. The drive witnessed enthusiastic participation across the Ministry and its organisations, contributing significantly to the achievement of the campaign's objectives.

The Ministry of Home Affairs reaffirmed its commitment to sustaining the momentum generated by Special Campaign 6, with continued emphasis on efficient service delivery, accountability, cleanliness and the promotion of a positive work culture. The active involvement of CAPFs and other affiliated organisations further strengthened the campaign and contributed significantly to its successful implementation.

Special Campaign 6 has not only contributed to cleaner and more organised workplaces but has also reinforced a culture of responsibility, transparency and efficiency across the Ministry and its field formations. The initiative reflects the Ministry's continued commitment to responsive governance, effective public service delivery and the institutionalisation of good administrative practices.

2334642.title: Press Note on Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) Quarterly Bulletin July-September 2026
2334642.body_html:
Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation
Press Note on Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) Quarterly Bulletin July-September 2026
LFPR and WPR improved in both rural and urban areas
Rural UR declined
Gain in employment in agriculture sector in rural areas
Posted On: 10 NOV 2026 4:00PM by PIB Delhi

 

Snapshots:

  • The overall LFPR for persons (15+ years) reported an increase to 55.5% in July-September, 2026 compared to 54.6% in the previous quarter.
  • Rural LFPR (15+ years) recorded at 58.1%, an increase of 0.9 percentage points compared with same period of last year.
  • Overall WPR (15+ years) stood at 52.7% during July-September, 2026, registering an increase of 1.0 percentage point over the previous quarter.
  • Rural WPR increased by 1.4 percentage points quarter-on-quarter to 55.6% during July-September, 2026.
  • The share of regular wage/ salaried employment in urban areas reported an increase of 0.3 percentage points to 49.6% compared to the previous quarter.
  • During July-September, 2026 the share of self-employed in rural areas increased by 1.3 percentage points to 62.7% compared with last quarter.
  • Rural agricultural employment increased by 3.8 percentage points over the quarter to 56.7% during July-September, 2026.
  • Rural UR declined to 4.3% during July-September, 2026 from 4.8% in the previous quarter.       

 

  1. Introduction

The Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) conducted by NSO, MoSPI, is the primary source of data on activity participation and employment-unemployment conditions of the population. The PLFS survey methodology has been modified from January, 2025 to provide monthly and quarterly estimates of labour force indicators for both rural and urban India under the CWS framework.

Considering the need to generate high-frequency labour force indicators with wider coverage, the sampling methodology of the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) was revamped from January, 2025. The redesigned PLFS aims to achieve the following objectives:

    • To generate key employment and unemployment indicators – namely Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR), Worker Population Ratio (WPR) and Unemployment Rate (UR) – every month for both rural and urban areas at the all-India level under the Current Weekly Status (CWS).
    • To extend the Quarterly PLFS results to rural areas, thereby producing quarterly estimates of labour market indicators for both rural and urban India under the CWS framework.
    • To provide annual estimates of key employment and unemployment indicators in both Usual Status (ps+ss) and Current Weekly Status (CWS) for rural as well as urban areas.

Earlier PLFS Quarterly Bulletins released up to December, 2024, presented labour market indicators only for urban areas. The Bulletin for April – June, 2025 marked the first in the series to provide estimates for both rural and urban areas and the current Bulletin for July – September, 2026 is the sixth in the series. In this Quarterly Bulletin, efforts have also been made to provide estimates of the number of workers in absolute terms.

This Quarterly Bulletin presents estimates of key labour force indicators — Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR), Worker Population Ratio (WPR), Unemployment Rate (UR), and the distribution of workers by broad employment status and industry of work — in the Current Weekly Status (CWS), separately for rural and urban areas at the all-India level. In addition, state-level estimates of LFPR, WPR, and UR in CWS are also provided for selected States.

 

Key findings for persons of age 15 years and above following CWS:

  • Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR) improved in both rural and urban sectors: Overall LFPR for persons of age 15 years and above increased to 55.5% during July-September, 2026 from 54.6% in the previous quarter. The improvement was driven by an increase in LFPR for both the rural and urban areas. In rural areas, LFPR for persons of age 15 years and above rose to 58.1% in the current quarter from 56.9% in the previous quarter. Similarly, urban LFPR increased marginally to 50.4% from 50.2% during the same period.

The overall female LFPR increased to 34.7% during the current quarter from 33.2% in the previous quarter. Among male, the urban LFPR registered a marginal increase, reaching 77.3% during the quarter from 77.0% in the quarter April-June, 2026.

On a year-on-year basis, the overall LFPR recorded an increase of 0.4 percentage points, rising from 55.1% in July-September, 2025 to 55.5% in July-September, 2026. Rural LFPR also improved by 0.9 percentage points, increasing from 57.2% to 58.1% during the same period, while the urban LFPR declined marginally by 0.3 percentage points.  


 

Overall LFPR for persons aged 15 years and above stood at 55.5% during July-September 2026, registering an increase over both the previous quarter and the corresponding quarter of 2025

 

  • Workforce participation increased: Overall Worker Population Ratio (WPR) for persons of age 15 years and above increased to 52.7% during the quarter July-September, 2026, from 51.7% in the previous quarter. WPR in rural areas increased to 55.6% from 54.2% in the last quarter. In urban areas, WPR remained largely stable at 46.9% during July-September, 2026, compared with 46.8% in April-June, 2026. Among male, WPR increased to 73.4% in the current quarter from 73.0% in the previous quarter, while the female WPR rose notably to 32.8% from 31.3% over the same period.

In comparison with the corresponding quarter of the previous year, the overall WPR increased by 0.5 percentage points during July-September, 2026. Rural WPR also recorded an increase of 0.9 percentage points over the same period. Urban WPR maintained stability in the current quarter compared with the previous year.

Compared with the previous quarter, WPR improved for both male and female aged 15 years and above, reaching 73.4% and 32.8%, respectively, in July-September 2026.

 

  • Overall and rural Unemployment Rate (UR) declined: Overall UR for persons of age 15 years and above improved to 5.1% during the current quarter, compared with 5.4% in the previous quarter. During the same period, the rural UR fell to 4.3% from 4.8%, while urban UR remained broadly stable at 6.8 % against 6.7% in the previous quarter.

Compared with the corresponding quarter of 2025, the rural UR remained largely unchanged at 4.3% during July-September, 2026 compared with 4.4% during July-September, 2025. Rural male UR declined by 0.3 percentage points to 4.4% during July-September, 2026 from 4.7% during July-September, 20265. Urban UR registered marginal improvements for both male (6.2% to 6.1%) and female (9.0% to 8.8%) over the same period.

 

Overall UR for persons of age 15 years and above improved to 5.1% in July-September, 2026 compared to 5.4% in previous quarter.

  

  • Rural self-employment and urban regular wage/ salaried employment increased: The share of workers in rural areas engaged in self-employment increased to 62.7% in the current quarter from 61.4% in previous quarter. In urban areas, share of regular wage/ salaried workers increased to 49.6% from 49.3% in the previous quarter. In both rural and urban areas, the share of workers engaged in casual labour declined during July–September, 2026 compared with the previous quarter. In rural areas, it decreased from 22.5% to 21.7%, while in urban areas, it declined from 11.1% to 10.7%.

A year-on-year comparison indicates a reduction in the proportion of workers engaged in casual labour employment. In rural areas, the share declined by 0.5 percentage points from 22.2% in July-September, 2025 to 21.7% in July-September 2026. Similarly, in urban areas, it decreased marginally by 0.2 percentage points from 10.9% to 10.7% during the same period. In rural areas, share of workers in self-employment remained stable while regular wage/ salaried employment increased by 0.6 percentage points over the year. In urban areas, self-employment increased by 0.4 percentage point, while for regular wage/ salaried employment declined marginally in comparison with the same quarter of last year.  

 

 

The share of workers engaged in casual labour employment declined during July-September, 2026, both quarter-on-quarter and year-on-year

 

  • Share of agriculture sector increased in rural areas, tertiary sector remained stable in urban areas: The sectoral distribution of employment continued to reflect the distinct rural–urban employment patterns, with the rural workforce predominantly engaged in agriculture and the urban workforce concentrated in the tertiary sector. In rural areas, the share of workers engaged in agriculture increased from 52.9% in April–June, 2026 to 56.7% in July–September, 2026. The share of workers engaged in the secondary sector, including mining and quarrying, stood at 21.9% against 24.4% in the previous quarter. In the tertiary sector, it is estimated at 21.4% in the current quarter against 22.7% in the last quarter.

Compared with July–September, 2025, the share of rural workers engaged in the secondary sector, including mining and quarrying, increased from 21.0% to 21.9%, while the share in the tertiary sector remained broadly stable, increasing marginally from 21.3% to 21.4% in July–September, 2026. In urban areas, the share of workers engaged in secondary and tertiary sectors remained broadly stable.

 

Over the year, rural employment shares in the secondary sector rose from 21.0% to 21.9%, while the tertiary sector remained stable at around 21.4%


Using the projected population figures of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW), the absolute number of workers aged 15 years and above has been estimated. On average, 57.9 crore persons aged 15 years and above were employed in the country during the quarter July-September, 2026, of which 40.5 crore were male and 17.4 crore were female.

2334463.title: Union Minister of Minority Affairs & Parliamentary Affairs, Shri Kiren Rijiju visits Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.
2334463.body_html:
Ministry of Minority Affairs
Union Minister of Minority Affairs & Parliamentary Affairs, Shri Kiren Rijiju visits Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.
Posted On: 09 NOV 2026 8:19PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Minority Affairs & Parliamentary Affairs , Shri Kiren Rijiju paid an official visit to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia from 06–09 November 2026. The Indian delegation included the Joint Secretary (Haj), Ministry of Minority Affairs and the CEO, Haj Committee of India.

On 09 November 2026, the Union Minister held a bilateral meeting with H.E. Dr. Tawfiq bin Fawzan Al-Rabiah, Minister of Hajj and Umrah, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, at the Jeddah Superdome. The Ambassador of India to KSA and the Joint Secretary (Haj) participated in fruitful discussions on the arrangements for Haj-2027. The Ministers reviewed the ongoing preparations for Haj-2027, discussed measures to strengthen bilateral coordination and logistical support, and reaffirmed their shared commitment to a safe, smooth and comfortable pilgrimage for each and every Indian Haj pilgrim. Following the meeting, the two sides signed the Bilateral Haj Agreement between India and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia for Haj-2027 in Jeddah. The country quota for India was confirmed at 175,025.

Ministers noted that the strategic partnership between India and Saudi Arabia rests on long-standing historical ties and deep people-to-people links, and reaffirmed the spirit of collaboration in ensuring a successful and comfortable Haj experience for every Indian pilgrim. The Hon’ble Minister appreciated the successful conduct of Haj-2026 and assured the Saudi side of India’s full cooperation for the successful conduct of Haj-2027.

On 08 November 2026, Shri Rijiju attended the inaugural ceremony of the 6th Hajj Conference and Exhibition and participated in the Ministerial Conference chaired by H.E. Dr. Tawfiq Al-Rabiah, Minister of Hajj and Umrah, Saudi Arabia. He conveyed India’s appreciation for the Saudi leadership’s continued commitment to pilgrims’ welfare and reaffirmed India’s commitment to close bilateral cooperation for Haj-2027. He also joined visiting Ministers in an interaction with HRH Prince Saud bin Mishaal bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, the Deputy Governor of the Makkah Region.

During the visit, the Union Minister Shri Rijiju attended the Noor-e-Diwali celebration at India House, Jeddah, where he interacted with members of the Indian community and officials. He appreciated the Indian diaspora’s contribution in strengthening ties between the two nations, and commended their role as a living bridge of friendship and goodwill between India and Saudi Arabia. The Hon’ble Minister also chaired a review meeting with officials of the Consulate General of India, Ministry of Minority Affairs and Haj Committee of India to assess preparations for Haj-2027. He appreciated the coordinated efforts of all stakeholders and urged continued close coordination to ensure the comfort and welfare of Indian pilgrims. He also visited key Haj-related and cultural sites in Jeddah.

The visit marks a further strengthening of the longstanding India–Saudi Arabia partnership, reaffirming the shared commitment to enhanced bilateral cooperation in Haj management, pilgrim’s welfare, cultural exchange and people-to-people ties.

2334453.title: From Financial Challenges to Global Research Opportunities
2334453.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Financial Challenges to Global Research Opportunities
A Journey Towards Scientific Excellence
Posted On: 09 NOV 2026 7:41PM by PIB Delhi

Mr Aravind Kumar’s (name changed) journey demonstrates how timely educational and research assistance can help students from disadvantaged backgrounds overcome financial barriers, access international research opportunities and pursue academic excellence.

At 35, Mr. Kumar, a Scheduled Caste student from Tamil Nadu, has pursued his academic aspirations with determination and a strong commitment to scientific research.

After completing his M.Tech degree, he continued his academic journey with a keen interest in cancer biology, molecular research and the development of innovative therapeutic approaches for critical diseases.

His dedication towards scientific research led him to pursue doctoral studies at Tampere University, Finland, where he is currently enrolled in the first year of his Ph.D. programme in medical and molecular research. However, coming from a modest family background, he faced several financial and academic challenges while pursuing higher education abroad.

Managing research expenses, international training opportunities, conference participation and living costs created considerable financial pressure. Adapting to an advanced international research environment and accessing specialised experimental training opportunities also required sustained effort and perseverance.

The educational and research financial assistance provided under the Government's scheme has played an important role in supporting his academic journey. The assistance has significantly reduced the financial burden associated with research activities, scientific training and academic development, enabling him to continue his doctoral studies with greater confidence and stability.

Alongside his academic pursuits, the support has enabled him to strengthen his research capabilities, participate in scientific collaborations and access advanced research-related opportunities.

He is currently actively involved in experimental cancer research and international scientific training related to animal model development, molecular signalling and therapeutic approaches for glioblastoma and other brain cancer-related disorders. These opportunities have further strengthened his research skills and contributed to his academic progress.

Today, Mr. Aravind Kumar is progressing towards his aspiration of becoming an independent researcher and contributing to India's scientific advancement. His research interests in translational medical science, molecular signalling and drug development reflect his commitment to developing innovative approaches to address critical health challenges.

It highlights the role of educational support in empowering aspiring researchers to contribute meaningfully to scientific innovation and national development.

2334440.title: From Addiction to Recovery
2334440.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Addiction to Recovery
A Journey Towards Self-Reliance
Posted On: 09 NOV 2026 7:11PM by PIB Delhi

At 32, Ramesh Kumar (name changed), a resident of Sultanpur district in Uttar Pradesh, faced significant challenges due to substance addiction. The condition adversely affected his physical and mental well-being, social relationships and economic stability.

His struggle created barriers to leading a stable and productive life. Despite these challenges, he remained hopeful of overcoming addiction, rebuilding his life and regaining his place in society with dignity.

The impact of addiction had also affected his family relationships and the trust he shared with those around him. He aspired to lead a healthy and responsible life, become financially independent and restore his relationships with his family and community.

A significant turning point came through the intervention of the Drug De-addiction Centre (DDAC), Sultanpur, supported under the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR) of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.

The centre provided him with medical treatment, rehabilitation facilities, timely medicines, healthcare services, safe accommodation and other essential facilities required during his recovery.

Alongside medical care, he received continuous counselling, motivation, yoga sessions and emotional guidance. This sustained support brought positive changes in his mindset, behaviour and lifestyle, helping him overcome addiction.

The encouragement and care provided by the centre also helped him rebuild his confidence, improve social relationships and reintegrate into society with dignity.

Today, Ramesh Kumar has made significant progress towards leading a stable and self-reliant life. He has started his own business, improving his economic condition and achieving financial stability compared to his earlier struggles. He is now living responsibly and has regained social respect and confidence.

Expressing gratitude for the support and guidance received from the centre, he acknowledges its important role in helping him rebuild his life.

His journey reflects how timely medical intervention, sustained rehabilitation, counselling and emotional support can help individuals overcome substance dependence and move towards a life of dignity, independence and social reintegration.

2334438.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Educational Support to Academic Excellence Through the NFSC Fellowship
Posted On: 09 NOV 2026 7:10PM by PIB Delhi

Dr. Amit Kumar, (name changed), as on date, is able to contribute to the economic and social well-being of his family. His journey reflects how timely financial and academic support can help students from economically weaker rural backgrounds overcome barriers, pursue higher education and translate their aspirations into meaningful professional achievements.

At 37, Dr. Amit Kumar has established himself as an Assistant Professor, reflecting a journey shaped by determination and the support received through the National Fellowship for Scheduled Caste Students (NFSC) Scheme.

He faced financial, educational and social challenges while pursuing higher studies. His experience highlights the role of fellowship assistance in reducing financial barriers and enabling students to work towards their academic and professional aspirations.

Limited access to quality education, financial instability, inadequate transportation facilities and restricted opportunities created significant hurdles in his educational journey. Despite these constraints, he remained committed to pursuing higher education, achieving financial independence and supporting his family.

A significant turning point came through the NFSC Scheme of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. The financial assistance and academic support enabled him to continue his higher education and research without undue financial strain. It helped him meet research-related expenses, purchase study materials and address other essential educational needs.

In 2024, following his upgradation from Junior Research Fellow (JRF) to Senior Research Fellow (SRF), he received additional government financial assistance of approximately ₹50,000. This support further strengthened his financial position and helped him continue his academic pursuits.

The assistance contributed to improved academic and professional opportunities, helping him move towards greater financial stability.

2334427.title: Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah inaugurates and lays foundation stones for various development works worth approximately ₹1,400 crore in Ahmedabad
2334427.body_html:
Ministry of Home Affairs
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah inaugurates and lays foundation stones for various development works worth approximately ₹1,400 crore in Ahmedabad
Of these, projects worth ₹1,100 crore were undertaken by AMC, while projects worth ₹400 crore were carried out with the support of the Government of Gujarat and the Government of India
Under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and Chief Minister of Gujarat, development initiatives in the state are progressing at a rapid pace
After a 'Naxal-free India,' Modi government now aims at creating a 'Drug-free India' by December 31, 2029; we must take the responsibility to make Gujarat drug-free a year ahead of that target
Report any information regarding the sale or consumption of drugs by calling 1033; the identity of the informant will remain confidential, and strict action will be taken
Teachers should arrange for testing and consult with parents as soon as they notice changes in a child's behavior; every citizen should also take the responsibility to report any drug-related activity in their vicinity
De-addiction centers are being established for youth struggling with substance abuse; there is no need to feel ashamed about seeking treatment, and the identities of those affected will not be made public
Cooperation of citizens, teachers and parents is essential to create a 'Drug-free Gujarat' and a 'Drug-free India'
For decades, poor voted for the opposition party, yet they never got homes; today, those same individuals are being moved out of slums and provided with well-built flats
The opposition party, which governed the country and Gujarat from 1947 to 1995, never showed any concern for areas like 'Ramapir No Tekro' in Ahmedabad
In the Gandhinagar Lok Sabha constituency, development projects worth ₹25,000 crore have been completed over the last seven years
We are committed to realizing the vision of a "Green Gandhinagar Lok Sabha, Developed Gandhinagar Lok Sabha"
Union Home Minister extended his best wishes to the people of Gujarat for Diwali and the upcoming Gujarati New Year ('Bestu Varas')
Posted On: 09 NOV 2026 6:43PM by PIB Delhi

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah today inaugurated and laid the foundation stone for various development projects worth approximately ₹1,400 crore in Ahmedabad, Gujarat. Gujarat Chief Minister Shri Bhupendra Patel and several other dignitaries were present on the occasion.

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that development works worth approximately ₹1,400 crore were inaugurated and their foundation stones laid today. Of these, works worth around ₹1,024 crore have been undertaken by the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation (AMC), while projects worth approximately ₹400 crore have been completed or initiated through the Gujarat Government’s Roads and Buildings Department and the Government of India.

Shri Amit Shah said that in 2007, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi had launched a scheme to provide permanent houses to people living in slums, which is now being taken forward by Chief Minister Shri Bhupendra Patel. He added that the residents of Ramapir No Tekro are now being provided with beautiful private flats. He said that once the entire project is implemented, more than 55,000 people will have access to social security, recreational, educational and healthcare facilities within a single complex. Shri Shah further said that Prime Minister Modi had launched a scheme to rehabilitate nearly one lakh slum dwellers in Ahmedabad by providing them with permanent houses, and the Chief Minister and the Gujarat Government are successfully taking this initiative forward.

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that the Opposition party, which ruled the country and Gujarat from 1947 to 1995, never paid attention to areas like Ramapir No Tekro. He said that the poor continued to vote for the Opposition party for a long time, but their houses were never built. He said that the process of change began in 1995 with the election of the first councilor, and in 2012, he himself was elected as the MLA from this constituency.

Shri Amit Shah urged the residents of Ramapir Ka Tila to give priority to their children's education. Referring to the inauguration of two primary schools today, he said that the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation has transformed all the primary schools in the area into smart schools. He added that the Primary Education Committees of the Gandhinagar Lok Sabha constituency have also converted schools into smart schools.

Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that the foundation stone for the construction of a pump house to facilitate the drainage of rainwater in the Bopal-Ghuma area was laid today. He said that he has been associated with this area for the past 30 years and had promised that a system would be put in place before 2029 to ensure that the area never faces waterlogging. Shri Shah said that work on the four-kilometre-long ISKCON overbridge also commenced today. He said that earlier, it used to take two and a half hours to travel from Sarkhej to Gandhinagar. However, once the project is completed in three years, people will be able to cover this distance in a much shorter time through a signal-free overbridge. He added that very few cities in the world have such modern infrastructure. He further said that the Jalasapur Water Treatment Plant was also inaugurated today.

The Home Minister said that, including the projects undertaken today, development works worth ₹25,000 crore have been completed in the Gandhinagar Lok Sabha constituency over the past seven years. He reiterated his commitment to realising the vision of a “Green Gandhinagar & Developed Gandhinagar” Lok Sabha Constituency.

Shri Amit Shah referred to the joint meeting held last Saturday between the Union Ministry of Home Affairs and the Home Department of Gujarat, during which discussions were held on the implementation of the Naveen Nyay Sanhitas (new criminal laws), modernisation of the Home Department and making Gujarat drug-free. He informed the gathering about the 1033 helpline number and said that anyone reporting the sale or consumption of drugs through 1033 would have their identity kept confidential and strict action would be taken.

The Home Minister described drug abuse as something that destroys the physical and mental health, as well as the concentration of young people, and promotes terrorism. Shri Shah said that after achieving the goal of a Naxal-free India, the Modi Government has now set a target of making a ‘Drug-Free India’ by December 31, 2029. He appealed to everyone to take responsibility for making a ‘Drug-free Gujarat’ before December 31, 2028. Shri Shah urged teachers to arrange tests and meet parents whenever they notice changes in a child's behaviour in the classroom. He also appealed to parents and citizens to fulfil their responsibility by reporting any information about drug-related activities in their neighbourhood. He said that de-addiction centres are being established for young people struggling with drug addiction. He emphasised that there should be no hesitation or shame in seeking treatment for drug addiction. He assured that the identities of such young people would also be kept confidential.

Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah emphasised that the fight to make Gujarat and India drug-free cannot be fought by the Government alone. The cooperation of citizens, teachers and parents is essential. He said that a control room would become operational from December 1, with a mechanism in place to ensure action within three hours of receiving any information related to drugs. Shri Shah said that a scientific mechanism has been developed for this purpose. Arrangements have also been made to ensure that the kingpins and operatives involved in the drug trade are sent to jail. Giving a guarantee on behalf of the Prime Minister and the Chief Minister, he said that the Government would not take even a single step back in its fight against the drug trade. During the programme, he also administered a pledge to local residents to actively contribute towards making Gujarat drug-free.

On the occasion, Union Home Minister also extended his greetings to the people of Gujarat on Diwali and the Gujarati New Year (Bestu Varas), which begins tomorrow.

2334417.title: MY Bharat-NSS Organises Nationwide ‘Diwali Sneh Milan’ to Promote Substance Abuse-Free Festive Celebrations
2334417.ministry: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
2334417.body_html:
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
MY Bharat-NSS Organises Nationwide ‘Diwali Sneh Milan’ to Promote Substance Abuse-Free Festive Celebrations
Posted On: 09 NOV 2026 6:23PM by PIB Delhi

MY Bharat-National Service Scheme (NSS) organised nationwide ‘Diwali Sneh Milan’ celebrations across 153 institutions under the Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat 100 Week Sankalp Abhiyan, recording 1,07,494 participations. The eighth weekly intervention marked the conclusion of the campaign's second month and brought together young people, families and community members to promote an addiction-free Diwali through community gatherings, cultural activities, collective pledges and voluntary service.

The initiative sought to extend the message of substance abuse prevention beyond educational institutions to homes and neighbourhoods, encouraging families and communities to take collective responsibility for promoting healthy choices and responsible festive celebrations. Activities at the remaining institutions will be held after the vacation period.

As part of the Nasha Mukt Deepotsav, volunteers, community elders and children lit earthen diyas, symbolising the victory of light over the darkness of addiction. The Deepotsav and Sneh Milan gatherings together engaged over 41,600 participants, using the festive occasion to promote community participation in substance abuse prevention.

Participating institutions organised Nukkad Nataks in regional languages, along with Rangoli-making activities and Nasha Mukt songs. These cultural programmes engaged over 24,100 participants and used traditional and creative forms of expression to communicate the importance of preventing substance abuse and adopting healthy lifestyles.

The collective ‘Addiction-Free Diwali Sankalp’ was a key component of the gatherings, with nearly 25,000 individuals and family members pledging to celebrate Diwali without intoxicants. The pledge encouraged families to adopt responsible festive practices and support young people in making healthy choices.

 

In keeping with the NSS motto, ‘Not Me, But You’, volunteers combined festive celebrations with community service. Under the Seva vertical, over 16,700 volunteers visited old-age homes, orphanages, hospitals and slum areas, distributing diyas and sweets. The outreach reflected the values of compassion, inclusivity and service to society.

Youth volunteers also used digital platforms to extend the campaign's reach. More than 1,100 social media posts and reels, specifically featuring the mandatory Nukkad Nataks, were uploaded on Instagram using the hashtag #NashaMuktYuva to spread the message of an addiction-free Diwali.

2334410.title: Indian Railways Successfully Concludes Special Campaign 6; Over 1 Lakh Cleanliness Drives Conducted
2334410.body_html:
Ministry of Railways
Indian Railways Successfully Concludes Special Campaign 6; Over 1 Lakh Cleanliness Drives Conducted
Generates ₹628.49 Crore Through Scrap Disposal, Surpassing the Target of ₹600 Crore
Rail Jan Samvad Organised at 5,884 Railway Stations to Strengthen Citizen Engagement
Posted On: 09 NOV 2026 6:10PM by PIB Delhi

Indian Railways successfully concluded Special Campaign 6 from 2nd to 31st October 2026 across Zonal Railways, Divisions, Production Units, Public Sector Undertakings and other railway establishments. The campaign recorded significant achievements in cleanliness, scrap disposal, e-waste management, space management, record management and timely disposal of pending matters.

As part of the campaign, over 1 lakh cleanliness drives were conducted across railway stations, offices, workshops and other railway establishments. Indian Railways generated ₹628.49 crore through scrap disposal, exceeding the target of ₹600 crore. The campaign also facilitated the freeing up of 6,20,121 square feet of space through the removal of scrap, obsolete materials and other unwanted items.

This year’s campaign placed special emphasis on “Effective Collection, Segregation and Disposal of E-waste”, the focus area of this year’s campaign. In a significant step towards responsible waste management, more than 1.50 lakh units of e-waste were disposed of, generating revenue of ₹10.43 crore.

Besides, Indian Railways undertook various activities, including a comprehensive review of old physical and electronic files, disposal of public grievances and appeals, Parliamentary assurances, VIP references and other pending matters. Significant achievements were recorded in these areas. These initiatives were aimed at improving record management, reducing pendency, and fostering a cleaner, more organized and efficient working environment. 

Rail Jan Samvad Strengthens Citizen Engagement

Indian Railways organised Rail Jan Samvad to facilitate direct interaction between senior railway officials and rail users as part of Special Campaign 6. A nationwide Rail Jan Samvad programme was conducted simultaneously at 5,884 railway stations on 22nd October 2026, providing passengers an opportunity to share their feedback and suggestions directly with railway officials.

The successful conclusion of Special Campaign 6 reflects Indian Railways' continued commitment to maintaining cleanliness across railway establishments, ensuring efficient utilisation of resources, promoting responsible waste disposal, improving record management and facilitating the timely resolution of pending matters. These initiatives further strengthen administrative efficiency and citizen-centric governance across Indian Railways.

2334385.title: Delhi Set to Get Its First Recreational Yamuna Cruise Service
2334385.ministry: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
2334385.body_html:
Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
Delhi Set to Get Its First Recreational Yamuna Cruise Service
Sarbananda Sonowal to Inaugurate it Tomorrow in presence of Delhi Lt Governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu & CM Rekha Gupta
Posted On: 09 NOV 2026 5:11PM by PIB Delhi

Delhi is set to add a new attraction to its tourism landscape with the launch of a recreational river cruise service along the Yamuna. Sarbananda Sonowal, Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways in presence of Lieutenant Governor Sardar Taranjit Singh Sandhu and Chief Minister of Delhi, Smt Rekha Gupta will inaugurate the service tomorrow (Tuesday, November 10, 2026), at Sonia Vihar. Developed along the Sonia Vihar-Jagatpur stretch of the river, the initiative aims to promote river-based tourism and offer visitors a new recreational experience in the national capital.
The inauguration ceremony will witness the presence of Shri Shantanu Thakur, Minister of State for Ports, Shipping and Waterways; Shri Harsh Malhotra, Minister of State for Road Transport and Highways. Delhi Government Ministers, including Shri Parvesh Sahib Singh, Minister for Public Works Department and Irrigation and Flood Control, and Shri Kapil Mishra, Tourism Minister, will also attend the event, along with Shri Manoj Tiwari, Member of Parliament, and senior officials of the Central and Delhi Governments.

The River Yamuna has been designated as National Waterway-110 under the National Waterways Act, 2016. The development of the recreational river cruise service along the Sonia Vihar-Jagatpur stretch of the Yamuna river in Delhi marks an important step towards harnessing the potential of this National Waterway for recreational navigation and river-based tourism. Ahead of the launch, trial runs of the cruise vessel were successfully conducted last month in the presence of senior officials from IWAI and the Delhi Government.

Spearheaded by the Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI) under the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, Government of India, the initiative reflects the Authority's commitment to promoting sustainable inland water transport and developing waterways as an integral component of urban mobility and tourism infrastructure.

The initiative is expected to offer Delhi residents and tourists a unique experience while fostering greater public engagement with the Yamuna. The use of electric-powered cruise vessels will also demonstrate the potential of inland waterways in promoting clean and sustainable mobility, while adding a new recreational attraction to the National Capital Region.

The Recreational Yamuna River Cruise Service is being developed by the Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI), under the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways (MoPSW), in collaboration with the Delhi Development Authority (DDA), Delhi Tourism and Transportation Development Corporation (DTTDC), Delhi Jal Board (DJB), and the Irrigation and Flood Control Department, Government of Delhi.

2334375.title: INDIAN NAVY TO CONDUCT PASSING OUT PARADE OF LARGEST BATCH OF AGNIVEERS AT INS CHILKA
2334375.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
INDIAN NAVY TO CONDUCT PASSING OUT PARADE OF LARGEST BATCH OF AGNIVEERS AT INS CHILKA
Posted On: 09 NOV 2026 4:47PM by PIB Delhi

INS Chilka, the Indian Navy’s premier ab-initio training establishment, will conduct the Passing Out Parade (POP) of the ninth batch of Agniveers of the Indian Navy and Naviks of the Indian Coast Guard on 13 Nov 2026. Adm Krishna Swaminathan, Chief of the Naval Staff, will be the Chief Guest and Reviewing Officer of the Parade.

The parade will mark the successful completion of 16 weeks of ab-initio training by over 3,300 trainees, making it the largest batch to pass out from INS Chilka. The parade will mark the culmination of an intensive training programme designed to transform young recruits into disciplined, physically agile, mentally resilient and professionally competent sea warriors.

The training curriculum integrates academics, physical conditioning, swimming, parade training, outdoor activities and camp, providing a holistic foundation for the trainees' professional journey. Equal emphasis is laid on character building, leadership, discipline, camaraderie and teamwork, while instilling the core naval values of Duty, Honour and Courage.

The Passing Out Parade will be a moment of pride and accomplishment for the trainees, as their families witness the culmination of training journey and beginning of a new career. Besides this, Naval veterans and distinguished guests will also be present for the occasion.

The Valedictory Function will be presided over by VAdm Sameer Saxena, Flag Officer Commanding-in-Chief, Southern Naval Command. Awards will be presented to meritorious trainees, the champion division and best instructor in recognition of their exemplary performance and contribution to training. The event will also witness the unveiling of ‘Ankur’, the bilingual trainees’ magazine.

The Passing Out Parade will be streamed live on the Indian Navy’s official social media platforms, enabling citizens across the country to witness the occasion.

2334371.title: Ministry of Power Successfully Concludes Special Campaign 6 for Disposal of Pending Matters and Cleanliness Drive
2334371.body_html:
Ministry of Power
Ministry of Power Successfully Concludes Special Campaign 6 for Disposal of Pending Matters and Cleanliness Drive
Over 2.5 Lakh Sq. Feet Office Space Freed in 342 Cleanliness Drives
Waste Disposal Generated Revenue of Rs 15.74 Crores
Posted On: 09 NOV 2026 4:40PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Power successfully concluded the Special Campaign 6 for the Disposal of Pending Matters, conducted from October 2 to October 31, 2026. The Special Campaign aimed at promoting cleanliness streamlining work, addressing pending grievances across the Ministry’s PSUs and organizations under it.

During the implementation phase of Special Campaign 6, observed from 2 October to 31 October 2026, Ministry of Power and its CPSEs/Organisations undertook various activities including comprehensive review of old physical and electronic files, identified unserviceable items, scrap and e-waste, and initiated measures for their proper disposal. These activities aimed at freeing up office space, improving record management and promoting cleaner, well-organised and efficient workplaces.

Special Focus on E-Waste Management

In line with this year's theme, special attention was given to the effective collection, segregation and disposal of e-waste across offices under Ministry of Power. The CPSEs/Organisations identified e-waste generated at their respective establishments and took necessary steps for its segregation and disposal in accordance with the E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022.

   

 

Disposal of E-waste at the premises of Powergrid, one of the PSUs under Ministry of Power

The initiative helped to ensure proper handling of e-waste and promote responsible waste management practices across the CPSEs/organisations under the Ministry.


 

Before                                                                                   After

 

During the campaign, the Ministry achieved significant milestones, including the completion of 342 cleanliness drives at various locations, resulting in 2,51,757 sq. ft. of freed space. Additionally, a revenue of ₹15,74,20,231 was generated through the disposal of scrap materials and e-waste.

In terms of Record Management, the Ministry reviewed 26,885 physical files, weeded out 13,282 files as per the provision of Record Management, and reviewed 34,572 e-files, of which 34,525 were closed.

  

The Ministry also made best efforts to meet the targets, achieving 33 out of 46 MP references, 3 out of 4 IMC references, 7 out of 7 PMO References and 4 out of 11 State Government references. Further, the Ministry effectively resolved 1589 public grievances (exceeding set target) and 86 grievance appeals (exceeding set target) during the campaign period.

Under the guidance of the Secretary (P), the progress of Special Campaign 6 was closely monitored, ensuring consistent momentum toward achieving the Ministry’s targets. Active participation from officers from the Ministry and its PSUs/ Organisations was instrumental in driving the campaign’s success.

To raise awareness and to give wide coverage, social media posts were posted on different social media handles, i.e X(formerly Twitter), Instagram, Facebook,  LinkedIn, etc., highlighting the significant activities undertaken by the Ministry along with its CPSEs/organisations under the Special Campaign 6.

2334365.title: TRAI releases “The Telecommunication Interconnection (Port Charges) (Third Amendment) Regulations, 2026”
2334365.body_html:
Ministry of Communications
TRAI releases “The Telecommunication Interconnection (Port Charges) (Third Amendment) Regulations, 2026”
Posted On: 09 NOV 2026 4:24PM by PIB Delhi

The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) today released “The Telecommunication Interconnection (Port Charges) (Third Amendment) Regulations, 2026”. These amendments introduce a framework for port charges for IP-based interconnection, supplementing the existing provisions applicable to ports for E1/TDM-based interconnection. These regulations will take effect from 1st January 2027.

Interconnection in telecommunications refers to the technical, operational, and commercial arrangements that connect two or more telecom networks, allowing telecommunications traffic to flow between them and enabling users of different service providers to communicate seamlessly. Section 11(1)(b) of the TRAI Act, 1997, inter alia, empowers TRAI to prescribe the terms and conditions of interconnection between service providers, and to ensure technical compatibility and effective interconnection between different service providers.

The Telecommunication Interconnection (Port Charges) Regulation, 2001 prescribes the charges payable by an interconnection seeker to an interconnection provider for terminating interconnection links at its point of interconnection. The extant regulations were based on legacy E1/TDM-based port technologies, and the charges prescribed therein were last revised in 2012.

To ensure that the existing regulatory framework governing interconnection matters remains relevant, transparent, and conducive to efficient interconnection between service providers, TRAI initiated a review of the regulatory framework through a Pre-Consultation Paper on the “Review of the existing TRAI Regulations on Interconnection matters”, dated 03.04.2025. Through this Pre-Consultation Paper, stakeholders’ comments were sought, inter alia, to review the Telecommunication Interconnection (Port Charges) Regulation, 2001.

Subsequently, a Consultation Paper on the “Review of the existing TRAI Regulations on Interconnection matters”, providing the background information and taking into account the stakeholders’ comments received during the pre-consultation process, was issued on 10.11.2025. Through the Consultation Paper, stakeholders’ comments were sought, inter alia, to review the Telecommunication Interconnection (Port Charges) Regulation, 2001. After extension, the last dates for furnishing written comments and counter-comments were 15.12.2025 and 29.12.2025, respectively.

In response to the issues raised in the Consultation Paper, seventeen stakeholders submitted their comments, while nine stakeholders submitted counter-comments. As part of the consultation process, an Open House Discussion (OHD) on the Consultation Paper was held on 28.01.2026. Based on the comments received from stakeholders during the consultation process, and its own analysis, TRAI has finalised the Telecommunication Interconnection (Port Charges) (Third Amendment) Regulations, 2026.

The salient points of the amendment regulations are given below:

  1. Recognition of IP ports: The definition of “Port” has been revised to include both legacy E1 ports (2.048 Mbps) and IP ports, with bandwidth expressed in Mbps or Gbps.
  2. Ceiling on annual IP-port charges: Annual ceilings on IP-port charges have been prescribed at ₹5.6 lakh per 1 Gbps IP port and ₹42.3 lakh per 10 Gbps IP port.
  3. Flexibility in interconnection arrangements: Interconnection providers and seekers may mutually agree to charges below the prescribed ceilings. They may also mutually agree to IP-port capacities other than 1 Gbps and 10 Gbps, with charges determined transparently using the same methodology as for 1 Gbps and 10 Gbps ports.
  4. Uniformity across services: IP-port charges apply uniformly across fixed-line, mobile, national long-distance and international long-distance services. The charges prescribed earlier shall continue to apply only to E1 ports.
  5. Graded framework for financial disincentives: For effective implementation of the regulations, a graded financial disincentive framework with a ceiling of ₹15 lakh per Service Area for each instance of contravention has been prescribed for contravention of specified provisions of these regulations.

The amendment regulations align the regulatory provisions with technological advancements and sectoral developments. They are expected to strengthen the interconnection framework and facilitate seamless communication across telecom networks. The regulatory framework aims to provide greater regulatory certainty to service providers while upholding the principles of effective interconnection, transparency, non-discrimination, and fair competition.

The full text of “The Telecommunication Interconnection (Port Charges) (Third Amendment) Regulations, 2026”, along with the Explanatory Memorandum, is available on TRAI’s website www.trai.gov.in.

For any clarification/ information, Shri Sameer Gupta, Advisor (Networks, Spectrum & Licensing-I), TRAI may be contacted at email ID: adv-nsl1@trai.gov.in or telephone number +91-11-20907752.

2334364.title: TRAI Assesses Mobile Network Quality across Railway route between New Tinsukia Railway station and Guwahati Railway station under Assam LSA
2334364.body_html:
Ministry of Communications
TRAI Assesses Mobile Network Quality across Railway route between New Tinsukia Railway station and Guwahati Railway station under Assam LSA
Posted On: 09 NOV 2026 4:20PM by PIB Delhi

The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has released findings of Independent Drive Test (IDT) conducted across Railway route between New Tinsukia Railway station and Guwahati Railway station in the state of Assam under Assam LSA, during the month of September 2026, for information of general telecom consumers. The purpose of this drive test is to assess and verify real time quality of mobile network services (both voice & data) provided by Telecom Service Providers (TSPs). During the IDT, TRAI captures performance of TSPs for key Quality of Service (QoS) parameters like Coverage, Call Drop Rate (CDR), Call Setup Success Rate (CSSR), data Download (DL) and Upload (UL) throughput etc., which are then published to inform Consumers and encourage TSPs to improve their services.

This IDT has been designed to capture on ground mobile network performance of all TSPs across diverse usages environment like cities, hotspots, public transport hubs, etc. In this type of drive testing, live data and voice sessions are established using SIM cards from all TSPs over 2G, 3G, 4G, and 5G networks. Multiple advanced test handsets are used, and the sessions are monitored and analysed in real-time using advanced Software Systems.

TRAI, through its appointed agency, conducted drive tests across Railway – 515.9 KMs, Hotspot locations - 2, in Assam state on 11th September 2026 in Assam LSA. These tests were conducted under the supervision of the TRAI Regional Office Kolkata. The observations presented in drive test reports represent the performance of the TSPs on the area/ route under test on the day/ time of conducting the drive test.

Drive Test Route Map: The following map provides overview of drive test routes indicating Railway, Hotspots as per the legends shown on the map: -

Key Parameters Assessed

  1. Coverage Gap: Percentage of samples, for which signal strength observed less than the minimum prescribed signal strength for respective technology (2G/ 3G/ 4G/ 5G).
  2. Voice Services: Call Setup Success Rate (CSSR), Drop Call Rate (DCR), Call Setup Time.
  3. Data Services: Download/ Upload Throughput, Latency, Jitter, Packet Drop Rate

The overall mobile network performance along the Railway route from New Tinsukia to Guwahati under Assam LSA for the key parameters has been summarised below: -

a)    Coverage Gap - The signal strength observed during voice testing on the Railway drive test route in auto-selection mode (5G/4G/3G/2G), measured as the number of samples having poor signal strength out of the total samples collected, was 4754 / 32385 for Airtel, 12486 /25698 for BSNL, 4808/ 33296 for RJIL and 12738 / 27285 for VIL. Details of the coverage gaps have been provided in the map Annexed.

b)    Dropped Calls - Dropped calls, measured as the number of dropped calls out of the number of successfully established calls, were 5/ 166 for Airtel, 65/ 205 for BSNL, 9/ 175 for RJIL and 34/ 164 for VIL. Details of the dropped call locations have been provided in the map Annexed.

c)    Data Download and Upload Throughput:

i)  Data Download performance (Overall): Average download speed was observed as 42.71 Mbps for Airtel (5G/4G), 5.00 Mbps for BSNL (4G/2G), 110.82 Mbps for RJIL (5G/4G) and 15.69 Mbps for VIL (4G/2G). Detail of Download throughput has been provided in the map Annexed.

ii) Data Upload performance (Overall): Average upload speed was observed as 11.75 Mbps for Airtel (5G/4G), 3.25 Mbps for BSNL (4G/ 2G), 8.29 Mbps for RJIL (5G/4G) and 5.46 Mbps for VIL (4G/2G). Detail of Upload throughput has been provided in the map Annexed.

Locations of Dropped Calls and Call Silence instances can be seen by clicking red dot on the map Annexed.

Details of drive test route and area covered during the IDT is as under: -

a)    Railway - The areas covered in the Railway drive are (i) New Tinsukia to Guwahati passing through Simaluguri Junction, (ii) Mariani Junction, (iii) Furkating Junction, (iv) Dimapur, (v) Diphu, (vi) Lumding Junction

b)   Hotspot - The hot spot locations, capturing stationary user experience, are (i) Guwahati Railway Station, (ii) New Tinsukia Railway Station.       

The findings of this IDT report have been shared with respective TSPs for taking further necessary action at their end. Detailed reports of IDT are made available on the TRAI website at www.trai.gov.in. For any clarification or additional information, an email can be sent to adv.kolkata@trai.gov.in or Regional Office of TRAI at Kolkata RO can be contacted on telephone no.  +91-33-22361401.

2334330.title: Department of Legal Affairs Achieves Significant Milestones under Special Campaign 6; Reviews Over 27,000 Physical Files, Disposes of 15,679 Files and Generates ₹4.71 Lakh through Scrap Disposal
2334330.body_html:
Ministry of Law and Justice
Department of Legal Affairs Achieves Significant Milestones under Special Campaign 6; Reviews Over 27,000 Physical Files, Disposes of 15,679 Files and Generates ₹4.71 Lakh through Scrap Disposal
Posted On: 09 NOV 2026 2:13PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Legal Affairs, Ministry of Law and Justice, Government of India, has undertaken a series of initiatives and activities under Special Campaign 6, reaffirming its commitment to efficient governance, institutional strengthening, environmental sustainability, transparency and citizen-centric administration.

During the preparatory phase, the Department deputed senior officers of the Department to visit field offices of the department to sensitise them about Swachhata Hi Sewa and Special Campaign 6.

During the implementation phase of the Special Campaign, the Department undertook a comprehensive range of activities encompassing cleanliness drives, disposal of pending references, review and weeding out of obsolete records, digitisation-oriented record management, disposal of redundant ICT and electrical equipment, space optimisation and effective grievance redressal. Special emphasis was also placed on systematic file management, reduction of administrative pendency, environmental protection and the creation of a clean, organised and productive workplace.

The campaign also provided an opportunity to strengthen institutional practices, encourage the active participation of officers and officials, promote the principles of Swachhata in day-to-day administration and ensure the responsible disposal of scrap and obsolete materials in accordance with the prescribed procedures.

Key Achievements during the Implementation Phase of the Special Campaign

The significant achievements of the Department during the campaign are highlighted below:

  1. Cleanliness and Swachhata Initiatives

A total of 30 cleanliness campaigns have been organised across the Department's offices and premises to promote workplace hygiene, cleanliness and environmental awareness. These initiatives contributed towards maintaining a clean, healthy and conducive working environment.

  1. Revenue Generation through Disposal of Scrap

Through the systematic identification and disposal of obsolete materials including e-waste, scrap and other unserviceable items, the Department generated revenue amounting to ₹4,71,881/-. This initiative facilitated the productive disposal of redundant resources while contributing to the efficient utilisation of Government assets.

  1. Efficient File Management and Reduction of Pendency

As part of the efforts to streamline official records and improve administrative efficiency, a total number of 27289 physical files against the target of 13523 files were reviewed, out of which 15679 files were weeded out. Similarly, total 20572 e-files against the target of 15188 files were reviewed, out of which 17798 files have been closed. The exercise has contributed to reducing unnecessary accumulation of records, improving file management practices and facilitating faster access to relevant official information.

  1. Disposal of Obsolete ICT and Electrical Equipment (e-Waste)

A total of 1,484 obsolete ICT and electrical items have been identified and weeded out against the target of 1418 items generating revenue to the tune of Rs.4.15 lakhs. This initiative has facilitated the removal of redundant equipment, improved the utilisation of office infrastructure and supported environmentally responsible disposal practices.

  1. Space Optimisation and Better Utilisation of Office Premises

The systematic disposal of obsolete records, scrap, redundant furniture and other unserviceable materials has resulted in the reclamation of 4,889 square feet of oce space. The freed-up space can be utilised more effectively for official purposes, thereby improving workplace organisation and operational efficiency.

  1. Effective Administration and Disposal of Important References

During the campaign, 58 references from Members of Parliament and 19 IMC references have been disposed of meeting 100 % target. Out of 14 parliamentary assurances, in 7 cases, Implementation Report has been uploaded on the OAMS Portal of Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs and 2 Parliamentary Assurances are under transfer to other Ministries / Departments. These efforts reflect the Department's commitment to expeditious handling of important official communications and strengthening accountability in administrative functioning.

  1. Public Grievance Redressal

Emphasising citizen-centric governance and responsive administration, the Department has taken steps towards the expeditious disposal of public grievances. A total of 534 public grievances have been disposed-o during the campaign against the target of 512 cases demonstrating its commitment to improving public service delivery and ensuring timely resolution of citizens' concerns.

Conclusion

The implementation of the Special Campaign has resulted in significant improvements in cleanliness, file management, disposal of obsolete materials, space optimisation, revenue generation and public grievance redressal in the Department of Legal Affairs.

The achievements reflect the Department's continued commitment to the principles of Swachhata, eciency, transparency, accountability and citizen-centric governance. The Department endeavours to sustain the momentum generated through the campaign by institutionalising best practices, ensuring regular monitoring and promoting continuous improvement in administrative functioning.

2334316.title: President of India to Confer 10th Edition Swachh Survekshan 2025-26 Awards
2334316.body_html:
Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs
President of India to Confer 10th Edition Swachh Survekshan 2025-26 Awards
Swachh Survekshan Awards to honour India’s cleanest cities
‘Swachh Shehar Jodi’ Top Performers to be honoured at Swachh Survekshan Awards 2025-26
Posted On: 09 NOV 2026 1:15PM by PIB Delhi

The President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu will confer Swachh Survekshan Awards 2025-26 at a ceremony to be held at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi on 11th November, 2026.

The 10th edition of the Swachh Survekshan on the theme of ‘Swachhata Ki Nayi Pehel- Badhayein Haath, Karein Safai Saath’ has been successfully completed. Under the aegis of the Department of Urban Development, Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, Swachh Survekshan (SS) Awards 2025-26 will honour India’s cleanest cities, celebrating their outstanding contributions to Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban. The President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu, will confer awards across various categories at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi, in the presence of Sh. Manohar Lal, Union Minister of MoHUA and Power and Sh. Tokhan Sahu, Minister of State, MoHUA.

The SS 2025-26 awards serve as a celebration of the collective achievements of cities and States in the past decade and a renewed commitment to sustain on-ground achievements.

Swachh Survekshan, SBM-U’s flagship cleanliness assessment, has grown in scale from 73 ULBs in 2016 to over 4,751 cities in its latest edition. Swachh Survekshan 2025-26 introduces several key enhancements, including greater emphasis on citizen feedback, expanded coverage of Urban River Fronts, Coastlines and Water bodies and focused indicators on prevention of open defection & open urination, cleanliness of tourist and heritage hotspots, and behaviour change initiatives in schools.

As part of the 10th edition of SS, Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) were evaluated across 43 indicators spanning 10 key assessment areas – Segregation, Collection & Transportation of Waste, Solid Waste Management, Visible Cleanliness, Access to Sanitation, Mechanisation of Desludging Services, Ecosystem Strengthening & Institutional Parameters, Used Water Management, Advocacy for Swachhata, Overall Welfare of Sanitation Workers & Citizen Feedback & Grievance Redressal . More than 3,000 trained assessors conducted extensive on-ground evaluations across the country, supported by real-time GPS-enabled monitoring. From evidence submission to verification, the assessment process remained fully digital, transparent, and subject to rigorous quality checks at every stage.

Alongside the top Swachh cities, this year’s awards also recognise top performers from the ‘Swachh Shehar Jodi’ initiative that has fostered peer learning between 70 mentor cities and 191 mentee cities across 33 States/UTs to accelerate urban waste management excellence. The ‘Swachh Shehar Jodi’ Initiative was launched by the Shri Manohar Lal, Hon’ble Union Minster, on 27th September 2025 as the first-ever urban waste management mentorship and peer-learning programme. At the launch event, a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was signed to commence this initiative between all mentor and mentee cities.

The performance of mentee cities has witnessed significant improvement across key Swachhata indicators between Swachh Survekshan 2024 and 2025. Notable improvements across mentee city performances has been recorded in the latest edition of Swachh Survekshan 2025-26. In the parameter of ‘Visible Cleanliness’ mentee cities have moved from 48% in SS 2024 to 70% in the latest edition. For ‘Door-to-Door Collection’, mentee cities were at 52% in SS 2024 and have now cumulatively reached 74%.  Mentee cities have also achieved notable improvements across key parameters such as: Source Segregation (from 16% to 30%), Access to Sanitation (from 11% to 38%), Used Water Management (from 32% to 53%), and Advocacy for Swachhata (from 48% to 66%), reflecting strengthened sanitation systems and improved service delivery outcomes through dedicated mentorship from high performing cities.

Following a year of dedicated efforts, healthy competition, and steadfast commitment to Swachhata, cities across the country now eagerly await the announcement of the Swachh Survekshan 2025-26 Award winners on 11 November, 2026.

2334306.title: INAUGURAL INDIA–MYANMAR BILATERAL TRI-SERVICES HADR EXERCISE ‘RAHAT MITRA’ CONCLUDES AT CHENNAI
2334306.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
INAUGURAL INDIA–MYANMAR BILATERAL TRI-SERVICES HADR EXERCISE ‘RAHAT MITRA’ CONCLUDES AT CHENNAI
Posted On: 09 NOV 2026 12:39PM by PIB Delhi

The inaugural bilateral Tri-Services Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR) Exercise ‘RAHAT MITRA’, conducted between the Defence Forces of India and Myanmar on 05 and 06 Nov 2026, concluded at Chennai. The two-day exercise brought together personnel from the Indian Navy, Indian Army and Indian Air Force, along with a delegation from the Myanmar Defence Forces, to enhance operational interoperability, improve coordination and facilitate the exchange of Best Practices in disaster response operations.

The exercise commenced with a focus on joint planning and familiarisation with HADR capabilities. A Table-Top Exercise (TTX), based on a severe cyclone scenario, facilitated discussions on coordinated response mechanisms and joint disaster management protocols. The participating contingents also witnessed demonstrations of obstacle clearance and bridge-laying capabilities by the Indian Army and visited INS Sukanya to gain insights into the Indian Navy’s shipborne HADR capabilities. (https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2333709 )

On the second day, the participating contingents witnessed demonstrations of multi-domain HADR capabilities by the Indian Defence Forces, highlighting coordinated response mechanisms across maritime, land and air domains. INS Adyar and Communication Network Centre, Chennai, showcased shore-based disaster response arrangements and communication infrastructure supporting command and control during emergencies. Military Hospital, Chennai, demonstrated field medical triage and the coordinated management of disaster relief camps.

The Indian Navy’s Flood Relief Teams (FRT) demonstrated specialised equipment and capabilities for flood relief operations. Maritime Search and Rescue (SAR) capabilities were also showcased through coordinated manoeuvres involving a Chetak helicopter and INS Bitra. The Indian Air Force demonstrated casualty evacuation capabilities, with Commodore Aung Niang Win and two officers of the Myanmar delegation onboard an IAF ALH during airborne operations.

Exercise ‘RAHAT MITRA’ provided an important platform for the Defence Forces of both countries to exchange operational experiences, share Best Practices and enhance mutual understanding in planning and executing HADR operations. The exercise also facilitated familiarisation with each other’s capabilities and procedures, contributing to improved coordination during disaster response operations.

The successful culmination of the inaugural exercise reinforces the commitment of India and Myanmar to advancing bilateral defence cooperation and enhancing collective preparedness for disaster response. It also underscores the shared resolve of both nations to contribute to regional stability, maritime cooperation and effective HADR.

2334268.title: Revised MRPs of 1,364 Anti-Cancer Formulations Come into Effect from Today
2334268.ministry: Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers : Department of Pharmaceuticals
2334268.body_html:
Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers :
Department of Pharmaceuticals
Revised MRPs of 1,364 Anti-Cancer Formulations Come into Effect from Today
Consumers to Save ₹3,540.38 Crore Annually
Posted On: 09 NOV 2026 11:51AM by PIB Delhi

The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA), under the Department of Pharmaceuticals, Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers, has capped trade margins on the Maximum Retail Price (MRP) of 137 anti-cancer drugs, based on the recommendations of an Expert Committee constituted by the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, on 17th October, 2026. The revised MRPs of these medicines come into effect from today, 9th November, 2026.

As on 8th of November, 2026, 85 Pharmaceutical Companies have reported revised MRPs for 1,364 anti-cancer formulations, covering 121 drugs. With 679 brands reporting price reductions of more than 50%. The highest reported reduction in MRP is 96.45%. As a result of the price reductions the estimated annual savings to consumers is expected to be ₹3,540.38 crore.

Consumers can check the revised MRP printed on the medicine pack and verify medicine prices through the Pharma Sahi Daam mobile app or NPPA website (nppa.gov.in). No chemist or hospital pharmacy can charge more than the revised MRP. In case of overcharging or any other pricing-related complaint, consumers can register their grievance through the Pharma Jan Samadhan portal or contact the NPPA helpline at 1800-111-255.

2334253.title: Sacred Relics of Shakyamuni Buddha Arrive at Thubchog Gatsel Ling (TGL) Monastery, Bomdila, on 8th November
2334253.body_html:
Ministry of Culture
Sacred Relics of Shakyamuni Buddha Arrive at Thubchog Gatsel Ling (TGL) Monastery, Bomdila, on 8th November
Sacred Relics Enshrined at the Monastery; Public Darshan from 8 to 13 November 2026
Posted On: 09 NOV 2026 10:38AM by PIB Delhi

The Sacred Relics of Shakyamuni Buddha  arrived at Thubchog Gatsel Ling (TGL) Monastery (Lower Gompa), Bomdila, Arunachal Pradesh, on 8 November 2026 and were enshrined at the monastery for public darshan. The Sacred Relics will be available for public darshan from 8 to 13 November 2026. The exposition is being organised by the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, in collaboration with the National Museum  New Delhi, Government of Arunachal Pradesh and the International Buddhist Confederation (IBC), New Delhi.

The first day of the public exposition on 8 November witnessed an encouraging response, with around 4,000 devotees visiting the monastery to have darshan of the Sacred Relics. Buddhist monks, dignitaries, senior citizens and persons with disabilities also offered prayers and paid their respects. From 9 to 13 November 2026, devotees from Bomdila constituency and neighbouring constituencies are scheduled to visit the monastery,  to offer prayers and seek blessings.

The Sacred Relics were transported from Tawang to Bomdila aboard an Indian Air Force Chinook helicopter, accompanied by Shri Bhikkhu Khemachara, Deputy Secretary General (DSG), IBC and officials from  Ministry of culture, National Museum, New Delhi, and IBC. At the Army Helipad, Rupa, the Sacred Relics were received with due protocol by Shri Pasang Dorjee Sona, Minister for Education, Tourism, Rural Works Department (RWD) and Public Libraries, Government of Arunachal Pradesh. A Guard of Honour was presented at the helipad. Thereafter, the Sacred Relics proceeded towards Bomdila, with a brief ceremonial halt at Upper Gompa before being taken to Thubchog Gatsel Ling Monastery (Lower Gompa) for enshrinement.

Following the enshrinement, two special exhibitions were inaugurated at the monastery by the Chief Guest, Shri Pasang Dorjee Sona,  Minister for Education, Tourism and Rural Works Department, Government of Arunachal Pradesh, in the presence of Padma Shri the 12th Guru Trulku Rinpoche. The exhibitions, organised by the International Buddhist Confederation (IBC) and the National Museum, New Delhi, showcase the historical, spiritual and cultural heritage associated with Buddhism and the Sacred Relics.

The arrival of the Sacred Relics in Bomdila follows the conclusion of the seven-day public exposition at Gaden Namgyal Lhatse (Tawang Monastery) on 7 November 2026. The exposition witnessed the participation of thousands of devotees and visitors from all blocks of Tawang  and neighbouring areas, who gathered to have darshan of the Sacred Relics, offer prayers and pay their respects. The overwhelming response reflected the deep spiritual reverence associated with the Sacred Relics of Shakyamuni Buddha.

Following the Bomdila exposition, the Sacred Relics will proceed to the Golden Pagoda, Namsai, where they will remain open for public darshan from 14 to 20 November 2026. Thereafter, the Sacred Relics are scheduled to return to the National Museum, New Delhi, on 21 November 2026.

2334234.body_html:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister extends greetings to the people of Uttarakhand on Statehood Day
Posted On: 09 NOV 2026 10:06AM by PIB Delhi

The Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi has extended his heartfelt greetings to all the people of Uttarakhand on the occasion of the their Statehood Day.

The Prime Minister said that Devbhoomi Uttarakhand is blessed with spiritual heritage and extraordinary natural beauty. He noted that the state is distinguished by its scenic mountain landscapes, sacred rivers, revered Char Dham and glorious cultural heritage.

Shri Modi said that with the active participation of its hardworking, talented and progressive people, Uttarakhand is scaling new heights of development across all sectors. He expressed confidence that the state would continue to progress rapidly and wished its people happiness, peace and prosperity.

Shri Modi said in a X post;

“उत्तराखंड स्थापना दिवस के अवसर पर राज्य के सभी निवासियों को मेरी हार्दिक शुभकामनाएं।
 
हमारी यह देवभूमि आध्यात्मिक चेतना और अद्भुत प्राकृतिक सौंदर्य से समृद्ध है। मनोरम पर्वतीय परिदृश्यों, पवित्र नदियों और पावन चारधाम के साथ-साथ यह प्रदेश अपनी गौरवशाली सांस्कृतिक विरासत के लिए भी विशिष्ट पहचान रखता है। 
 
राज्य के परिश्रमी, प्रतिभाशाली और प्रगतिशील लोगों की सक्रिय भागीदारी से उत्तराखंड आज हर क्षेत्र में विकास की नई ऊंचाइयों को छू रहा है। मुझे विश्वास है कि प्रकृति एवं संस्कृति प्रेमियों का यह प्रदेश प्रगति के पथ पर निरंतर तेज गति से आगे बढ़ता रहेगा।
 
यह विशेष अवसर राज्य के सभी लोगों के जीवन में सुख, शांति एवं समृद्धि लेकर आए।”
