2334133.title: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi celebrates Diwali with the security forces at CoBRA Operations Base at Karanpur in Bastar, Chhattisgarh
2334133.body_html:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi celebrates Diwali with the security forces at CoBRA Operations Base at Karanpur in Bastar, Chhattisgarh
This is the first Diwali when every district in country is free from Naxalism: PM
For the first time in 47 years, not a single CRPF jawan had to lose their life during duty in the past one year; This is a triumph of the nation's sound policies and strong resolve: PM
Driven by a spirit of service, we have transformed lives in Naxal-affected areas; as a result, even the victims of Naxalism have stood firmly alongside the government and security forces: PM
Today, on one hand, 50 crore people have come out of extreme poverty; On the other hand, Naxal violence has also come to an end in the country: PM
Posted On: 08 NOV 2026 4:04PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today visited the CoBRA Operations Base at Karanpur in Bastar, Chhattisgarh, which served as the training base and launch pad for counter-Naxal operations in Bastar and Abujhmad, to celebrate Diwali with the security forces. Addressing the jawans on the occasion as crores of Indians across the nation and the world celebrate the sacred festival of lights with their loved ones, the Prime Minister recalled his memorable Diwali celebrations with brave soldiers from Kargil and Lepcha in the Himalayas to Sir Creek on the coast and aboard INS Vikrant in the ocean. “At the borders and within the country, the sentinels of the nation who protect the country, the brave sons of Maa Bharati, all of you are my loved ones, all of you are a part of my family,” remarked Shri Modi.

Describing the 2026 Diwali as truly special because it marks the first festival of lights after India won its decades-old battle against Maoist terror, rendered every district Naxal-free, and enabled crores of citizens to overcome fear, the Prime Minister explained that he had come to Bastar to celebrate this extraordinary milestone with the lakhs of security personnel who made it possible and to convey the gratitude of 140 crore citizens. “Today I have come to express gratitude towards your sacrifice, dedication, and spirit of service,” affirmed PM Modi.

Quoting the ancient Sanskrit wisdom ‘Aabhyantaram Bhayam Rakshyam, Asaaram Baahyato Bhayam’ to explain that external enemies cannot harm a nation whose internal security is strong but raise their heads when internal security weakens, the Prime Minister equated the internal role of security forces with that of the armed forces at the borders and lauded the boundless sacrifices of personnel from the CRPF, CoBRA, BSF, ITBP, SSB, IRB, state police forces, Bastar Fighters commandos, and women fighters, while also extending festive greetings to soldiers guarding the nation's frontiers. “This country is indebted to you for your services, and crores of countrymen are proud of you,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Recalling the grim era when Left-Wing Extremism gripped over 230 districts across nearly 20 states including Bihar, Maharashtra, Odisha, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, and Chhattisgarh, where evening curfews of fear prevailed, voting rights were snatched, up to 2,000 annual attacks occurred, over 1,000 personnel laid down their lives in Chhattisgarh alone, countless soldiers lost limbs to IED blasts, and 76 CRPF personnel and 44 innocent civilians were killed in separate 2010 Dantewada attacks, the Prime Minister pointed out that between 2004 and 2013 more security personnel were martyred annually than Naxals killed, emboldening Maoist leaders.

Emphasizing that no nation can progress with a passive approach toward its enemies and must instead crush them strategically with high morale, the Prime Minister stated that after 2014, reversing the decades-old trend of higher casualties among security forces and resulting in a historic milestone where not a single CRPF soldier lost their life on duty over the past year for the first time in 47 years. “This is the victory of the country's right policies and firm willpower, and this is the victory of your valor, courage, and restraint,” asserted Shri Modi.

Stating that success requires both the right intention and the right policies, the Prime Minister noted that the government took a series of tough, including several unpublicized, national security decisions that struck at Naxal and separatist funding and destroyed the fake currency nexus. “Not only did this break their economic backbone, rather the entire supply line was choked, stopping the supply of weapons and curbing the movement and recruitment of Naxals,” noted PM Modi.

The Prime Minister stated that his government granted full operational freedom to security forces to take every necessary decision. Explaining that the government worked tirelessly without publicity or ostentation toward the singular goal of ensuring no mother loses her child, no family is ruined, and no youth takes up arms, he highlighted how combining sensitive security operations that broke the back of Maoist terror with a spirit of public service transformed lives and rallied affected citizens behind the government and security forces, including local citizens present at the event whom he thanked for their vital cooperation. “With a spirit of service, we transformed the lives of people in Naxal-affected areas,” remarked PM Modi.

Observing that working with the spirit of Nation First ensures peace and security, propels the country to new developmental heights, and expands the participation of the poor and deprived in national progress, the Prime Minister pointed out the dual triumph achieved by the nation over the past dozen years. “In the past 12 years, the country has not only won the battle against Naxalism and separatism, rather the country has also won a major war against poverty,” asserted Shri Modi.

Highlighting the widely discussed World Bank report released just ahead of Deepavali, the Prime Minister noted that 50 crore Indians have escaped extreme poverty over the past 12 years. 

Comparing India's welfare architecture over the past 12 years to a Diwali Rangoli where small, distinct lines come together to form a grand picture, the Prime Minister detailed how Jan Dhan banking, PM Awas pucca homes, collateral-free Mudra loans, SVANidhi support for street vendors, Ayushman Bharat healthcare, free monthly rations, child education policies, Swachh Bharat, and Har Ghar Jal collectively ensured free medicine, free education, and a free kitchen while removing basic anxieties so families once trapped in generational poverty now inherit a stronger future. “The poor families whose entire lives used to be spent only in worry have now received the assurance of the government, and a new self-confidence has come into them,” noted Shri Modi.

Pointing out that this victory over poverty is deeply linked to the fight against Naxalism, which previously trapped lakhs of innocent citizens in deprivation by blocking schools, hospitals, medical stores, polio vaccinations, mobile towers, and industries while bombing railway tracks, the Prime Minister detailed the special development drive in Left-Wing Extremism-affected areas that built over 15,000 kilometers of roads, over 9,500 mobile towers, nearly 175 Eklavya schools, around 50 ITIs, 50 Skill Development Centres, and thousands of post offices, bank branches, and ATMs, alongside rehabilitating surrendered Naxals and bringing water, electricity, and roads to remote tribal villages for the first time under PM JANMAN. “When we started the fight against Naxalism, at the same time we also ran special campaigns for the development of Naxal-affected areas,” noted PM Modi.

Stating that the ‘Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas’ campaign energized the fight against poverty and brought an end to Naxal violence alongside lifting 50 crore people out of extreme poverty, the Prime Minister cited the ongoing Bastar Olympics as a symbol of transformation in the region. “Today in this very Bastar, the Bastar Olympics are taking place, and children are trying their hand at sports, not guns,” remarked Shri Modi.

Emphasizing that today's milestones are a launchpad rather than a stopping point, the Prime Minister stated that the nation's new flight will fulfill the centuries-old dreams of freedom fighters, border soldiers, and personnel who laid down their lives fighting Naxalism and terrorism, urging the forces who live by the motto ‘Tera Gaurav Amar Rahe Maa, Hum Din Chaar Rahein Na Rahein’ to channel their spirit into new confidence. “Now is the time to live for the nation and to take the nation to a new height,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Citing the nation's proven track record of fulfilling major pledges such as abrogating Article 370 in Kashmir, building household toilets, and expanding vaccination coverage, the Prime Minister expressed complete confidence in the security forces and citizens that India will similarly achieve its goals of eradicating poverty and building a Drug-Free, Atmanirbhar, and Viksit Bharat, urging everyone to work toward witnessing these dreams become a reality before concluding with Deepavali greetings. “Your sacrifices and hard work will become a strong foundation for the grand edifice of a Viksit Bharat,” affirmed PM Modi.

2334114.title: Raksha Mantri celebrates Deepawali with troops in forward areas of Sikkim
2334114.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
Raksha Mantri celebrates Deepawali with troops in forward areas of Sikkim
Commends the courage, professionalism & dedication of soldiers guarding the borders in challenging high-altitude conditions
Shri Rajnath Singh honours fallen heroes at Sherathang War Memorial; pays respects at Baba Harbhajan Singh Memorial
Posted On: 08 NOV 2026 3:08PM by PIB Delhi

Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh celebrated Deepawali with the soldiers of the Trishakti Corps (33 Corps) deployed in the forward areas of Sikkim, on November 8, 2026. He was accompanied by the Chief of the Army Staff General Dhiraj Seth; General Officer Commanding-in-Chief, Eastern Command Lt Gen VMB Krishnan; General Officer Commanding, 33 Corps Lt Gen Man Raj Singh Mann, and other senior officers of the Indian Army.

Interacting with the soldiers at Sherathang, Shri Rajnath Singh described them as the brightest lights of Diwali, stating that their dedication and vigilance at the borders provide the entire nation with a sense of security. “Like a lamp which dispels darkness without seeking attention, soldiers perform their duties silently, ensuring that citizens can celebrate festivals with peace and security,” he said.

Raksha Mantri commended the soldiers for their professionalism, high morale and steadfast commitment to safeguarding the Nation's borders in challenging high-altitude conditions, urging them to continue protecting the motherland with the same enthusiasm and dedication. He acknowledged the sacrifices of soldiers who serve far away from their families, placing duty to the Nation above self and personal celebrations.

Underlining the importance of discipline and courage, Shri Rajnath Singh asserted that no matter how advanced technology may become, it is of little use if a soldier lacks these qualities. He underlined that the conduct, uniform, language and restraint of the personnel shape the image of the military among local communities. He urged the soldiers to continue strengthening the bond of trust & goodwill shared by the Indian Army and the local population in Sherathang & surrounding areas.

Raksha Mantri also paid homage at the Sherathang War Memorial to the soldiers who made the supreme sacrifice in the service of the Nation. He also visited Baba Harbhajan Singh Memorial, paying his respects to the revered soldier whose legacy continues to hold a special place in the military-civil traditions of the region.

Highlighting the significance of the Sherathang War Memorial, Shri Rajnath Singh emphasised that such monuments do more than commemorate past events and sacrifices; they shape collective memory and awaken national consciousness & pride. He stated that the soldiers honoured at the Memorial belonged to different parts of the country, including Nagaland, Uttar Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Rajasthan and Assam. He added that these bravehearts laid down their lives to protect the people, irrespective of their region, language or community. This spirit of unity and selfless service, he said, is the very soul and ethos of India, where every citizen considers fellow Indians as members of one family. 

Raksha Mantri emphasised that the Government, under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, established the National War Memorial in New Delhi to honour the gallant soldiers who made the supreme sacrifice in the service of the nation. “Approximately 26,000 names of the fallen heroes have been inscribed in golden letters at the National War Memorial to honour their unmatched valour and sacrifice. Seeing the name of a fallen soldier at the memorial evokes a deep sense of pride among their families, relatives and people from their native villages and regions. These memorials serve as sources of inspiration for the present and future generations.

SR/Savvy

2334105.title: Text of PM's speech during interaction with the Security Forces in Bastar, Chhattisgarh
2334105.body_html:
Prime Minister's Office
Text of PM's speech during interaction with the Security Forces in Bastar, Chhattisgarh
Posted On: 08 NOV 2026 2:53PM by PIB Delhi

भारत माता की जय।

भारत माता की जय।

भारत माता की जय।

 मेरे प्यारे देशवासियों,

आज पूरा देश दुनिया के कोने-कोने में करोड़ों भारतीय प्रकाश का पावन पर्व मना रहे हैं, दूर-दूर से लोग अपने घर पहुंच रहे हैं। परिवार और परिजनों के साथ मिलने-जुलने का एक बड़ा महोत्सव होता है, और मैं भी दिवाली मनाने आपके बीच पहुंच गया हूँ। सीमा पर और देश के भीतर, राष्ट्र की रक्षा करने वाले, राष्ट्र के प्रहरी, मॉं भारती के वीर, आप सब बेटे-बेटियां, आप सब मेरे परिजन हैं, आप सब मेरे परिवार का हिस्सा है। हिमालय की गोद में कारगिल से लेकर लेपचा तक, समंदर किनारे सरक्रीक से लेकर, समंदर की गोद में INS-विक्रांत तक, वीर जवानों के साथ हर दिवाली मेरे लिए यादगार रही है।

मेरे वीर जवानों,

इस बार मैं दिवाली मनाने बस्तर के जंगलों में आया हूँ, आप सबके बीच आया हूँ। ये वो भूमि है, जहां कभी नक्सली आतंक का कहर था और आप सबकी त्याग-तपस्या के कारण उसी भूमि पर आज नक्सली आतंक का कहर खत्म हुआ, विकास की बहार शुरू हो गई।

और साथियों,

साल 2026 की ये दिवाली वाकई विशेष है। 40-50 साल के बाद आपके लिए ऐसी दिवाली आई है।  ये पहली दीवाली है- जब देश नक्सलवाद-माओवादी आतंक के खिलाफ दशकों पुरानी लड़ाई जीत चुका है। ये पहली दीवाली है- जब देश का हर जिला नक्सलवाद से मुक्त है। ये पहली दीवाली है- जब करोड़ों देशवासी नक्सलवाद के भय को परास्त कर चुके हैं। ये एक असाधारण उपलब्धि है। इसका बहुत बड़ा श्रेय आपका है, आप जैसे लाखों वीरों का, जवानों का, बेटे-बेटियों का, सुरक्षा कर्मियों का  है। इसलिए, आज मैं आपके साथ दिवाली मनाने आया हूँ।। और, 140 करोड़ देशवासियों की ओर से आपके त्याग, समर्पण और सेवाभाव के प्रति आभार भी व्यक्त करने के लिए आया हूँ।

साथियों,

हमारे दूरदर्शी पूर्वजों ने कहा है- आभ्यन्तरं भयं रक्ष्यम्, असारं बाह्यतो भयम्। अर्थात्, जब राष्ट्र की आंतरिक सुरक्षा मजबूत होती है, तो बाहरी दुश्मन कुछ नहीं कर पाता है। लेकिन, अगर आंतरिक सुरक्षा कम पड़ती है, तो बाहरी दुश्मन भी सर उठाने लगते हैं। इसलिए, जो भूमिका सीमाओं पर हमारी सेनाओं की है, देश के भीतर वही रोल आप सब सुरक्षाबलों का है। आपने देश की एकता, अखंडता के लिए अनगिनत बलिदान दिये हैं, आपने असीम त्याग किया है। देश की आंतरिक सुरक्षा में लगे सुरक्षा बल, हमारे CRPF, कोबरा, BSF, ITBP, एक-एक जवान, SSB, IRB और राज्यों की पुलिस का एक-एक सिपाही, बस्तर फाइटर्स जैसे स्पेशल फोर्सेस के कमांडोज़, महिला फाइटर्स, ये देश आपकी सेवाओं के लिए, आपका ऋणी है। करोड़ों-करोड़ों देशवासी आप पर गर्व करते हैं। कृतज्ञता और अपनेपन के इसी भाव के साथ मैं आप सभी को, जो-जो, जहां-जहां डटे हैं, सबको दीपावली की बहुत-बहुत बधाई देता हूँ। मैं देश की सीमाओं पर राष्ट्र रक्षा के लिए तैनात हमारे सैनिकों को भी बधाई देता हूँ।

साथियों,

माओवादी आतंक-नक्सलवाद के खिलाफ ये लड़ाई आसान नहीं थी। एक समय था, जब देश के करीब 20 राज्यों में 230 से ज्यादा जिले नक्सलवाद की चपेट में थे, नक्सलवाद से प्रभावित थे। शाम होने के बाद यहां जीवन ठहर जाता था, घरों से बाहर निकलना नामुमकिन हो जाता था। लोगों से उनका वोट डालने का अधिकार भी इन नक्सलियों ने छीन लिया था। बिहार, महाराष्ट्र, ओडिशा, यूपी, मध्य प्रदेश, छत्तीसगढ़, देश का एक बहुत बड़ा हिस्सा वामपंथी उग्रवाद की चपेट में था। हजारों गाँव, करोड़ों की आबादी, एक साल में दो-दो हजार तक नक्सली हमले, एक साल में दो हजार हमले। आप याद करिए, 2010 में, यहीं पास ही दंतेवाड़ा में नक्सलियों से मुठभेड़ में CRPF के हमारे 76 सुरक्षाकर्मी शहीद हुए। 2010 में ही, दंतेवाड़ा में ही एक और घटना में 44 निर्दोष नागरिकों की हत्या हुई थी। ये धरती हमारे वीरों के रक्त से अभिषिक्त हो गई थी। लेकिन, महलों में रहने वाले किसी भी नामदार की सिसकी नहीं सुनाई दी। किसी भी महलों में रहने वाले नामदार की आंखों से एक बिंदु भी नहीं निकला था। आए दिन कहीं न कहीं ऐसे हमले होते रहते थे। दशकों तक ये सिलसिला चलता रहा, इस दौरान छत्तीसगढ़ में ही एक हजार से ज्यादा जवानों का बलिदान हुआ। IED के विस्फोटों में कितने ही जवानों को अपने हाथ-पैर गँवाने पड़े। आप 2004 से 2013 तक के आंकड़ें देखेंगे, तो हर साल जितने नक्सली मारे जाते थे, उससे ज्यादा संख्या में हमारे वीर जवान शहीद होते थे। नक्सली संगठनों के मुखिया इसे अपनी जीत समझते थे, जश्न मनाते थे। और दुर्भाग्य से तब की सरकारों द्वारा नक्सलवाद को लाइलाज बीमारी समझकर छोड़ दिया गया था। मेरे आदिवासी परिवारों को, उनके नसीब पर जीने के लिए छोड़ दिया गया था। और इसे स्वीकार कर लिया गया था कि ये तो बस ऐसे ही चलता रहेगा, गोलियां चलेगी, जवान मरेंगे, नागरिक पीटेंगे।

साथियों,

कोई भी देश अपने दुश्मनों के लिए - ऐसे ही चलता रहेगा - की अप्रोच से नहीं चलता। देश को आगे बढ़ाने के लिए, देश के दुश्मनों को बुलंद हौसले के साथ, एक रणनीति बनाकर कुचलना ही होता है। इसके लिए जिस राजनीतिक इच्छाशक्ति की कमी देश में थी, वो कमी साल 2014 में दूर हुई। आपने इस प्रधानसेवक को मॉं भारती की सेवा का मौका दिया। और हमने देखा है, 2014 के बाद हालात भी बदलने लगे और आंकड़ें भी बदलने लगे। हमारे यहां हमेशा नक्सलियों से ज्यादा संख्या में जवानों के मारे जाने की चर्चा रही। लेकिन 47 साल बाद, पहली बार ऐसा हुआ, जब पिछले एक वर्ष में CRPF के एक भी जवान को ड्यूटी के दौरान जान नहीं गंवानी पड़ी। ये देश की सही नीतियों और दृढ़ इच्छाशक्ति की जीत है। ये आपके, मैं फिर दोहराता हूँ, ये आपके शौर्य, साहस और संयम की जीत है।

भारत माता की जय।

भारत माता की जय।

इन वीर जवानों की जय।

हमारे सुरक्षाबल और पुलिस के जवान विपरीत परिस्थितियों में भी डटे रहे। यह उस कर्तव्य परायणता की जीत है।

साथियों,

सफलता के लिए सही नियत और सही नीतियाँ आवश्यक हैं। राष्ट्रीय सुरक्षा के लिए हमने एक के बाद एक कड़े निर्णय लिए। कई ऐसे कदम भी उठाए गए, जो आज तक लोगों की जानकारी में नहीं हैं। इन निर्णयों और प्रयासों से नक्सलवादियों, अलगाववादियों की फंडिंग पर बहुत बड़ी चोट की गई। फेक करेंसी के नेक्सस को तबाह किया गया। इससे उनकी आर्थिक कमर ही नहीं टूटी, बल्कि पूरी सप्लाई लाइन ही चोक हो गई। इससे हथियारों की सप्लाइ बंद हुई, नक्सलियों के मूवमेंट और रिक्रूटमेंट पर लगाम लगी।

साथियों,

पहले की सरकारों ने जमीन पर लड़ रहे सुरक्षाबलों के भी हाथ बांधकर रखे थे। नक्सली हमले होते जाते थे, लेकिन सुरक्षाबलों के पास खुलकर पलटवार करने की आज़ादी नहीं थी। हमने सिक्योरिटी  फोर्सेस को हर जरूरी निर्णय लेने की आज़ादी दी। पहले सरकार और सिस्टम में बैठे कुछ लोगों से वामपंथी उग्रवाद को जो सपोर्ट मिलता था, हमने उसे रोकने का भी काम किया।

साथियों,

हम एक बहुत बड़े लक्ष्य को लेकर चल रहे थे। हमारा लक्ष्य था- किसी माँ की गोद सूनी न हो, कोई परिवार तबाही के भंवर में न फंसे, कोई बच्चा हथियार उठाकर हिंसा की राह पर न निकले, किसी युवा का भविष्य बर्बाद ना हो। इसलिए, जब तक ये लक्ष्य पूरा नहीं हो गया, हम संकल्प के साथ लगातार लगे रहे। कोई प्रचार-प्रसार नहीं, कोई दिखावा नहीं, हमने संवेदनशीलता के साथ काम करते हुए माओवादी आतंक की कमर तोड़ दी। हमने सेवा भाव से नक्सल प्रभावित इलाकों में लोगों के जीवन को बदला। इसलिए, नक्सलवाद से पीड़ित लोग भी सरकार और सुरक्षाबलों के साथ मजबूती से खड़े हुये। आज यहां भी ऐसे नागरिक उपस्थित हैं, जिन्होंने इस बड़ी लड़ाई को जीतने में बहुत सहयोग किया है। मैं उन सबका भी आभार व्यक्त करता हूं।

साथियों,

जब हम राष्ट्र प्रथम की भावना के साथ काम करते हैं, तो देश की शांति और सुरक्षा भी सुनिश्चित होती है, देश विकास की नई ऊंचाइयों को भी छूता है और हर गरीब वंचित की विकास में भागीदारी भी बढ़ती है। और इसलिए, बीते 12 वर्षों में देश ने नक्सलवाद और अलगाववाद के खिलाफ ही लड़ाई नहीं जीती है सिर्फ, बल्कि देश ने गरीबी के खिलाफ भी बड़ी जंग जीती है।

साथियों,

इस बार दीपावली के ठीक पहले एक ऐसी खबर आई है, जिसकी पूरे देश और दुनिया में चर्चा है। अभी कुछ दिन पहले वर्ल्ड बैंक ने अपनी रिपोर्ट में कहा है कि भारत में, बीते 12 वर्षों में 50 करोड़ लोग, 50 करोड़ लोग भीषण गरीबी से बाहर निकले हैं। जो काम दशकों तक गरीबी हटाओ के नारों से नहीं हुआ, केवल 12 वर्षों में वो देश ने करके दिखाया। आप कल्पना कीजिए, ये कितनी बड़ी उपलब्धि है। सोचिए, ये कैसे हुआ?

साथियों,

हम दीवाली में रंगोली बनाते हैं, पहले रंगोली की कुछ लाइनें बनाई जाती हैं, शुरुआती लाइनें और आकृतियाँ छोटी और अलग लगती हैं, लेकिन जैसे-जैसे छोटे-छोटे हिस्से रंगोली के एक साथ जुड़ते हैं, तो एक बड़ी सुंदर तस्वीर बन जाती है। बीते 12 वर्षों में, भारत में भी ऐसा ही हुआ है। हमने गरीब कल्याण की योजनाओं की ऐसी रंगोली बनाई, जो गरीब को सशक्त करती चली गई। जनधन योजना से करोड़ों लोग बैंकिंग व्यवस्था से जुड़े। पीएम आवास योजना से करोड़ों परिवारों को पक्की छत मिली। हमने मुद्रा योजना के तहत लोगों को बिना गारंटी का लोन दिया। स्वनिधि योजना के जरिए, रेहड़ी-पटरी वाले व्यापारियों को भी सहायता दी, उन्हें अपना व्यापार बढ़ाने के मौके मिल रहे हैं। हमने आयुष्मान भारत के तहत गरीबों को मुफ्त इलाज की सुविधा दी। करोड़ों परिवारों को हर महीने मुफ्त राशन दिया। बच्चों की शिक्षा के लिए नीतियाँ बनाईं। यानी, हमने हर गरीब परिवार के लिए मुफ्त दवाई, मुफ्त पढ़ाई, मुफ्त रसोई, ये सुनिश्चित की। यही नहीं, स्वच्छ भारत मिशन और हर घर जल, जैसी योजनाओं ने जीवन की बुनियादी चिंताओं को भी दूर किया। इसी का परिणाम है कि आज करोड़ों लोग गरीबी से बाहर निकले हैं। जिन परिवारों को पहले गरीबी विरासत में मिलती थी, उन्हें अब विरासत में एक बेहतर भविष्य की नींव मिल रही है। जिन गरीब परिवारों का पूरा जीवन सिर्फ चिंता में बीतता था, उन्हें अब सरकार का भरोसा मिला है, उनमें एक नया आत्मविश्वास आया है।

साथियों,

गरीबी के खिलाफ इस बड़ी विजय, एक बड़ा आधार नक्सलवाद-अलगाववाद के खिलाफ देश की लड़ाई से भी जुड़ा है। बस्तर के लोग और आप सब जानते हैं, जहां-जहां नक्सलियों का प्रभाव होता था, वहाँ उनका पहला एजेंडा होता था- विकास को रोकना, आम लोगों के जीवन पर चोट करना, बच्चों के लिए स्कूल नहीं खुलने दिये जाते थे, स्कूलों को आग लगा दी जाती थी। बीमारों के लिए हॉस्पिटल नहीं बनने दिये जाते थे, डॉक्टरों को घुसने नहीं दिया जाता था। जिंदगी बचाने के लिए मेडिकल स्टोर जैसी सुविधाएं नहीं होने देते थे। ये नक्सली हमारे बच्चों को पोलियो तक की वैक्सीन नहीं लगने देते थे। ये नक्सली मोबाइल टावर नहीं लगाने देते थे। किस तरह, रेलवे ट्रैक्स को बम लगाकर उड़ाने जैसी घटनाएँ होती थीं। उद्योग धंधों को किस तरह रोका जाता था। आप सबने ये सालों तक देखा है। और इसी का  परिणाम ये होता था कि लाखों गरीब निर्दोष, मेरे नागरिक भाई-बहन, मेरे युवा भाई-बहन अवसरों से वंचित रह जाते थे। उनका जीवन गरीबी के भंवर से निकल ही नहीं पाता था। और इसलिए हमने जब नक्सलवाद के खिलाफ लड़ाई शुरू की, तो साथ ही नक्सल प्रभावित इलाकों के विकास के लिए विशेष अभियान भी चलाये। हमने वामपंथी उग्रवाद से पीड़ित इलाकों में 15 हजार किलोमीटर से ज्यादा सड़कें बनाईं, सुरक्षा के पूरे प्रबंध करके बनाई। साढ़े नौ हजार से ज्यादा मोबाइल टावर्स इन इलाकों में लगाए गए। आदिवासी बच्चों की शिक्षा के लिए करीब पौने दो सौ एकलव्य स्कूल खोले।  युवाओं को रोजगार से जोड़ने के लिए करीब 50 ITI खोले। 50 के आसपास Skill Development Centres बनाए। हजारों पोस्ट ऑफिस, बैंक ब्रांच और ATM खोले गए। अति पिछड़े आदिवासी इलाकों के विकास के लिए पीएम जनमन योजना शुरू की।  इससे हजारों सुदूर गाँवों में पहली बार पानी, बिजली और सड़क जैसी सुविधाएं पहुंची। यही नहीं, आत्मसमर्पण करने वाले नक्सलियों को मौका दिया गया। उनके पुनर्वास के लिए योजनाएं बनाई गईं।

साथियों,

‘सबका साथ, सबका विकास’ के इस अभियान ने गरीबी के खिलाफ देश की लड़ाई को नई ऊर्जा और एक नया विश्वास दिया। और इसलिए, आज एक तरफ 50 करोड़ लोग भीषण गरीबी से बाहर आए हैं,  दूसरी ओर, देश में नक्सली हिंसा का भी अंत हुआ है। आप बस्तर को ही लीजिये, आज इसी बस्तर में बस्तर ओलंपिक हो रहा है, बच्चे बंदूक नहीं, स्पोर्टस में हाथ आजमा रहे हैं।

साथियों,

इन सफलताओं के बीच हमें एक और बात याद रखनी है, नक्सली खत्म हुए हैं, लेकिन खतरा अभी टला नहीं है। जंगलों से हथियारी नक्सली तो मिट गए, लेकिन दिमागी नक्सलियों ने कई संगठनों पर कब्जा कर रखा है। ये आज भी देश के संविधान और लोकतंत्र के खिलाफ लोगों को उकसा रहे हैं। कई राजनीतिक दलों में, अलग-अलग संगठनों में भी इन दिमागी नक्सलियों ने अपनी घुसपैठ कर ली है। हमें इन्हें पहचानना है, इन्हें परास्त करना है और देश को सुरक्षित करना है।

साथियों,

आज की उपलब्धियां हमें प्रेरणा देती हैं, लेकिन ये विराम नहीं हैं। मैं फिर कहता हूं, ये विराम नहीं है। ये जीत, ये सफलताएँ, ये मंच हैं नई उड़ान का, ये उड़ान राष्ट्र के उन सपनों की होगी, जिन्हें सदियों से हमारी पीढ़ियों ने देखा है। ये सपने उन सेनानियों के होंगे, जिन्होंने आज़ादी के लिए अनगिनत बलिदान दिये। ये सपने उन शूरवीर सैनिकों के होंगे, जिन्होंने सीमाओं पर माँ भारती के लिए अपने प्राणों का उत्सर्ग दिया। ये सपने, उन वीर जवानों के होंगे, जिन्होंने नक्सलवाद और आतंकवाद के खिलाफ लड़ाई में अपनी जिंदगी न्योछावर कर दी। आप हर दिन इस भाव के साथ जीते हैं- तेरा गौरव अमर रहे माँ, तेरा गौरव अमर रहे माँ, हम दिन चार रहें न रहें, तेरा गौरव अमर रहे माँ। अब समय है, आपका ये भाव नए विश्वास में बदले, अब समय राष्ट्र के लिए जीने का है, राष्ट्र को नई ऊंचाई पर पहुंचाने का है।

साथियों,

हमारा देश जो संकल्प लेता है, उसे पूरा करने का सामर्थ्य भी उसके पास है। हमने वादा किया था कि हम कश्मीर से धारा 370 हटाएँगे, हमने वो वादा पूरा करके दिखाया। हमने वादा किया था कि हम हर घर में शौचालय बनाएँगे, हमने शौचालय बनाकर दिखाये। हमने वैक्सीनेशन का दायरा बढ़ाने की बात की, हमने उसे पूरा करके दिखाया। इसलिए, आज जब हम गरीबी को दूर करने की बात करते हैं, आज जब हम ड्रग्स फ्री भारत की बात करते हैं, नशा-मुक्त भारत की बात करते हैं, आज जब हम विकसित भारत की बात करते हैं, आज जब हम आत्मनिर्भर भारत की बात करते हैं, तो देश ये लक्ष्य भी हासिल करके रहेगा। हमें अपनी आँखों के सामने इन सपनों को साकार होते देखना है। मुझे आप पर भरोसा है, मुझे मेरे देश की युवाशक्ति पर भरोसा है, मुझे हमारे देशवासियों पर भरोसा है। देश अपने इस लक्ष्य तक जरूर पहुंचेगा। आपके त्याग और परिश्रम विकसित भारत की भव्य इमारत के लिए मजबूत नींव बनेंगे। इसी विश्वास के साथ, मैं एक बार फिर आपको दीपावली की हार्दिक बधाई देता हूँ। आप सबका बहुत-बहुत धन्यवाद।

2334104.title: Celebrate an Eco-Friendly Green Diwali for Cleaner Air: WWF-India EIACP appeals to citizens of Delhi-NCR to take the Green Diwali Pledge
2334104.ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
2334104.body_html:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
Celebrate an Eco-Friendly Green Diwali for Cleaner Air: WWF-India EIACP appeals to citizens of Delhi-NCR to take the Green Diwali Pledge
Posted On: 08 NOV 2026 2:51PM by PIB Delhi

WWF-India's EIACP Programme Centre – Resource Partner (PC-RP), supported by the Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEF&CC), Government of India, has appealed to the people of Delhi-NCR to celebrate a cracker-free Green Diwali this year and help keep the air clean. The appeal is part of the nationwide Green Diwali Campaign 2026, running from 20th October to 8th November 2026 under Mission LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment), with a special focus on the 130 cities covered under the National Clean Air Programme (NCAP) across 24 States and Union Territories. 

As per the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), Delhi's air quality is in the 'Very Poor' category, and as per the Air Quality Early Warning System forecasts it may reach the 'Severe' category during the festive days. The Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM) is implementing measures under the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) across the region to prevent further deterioration of air quality. Citizens have been urged to support these efforts and follow the measures in force.

WWF EIACP has invited every citizen to take a Green Diwali Pledge to perform their part for clean air, good health and a pollution-free environment. It has also laid out simple steps towards a Green Diwali, as below:

  • Choose Eco-Friendly Diyas and Candles: Use traditional earthen diyas and eco-friendly candles, and avoid excessive energy consumption.
  • Go Sustainable with Gifts: Choose locally made, eco-friendly gifts with minimal packaging.
  • Say No to Firecrackers: Avoid firecrackers to help reduce air and noise pollution and protect public health.
  • Decorate Naturally: Make rangolis using natural materials such as flower petals, rice flour and turmeric, and try DIY decorations using upcycled materials.
  • Minimise Waste: Avoid single-use plastics, reuse decorations, and segregate waste for recycling.
  • Organise Community Events: Host plantation drives, neighbourhood clean-up activities and environmental awareness walks to encourage collective action.
  • Donate for a Good Cause: Donate old clothes and unused, usable household items to people in need, promoting reuse and reducing waste.
  • Adopt Greener Mobility: Walk, cycle or use public or shared transport for festive travel whenever practical.
  • Check Your Air: Follow the daily Air Quality Index (AQI) on the Central Pollution Control Board’s SAMEER app and limit outdoor exposure on poor air days.

Citizens have also been encouraged to take WWF-India's Carbon Footprint Survey (https://wwfindiawebgis.in/Carbon_Footprint/Carbon_Footprint.html) to understand their environmental footprint and adopt more sustainable habits. Further, participating institutions and groups have been invited to share their activities through the online form - https://docs.google.com/forms/d/15hDbjbqZzeo68kNjAxeHQA_SMIQ7lUlPdvCIi-gvwdY/viewform. Each submission should include the name and location of the institution or organisation, the activity details and date, the number of participants who took the pledge, geo-tagged photographs and a brief report. Selected entries may be featured on EIACP websites and social media platforms.

2334086.title: 31,000 Devotees Seek Blessings of the Sacred Relics of Shakyamuni Buddha at Tawang, Arunachal Pradesh
2334086.body_html:
Ministry of Culture
31,000 Devotees Seek Blessings of the Sacred Relics of Shakyamuni Buddha at Tawang, Arunachal Pradesh
Seven-Day Exposition at Tawang Monastery Concludes on November 7; Sacred Relics to Be Enshrined at Bomdila from November 8
Posted On: 08 NOV 2026 11:44AM by PIB Delhi

The Sacred exposition of the Holy Relics of  Shakyamuni Buddha organised by the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, in collaboration with the Government of Arunachal Pradesh and the International Buddhist Confederation (IBC), New Delhi, concluded its Tawang leg today, 7 November 2026, after witnessing an overwhelming response from devotees and visitors. A total of 31,000 devotees and visitors visited Gaden Namgyal Lhatse (Tawang Monastery) to have darshan of the sacred relics during the seven-day exposition.

The Sacred Relics arrived in Tawang on 31 October 2026 from the National Museum, New Delhi, with due protocol and ceremonial arrangements. The Chief Minister of Arunachal Pradesh, Shri Pema Khandu, ceremonially received the sacred relics in the presence of the Union Minister of Culture and Tourism, Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat.

The sacred exposition provided an opportunity for Buddhist monks, senior citizens and the general public to pay their respects, offer prayers and seek blessings in the presence of the sacred relics of Shakyamuni Buddha. Throughout the seven days, Tawang Monastery witnessed an outpouring of devotion, with devotees arriving from all blocks of Tawang district and neighbouring areas. The large turnout reflected the deep spiritual and cultural significance of the sacred relics among the people of the region.

As part of the exposition, the Chief Minister of Arunachal Pradesh Shri Pema Khandu inaugurated two special exhibitions at Tawang Monastery. The exhibition ‘Unearthing the Sacred Piprahwa: The Story of the Holy Buddha Relics and Their Discovery’, organised by the International Buddhist Confederation (IBC), showcased the historical discovery of the Piprahwa relics in 1898. The second exhibition, ‘Crossroads of Dhamma: Classical Legacies, Living Art, and Anthropological Perspectives’, curated by the National Museum, New Delhi, offered visitors an opportunity to explore the historical, artistic and cultural legacy of Buddhism and its enduring influence.

On 2 November 2026, the International Buddhist Confederation organised an international conference titled ‘Buddhism: Dissemination in the Himalayan Region and Beyond’ at the Kalawangpo Convention Centre, Tawang. The conference brought together Buddhist scholars, religious leaders and representatives from India and several other countries to deliberate on the dissemination and preservation of Buddhist teachings and heritage in the Himalayan region and beyond.

Following the conclusion of the sacred exposition at Tawang on 7 November, the Sacred Relics will continue their journey to  Bomdila as the next destination of exposition. On 8 November 2026, the Sacred Relics will be transported to Bomdila by the Indian Air Force. After a brief halt at Upper Gompa, the relics will be enshrined at TGL Monastery (Lower Gompa), Bomdila, where they will remain open for public darshan from 8 to 13 November 2026.

Thereafter, the Sacred Relics will move to the Golden Pagoda, Namsai, where the Sacred Relics will be available for public darshan from 14 to 20 November 2026, before returning to the National Museum, New Delhi, on 21 November 2026.

The exposition reflects the Government of India's continued commitment to preserving and promoting India's rich Buddhist heritage and strengthening the country's cultural and spiritual connections with Buddhist communities across the world.

2334064.title: Shram Samvad: District Level Capacity-Building and Awareness Programme on Labour Codes held in Dewas, Madhya Pradesh
2334064.body_html:
Ministry of Labour & Employment
Shram Samvad: District Level Capacity-Building and Awareness Programme on Labour Codes held in Dewas, Madhya Pradesh
Posted On: 08 NOV 2026 9:11AM by PIB Delhi

A District Level Capacity-Building and Awareness Programme, “Shram Samvad”, on Labour Codes, Labour Welfare and Social Protection, was jointly organized by Ministry of Labour & Employment (MoLE), Government of India (GoI) and Labour Department, Government of Madhya Pradesh in collaboration with Association of Industries Madhya Pradesh and M/s Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd at Dewas, Madhya Pradesh on 5th November, 2026.

The programme aimed at enhancing awareness among employers, HR, Legal and Finance professionals regarding the Labour Codes and rules made thereunder. It also focused on strengthening awareness and institutional capacity on labour reforms, welfare and social protection, promoting Centre-State coordination and stakeholder engagement. Shri S.R. Datta, Director, MoLE presided over the programme and participants included senior officials from MoLE, Labour Department, GoMP, Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) , Employees' State Insurance Corporation (ESIC), Chief Labour Commissioner (Central) [CLC(C)], Directorate General Labour Welfare (DGLW) along with more than 100 participants from employers, industry representatives, legal, HR and finance professionals.

The programme featured a series of technical sessions designed to provide participants with practical insights into the Labour Codes, employer obligations, and key social security initiatives of the GoI.

Shri S.R. Datta, Director, MoLE presented the keynote address highlighting the key features of the Labour Codes. Various sessions were conducted by officials from MoLE, focusing on the key compliance requirements for employers under each of the four Labour Codes and Central Rules notified under the Labour Codes. The sessions provided practical guidance on statutory obligations and compliance responsibilities, enabling participants to better understand the operational aspects of the new labour codes.

Representatives from EPFO and DGLW also led sessions on Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana (PMVBRY) and Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maandhan (PM-SYM) Scheme, respectively.

To facilitate the employers and compliance professionals in effective implementation of the Labour Codes and Rules, ‘Handbook of Compliance for Employers’ and ‘Compilation of Frequently Asked Questions’ developed by MoLE were also shared with the participants.

An engaging Question and Answer session was also held, enabling participants to address their queries and gain greater clarity on the Labour Codes, compliance requirements, and social security provisions. By bringing together Central Government and State Government authorities and industry representatives, the event contributed to enhanced awareness, improved understanding, and stronger stakeholder engagement, thereby supporting the effective adoption and implementation of the New Labour Codes.

*****

2334045.title: Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan inaugurates Deepotsav 2026 celebrations in Ayodhya
2334045.body_html:
Vice President's Secretariat
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan inaugurates Deepotsav 2026 celebrations in Ayodhya
Deepotsav has evolved into a celebration of Jan Bhagidari, reflecting Bharat’s collective faith: Vice-President
Millions of lamps in Ayodhya symbolise transformation in the lives of crores of Indians: Vice-President
India must embrace modern aspirations while remaining rooted in its civilisational values: Vice-President
Posted On: 07 NOV 2026 9:39PM by PIB Delhi

Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, inaugurated the Deepotsav 2026 celebrations at Ram Ki Paidi in Ayodhya, Uttar Pradesh, today. He witnessed the spectacular illumination of the ghats with millions of diyas, cultural presentations depicting the Ramayana and musical fireworks. He also participated in the sacred Saryu Aarti at Naya Ghat.

Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan participated as the Chief Guest in the grand Deepotsav 2026 celebrations at Ram Ki Paidi, Ayodhya, today, witnessing the spectacular illumination of the ghats with millions of diyas. https://t.co/bBGAik7gMs

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) November 7, 2026

Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan performed aarti on the banks of the Saryu in Ayodhya as he participates in Deepotsav 2026 https://t.co/igtgnFjFbZ

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) November 7, 2026

Addressing the gathering at Ram Ki Paidi, the Vice-President highlighted the remarkable growth of Deepotsav since its inception in 2017, when over 1.7 lakh lamps were illuminated. He said that the celebration reached over 26 lakh lamps in 2025, while its tenth edition envisaged more than 30 lakh diyas at Ram Ki Paidi and over 70 lakh across Ayodhya. He congratulated the Uttar Pradesh Government for taking the festival to national and international prominence.

The Vice-President appreciated the festival’s contribution to local livelihoods, creating opportunities for potters, rural women, artisans, performers, hotel and homestay operators, guides and transport providers. He also welcomed the innovative use of technology, including more than 2,100 indigenous drones depicting scenes from the Ramayana and the participation of around 1,000 artists in cultural programmes.

Referring to the millions of lamps illuminating Ayodhya, he said they symbolised the transformation taking place in the lives of crores of Indians. He appreciated Uttar Pradesh’s initiatives in women’s empowerment, education, agriculture, healthcare, housing and entrepreneurship, and observed that the State was progressing towards becoming ‘Uttam Pradesh’.

Addressing the youth, the Vice-President urged them to understand the Ramayana and imbibe its teachings in their daily conduct. He called upon young people to embrace science, innovation and technology while remaining connected to India’s values, languages, traditions and cultural wisdom. India must be modern in its aspirations while remaining firmly rooted in its civilisational values, he said.

Earlier, the Vice-President offered prayers at the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Temple and participated in special prayers and aarti of Shri Ram-Janaki at Ram Katha Park.

 

Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan offered prayers at the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Temple in Ayodhya today and sought the blessings of Bhagwan Shri Ram. https://t.co/U5Dze438YF

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) November 7, 2026


Addressing the gathering at Ram Katha Park, the Vice-President said that Bhagwan Shri Ram is the eternal embodiment of Dharma, righteousness, compassion and ideal conduct.

 

Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan participated in the special prayers and aarti of Shri Ram-Janaki at Ram Katha Park, Ayodhya, as part of the Deepotsav 2026 celebrations. https://t.co/JTJD3IILZk

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) November 7, 2026


Describing Ayodhya as a shining example of ‘Vikas Bhi, Virasat Bhi’, the Vice-President noted that the development of roads, ghats, pilgrimage facilities, accommodation and improved rail and air connectivity had significantly transformed the experience of pilgrims and visitors.

The Vice-President congratulated the Uttar Pradesh Government, the administration, artists, volunteers, artisans and citizens for making the tenth edition of Deepotsav a grand celebration of Jan Bhagidari, reflecting Bharat’s collective faith and devotion.

The celebrations were attended by Governor of Uttar Pradesh Smt. Anandiben Patel, Chief Minister Shri Yogi Adityanath, Deputy Chief Ministers Shri Keshav Prasad Maurya and Shri Brajesh Pathak, Ministers, revered saints and seers, and other distinguished guests.

2334030.title: EPFO successfully concludes Special Campaign 6
2334030.body_html:
Ministry of Labour & Employment
EPFO successfully concludes Special Campaign 6
Successful public grievance disposal, cleanliness drives and record management by EPFO meeting all targets set
Posted On: 07 NOV 2026 8:06PM by PIB Delhi

Employees’ Provident Fund Organization (EPFO) has successfully concluded the Special Campaign 6 conducted during the month of October 2026, reaffirming its commitment to administrative efficiency, cleanliness, transparency and improved public service delivery. The campaign was made successful by active participation of EPFO Head Office, Training Academies, 21 Zonal Offices and various Regional and District offices. The key achievements on various parameters are as under:

  1. Disposal of public grievances (PG): EPFO disposed 2,36,021 grievances against a target of 2,05,000 (15.1% above target). This includes disposal of 2,02,984 grievances on EPFiGMS against a target of 1,80,000 (12.8% above target) and 33,037 grievances on CPGRAM (32.1% above target).
  2. Disposal of appeals and PMOPG: Similarly, 10,343 CPGRAM Appeals were disposed of against a target of 5,758, (88.1% above target), while 758 PMOPG were disposed of against a target of 747 (5.1% above target). Target to dispose off 36 VIP references and 2 Parliamentary Assurances was also achieved.
  3. Conduct of Cleanliness Drives: 598 Cleanliness Target Units were identified and transformed successfully against a target of 570, which is 5% above the target. Besides this, drive of beautification of offices, tree plantation and Blood Donation Camp were also conducted during the Campaign. Further, a total of 68,178 sq. ft space has been freed against a target of 28,300 sq. ft (140.1% above target).
  4. Record management: A total of 41,875 physical files have been reviewed against a target of 28,770 (45.6% above target), and 1.383 files have been transferred to the National Archives against a target of 1,277 (8.3% above target). 517 physical files have been identified for weeding against a target of 109 while 342 files have been weeded against the target of 82. As regards e-files, 8,355 e-files have been reviewed against a target of 8,160 (2.4% above target) and 3,106 e-files closed against the target of 3,000 (3.5% above target).

The campaign’s progress was regularly monitored at various levels within the EPFO. Mass pledge-taking activities and other grievance redressal drives were conducted at various offices of EPFO. While redressal of public grievances is an on-going activity, quality disposal of grievances in a time-bound manner was undertaken during the Campaign period. As regards PMOPG, telephonic feedback was taken from the petitioners after its disposal, and an overwhelming percentage of such petitioners expressed satisfaction on the disposal. Furthermore, any suggestions for improvement were also obtained for effecting any micro-level systemic changes. The activities pertaining to cleanliness and record management have not only made offices clean for public dealing but also created space for efficient office management.

The successful conclusion of Special Campaign 6 reflects the EPFO’S continued commitment to good governance, efficient administration, employee well-being and citizen-centric service delivery.

2334029.title: Raksha Mantri reviews infrastructure development along LAC & deployment of advanced military equipment during visit to Trishakti Corps at Sukna
2334029.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
Raksha Mantri reviews infrastructure development along LAC & deployment of advanced military equipment during visit to Trishakti Corps at Sukna
Lauds the Corps’ role in nation building through progress & community welfare initiatives in border areas
Sukna is a vital link in security architecture of Eastern India; Government is committed to strengthening supply chains to ensure availability of essential supplies to soldiers: Shri Rajnath Singh
“Modern warfare extends beyond conventional battles to encompass hybrid warfare, proxy wars, cyber-attacks, drone incursions & information warfare; Defence Forces must remain vigilant”
Posted On: 07 NOV 2026 8:03PM by PIB Delhi

Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh reviewed the operational preparedness of Trishakti Corps at Sukna, West Bengal, on November 7, 2026. He was briefed on infrastructure development along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) and the deployment of advanced military equipment and emerging technologies to enhance operational capabilities & combat effectiveness. Raksha Mantri expressed satisfaction with the operational preparedness of the Corps and appreciated its contribution to nation-building through infrastructure development and community welfare initiatives in border areas, aimed at strengthening ties with local communities. Chief of the Army Staff General Dhiraj Seth; General Officer Commanding-in-Chief, Eastern Command, Lt Gen VMB Krishnan; and General Officer Commanding, 33 Corps, Lt Gen Man Raj Singh Mann were present on the occasion, along with other senior Army officers.

Later, addressing the soldiers during Barakhana on the eve of Diwali, Raksha Mantri commended their courage, professionalism and unwavering dedication towards safeguarding the nation's frontiers under challenging operational conditions. Underlining the importance of logistics in national security, he described Sukna and its surrounding region as a critical hub for the movement of supplies, weaponry, food, medical provisions and personnel to forward locations. He stated that Sukna serves as a vital link in the security architecture of Eastern India and its geographical sensitivity necessitates round-the-clock operational readiness. He added that the Government, under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, is continuously working to strengthen supply chains and ensure that soldiers deployed at forward locations have access to all essential requirements.

Shri Rajnath Singh highlighted that budgetary allocations for roads, tunnels, border infrastructure and modern equipment have been increased, with the nation steadily progressing towards 'Aatmanirbhar Bharat'. “Our start-ups and industries are now manufacturing drones, anti-drone systems, and other state-of-the-art equipment for the soldiers. It is a matter of pride that our Defence Forces are actively embracing emerging technologies, learning drone operations, enhancing their understanding of cyber security, and undergoing training in new methodologies. This transformation will prepare us for the future,” he said.

Highlighting the changing nature of modern warfare, Raksha Mantri emphasised that security challenges are no longer confined to conventional exchanges of gunfire or artillery along the borders, but encompass hybrid warfare, proxy wars, cyber-attacks, drone incursions and information warfare. He stated that adversaries increasingly resort to spreading rumours through social media, monitoring sensitive locations using drones and attempting to compromise military systems through cyber-attacks. He exhorted the personnel to remain vigilant and prepared to safeguard national security across all domains.

Shri Rajnath Singh reaffirmed the Government's commitment to taking every possible step to boost troop morale and urged officers to spend quality time with soldiers whenever possible. Such interactions, he said, would foster a strong sense of belonging among personnel and reinforce their confidence that the Government and the entire nation stand firmly with them.

Raksha Mantri also underscored the importance of mental health and emotional well-being among Defence Forces personnel. Acknowledging that soldiers may experience stress due to separation from their families and the demands of their duties, he encouraged them to communicate openly with their comrades and seek support rather than suppress their feelings.

Describing the North-Eastern region as the 'first edge' rather than the 'last edge' of India, Shri Rajnath Singh said that the region represents the beginning of the nation's geographical and cultural landscape, as it receives the first rays of the morning sun. He highlighted the North-East's rich biodiversity, natural beauty, cultural diversity and unique traditions, describing it as an integral part of India's identity.

Raksha Mantri extended Diwali greetings to the personnel and their families, assuring them that the Government remains committed to their safety, dignity and well-being. He described Barakhana as a reflection of the spirit of togetherness and equality, stating that such gatherings transcend ranks and hierarchies, bringing personnel from diverse regions, cultures and linguistic backgrounds together as one family.

2334016.title: Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah reviews Gujarat’s law and order and internal security situation at a high-level meeting in Ahmedabad
2334016.body_html:
Ministry of Home Affairs
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah reviews Gujarat’s law and order and internal security situation at a high-level meeting in Ahmedabad
Home Minister directs strengthening of border and coastal security, action against drug networks and effective control of cybercrime
Emphasises strengthening surveillance along Gujarat’s nearly 2,340-km-long coastline and better coordination among BSF, State Police, Coast Guard and central agencies
Gujarat’s performance in implementation of new criminal laws commendable; 92 per cent of chargesheets filed within 60 days and 86 per cent within 90 days
Stresses action against entire drug networks and their kingpins, rather than just small-time peddlers, and prioritising financial investigations to seize illicit assets
Directs enhancing the capacity of S4C and the 1930 helpline, strengthening counter-terrorism agencies, and expediting identification and deportation of illegal foreign nationals as per law
Home Minister reiterates commitment to building a secure India through a safe, developed and drug-free Gujarat
Posted On: 07 NOV 2026 7:41PM by PIB Delhi

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah today reviewed the law and order and internal security situation in Gujarat at a high-level meeting in Ahmedabad.

Chief Minister of Gujarat Shri Bhupendra Patel, Deputy Chief Minister Shri Harsh Sanghavi, Union Home Secretary, senior officials of the Ministry of Home Affairs and its subordinate offices, and officials of the State Home Department and other concerned departments attended the meeting.

Several important issues, including border and coastal security, implementation of the new criminal laws, drug trafficking, cybercrime, terrorism, illegal migration and disaster management, were discussed during the meeting.

Keeping in view Gujarat’s nearly 2,340-kilometre-long coastline and its international border with Pakistan, Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah emphasised the need to strengthen border and coastal surveillance and ensure better coordination among the Border Security Force (BSF), State Police, Coast Guard and central agencies.

Shri Amit Shah appreciated Gujarat’s performance in the implementation of the new criminal laws, stating that 92 per cent of chargesheets in the state were filed within 60 days and 86 per cent within 90 days. The Home Minister directed the state to launch a special drive to clear more than 25,000 pending forensic cases.

The Union Home Minister said that action against drug trafficking must not remain confined to small-time peddlers. Instead, the entire drug network and its principal kingpins must be targeted, with financial investigations being prioritised to seize their illicit assets.

Shri Amit Shah directed that the capacity of S4C and the 1930 helpline be enhanced to tackle cybercrime, counter-terrorism agencies be strengthened, and the identification and deportation of illegal foreign nationals be expedited in accordance with the law. He appreciated the deportation of 2,412 illegal foreign nationals under special drives.

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation also emphasised the need to accelerate work relating to disaster management, fire safety, the Ahmedabad Urban Flood Management Project, and the survey and disposal of enemy properties.

At the conclusion of the meeting, the Union Home Minister directed all Central and State agencies to work in close coordination and regularly review progress against prescribed targets. He reiterated the commitment to building a secure India through a safe, developed and drug-free Gujarat.

2333992.title: PRESIDENT OF INDIA’S GREETINGS ON THE EVE OF DIWALI
2333992.body_html:
President's Secretariat
PRESIDENT OF INDIA’S GREETINGS ON THE EVE OF DIWALI
Posted On: 07 NOV 2026 6:50PM by PIB Delhi

The President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu sends greetings to her fellow citizens on the eve of Diwali.

In a message, the President has said, “On the auspicious occasion of Diwali, I extend my heartfelt greetings and best wishes to all Indians living in India and abroad.

The joyous celebrations followed Bhagwan Shri Ram’s return to Ayodhya after his victory over Ravana. Bhagwan Shri Ram beheld the beautiful rows of illuminated lamps. This forms the cultural and devotional significance of Diwali. The festival also symbolises the auspicious beginning of Ram Rajya.

The festival of Diwali marks the victory of virtues over negative tendencies. It also signifies the end of suffering and the beginning of a joyful and prosperous life. On this occasion, people worship Bhagwan Ganesh for auspicious beginnings and well-being, and Mahalakshmi Mata for prosperity. Prayers are offered for the happiness of all.

I wish good health, happiness and prosperity to every citizen of our country. May we preserve the environment, live with harmony and may our patriotic youth, guided by Indian values, contribute enthusiastically to building a Viksit Bharat”.

2333987.title: LOK SABHA SPEAKER EXTENDS GREETINGS FOR DEEPAVALI, GOVARDHAN PUJA, AND BHAI DOOJ
2333987.body_html:
Lok Sabha Secretariat
LOK SABHA SPEAKER EXTENDS GREETINGS FOR DEEPAVALI, GOVARDHAN PUJA, AND BHAI DOOJ
Posted On: 07 NOV 2026 6:32PM by PIB Delhi

Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla has extended greetings for Deepavali, Govardhan Puja, and Bhai Dooj.

In his message Shri Birla said: “Heartfelt greetings to all of you on Diwali, the grand festival of joy. I also extend my warmest wishes to you for Govardhan Puja, and Bhai Dooj.

Deepavali is not merely a festival of lighting lamps and celebrating; it is also an opportunity to fill the lives of others with the light of hope, faith, and happiness.

Just as a lamp burns itself to spread light all around, let us also make an effort in our lives to ensure that our joy brings happiness to the lives of others. Let us pledge to bring a smile not only to our own families but also to the faces of those who remain deprived of the festival's joys due to hardships. Help the needy, share happiness with them, and promote love, harmony, and mutual cooperation in society.

Our Deepavali will only be truly meaningful when no one around us feels lonely or neglected.

On this auspicious occasion, special greetings to our brave soldiers guarding the nation's borders, our farmer brothers who fill the country's granaries, the workers engaged in nation-building, entrepreneurs, businessmen, and all fellow citizens.

By the grace of Goddess Lakshmi, may happiness and prosperity enter every home, may the lives of farmers flourish, may the youth find new opportunities, may trade and industry advance, and may our India continuously grow economically and socially strong and prosperous.

Wishing you all a very Happy Deepavali.”

2333949.title: Revised Prices of Anti-Cancer Medicines to Come into Effect from 9th November;
2333949.ministry: Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers : Department of Pharmaceuticals
2333949.body_html:
Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers :
Department of Pharmaceuticals
Revised Prices of Anti-Cancer Medicines to Come into Effect from 9th November;
More than 1000 medicines of different brands show marked Price reduction;
Estimated annual savings to consumers expected to be above ₹3500 crore
Posted On: 07 NOV 2026 3:51PM by PIB Delhi

National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA), under the Department of Pharmaceuticals, Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers, capped trade margins on MRP of 137 anti-cancer drugs, based on the recommendations of Expert Committee constituted by the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) under Ministry of Health & Family Welfare on 17th October, 2026.  The revised prices of these drugs will come into effect from 9th November, 2026.

As on date, 76 pharmaceutical companies have reported revised MRP for 1225 anti-cancer formulations, covering 121 drugs. Reduction in the MRP have been reported in 1031 formulations of anti-cancer medicines, with 600 brands reporting above 50% reduction and the highest reduction being 96.45%. Further, out of the 137 identified anti-cancer drugs, there are 10-15 drugs which are yet to be launched in India. However, Trade Margin Rationalization (TMR) will be applicable on these drugs also as and when they are launched.   

As a result of the price reductions to be effected from 9th November, 2026, the estimated annual savings to consumers would be ₹3,502.31 crore.

2333923.title: Ministry of Steel Successfully Concludes Special Campaign for Disposal of Pending Matters (SCDPM) 6
2333923.body_html:
Ministry of Steel
Ministry of Steel Successfully Concludes Special Campaign for Disposal of Pending Matters (SCDPM) 6
Posted On: 07 NOV 2026 1:49PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Steel has successfully conducted the Special Campaign for Disposal of Pending Matters (SCDPM) 6 from 2nd October to 31st October, 2026. The Ministry of Steel and its Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) actively participated in the campaign, which focused on streamlining governance through effective disposal of pending matters and promoting cleanliness and efficiency in official functioning.

The campaign aimed at institutionalizing Swachhta and address pending matters across various categories, including references from Members of Parliament (MPs), the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), VIPs and Cabinet, State Governments and CPGRAMS cases among others.

Significant Progress Achieved

  • 100% of public grievances and Appeals redressal targets achieved.
  • 21,164 physical files reviewed, achieving 101% of the set target.
  • 17,107 physical files successfully weeded out.
  • 301 cleanliness drives conducted against a target of 301.
  • Approximately 17,501 sq. ft. of office space freed through the disposal of scrap, e-waste, and redundant files.

Several CPSEs under the Ministry implemented innovative best practices in record management and grievance resolution, setting benchmarks for other departments.

The Ministry of Steel remains steadfast in its commitment to enhancing administrative efficiency, promoting cleanliness, and ensuring timely resolution of pending matters in alignment with the Government of India’s broader goals of administrative reforms, transparency and good governance.

2333922.title: Defence Forces must maintain highest level of operational readiness, with focus on domain awareness, cyber resilience & information integrity to counter emerging threats: Raksha Mantri at Air Force Station, Bagdogra
2333922.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
Defence Forces must maintain highest level of operational readiness, with focus on domain awareness, cyber resilience & information integrity to counter emerging threats: Raksha Mantri at Air Force Station, Bagdogra
“Air Warriors deployed at Bagdogra serve as a robust shield for security of eastern sector”
‘Second Tour of Duty’ is a significant Diwali gift for Agniveers, says Shri Rajnath Singh
Posted On: 07 NOV 2026 1:44PM by PIB Delhi

Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh has called upon the Defence Forces to maintain the highest level of operational readiness, with special focus on strengthening domain awareness, cyber resilience and information integrity to effectively counter emerging security threats. Interacting with the personnel of the Indian Air Force (IAF) on the eve of Diwali at Air Force Station, Bagdogra, West Bengal, on November 7, 2026, he emphasised that the security landscape has become increasingly complex, with warfare extending beyond conventional engagements along the borders to encompass asymmetric warfare, proxy wars, cyber-attacks, drone swarms, information operations and narrative management.

“Often, the adversary avoids direct confrontation and instead seeks to exploit our vulnerabilities. Through social media, the adversary may attempt to sow doubt in the minds of the local population and our soldiers by spreading misleading information. In such a scenario, your role extends beyond that of an ordinary soldier,” said Raksha Mantri.

Describing Bagdogra as a strategically important region and a crucial link in India's security framework, particularly for the North-Eastern region, Shri Rajnath Singh commended the courage and dedication of the defence forces personnel towards safeguarding national interests. He stated that the Air Warriors deployed in the region serve as a robust shield for the security of the eastern sector, and their preparedness is fundamental to maintaining stability in the region.

Raksha Mantri underscored that discipline and courage remain indispensable, irrespective of technological advancements, stating that the conduct, bearing, language and restraint of the Defence Forces personnel shape the image of the military among local communities. Lauding the soldiers for discharging their duties with these qualities, he urged them to strengthen their engagement with the local population, particularly in and around Bagdogra, and nurture the deep bond of trust and affection between the people and the Defence Forces. “The more you engage with the local community, the weaker the adversary’s conspiracies will become,” he said.

Reaffirming the Government's resolve to achieve ‘Aatmanirbhar Bharat’, Shri Rajnath Singh highlighted the growing contribution of Indian start-ups and industries in developing drones, anti-drone systems and advanced military equipment. He appreciated the defence forces for embracing indigenous technologies and acquiring new skills in drone operations and cyber security. He underlined the importance of making the military increasingly technology-driven to effectively address future security challenges.

Referring to the Cabinet’s approval of the 'Second Tour of Duty' for Agniveers, Raksha Mantri stated that the decision would provide Agniveers with another opportunity to serve the nation. He added that upon completion of the two-year engagement period, all Agniveers will get an opportunity to be enrolled as regular soldiers subject to their willingness and their meeting selection criteria. He termed the decision as a significant Diwali gift for Agniveers, reiterating the Government's commitment to the welfare of the Defence Forces personnel and their families.

Shri Rajnath Singh extended his Diwali greetings and wished the Air Warriors and their families good health, happiness and prosperity. He said that the personnel, despite missing their families during the festival, remain steadfast in ensuring the security of their fellow citizens. He expressed gratitude to their families for their sacrifices and contributions. He emphasised that while the soldiers remain committed towards safeguarding the borders, the nation will always stand by their families and ensure their well-being.

Chief of the Air Staff Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit; Air Officer Commanding, Air Force Station, Bagdogra Air Commodore Manish Sharma; and other senior officials of the IAF were present on the occasion.

****

2333919.title: E20 Petrol Supplied by PSU Oil Marketing Companies Meets Prescribed Quality Standards; 893 Samples Across 27 States and UTs Found Compliant
2333919.body_html:
Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas
E20 Petrol Supplied by PSU Oil Marketing Companies Meets Prescribed Quality Standards; 893 Samples Across 27 States and UTs Found Compliant
All 56 samples tested in Karnataka also conform to IS 17021 specifications, with ethanol content ranging from 19% to 20%
OMCs seek joint sampling and independent testing under prescribed standards to verify reported ethanol levels in Karnataka
Posted On: 07 NOV 2026 1:18PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas has taken note of the press release issued by the Department of Food, Civil Supplies, Consumer Affairs and Legal Metrology, Government of Karnataka, claiming that petrol sold at certain retail outlets in the State contains between 26% and 31% ethanol.

In this regard, the three public sector Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs) — Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL), Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL) and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited (HPCL) have clarified that the claims, as reported, are not supported by testing conducted in accordance with the prescribed statutory and technical procedures. E20 petrol supplied by the three OMCs across the country, including Karnataka, conforms to IS 17021, the Bureau of Indian Standards specification for ethanol-blended motor gasoline.

They have also raised concerns regarding the sampling procedure and testing methodology adopted for the October 2026 exercise.

Concerns over Sampling and Testing Methodology

The Motor Spirit and High Speed Diesel (Regulation of Supply, Distribution and Prevention of Malpractices) Order, 2005, issued under the Essential Commodities Act, 1955, read with the Marketing Discipline Guidelines (MDG) 2024, prescribes a defined procedure for sampling, retention, testing and communication of results.

The prescribed procedure requires six one-litre samples to be drawn, with two samples handed over to the dealer against acknowledgement, two retained by the oil company or department, and two sent to a laboratory specified under Schedule III of the Control Order or notified in the Official Gazette. The sample labels are required to be jointly signed, and the test results communicated to the dealer and the oil company within the prescribed timeframe.

While samples drawn during the September 2026 exercise were routed through the State Level Coordinator to designated OMC laboratories and tested for the quality parameters requested under the MDG 2024, the subsequent exercise in October reportedly involved samples drawn without the participation of OMC representatives. The OMCs have also not received the corresponding retention samples, complete outlet-wise details or laboratory reports, despite seeking these through the State Level Coordinator.

The OMCs have further stated that the reported findings rely on certificates issued by a third-party laboratory rather than testing conducted at a laboratory specified under the Control Order. The certificates do not provide the complete technical details necessary to independently verify the reported ethanol content. The absence of counterpart samples and the prescribed documentation has also denied the OMCs and concerned dealers an opportunity to seek verification or retesting.

Testing Methodology Must Conform to IS 17021

A preliminary technical assessment by the OMCs has also highlighted concerns regarding the ethanol testing methodology cited in the certificates.

Under IS 17021:2018 (Amendment No. 3, August 2025), ethanol content in E20 fuel is required to be determined through prescribed methods, namely Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR) under ASTM D5845, water extraction under Annex C, or Gas Chromatography under ASTM D4815/D6839.

Importantly, when Gas Chromatography is used under ASTM D4815/D6839, the sample must first be diluted in a 1:1 ratio with oxygenate-free petrol, and the result corrected against an E10 certified reference material.

However, the certificates cited in the Karnataka press release merely mention “Ethanol % by Gas Chromatography”, without specifying the applicable standard test method, the prescribed dilution procedure or the reference material used for correction. In the absence of these essential details, the reported ethanol figures of 26–31% cannot be independently validated against the methodology prescribed under IS 17021.

The reported density readings also warrant examination. The certificates indicate densities ranging from 0.742 to 0.749 g/cc for samples claimed to contain 26–31% ethanol. This is lower than the 0.752–0.760 g/cc recorded for E20 samples tested by the OMCs under the QCC-1 and QCC-2 surveys. Given that ethanol has a higher density than petrol, a higher ethanol proportion would ordinarily be expected to increase the density of the blend. This discrepancy further underscores the need for testing through the prescribed methodology and verification against appropriate reference samples.

OMC and CHT Quality Monitoring Confirms Compliance

The Centre for High Technology (CHT), under the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, has been continuously monitoring ethanol blending and fuel quality across OMC retail outlets.

As part of the OMC/CHT Quality Coordination Cell (QCC) exercise, 893 E20 samples drawn from IOCL (330), BPCL (280) and HPCL (283) depots and retail outlets across 27 States and Union Territories have been tested for ethanol content as per IS 17021, Annex C, at refinery and OMC quality-control laboratories. All 893 samples were found within the prescribed ethanol content range of 19–21%.

Significantly, all 56 samples tested in Karnataka, comprising samples from different locations and all three OMCs, also conformed to the prescribed specifications, recording ethanol content between 19% and 20%, with an average of 19.30%.

These results demonstrate that ethanol blending at OMC retail outlets is monitored and controlled within the prescribed specifications. The findings are inconsistent with the substantially higher ethanol levels reported in the Karnataka press release and reinforce the need for a transparent, technically sound and jointly verifiable testing exercise.

Ethanol Blending is a Controlled and Automated Process

Ethanol blending at OMC refineries and depots is undertaken through established, calibrated and controlled systems. The process involves automatic calibration and proportioning arrangements at the refinery and depot levels, with blending governed by prescribed specifications and quality-control protocols. It is not a manual or arbitrary process of adding ethanol to petrol.

The OMCs maintain established quality-assurance systems across their supply and distribution networks to ensure that the blended fuel meets the applicable BIS specifications before it reaches consumers.

Consumer Impact Claims Require Scientific Assessment

The claims of an estimated annual consumer mileage loss of approximately ₹62,000 crore and vehicle-repair costs of approximately ₹39,000 crore, aggregating to around ₹1.01 lakh crore, also require careful examination against established technical evidence.

More than 30 crore two-wheelers and 4 crore four-wheelers have been running on E20 fuel for over three years. Every day, over 6 crore people visit petrol pumps to refuel their vehicles. If there were a widespread issue with E20 fuel quality, it would be expected to manifest in vehicle breakdowns across this large vehicle base. No such widespread incidence has been reported. This extensive, real-world usage is an important consideration in assessing claims relating to fuel quality and vehicle performance.

The performance and mileage implications of E20 have been examined by the Inter-Ministerial Committee and through studies involving Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL), the Automotive Research Association of India (ARAI) and the Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (SIAM).

As outlined by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas in its response titled “Response to Concerns on Blending of Ethanol in Petrol and Beyond”, published by the Press Information Bureau on August 12, 2025, vehicles calibrated for E20 can experience a mileage reduction of approximately 1–2%, while certain other vehicles may experience reductions of approximately 3–6%, depending on vehicle category and calibration.

Accordingly, applying a blanket assumption of 10% mileage loss across the entire vehicle population and extrapolating it into a national consumer-loss figure of ₹62,000 crore does not constitute a scientifically established assessment. Similarly, the ₹39,000 crore vehicle-repair estimate needs to be substantiated through a transparent assessment of actual vehicle-performance data, materials compatibility studies and documented repair costs.

Concerns relating to materials compatibility and vehicle performance have already been examined through studies involving technical agencies and the automobile industry. Any assessment of the programme's impact must therefore take into account vehicle category, manufacturing specifications, fuel compatibility and the findings of these technical studies, rather than relying on blanket assumptions.

Ethanol Blending Programme Delivers Wider Economic and Environmental Benefits

India's ethanol-blending journey spans more than two decades, beginning with the pilot programme in 2001 and progressing through successive policy interventions, including the National Policy on Biofuels, 2018, and the NITI Aayog Roadmap for Ethanol Blending in India by 2025, prepared in consultation with stakeholders.

The Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) Programme is an important component of India's efforts to reduce dependence on imported crude oil, strengthen domestic agricultural value chains and advance energy security.

Ethanol blending programme, since ESY 2014-15, has resulted in:

  • Foreign-exchange savings of more than ₹1.97 lakh crore.
  • Substitution of approximately 316 lakh metric tonnes of crude oil.
  • Reduction of approximately 952 lakh metric tonnes of CO₂ emissions.
  • Transfer of more than ₹1.66 lakh crore to farmers.

These measurable outcomes underline the wider economic, environmental and agricultural benefits of the programme, which cannot be assessed solely through a selective comparison of OMC profitability and alleged consumer costs.

During ESY 2025-26 ending 31st October 2026, PSU OMCs procured 1,089 crore litres of ethanol and blended 1,134 crore litres against petrol sales of approximately 5,673 crore litres, in pursuit of the national 20% blending target. The programme operates within a defined national framework, with blending levels and quality parameters monitored across the supply chain. Isolated and unverified allegations of substantially higher or lower blending at individual locations do not provide a meaningful assessment of the programme's overall performance.

The suggestion that OMCs have a commercial incentive to undertake blending beyond the prescribed target is also misplaced. Ethanol procurement involves a significant cost, and every additional litre blended beyond the prescribed proportion would add to the OMCs' procurement costs. The OMCs have no commercial rationale to undertake arbitrary or excess blending.

OMCs Seek Transparency and Independent Verification

In view of the concerns raised, the three OMCs have requested the Government of Karnataka to share the complete sampling documentation, outlet-wise laboratory reports and details of the test methodology adopted for the reported findings. They have also sought access to the counterpart samples for independent testing at an authorised laboratory using the prescribed referee method, in the presence of representatives of the State Government and OMCs.

The OMCs remain committed to cooperating with the State Government and other competent authorities in conducting joint sampling and testing in accordance with the Control Order and the MDG 2024. Any deviation established through the prescribed procedure will be dealt with in accordance with the applicable guidelines.

The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas reiterates its commitment to ensuring the quality of petroleum products supplied to consumers, regulatory compliance and consumer protection, supported by established quality-assurance and monitoring mechanisms across the nationwide supply and distribution networks of OMCs.

****
