2333906.title: WaveX Invites Startups to Participate in WAVES Bazaar at IFFI Goa 2026
2333906.bureau: PIB Delhi The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting
2333906.body_html:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
WaveX Invites Startups to Participate in WAVES Bazaar at IFFI Goa 2026
Startup Pod Bookings open for WAVES BAZAR under WaveX at IFFI Goa 2026
WaveX Booths to Showcase Emerging Film and related Technology Startups at WAVES Bazaar, Providing Global Visibility and Networking Opportunities
Posted On: 07 NOV 2026 11:53AM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Government of India, has invited applications from startups working in the field of film and allied technologies for participation in the WaveX Startup Pavilion at WAVES Bazaar during the International Film Festival of India (IFFI), Goa 2026.

The initiative aims to provide an exclusive platform for innovative startups to showcase their products, technologies and solutions to the national and international film and media industry. It will also facilitate opportunities for networking, industry engagement and collaboration with filmmakers, production houses, investors in the global creative ecosystem.

Applications are open to DPIIT-registered startups operating in the film and related technology domains. Eligible startups will be considered through a screening and evaluation process conducted by a Selection Committee constituted by WaveX.

Interested and eligible startups are encouraged to apply and take advantage of this opportunity to showcase their innovations on an international platform.

Registration form and more information are available at : wavex.wavesbazaar.com Queries may be directed to Wavex-mib [at]gov[dot]in.

About IFFI, Goa

The International Film Festival of India (IFFI), established in 1952, is one of Asia's significant film festivals, celebrating excellence in world cinema and providing a platform for filmmakers, artists, producers and cinema enthusiasts from India and across the world. Held annually in Goa, IFFI brings together the global film fraternity to showcase diverse cinematic works, encourage creative exchange and promote international collaboration in the field of cinema.

About WaveX

WaveX (WAVES Startup Accelerator) is a startup accelerator and incubation initiative of the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Government of India, dedicated to nurturing innovation, entrepreneurship and emerging talent in the Media and Entertainment sector. It focuses on supporting startups working in areas such as Animation, Visual Effects, Gaming, Comics, Extended Reality (AVGC-XR) and media technologies.

****

2333905.title: Legislative Department Initiates Interaction Series; First Session Focuses on Improving Values and Personal Effectiveness in Leadership
2333905.body_html:
Ministry of Law and Justice
Legislative Department Initiates Interaction Series; First Session Focuses on Improving Values and Personal Effectiveness in Leadership
Posted On: 07 NOV 2026 11:45AM by PIB Delhi

The Legislative Department, Ministry of Law and Justice, has initiated an Interaction Series with the objective of providing a platform for senior officers to share their experiences, professional insights and perspectives on various aspects of leadership, administration and personal effectiveness with the officers and officials of the Department.

The first session of the series was held on 5 November 2026 at the विधायी प्रशिक्षण सभागार, Kartavya Bhavan 2, New Delhi. The session was chaired by Dr. Manoj Kumar, Additional Secretary, Legislative Department. Smt. Akali V. Konghay, Additional Secretary, Legislative Department, delivered an insightful talk on the theme “Improving Values and Personal Effectiveness in Leadership”, sharing her personal experiences and perspectives on the principles of effective leadership.

During the session, Smt. Konghay emphasised that leadership is not confined to positions of authority or formal designations but is reflected in the ability of every individual to influence others through personal conduct, values and actions. She highlighted that leadership begins with personal transformation and requires vision, purpose, effective communication, accountability, collaboration and a commitment to empowering and developing others. She also underscored that leadership is fundamentally rooted in service rather than authority.

Elaborating on the importance of values and purpose in leadership, she introduced the concept of the ‘Five Cs of Purposeful Leadership’, namely, Consistency, Culture, Contribution, Community and Curiosity. She explained that these principles encourage individuals to consciously practise values such as integrity, humility, honesty, compassion and accountability; foster a positive and inspiring organisational culture; recognise and utilise their unique gifts, passions, talents, abilities and resources for meaningful contributions; develop a sense of responsibility towards the larger community; and remain curious, receptive to feedback and committed to continuous learning.

She further emphasised that personal effectiveness goes beyond efficiency in accomplishing tasks and involves becoming a better individual who contributes meaningfully to the lives of others. Highlighting the importance of self-reflection, she encouraged participants to assess their conduct, influence on others and contribution to society. She observed that the true measure of leadership lies in the positive difference one makes in the lives of others and in the ability to inspire and develop future leaders.

The session witnessed the participation of more than 80 officers and officials of the Legislative Department. The interaction provided an opportunity for participants to reflect on the importance of ethical values, purposeful leadership, personal growth and collective responsibility in professional and personal life.

The Interaction Series is envisaged as a continuing initiative of the Legislative Department to promote knowledge-sharing, encourage meaningful interaction and facilitate the sharing of experiences and best practices among officers and officials of the Department.

2333903.title: India-EU conclude negotiations to join Horizon Europe programme
2333903.body_html:
Ministry of Science & Technology
India-EU conclude negotiations to join Horizon Europe programme
Posted On: 07 NOV 2026 11:26AM by PIB Delhi

India and the European Union (EU) have successfully completed negotiations for India’s association with Horizon Europe, the EU’s flagship research and innovation programme. The association of India with the programme marks a strategic move into a long-term institutional framework of research cooperation between both sides, building on existing R&D projects and cooperation under the India–EU Agreement on Science and Technology Cooperation and the India-EU Trade and Technology Council.

The association will facilitate Indian researchers, institutions and industry to participate in the calls for funding under the Programme through collaborative research projects, and have access to European consortia and cutting-edge research infrastructure. It will also deepen talent mobility and lead to co-development of critical technologies, standards and solutions at scale.
The thematic clusters of Pillar II of Horizon Europe, which include health, digital technologies, industry and space, climate, energy and mobility, food and the bioeconomy, align closely with India's research priorities and can build on its scientific strengths. The association adds a significant value to the innovation ecosystem of the country as it marches towards Viksit Bharat 2047.
An exploration of the possible association was launched after the historic India-EU Summit on January 27, 2026, and formal negotiations were initiated as an outcome of the ministerial meeting of the Trade and Technology Council held in Brussels on July 15, 2026.

2333894.title: India’s Chemicals and Petrochemicals Sector: A Foundation for Industrial Growth
2333894.body_html:
PIB Backgrounder
India’s Chemicals and Petrochemicals Sector: A Foundation for Industrial Growth
Posted On: 07 NOV 2026 10:47AM by PIB Delhi

 

 

 

India’s chemicals and petrochemicals industry is expanding its manufacturing base, investment potential and international engagement. Dedicated industrial parks and integrated infrastructure aim to improve production capacity and attract investment. Research funding, specialised institutions and skill development are building expertise for advanced applications. Quality standards and workplace safety measures reinforce responsible industrial practices. Together, these efforts position the sector to pursue greater value addition, technological capability and a stronger role in global chemical markets.

 

 

 An Industry of Strategic Importance

India’s chemicals and petrochemicals industry is an important pillar of manufacturing, agriculture and industrial development. Its products serve diverse sectors, including pharmaceuticals, textiles, construction, automobiles, electronics and consumer goods. India is the sixth-largest producer of chemicals in the world and the fourth-largest in Asia. The sector is currently valued at around USD 220 billion. It is projected to reach USD 300 billion by 2030 and USD 1 trillion by 2040.

India also holds prominent positions in specialised chemical segments. It is the second-largest manufacturer and exporter of dyes and 3rd largest exporter of agrochemicals globally. There are approximately 13,000 large-scale units and 4.45 lakh micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in the sector. Several initiatives are advancing chemical manufacturing, research and industrial infrastructure. These include dedicated chemical parks, funding opportunities and measures promoting quality and investment. Together, these efforts seek to strengthen India’s participation in global value chains.

India Chem 2026: Connecting Industry, Investment and Global Markets

The 14th India Chem 2026 was organised from 22 to 24 October 2026 in Mumbai. The three-day event sought to attract investment and promote sustainable growth in the chemicals and petrochemicals sector. Its theme, “Advantage Bharat: An Emerging Global Chemicals Hub,” highlighted India’s industrial capabilities and opportunities for international collaboration. With a footfall exceeding 5,000 visitors, the event brought together industry leaders and businesses through country forums, the CEO Forum and sector-specific roundtables. The exhibition showcased technologies, equipment and investment opportunities, while the inaugural India Chem Youth Innovation Challenge encouraged students to develop practical, research-based solutions.

 

 Strengthening Manufacturing Capacity and Industrial Infrastructure

Strengthening domestic manufacturing requires investment, industrial infrastructure and an enabling policy environment. India permits 100% FDI through the automatic route for most chemical sectors. Under the Automatic Route, investment by a person resident outside India does not require prior approval from the government. FDI inflows reached ₹1,04,895 crore during 2014–2026, more than double the ₹45,240 crore recorded during 2004–2014.

The production of major chemicals and petrochemicals increased from 45,638 thousand metric tonnes (MT) in 2015–16 to 58,617 thousand MT in 2024–25. This momentum complements initiatives to expand industrial capacity, develop specialised manufacturing hubs and enhance infrastructure across the sector.

Petroleum, Chemicals and Petrochemicals Investment Regions

The concept of Petroleum, Chemicals and Petrochemicals Investment Regions (PCPIRs) is to promote the sector in an integrated manner. PCPIR is a specifically delineated investment region having an area of about 250 sq. km with around 40% of the area earmarked for processing activities. PCPIRs follow a cluster-based approach with common infrastructure, basic utilities and support services. These include roads, rail networks, ports, Common Effluent Treatment Plants, sewage disposal plants, water supply and steam generation units. This infrastructure provides a competitive environment conducive to setting up businesses.

  • India has three operational PCPIRs: Dahej in Gujarat, Visakhapatnam–Kakinada in Andhra Pradesh, and Paradeep in Odisha.
  • Together, these regions have attracted ₹3.4 lakh crore in investment.
  • They have generated 3.7 lakh jobs and facilitated the establishment of over 2,200 chemical manufacturing units.

This shared industrial ecosystem provides a foundation for further investment and value addition.

BHAVYA Rasayan: Dedicated Chemical Parks

The Bharat Audyogik Vikas Yojana Rasayan (BHAVYA Rasayan) Scheme, approved in July 2026, aims to establish three dedicated chemical parks. Each park will cover at least 8 square kilometres (2,000 acres) of land. The Centre will provide grants of up to ₹1,000 crore per park, subject to a minimum contribution of ₹500 crore by the concerned State Government. The scheme has a total financial outlay of ₹3,030 crore. Of this, ₹3,000 crore is allocated for common infrastructure and basic utilities, while ₹30 crore covers administrative expenditure. It will run for five years, from FY 2026–27 to FY 2030–31.

The parks will provide plug-and-play infrastructure for the chemical industry, helping improve resource utilisation and reduce logistics costs. It will also foster sustainable industrial development through an environment-friendly ecosystem. This includes centralised facilities such as Common Effluent Treatment Plants, Storage and Disposal Facilities, and hazardous waste management infrastructure. The scheme is expected to attract investment, expand domestic production capacity and strengthen global competitiveness.

Plastic Parks: Strengthening Downstream Processing

The Scheme for Setting up of Plastic Parks supports India’s downstream plastic processing industry. It focuses on increasing polymer (a petrochemical) absorption capacity and value addition in the domestic downstream plastic processing industry. Plastic Parks are industrial zones dedicated to plastic-related businesses and industries. Their objective is to consolidate and synergise the capacities of the plastic processing industry. This promotes investment, production and exports while generating employment. Under the scheme, the government provides grant funding up to 50% of the project cost, subject to a ceiling of Rs.40 crore per project. The remaining project cost is funded by the State Government or its agencies, beneficiary industries, etc.

The parks also encourage environmentally sustainable growth through waste management and recycling initiatives. This makes them an important part of India’s efforts to manage plastic waste and strengthen the chemical industry. Ten Plastic Parks have been approved across India, of which 4 have achieved 100% infrastructure completion, including 3 completed during 2025–26.

 

 

 Research, Innovation and Skill Development

As chemical applications expand across industries, the need for specialised knowledge and technical expertise continues to grow. Several initiatives are advancing these efforts through sector-specific research, specialised technical education and industry-oriented skill development.

Chemical Promotion and Development Scheme

The Chemical Promotion and Development Scheme (CPDS) facilitates the growth of the chemicals and petrochemicals industry through knowledge creation, dissemination and research promotion. It supports studies, surveys, databases and promotional materials to generate sector-specific knowledge. The scheme also incentivises research and innovation by recognising outstanding contributions to these sectors. It provides Grants-in-Aid (General) to organisations, industry associations and other entities for workshops, seminars, studies and related activities.

  • Since 2016, HIL (India) Limited, a public sector undertaking, has conducted farmer training programmes under CPDS.
  • The Institute of Pesticide Formulation Technology (IPFT) also began conducting these programmes from 2022–23. They promote the safe and judicious use of pesticides and encourage Integrated Pest Management practices.
  • These practices aim to minimise pesticide residues in food grains, edible oils, fruits and vegetables. As of August 2026, more than 250 programmes have benefited over 1 lakh farmers across the country.

Research, Development and Innovation Scheme

Launched in November 2025, the Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Scheme has a corpus of ₹1 lakh crore to catalyse private-sector investment in research and innovation. It provides long-term financing and refinancing on favourable terms for transformative projects. The scheme aims to accelerate advanced technology adoption, strengthen industrial competitiveness and promote self-reliance in critical and emerging technology areas.

Effective 8 October 2026, Advanced Chemicals, Petrochemicals and Material Technologies became an additional technology area eligible for funding under the scheme. This inclusion will strengthen sectoral research and innovation and facilitate the development of indigenous technologies for advanced industrial applications.

CIPET: Technical Education, Skills and Industry Support

The Central Institute of Petrochemicals Engineering & Technology (CIPET) is a centrally funded technical higher education institution. It undertakes Skill Development, Technology Support, Academic and Research (STAR) activities to advance India’s petrochemical and allied industries. CIPET has expanded through several centres and laboratories. These include the Centre for Skilling and Technical Support (CSTS), Plastic Waste Management Centre (PWMC) and School of Advance Research in Petrochemicals (SARP). Other facilities include the Advance Research School for Technology and Product Simulation (ARSTPS) and Advance Polymer Design and Development Research Laboratory (APDDRL).

  • CIPET’s network now comprises 51 centres, including 19 established since 2014. Three of these centres are dedicated to plastic waste management.
  • The institute has trained nearly 6.72 lakh skilled professionals, including over 5.21 lakh during 2014–24. It also completed 8.53 lakh Technology Support Service assignments during the same period.

 

Centres of Excellence

Centres of Excellence have been established to advance existing technologies, strengthen research and promote the development of new applications. 18 centres have filed 85 patents, published over 600 research papers and developed 105 new technologies and products. These achievements demonstrate the role of research institutions in building indigenous capabilities and supporting industrial innovation.

 Quality, Safety and Responsible Chemical Use

Quality standards and workplace safety are essential to responsible growth in the chemicals and petrochemicals sector. Regulatory measures help ensure product quality, while targeted training equips industrial workers to handle hazardous chemicals safely.

Quality Control Orders

To protect consumers, promote quality manufacturing and curb substandard imports, Quality Control Orders (QCOs) have been issued. As of August 2026, 37 QCOs are in force, making specified chemical and petrochemical standards mandatory. These orders require domestic manufacturers and importers to comply with the quality parameters prescribed by the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS).

Workplace Safety and Hazardous Chemical Management

A nationwide training programme has been launched under the Viksit Bharat@2047 Action Plan for the workforce of Major Accident Hazardous (MAH) Units. It focuses on the “Safe Handling of Hazardous Chemicals at the Workplace and Reducing Risk Associated with Hazardous Chemicals”. The programme is designed to cover all 2,393 MAH units over 5 years. Each training programme covers 100 participants from 50 MAH units, with two employees attending from each unit.

As of August 2026, 21 training programmes have been conducted nationwide. These programmes have been attended by 1,376 industrial units and have trained 2,441 personnel. The initiative seeks to strengthen workplace preparedness and improve awareness of hazardous chemical management.

 Towards an Integrated and Competitive Industry

India’s chemicals and petrochemicals industry spans a wide range of manufacturing activities, industrial applications and downstream products. Its development involves expanding production capacity, establishing specialised industrial facilities and creating an enabling environment for investment. Alongside manufacturing, research initiatives and technical institutions contribute to knowledge development, technology advancement and workforce training. Quality standards and hazardous chemical management address product compliance and workplace safety. India Chem 2026 connected these domestic developments with international participation, industry engagement and opportunities for collaboration. Together, these areas reflect the breadth of efforts shaping the sector’s industrial development and global engagement.

2333904.title: CAQM invokes Stage-III of GRAP in Delhi-NCR with immediate effect as Delhi records an AQI of 382
2333904.ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
2333904.body_html:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
 CAQM invokes Stage-III of GRAP in Delhi-NCR with immediate effect as Delhi records an AQI of 382
Posted On: 06 NOV 2026 10:00PM by PIB Delhi

The Sub-Committee on GRAP in its meeting held on 6th November 2026 comprehensively reviewed the air quality scenario in the Delhi-NCR region, along with the IMD/IITM forecasts. Delhi recorded a daily average Air Quality Index (AQI) of 382 i.e. ‘Very Poor’ category, as per the daily AQI Bulletin provided by the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) on 6th November 2026, due to poor dispersion of pollutants on account of unfavourable meteorological conditions, as observed by the sub-committee. Also, IMD/IITM forecasts indicated that the AQI was likely to slip into the ‘Severe’ category in the coming days.

In an effort to prevent further deterioration of air quality, the CAQM Sub-Committee on GRAP has taken the call to invoke the action plan as per Stage-III of the extant GRAP in the entire NCR. All actions as envisaged under Stage-III of the extant GRAP, are required to be implemented with immediate effect in right earnest by all the agencies concerned in NCR, in addition to all Stage- I and Stage-II actions of GRAP already in force. Further, agencies responsible for implementing measures under GRAP including Pollution Control Boards (PCBs) of NCR States and DPCC have been advised to ensure strict implementation of actions under all three stages of the GRAP, during this period. 

The action plan includes steps to be implemented/ ensured by various agencies including Pollution Control Boards of NCR States and DPCC. The Sub-Committee has urged citizens to adhere to the following specific steps listed in Citizen Charter of Stage-III along with Stage-I and Stage-II of GRAP and assist in effective implementation of the under: 

  • Walk or use cycles for small distances.

  • Choose a cleaner transport mode to commute.

  • Combine short journeys and reduce trips.

  • Postpone private gatherings that increase traffic and outdoor exposure.

  • Do not use coal and wood for heating purpose.

  • House owners may also provide electric heaters to security/other staff employed by them to avoid open burning of biomass / wood / MSW.

  • Follow hybrid mode for primary schools and work-from-home when instructed. 

The Commission is closely monitoring the situation and will review the air quality scenario on a regular basis in the coming days. The extant GRAP order is available on the Commission’s official website and may be accessed on the given link:  https://caqm.nic.in/FileUploadDomain/WebsiteDocument/GRAP/GRAP%20Orders/e93ab81c-af66-4c41-a6b1-41bdd4a8ff28.pdf.

2333803.title: From Occupational Risks to Safer Livelihoods
2333803.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Occupational Risks to Safer Livelihoods
A Journey Towards Dignified Sanitation Work Through NAMASTE
Posted On: 06 NOV 2026 8:50PM by PIB Delhi

For Mr. Ramesh Kumar (name changed), the NAMASTE Scheme has provided more than a set of safety equipment. It has strengthened his ability to work with greater security and dignity. His experience reflects the importance of extending occupational protection, safety awareness and support to sanitation workers, whose services are essential to public health and cleanliness.

At the age of 60, Mr. Ramesh Kumar, a Scheduled Caste sanitation worker from Pondicherry, has experienced a positive change in his working conditions through the National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) Scheme. His journey highlights the importance of occupational safety, protective equipment and awareness in ensuring the health and dignity of sanitation workers.

A sewer and septic tank cleaner with the Pondicherry Municipality for more than 15 years, Mr. Ramesh Kumar had spent years working in hazardous conditions without adequate personal protective equipment.

Prolonged exposure to hazardous waste resulted in recurring skin infections and respiratory discomfort, affecting his ability to work consistently and increasing his medical expenses. Having studied up to Class 5, he is the sole earning member of a family of four, and health-related interruptions and medical costs placed additional pressure on the household.

A significant change came in 2025, when he received support under the NAMASTE Scheme of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. He was provided with a complete Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) kit, including protective overalls, heavy-duty gloves, gumboots, a face mask and a safety helmet. He also received awareness training on safe sanitation practices and the prevention of occupational health risks.

The assistance brought a positive change in his day-to-day work. With access to protective equipment and greater awareness of safety practices, he was able to perform his duties with improved protection and confidence. His health improved considerably, work-related absences reduced and medical expenses declined.

The improvement in his health and work consistency also contributed to better financial stability. His monthly income, which was approximately ₹12,000 before the intervention, increased to around ₹16,000–₹18,000 after receiving the support. This has helped him meet household expenses and continue supporting his family.

2333799.title: Union Minister of State Shri Ramdas Athawale Visits Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 at Dilli Haat, INA
2333799.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Union Minister of State Shri Ramdas Athawale Visits Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 at Dilli Haat, INA
Mela Records Cumulative Sales of Approximately ₹ 37.90 Lakh, Reflecting Strong Public Response and Growing Market Opportunities for Artisans
Cultural Evening Programmes Offer Audiences A Mesmerizing Window Into India's Pluralistic Cultural Expressions, Creating A Festive Atmosphere And Fostering Regional Cultural Exchange
Posted On: 06 NOV 2026 8:38PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri Ramdas Athawale visited the ongoing Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 at Dilli Haat INA, in the National Capital, here this evening. The Mela is being organised by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India.

Smt Nimuben Jayantibhai Bambhaniya, Union Minister of State for Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution; Chairman-cum-Managing Director, National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), Shri Prabhat Tyagi; GM, NSFDC, Shri Sapan Barua; DGM, NSFDC Rajnish Banker, AGM NSFDC, Shri Gulshan Pahadiya; Manager NSFDC, Shri P. K. Jha; Assistant Manager, NSFDC, Shri Mahesh Chand besides other senior officials of the Ministry were present on the occasion.

Organized around the theme ‘प्रकाश और परंपरा – ज्योति से ज्योति जलाएँ’, the 15-day Mela brings together India's rich cultural heritage and traditional craftsmanship through seven distinct thematic zones. These include कला आँगन, प्रकाश चौक, पूजा पथ, सजावट बाज़ार, घराना, स्वाद चौक and मंच, offering visitors a comprehensive experience of India's artistic, cultural and culinary diversity.

Shri Ramdas Athawale toured and inspected the stalls, showcasing the Ministry's continued commitment towards promoting the entrepreneurial capabilities of artisans and beneficiaries belonging to Scheduled Castes, Other Backward Classes, Safai Karamcharis and persons with disabilities by providing them with an accessible platform to showcase and market their products.

Shri Ramdas Athawale said the Shilp Samagam Mela has emerged as an important platform for connecting traditional artisans and entrepreneurs with consumers, creating market linkages and strengthening livelihood opportunities.

He said the Central Government led by Hon’ble Prime Shri Narendra Modi, is committed to work for the inclusive socio economic development of all the sections of the people particularly the sections which need adequate opportunities to earn dignified livelihoods.

The Minister said the Mela showcases a diverse range of handicrafts, handloom products, traditional textiles, festive decorations, lamps, home décor items and other indigenous products through more than 130 stalls.

He added the Ministry has been organising Shilp Samagam Melas since 2022. Through these fairs, more than 1,000 artisans from Scheduled Castes, Other Backward Classes and Safai Karamchari communities have benefited from opportunities to exhibit and market their products.

The Minister said the event brings together traditional craftsmanship, handloom products, live craft demonstrations and cultural programmes, while promoting entrepreneurship, livelihood generation and inclusive participation.

Shri Athawale said the artisans are provided with free stalls, travel expenses, daily allowances, and transportation facilities for their goods.

Citizens, families and young visitors are thronging the Mela to explore the diverse range of traditional products, enjoy and apptreciate the craftsmanship of participating artisans and support their efforts towards entrepreneurship, economic empowerment and self-reliance.

A Senior Official in the Ministry said the Mela has witnessed encouraging sales since its commencement, reflecting the enthusiastic response of visitors and the growing appreciation for products crafted by beneficiary communities.

He said the total sales of approximately ₹37.90 Lakh have been recorded on the part of the four participating corporations, namely NSFDC, National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC), National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC) and National Divyangjan Finance and Development Corporation (NDFDC), between November 1 and November 5, 2026. The cumulative sales reflect the positive market response to the products showcased at the Mela and the growing market opportunities for participating artisans, he said.

He added the Mela also provides an opportunity for artisans to expand their market reach through initiatives such as Bharat TULIP, which connects artisans with e-commerce platforms, and Purple Fest, which celebrates the creativity and capabilities of persons with disabilities while promoting inclusion and equal opportunities.

A major attraction captivating visitors every evening is the series of cultural activities and programmes hosted at the Manch. Artists and troupe performers from different States come together to present colourful folk dances, traditional music, and regional art forms.

These evening programmes offer audiences a mesmerizing window into India's pluralistic cultural expressions on a single platform, creating a festive atmosphere and fostering regional cultural exchange.

The participating beneficiaries are supported by the Ministry's apex corporations, including the National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC), National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC) and National Divyangjan Finance and Development Corporation (NDFDC). The Ministry facilitates their participation by providing free stalls, travel expenses, daily allowances and transportation facilities for their goods.

The Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 will continue at Dilli Haat, INA, until November 15, 2026.

****

2333782.title: Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN) celebrates 77th Foundation Day and reaffirms India's vision for a “Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat”, through intensified enforcement, digital governance, and mission "Yuva Raksha"
2333782.body_html:
Ministry of Finance
Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN) celebrates 77th Foundation Day and reaffirms India's vision for a “Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat”, through intensified enforcement, digital governance, and mission "Yuva Raksha"
Posted On: 06 NOV 2026 8:22PM by PIB Delhi

Marking its historic Foundation Day, the Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN) celebrated its 77th foundation Day on 6th November 2026. On this occasion a programme was organised at CBN Headquarters Gwalior in which all the officers and staff participated.

Image: 77th CBN foundation Day celebration programme organised at CBN Headquarters Gwalior.

Deputy Narcotics Commissioner on welcome remarks said that Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN), is a premier and the oldest agency working in the field of Drug Law Enforcement under the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, regulating Licit Cultivation of Opium Poppy, Overseeing Import and Export of Narcotic Drugs, Psychotropic Substances and Precursor Chemicals, and undertaking intelligence-driven enforcement operations to prevent trafficking of contrabands which falls under NDPS Act 1985.

Underlining the Government of India's zero-tolerance policy against drug trafficking and aligning with the vision of a ‘Drug-Free Youth for a Developed India’, the Bureau has significantly scaled up its operational footprint. Originally established on November 6, 1950, to unify regional opium administrations, CBN has evolved into a premier National Law Enforcement Powerhouse and India's Competent National Authority (CNA) under United Nations Conventions.

On this Special occasion, CBN also unveiled its Hindi Magazine- ‘संयम 2.0’.

Image: Group Photo on CBN Raising day on which CBN also unveiled its Hindi Magazine- ‘संयम 2.0’.

CBN at Glance:

1. SEVENTY-SIX YEARS OF CHRONOLOGICAL EVOLUTION

From its roots in the All-India Narcotics Board created on April 2, 1949, the unified Opium Department was formally centralized into the Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN) on November 6, 1950 with its Headquarters at Shimla. To place leadership directly alongside the core traditional poppy-growing belts and to effectively monitor the same, the headquarters was permanently relocated from Shimla to Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh, in 1960. The enactment of the landmark Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985, completely modernized the agency, converting the CBN from a regulatory administrative department into a multi-role national law enforcement, facilitator and regulatory agency.

2. DISMANTLING TRANSNATIONAL SYNTHETIC DRUG SYNDICATES

From 2022 through October 2026, the CBN's specialized Preventive and Intelligence (P&I) Cells mounted an effective enforcement campaign, booking over 1,000 cases and arresting 1,325 individuals.

  • Historic Pharmaceutical Diversion Bust: Highlighting this multi-year crackdown, the CBN executed a monumental seizure in Delhi in July 2026, intercepting 12 crore (120 million) Tramadol Hydrochloride tablets (250 mg) weighing approximately 100 metric tons, permanently dismantling a major international pharmaceutical smuggling ring.
  • Environmentally Safe Disposal & Reclamation: CBN successfully destructed/ incinerated Total 342 Metric tonnes (3,42,000 kg) of seized narcotics, psychotropics and controlled substances. Concurrently, 2535 kg of highly pure raw opium seized from illegal channels was transferred to the Government Opium and Alkaloid Works (GOAW) facility in Neemuch to be reclaimed as vital medicinal alkaloids.

3. SOURCE-LEVEL ELIMINATION: ILLICIT CROP DESTRUCTION DRIVES

From 2022 to October 2026, Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN) mapped and eradicated huge volume of illegal crops directly at the source. CBN has destructed more than 1,11,300 Acres of illicit cultivation of opium and cannabis across high-risk states including Himachal Pradesh, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur and Uttarakhand.

  • Operation Parivartan (Himachal Pradesh): In the rugged, high-altitude terrains of the Kullu district, CBN units trekked up to 3,500 meters (11,000 feet) to manually uproot 2,070 hectares (5,165 acres) of illicit cannabis, by way of blending ground teams with drone technology and precise technological mapping.
  • Opium Poppy Destruction (Arunachal Pradesh): Deploying into remote mountain corridors alongside forest and paramilitary forces, the CBN mapped and manually destroyed 3,600 hectares (8,896 acres) of illegal opium poppy fields during the crop's critical flowering season.
  • Alternative Development Strategy & "Jan Samvad": Paired with enforcement, the CBN hosted public town-hall dialogues (Jan Samvad) in isolated villages like Malana, for transition farmers into legal, sustainable livelihoods like apiculture, dairy production, animal husbandry, and eco-tourism.

4. MISSION "YUVA RAKSHA": SAFEGUARDING INDIA'S YOUTH

Marking a major transition toward combining statutory enforcement with grassroots social interventions, the CBN’s flagship initiative—Mission "Yuva Raksha" and CBN outreach initiatives empowered and educated over 20,000 participants across Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, and Delhi during the 2026 calendar year.

  • Milestone Spiritual Partnership: On September 18, 2026, at Mount Abu, Rajasthan, the CBN signed a MoU with the Prajapita Brahma Kumaris Ishwariya Vishwa Vidyalaya to integrate values-based preventive education and community counselling deep into vulnerable hubs.
  • Insulating Farming Communities: Through rural public grievance cells (Jan Sunwai), the CBN actively works alongside traditional poppy-growing belts to protect rural youth from the reach of illicit trafficking networks.

5. DIGITAL GOVERNANCE AND EASE OF DOING BUSINESS (EoDB)

The CBN has successfully transitioned from traditional workflows into an automated, single-window digital architecture. By integrating its LPCO (License, Permit, Certificate, and Other documents) onto the centralized ICEGATE SWIFT 2.0 Portal, the Bureau seamlessly processes more than 15,000 import and export applications annually.

To secure international bulk drug and API supply chains while facilitating rapid trade clearances and awareness, the Bureau has progressively signed strategic MoUs with premier trade promotion bodies: the Indian Chemical Council (ICC) in 2022, CHEMEXCIL on April 28, 2025, and PHARMEXCIL on August 24, 2026.

FUTURE ROADMAP

Looking ahead, the modernized CBN is building an advanced technological ecosystem designed to pre-emptively counter emerging narcotic threats and New Psychoactive Substances (NPS). Future frameworks include the deployment of advanced crop-tracking tools, the establishment of a dedicated Chemical Management Division (CMD) to monitor high-risk non-scheduled industrial chemicals and the nationwide expansion of its holistic alternative development strategy.

“Drugs Out, Dreams In”

“Safe Supply Chain from Farm to Pharmacy”

"Drug-Free Youth for a Developed India"

2333760.title: Union Minister for Railways Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw Reviews Passenger Facilities and Security Arrangements at New Delhi Railway Station
2333760.body_html:
Ministry of Railways
Union Minister for Railways Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw Reviews Passenger Facilities and Security Arrangements at New Delhi Railway Station
Delhi Railway Area Handles Over 5 Lakh Passengers Daily, with Footfall Rising to Around 8 Lakh During Peak Festive Periods
Dedicated Holding Areas, Additional Special Trains, RPF Deployment and Additional AI Cameras Strengthen Festive Season Arrangements
Posted On: 06 NOV 2026 7:24PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Railways Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw today undertook a comprehensive inspection of New Delhi Railway Station to review passenger facilities, security arrangements and preparations for managing the increased rush during the Diwali and Chhath festive season. During the visit, he also interacted with passengers to seek their feedback on the facilities, with passengers expressing satisfaction over the arrangements made at the station.

Shri Vaishnaw stated that the festive season, which includes Durga Puja, Diwali and Chhath, witnesses the maximum passenger rush every year. He said that Indian Railways is making continuous improvements every day to enhance passenger facilities, improve services and provide greater convenience to travellers.

The Union Minister said that additional special trains and enhanced deployment of Railway Protection Force personnel have been arranged to manage the increased passenger movement. Additional 700 AI cameras have also been installed to strengthen surveillance and security. He further emphasised that special attention is being given to ensure that passengers can reach their respective trains in the shortest possible time after arriving at the station.

बेहतर भीड़ प्रबंधन के लिए रेलवे स्टेशनों पर 700 से अधिक AI कैमरे लगाए गए हैं और प्रमुख स्टेशनों पर विशाल होल्डिंग एरिया बनाए गए हैं: माननीय रेल मंत्री श्री @AshwiniVaishnaw जी https://t.co/lRHNNOBJkc

— Ministry of Railways (@RailMinIndia) November 6, 2026

Indian Railways is undertaking extensive efforts to facilitate passenger movement and improve travel arrangements during the festive season. These include dedicated holding facilities, additional ticketing arrangements, baggage screening, drinking water facilities and clean washrooms at major stations. The arrangements are aimed at providing passengers with a more organised and comfortable travel experience during periods of heavy rush.

Improved Holding Area Arrangements at New Delhi Railway Station

At New Delhi Railway Station, a dedicated holding area has been created for passengers travelling with reserved tickets, in addition to the facility for unreserved passengers introduced last year. A common holding area has now been created to streamline entry and passenger movement. Facilities for luggage checking have also been shifted outside the station building. As a result, the space previously used for ticketing inside the station has been converted into a comfortable waiting area. These arrangements help reduce congestion, simplify passenger movement and provide a more convenient waiting experience before passengers proceed to their respective platforms.

Significant Passenger Footfall Across Major Railway Stations

Delhi's major railway stations, including New Delhi (NDLS), Old Delhi, Anand Vihar Terminal (ANVT), Hazrat Nizamuddin and Sarai Rohilla, recorded approximately 2 crore passenger movements during the period 1 October-5 November 2026. Against the usual average of nearly 5 lakh passengers per day, the average daily footfall increased to approximately 8 lakh during the peak period of 1-5 November 2026.

Major railway stations in the Mumbai area, including Bandra Terminus, Lokmanya Tilak Terminus (LTT) and Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT), collectively recorded approximately 1.5 crore passenger movements  during the period 1 October-5 November 2026. The usual average daily passenger footfall of nearly 4 lakh increased to approximately 5 lakh during the peak period 1-5 November 2026.

Railway stations in the Hyderabad area, including Secunderabad, Kacheguda and Charlapalli, registered approximately 90 lakh passenger movements during the period 1 October-5 November 2026. The usual average daily footfall of nearly 2.5 lakh rose to approximately 4 lakh passengers per day during the period of peak 1-5 November 2026.

Railway stations in the Bengaluru area, including Bengaluru City, Sir M. Visvesvaraya Terminal (SMVB), Yesvantpur and Yelahanka, collectively recorded approximately 1 crore passenger movements during the period 1 October-5 November 2026. The usual average daily passenger footfall of nearly 2.5 lakh increased to approximately 3.5 lakh during the peak period of 1-5 November 2026.

Surat and Udhna railway stations collectively recorded approximately 50 lakh passenger movements during the period 1 October-5 November 2026. The usual average daily passenger footfall of nearly 1 lakh increased to approximately 1.6 lakh during the peak period of 1-5 November 2026.

Indian Railways continues to focus on improving passenger amenities, strengthening security infrastructure and introducing operational improvements based on experience and passenger feedback. These efforts are directed towards ensuring safe, convenient and hassle-free journeys during the festive season.

*****

2333753.title: Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah presents the President’s Colour to Uttarakhand Police in Dehradun
2333753.body_html:
Ministry of Home Affairs
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah presents the President’s Colour to Uttarakhand Police in Dehradun
Congratulations to Uttarakhand Police on receiving the President’s Colour; Uttarakhand becomes the 16th state in the country whose police force has received this highest honour
This is a moment of pride for every jawan and officer of Uttarakhand Police who has made “Karm Satyam Shauryam” the foundation of their life
This honour, earned through the dedication, discipline and sacrifice of the jawans, is dedicated to the 206 brave jawans who made the supreme sacrifice
Under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the country has been freed from Naxalism; now the resolve is to make a Drug-Free India
Within three years, we will also fulfil the resolve of making Devbhoomi drug-free
From forest fires and landslides to the rescue of workers trapped in tunnels, the jawans of Uttarakhand Police have resolutely dealt with every kind of sudden disaster
Uttarakhand Police has handled the burden of a growing population and the continuous movement of lakhs of pilgrims every month with great efficiency
In any remote area, it is either an ITBP jawan or a Uttarakhand Police jawan who reaches a stranded person first
Uttarakhand Police displayed indomitable valour in the rescue of workers trapped in the Silkyara tunnel and during several disasters, including those at Dharali and Tharali
Uttarakhand Police has a crucial responsibility in promoting tourism, attracting industrial investment, and ensuring speedy justice to citizens
Uttarakhand Police, which is working hard on the Naveen Nyaya Sanhitas, will ensure convictions in every FIR registered after May 2027 within three years
Uttarakhand Police bears the responsibility of ensuring the safety of lakhs of pilgrims visiting the Kumbh Mela, Char Dham Yatra, Hemkund Sahib and Kainchi Dham
Prime Minister Modi has addressed the migration from mountain villages through the Vibrant Villages Programme; with the efforts of the Uttarakhand Police, working alongside the CAPFs, border villages have begun to be resettled
Uttarakhand Police is the first police force in the country to successfully scale Mount Everest
Under our government, Uttarakhand is progressing at a rapid pace; tourists are increasing and industrial investment is also rising
Home Minister extended heartfelt wishes to the people of the country, especially the residents of Uttarakhand, on Dhanteras and Diwali
Posted On: 06 NOV 2026 7:16PM by PIB Delhi

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah today presented the President’s Colour to the Uttarakhand Police in Dehradun. On this occasion, Uttarakhand Chief Minister Shri Pushkar Singh Dhami, along with several other dignitaries, was present.

Addressing the President’s Colour investiture ceremony, Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah congratulated the Uttarakhand Police on receiving the President’s Colour and said that Uttarakhand Police has become the 16th force in the country to receive this highest honour. He said that this is a moment of immense pride for all those jawans and officers who have served in the Uttarakhand Police over the past 25 years since the formation of the state, those currently serving, and those who have retired. Shri Shah said that the Uttarakhand Police jawans and officers have not only adopted the three guiding principles of “Karm Satyam Shauryam” as their ideal, but have also made them the foundation of their lives and duties. It is on the strength of these very values that the Uttarakhand Police has achieved the honour of receiving the President’s Colour in such a short span of time.

Shri Amit Shah said that Devbhoomi Uttarakhand is endowed with natural beauty. Its snow-clad peaks, beautiful lakes, dense forests, elephant safaris, and the origins of Mother Ganga and Yamuna attract tourists from across the world. At the same time, Lord Badrinath himself resides here, Baba Kedarnath protects us, and the two mother goddesses emerging from Gangotri and Yamunotri not only bring prosperity to the lives of crores of people but also elevate them spiritually. Shri Shah said that Hemkund Sahib, described by the tenth Sikh Guru, is a major centre of attraction not only for Sikh devotees but for all pilgrims. Along with so many pilgrimage sites, the responsibility of ensuring the safety of lakhs of pilgrims who visit the prestigious Kumbh Mela, the annual Char Dham Yatra, Hemkund Sahib, and Kainchi Dham rests with the jawans of the Uttarakhand Police.

The Home Minister said that he comes from a state from where the largest number of pilgrims visit Devbhoomi, yet he has never heard any complaint about the Uttarakhand Police from any pilgrim of his state, which is a matter of pride for the state police and for all of us.

Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that receiving the President’s Colour is a moment of great pride for any force. He said that today we have all felt this moment with many hopes and aspirations, and with a sense of responsibility to instil confidence of security among the citizens of Uttarakhand and the people coming here from across the country. However, before this moment arrived, 206 brave jawans of the Uttarakhand Police made the supreme sacrifice. Shri Shah said that with moist eyes we not only pay homage to those jawans but also express our gratitude to them. It is on the strength of their dedication, discipline and valour, along with the service, sacrifice, unwavering commitment, continuous devotion to duty, outstanding professionalism and discipline of those currently serving, that the Uttarakhand Police has today become the 16th police force in the country to be awarded the President’s Colour.

Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that the journey of the Uttarakhand Police, which has grown from 13,000 jawans to over 26,000 personnel, has been quite challenging. He said that Uttarakhand has always struggled against various kinds of natural disasters. Major natural calamities have repeatedly forced the state into hardship. Yet, the jawans of the Uttarakhand Police, whether serving as part of the SDRF or as regular police, have resolutely confronted every kind of sudden disaster, from forest fires and landslides to the workers trapped in tunnels. He said that the Uttarakhand Police has handled the burden of a growing population and the continuous movement of lakhs of pilgrims every month with great efficiency. Shri Shah said that if anyone reaches a person stranded in a remote area first, it is either a jawan of the ITBP or of the Uttarakhand Police. It is because of this trust and confidence that crores of devotees find the courage to come here. He said that the Uttarakhand Police displayed indomitable valour during the rescue of workers trapped in the Silkyara tunnel, and several other calamities including those at Dharali, Tharali, Syanchatti and Maldevta.

Shri Amit Shah said that one of the major problems of Uttarakhand is the migration taking place from villages situated on the peaks and in the border areas. He said that Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has launched the Vibrant Villages Programme to address this issue. Working shoulder to shoulder with the Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF), the Uttarakhand Police is also fully dedicated to fulfilling all the standards of this programme. He said that as a result, there are at least 50 villages where, instead of migration, people have started resettling, which is a ray of hope for us.

Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that if the greatest efforts in the country to implement the Naveen Nyay Sanhitas (new criminal laws) have been made anywhere, they have been made in Uttarakhand. He assured the people of the state on behalf of the Uttarakhand government that the Uttarakhand Police will complete the process of securing convictions for the accused in any FIR registered after May 2027 within three years. He said that the residents of Devbhoomi will now be free from the endless cycle of dates. For this, the Uttarakhand Police has not only restructured its administrative framework but has also issued several notifications. The police have fully integrated forensic science laboratories and forensic science into their work. Computerisation has been implemented on the ground. With an outstanding score of 93.46 on the CCTNS/ICJS 2.0 Dashboard, the Uttarakhand Police has secured the top position at the national level. Jails, courts, FSLs, prosecution and the police have been linked electronically. He expressed confidence that in the coming days, the people of Uttarakhand will face no obstacles in receiving speedy justice.

Shri Amit Shah said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the country has been freed from Naxalism. The police of several states, along with the CRPF, ITBP, BSF and SSB, together brought an end to this five-decade-old menace. Lakhs of people lost their lives. He said that on 30 March 2026, he had declared in Parliament that the country is now Naxal-free, which is a matter of joy for all of us. However, we have no right to be complacent. He said that we cannot pause, as another serious problem confronts the nation — the menace of drugs. Shri Shah said that making India drug-free is our resolve. He said that we have decided that by 31 December 2029, India will be completely drug-free, and those engaged in the drug trade will be put behind bars. He said that the Uttarakhand Police has also done excellent work towards fulfilling the resolve of a drug-free India. Just as the Uttarakhand Police secured its place among the best-performing police forces in the country by achieving 93.46 per cent on the CCTNS, ICJS 2.0 and NCRB Dashboard, it has similarly done outstanding work in the areas of a drug-free India and cyber security. He said that the resolve for a drug-free India is a three-year plan, and we are confident that within three years we will also fulfil the resolve of making Devbhoomi drug-free.

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that Uttarakhand Police has also earned the distinction of becoming the first state police force in the country to successfully scale the world’s highest peak, Mount Everest. Uttarakhand Police has performed commendably by winning 37 medals at the World Police and Fire Games. He called upon Uttarakhand Police to top the medal tally and break all previous records at the next World Police and Fire Games, which are scheduled to be held in Gandhinagar, Gujarat.

Shri Amit Shah said that under the leadership of Chief Minister Shri Pushkar Singh Dhami, Uttarakhand is progressing by leaps and bounds. He said that our responsibility towards ensuring security increases alongside development. We want to attract tourists from across the world and the country to Uttarakhand, and they are visiting the state in large numbers. Therefore, our responsibility is even greater. He said that we also want to attract industrial investment so that the youth of Uttarakhand do not have to migrate outside the state in search of employment. This further increases our responsibility towards security. Shri Shah said that the resolve of the Modi government is to ensure justice for every citizen within three years, and keeping this in mind, the responsibility of Uttarakhand Police also increases. He expressed confidence that the President’s Colour awarded to Uttarakhand Police would boost the morale of the force and infuse new energy into its resolve.

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation also extended his warm greetings to the people of the country, particularly the people of Uttarakhand, on the occasions of Dhanteras and Diwali.

****

IAF’s SDI-IIT MADRAS AND IITM PRAVARTAK TECHNOLOGIES FOUNDATION SIGNS MEMORANDUM OF AGREEMENT FOR INDIGENOUS DIGITAL SECURE COMMUNICATION SYSTEM FOR AIRBORNE APPLICATIONS

The Software Development Institute (SDI) of the Indian Air Force (IAF) has signed a Memorandum of Agreement (MoA) with the Indian Institute of Technology Madras (IIT Madras) and IITM Pravartak Technologies Foundation for the joint design and development of an indigenous digital communication system for airborne applications. The MoA was signed by Air Vice Marshal Sarabjit Singh, Commandant SDI and Dr MJ Shankar Raman, CEO, IIM Pravartak Technologies Foundation, in the presence of Prof V Kamakoti, Director, IIT Madras.

Through this collaboration, the IAF intends to undertake joint development with IIT Madras and IITM Pravartak Technologies Foundation on advanced algorithms for communication system and networking. The indigenous development aims to reduce reliance on imported systems and bolster the operational efficiency of IAF contributing to Atmanirbhar Bharat vision.

2333744.title: Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, successfully concludes Special Campaign 6 for institutionalising Swachhata and reducing pendency
2333744.body_html:
Ministry of Finance
Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, successfully concludes Special Campaign 6 for institutionalising Swachhata and reducing pendency
Posted On: 06 NOV 2026 6:53PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG), Government of India, has issued guidelines vide Office Memorandum No. Q-11/01/2026-O&M (e-10171) dated 13.08.2026 for the implementation of Special Campaign 6 from 2 October to 31 October 2026. The campaign aims to institutionalize Swachhata (cleanliness), optimize workspace utilization, reduce pendency and enhance administrative efficiency across Government offices.

In line with these objectives, the Department of Revenue (DoR) undertook focused initiatives to promote cleanliness, improve workplace efficiency, ensure systematic record management, facilitate e-waste disposal, reduce pendency and strengthen citizen-centric service delivery. These efforts reaffirm the Department’s commitment to transparent, responsive and accountable governance.

As part of Special Campaign 6, a cleanliness drive was conducted at the lawns near India Gate and within office premises. The Department has also made significant progress in reducing pendency and improving record management. Approximately 400 files were weeded out or closed, around 1836 public grievances were disposed of, and 5 references received from the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) were addressed. Furthermore, revenue amounting to approximately ₹6,00,000/- was generated up to 31 October 2026 through campaign-related activities such as e-waste disposal & scrap disposal.

Special Campaign 6 extends beyond cleanliness to encompass the broader goals of administrative reform. Through the systematic decluttering of office spaces and processes, improved records management, timely disposal of pending matters and enhanced accountability, the Department of Revenue is working towards a more efficient, responsive and citizen-centric administrative ecosystem.

The Department remains committed to sustaining these initiatives and embedding the principles of Swachhata, efficiency and good governance into its day-to-day functioning.

2333743.title: Department of Fertilizers and Its PSUs Make Significant Progress under Special Campaign 6
2333743.ministry: Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers : Department of Fertilizers
2333743.body_html:
Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers :
Department of Fertilizers
Department of Fertilizers and Its PSUs Make Significant Progress under Special Campaign 6
1,26,052 Sq. Ft. of Office Space Freed Through Campaign Activities
3,184 Outdoor Cleanliness Campaigns Conducted
 Significant Progress in File Review, Record Weeding and Scrap Disposal
Posted On: 06 NOV 2026 6:48PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Fertilizers (DoF) and its Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) successfully implemented Special Campaign 6 from 2 October to 31 October 2026. The campaign aimed to institutionalize Swachhata, reduce pendency and enhance efficiency in government offices, in accordance with the guidelines issued by the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG).

As part of #SpecialCampaign6, The Fertilisers And Chemicals Travancore Limited organized a cleanliness drive at the #PMKSK, Udupi, Karnataka, in accordance with the Department of Fertilizers' directives. Before and After photographs highlight the remarkable improvement. https://t.co/wHogIvfHrM

— Department of Fertilizers (@BharatUrvarak) October 29, 2026

As of 31 October 2026, the Department and its PSUs have made significant progress in reviewing physical files and e-files, weeding out old records, disposing of scrap materials and improving cleanliness in office premises. The campaign also focused on the disposal of public grievances, appeals and other pending matters.

Key Achievements as of 31 October 2026

The Department and its PSUs recorded the following achievements under Special Campaign 6 :

  • Review of Physical Files: 14,190 physical files reviewed against 81,00 files identified for review.
  • E-File Management: 7,257 e-files reviewed against a target of 637, out of which 6,783 successfully closed.
  • Weeding Out of Records: 2,705 physical files weeded out against 5,516 files identified for weeding.
  • Cleanliness Drives: 3,184 outdoor cleanliness campaigns conducted by the Department and its PSUs, including cleanliness activities at PMKSKs.
  • Scrap Disposal: Revenue of ₹87,54,854 generated through the disposal of office scrap.
  • Space Freed: 1,26,052 square feet of space freed, enabling better utilization of office premises.
  • Public Grievance Appeals: All public grievance and appeals reported in the campaign data have been disposed of.

Social Media Outreach

As part of Special Campaign 6, the Department published more than 100 social media posts to raise awareness about cleanliness and efficient office management. These posts were disseminated through social media platforms such as  X (Twitter), Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp Channel and the PIB X handle.

#SpecialCampaign6 के अंतर्गत उर्वरक विभाग के निर्देश पर नेशनल फर्टिलाइजर्स लिमिटेड (NFL) द्वारा पंजाब के जालंधर जिले स्थित प्रधानमंत्री किसान समृद्धि केंद्र (PMKSK) में स्वच्छता अभियान चलाया गया। Before और After की तस्वीरों के माध्यम से सकारात्मक बदलाव को दर्शाया गया। https://t.co/8ZMY6L3f2j

— Department of Fertilizers (@BharatUrvarak) October 28, 2026

The posts highlighted cleanliness drives, records management, proper disposal of e-waste and scrap, and other campaign-related activities, thereby promoting awareness about Swachhata and efficient governance.

Special Campaign 6 Concludes

Special Campaign 6 concluded on 31 October 2026. The Department of Fertilizers and its PSUs remain committed to sustaining cleanliness, reducing pendency, improving workplace efficiency and ensuring the proper disposal of obsolete records, e-waste and scrap materials.

The campaign reflects the Government of India’s commitment to promoting cleanliness, improving efficiency and creating cleaner and more organized workplaces.

2333736.title: Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser and DPIIT Launches API Integration between Startup India and I-STEM Portals to Strengthen Access to National Research Infrastructure
2333736.ministry: Office of Principal Scientific Advisor to GoI
2333736.body_html:
Office of Principal Scientific Advisor to GoI
Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser and DPIIT Launches API Integration between Startup India and I-STEM Portals to Strengthen Access to National Research Infrastructure
Posted On: 06 NOV 2026 6:39PM by PIB Delhi

The Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India, in collaboration with the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry, launched the API integration of DPIIT’s Startup India Portal with the Indian Science, Technology and Engineering Facilities Map (I-STEM) Portal on 6 November 2026, under the chairmanship of Prof. Ajay Kumar Sood, Principal Scientific Adviser (PSA). The initiative seeks to strengthen linkages between the startup ecosystem and the country’s research infrastructure by enabling DPIIT-recognised startups to discover and access existing scientific and testing facilities.

The launch was attended by Dr. (Mrs.) Parvinder Maini, Scientific Secretary, Office of the PSA; and Shri Ateesh Kumar Singh, Additional Secretary, DPIIT. Dr. Vishal Choudhary, Scientist-F; Dr. Santhosh Nair, Scientist-D; Dr. Shefali Uttam, Technical Staff, Office of the PSA; and members of the DPIIT and I-STEM teams were also present. Dr. Vishal Choudhary gave a brief presentation about the current status and impact of I-STEM.

Speaking on the occasion, Prof. Sood highlighted that the integration represents an institutional convergence beyond a digital interface, connecting startup requirements with the scientific infrastructure and technical capabilities available across the country. He emphasised its potential to lower R&D costs, avoid duplication of capital-intensive facilities and enhance the utilisation of publicly funded infrastructure. He also underscored the importance of stronger industry–academia linkages and access to specialised facilities for deep-tech startups across technology development, prototyping, testing and validation.

Dr. Maini highlighted I-STEM’s role in promoting the sharing and optimal utilisation of scientific infrastructure across academic and research institutions. She noted that the integration would simplify the discovery of relevant facilities for DPIIT-recognised startups, helping address infrastructure-related barriers to technology development and innovation.

Shri Ateesh Kumar Singh highlighted the role of the integration in strengthening DPIIT’s efforts to build an enabling environment for startups, particularly in the deep-tech sector. He noted that the integration would provide DPIIT-recognised startups with improved visibility of specialised research, testing and prototyping facilities, enabling them to identify suitable infrastructure, reduce the need for independent capital investment in expensive equipment, and access institutional capabilities to support product development, testing and technology validation.

The integration will facilitate seamless, API-enabled interoperability between the Startup India Portal and I-STEM, with the proposed incorporation of Single Sign-On (SSO) functionality in subsequent phases, enabling DPIIT-recognised startups to directly access and leverage I-STEM's scientific infrastructure and research facilities through the Startup India Portal. Automated verification of DPIIT recognition status and seamless linking will streamline onboarding and facilitate the discovery of scientific equipment and research facilities. While the integration simplifies the process of identifying and requesting access to infrastructure, individual requests will continue to be evaluated and approved by the respective host institutions based on technical suitability, availability, applicable charges, safety requirements and institutional permissions. As of 6 November 2026, I-STEM listed 31,540 equipment items across 4,044 registered institutions, providing a substantial national resource base for researchers and innovators.

The initiative brings together the complementary institutional strengths of DPIIT and the Office of the PSA to build a more connected and resource-efficient innovation ecosystem. Wider onboarding of research facilities, regular updation of infrastructure information and sustained engagement with startups and host institutions will be essential to maximise its reach and facilitate the translation of scientific capabilities into technology-based solutions.

2333721.title: CULMINATION OF THE MAIDEN BIMSTEC MARITIME SECURITY EXERCISE AT ANDAMAN AND NICOBAR COMMAND
2333721.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
CULMINATION OF THE MAIDEN BIMSTEC MARITIME SECURITY EXERCISE AT ANDAMAN AND NICOBAR COMMAND
Posted On: 06 NOV 2026 6:13PM by PIB Delhi

The maiden BIMSTEC Maritime Security Exercise culminated successfully at Sri Vijaya Puram on 03 Nov 2026, following a series of engagements and coordinated maritime activities conducted from 30 Oct to 03 Nov 2026 under the aegis of the Andaman and Nicobar Command (ANC), India's only Operational Quad Service Command, headed by VAdm Vineet McCarty, Commander-in-Chief, Andaman and Nicobar Command.

The exercise witnessed the participation of naval ships from BIMSTEC member states: Indian Naval Ships INS Taragiri, INS Karmuk and INS Saryu; Myanmar Navy Ship UMS King Aung Zeya; and Sri Lanka Navy Ship SLNS Gajabahu. The event marks a significant milestone in advancing regional maritime collaboration and collective security.

The exercise brought together senior dignitaries and distinguished representatives, including HE Indra Mani Pandey, Secretary General, BIMSTEC; VAdm Biswajit Dasgupta (Retd), National Maritime Security Coordinator; RAdm Kyaw Kyaw Htoo, Commander, Central Naval Command, Myanmar Navy; Air Vice Marshal MDR Prasad (Retd.), Director (Monitoring and Evaluation), Ministry of Ports and Civil Aviation, Sri Lanka; and Capt Mohammad Monzurul Islam, Commanding Officer, BNS Prottoy, Bangladesh. Their participation underscored the importance accorded to strengthening regional maritime cooperation and collective security.

Conducted in the spirit of the Delhi Declaration and in furtherance of the outcomes of the 4th BIMSTEC Experts Group Meeting on Maritime Security Cooperation held in Nov 2025, the exercise provided a valuable platform for participating navies to enhance interoperability, strengthen professional interactions and foster mutual understanding through collaborative maritime engagements.

The harbour phase at Sri Vijaya Puram featured high-level engagements, professional interactions and cultural exchanges, providing opportunities for participating delegations to deepen institutional ties and strengthen bonds of friendship. The subsequent sea phase, conducted off Sri Vijaya Puram from 02 to 03 Nov 2026, involved coordinated maritime deployments and collaborative operational activities, underscoring the collective commitment of BIMSTEC member states towards a secure and stable maritime environment.

Beyond operational cooperation, the exercise fostered enduring camaraderie among participating personnel and reinforced the shared vision of a prosperous, resilient and open Bay of Bengal. It showcased the collective resolve of BIMSTEC nations to address common maritime challenges and safeguard shared maritime interests through sustained cooperation.

The successful culmination of the maiden exercise marks an important step towards institutionalising greater maritime engagement among BIMSTEC member states. For the Andaman and Nicobar Command, hosting this landmark event reaffirms its pivotal role in promoting regional maritime cooperation and contributing to peace, security and stability across the Bay of Bengal region. The exercise also lays a strong foundation for future collaborative initiatives under the BIMSTEC framework.
