2333311.title: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) signs MoU with TRIFED to Strengthen Market Access for PM Vishwakarma Artisans
2333311.body_html:
Ministry of Micro,Small & Medium Enterprises
Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) signs MoU with TRIFED to Strengthen Market Access for PM Vishwakarma Artisans
TRIFED to facilitate onboarding, capacity building, product promotion and market access through Tribes India retail outlets and its online marketplace
Collaboration to establish a “Tribes India–PM Vishwakarma Collection” and expand the visibility of products made by artisans
Posted On: 05 NOV 2026 8:34PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Tribal Cooperative Marketing Development Federation of India (TRIFED), under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs, to strengthen market access for eligible tribal artisans registered under the PM Vishwakarma Scheme. The MoU was signed in the presence of Dr. Rajneesh, Additional Secretary & Development Commissioner, Ministry of MSME; Shri M. Raja Murugan, Managing Director, TRIFED; along with Shri Nitish Kumar, Deputy Director General (DDG); Shri Danish Ashraf, Joint Development Commissioner, Ministry of MSME;  and Shri Prateek Singh Meena, Executive Director, TRIFED.
The collaboration brings together the Ministry of MSME’s PM Vishwakarma framework and TRIFED’s established Tribes India marketplace and retail network.

     The PM Vishwakarma Scheme, launched on 17 September 2023, seeks to improve the quality and reach of the products and services of traditional artisans and craftspeople. The Scheme supports artisans whose         skills are passed from generation to generation through the traditional guru-shishya model of training within families and informal groups.


Objectives of the MoU:-

  • Under the MoU, the Ministry of MSME and TRIFED will collaborate to facilitate the display, promotion and sale of products made by eligible tribal artisans registered under PM Vishwakarma scheme. The collaboration will cover product-based trades such as carpenter, metalsmith, sculptor, goldsmith, potter, shoe smith, basket, mat /broom maker/ coir weaver, doll and toy maker, garland maker, etc.
  • TRIFED will facilitate the onboarding and capacity building of eligible tribal artisans referred by the Ministry of MSME and provide them market access through the Tribes India retail network and its online marketplace, subject to applicable onboarding conditions and policies.
  • Products made by participating tribal artisans will be displayed through the Tribes India retail network and on tribesindia.com under the proposed “Tribes India–PM Vishwakarma Collection”, subject to sellers’ consent and compliance with applicable TRIFED policies.
  • TRIFED will facilitate aggregation, quality assurance and packaging support for market-ready products and will work with the Ministry of MSME to provide initial product imaging and cataloguing support to mutually identified sellers.
  • TRIFED will facilitate promotion of products made by identified tribal Vishwakarmas through its e-marketplace and provide dedicated display and sales space across its outlets, subject to the provisions and applicable terms of the MoU.
  • The Ministry of MSME will identify and facilitate potential sellers, encourage them to list products across different categories on tribesindia.com, conduct awareness workshops and support coordination between artisans and TRIFED.
  • TRIFED’s product portfolio includes tribal textiles, metal crafts, cane and bamboo products, organic foods, tribal paintings, jewellery and pottery, while its retail outlets showcase tribal handloom and handicraft products from communities across the country.

This collaboration represents an important step towards expanding the market visibility of tribal artisans registered under PM Vishwakarma by connecting their traditional products with the Tribes India retail and digital marketplace network. It will support product presentation, capacity building and broader market access for participating artisans, in accordance with the applicable terms and policies of the two organisations.

2333284.title: Ministry of Railways Concludes Year-Long Celebrations Marking 150 Years of Vande Mataram
2333284.body_html:
Ministry of Railways
Ministry of Railways Concludes Year-Long Celebrations Marking 150 Years of Vande Mataram
Mass Singing, Essay Competition, Quiz and Tiranga Rally Organised as Part of Four-Phase Celebrations
Posted On: 05 NOV 2026 7:59PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Railways organised a cultural programme at Rail Bhawan, today, marking the fourth phase (closing week, 1-7 November 2026) of the year-long celebrations commemorating 150 years of Vande Mataram. The programme was attended by the Chairman and CEO of Railway Board Shri Satish Kumar, Board Members, Director Generals and other senior railway officials.

The year-long celebrations were organised in four phases through a series of activities highlighting national unity, patriotism and India’s rich cultural heritage associated with the National Song.

First Phase: Mass Singing of Vande Mataram

The first phase commenced with a mass singing of Vande Mataram on 7 November 2025 at Conference Hall, Rail Bhawan. The programme was attended by the Union Minister for Railways, Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw.

Second Phase: Essay Competition

An essay competition on the theme “Vande Mataram: The Spirit of Unity in India’s Diversity” was organised at Railway Board on 22 January 2026, providing participants an opportunity to reflect on the significance of the National Song and its message of unity.

Third Phase: Quiz Competition and Tiranga Rally

A quiz competition based on the 150-year journey of Vande Mataram was organised at Railway Board on 10 August 2026. A Tiranga Rally, led by the Union Minister for Railways, Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw, was also conducted within the premises of Rail Bhawan. The Chairman and CEO, Railway Board, Shri Satish Kumar, Board Members, Director Generals and other senior officials participated in the rally.

Fourth Phase: Felicitation of Winners and Closing Programme

During the programme held on 5 November 2026, the winners of the Essay Competition conducted during the second phase and the Quiz Competition organised during the third phase were felicitated with prizes and merit certificates.

The Railway Board Cultural Group was also felicitated for its contribution to the successful organisation of various programmes throughout the year-long celebrations. The group was awarded a prize along with a merit certificate in recognition of its efforts.

The spirit of Vande Mataram continues to inspire the values of unity, dedication and collective effort. These values are also reflected in the functioning of Indian Railways. The celebrations reaffirmed the commitment of railway officials to discharge their duties with utmost sincerity, integrity and efficiency, while contributing towards taking Indian Railways to greater heights.

2333283.title: ‘Nasha Mukt Yuva, Viksit Bharat Quiz’ Records Participation of Over 16,517 Citizens
2333283.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
‘Nasha Mukt Yuva, Viksit Bharat Quiz’ Records Participation of Over 16,517 Citizens
Quiz to Remain Open for Participation Until November 25, 2026
Campaign Reaches Over 35.70 Crore People, Including 14.26 Crore Youth and 11.24 Crore Women
Over 33.28 Lakh Activities Conducted in Educational Institutions; 39.91 Lakh Persons Treated and Rehabilitated; More Than 755 DoSJE-Supported De-addiction Centres Working Across the Country
Over 46.70 Lakh Nasha Mukt Pledges Taken; More Than 2 Lakh Nasha Mukti Mitras Registered
Posted On: 05 NOV 2026 7:55PM by PIB Delhi

The online ‘Nasha Mukt Yuva, Viksit Bharat Quiz’ has witnessed an encouraging response, with participation crossing 16,517 citizens as of November 5, 2026. The growing participation reflects increasing public engagement, particularly among young people, in the collective endeavour of building a drug-free India.

The quiz was launched on October 26, 2026, by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, under the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (NMBA). The initiative aims to promote awareness about the harmful effects of substance use and encourage citizens, especially youth, to actively contribute towards creating a Nasha Mukt Bharat.

 

The quiz is being conducted from October 26 to November 25, 2026, and is open to all citizens. Participants can access the quiz through the MY Bharat portal.

Participation Link:

https://mybharat.gov.in/quizzes/yuva/detail/Url9dlIwCinQVSf8lwPB9w/

Launched on August 15, 2020, the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan aims to strengthen drug demand reduction efforts through preventive education, awareness generation, treatment, rehabilitation and community participation. Initially launched in 272 vulnerable districts, the Abhiyaan has since expanded its reach to cover all districts across the country.

 

The campaign has reached over 35.09 crore people, including 13.99 crore youth and 10.91 crore women, reflecting the nationwide scale of its awareness and outreach initiatives.

Under the Abhiyaan, over 32.43 lakh activities have been conducted in educational institutions, while 39.91 lakh persons have been treated and rehabilitated through a network of more than 755 Department of Social Justice and Empowerment (DoSJE)-supported de-addiction centres working across the country. The total number of Nasha Mukt pledges taken has crossed 45.07 lakh, with more than 2 lakh Nasha Mukti Mitras registered.

MY Bharat Quiz QR

As the Abhiyaan enters its seventh year, the quiz seeks to deepen public understanding of the harmful effects of substance use, promote informed decision-making and encourage young people to become active ambassadors of awareness and prevention. The initiative reinforces the vision of a Nasha Mukt Bharat and Viksit Bharat, recognising the importance of healthy individuals, families and communities in the country's development.

 

The quiz comprises 20 Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs), which participants are required to answer within 10 minutes. A participation certificate is generated for every participant who successfully submits the quiz.

 

 

 

 

 

 

Nasha Mukti Mitr Registration QR Code


Participants can also view the correct answers upon completion, enabling them to enhance their understanding of substance use prevention.

NMBA Mobile App

Through this digital initiative, the Ministry aims to strengthen community participation, encourage responsible choices and mobilise citizens, especially youth, to contribute to the movement against substance use.

NMBA e-pledge QR Code

The Ministry encourages all citizens, particularly young people, to participate in the ‘Nasha Mukt Yuva, Viksit Bharat Quiz’ before November 25, 2026, and become active contributors to the collective vision of a drug-free India.

2333281.title: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi interacts with Indian Contingent that participated in Asian Para Games 2026
2333281.body_html:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi interacts with Indian Contingent that participated in Asian Para Games 2026
The phenomenal journey from 14 in 2010 to 114 medals is the ultimate testament to your relentless hard work and dedication: PM
Keeping the Olympics firmly in focus, from the ramparts of the Red Fort this time, I have urged our youth to step forward and participate in the talent hunt campaign: PM
The government has approved the Khelo India Sports Goods Manufacturing Scheme; It is now time for our sports goods manufacturing industry to achieve new milestones: PM
Whenever an Indian or foreign athlete steps onto the field, their sports gear, as well as their apparel and footwear, should be 'Made in India': PM
We want India to produce world-class players and also manufacture world-class sports equipment: PM
Posted On: 05 NOV 2026 7:52PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today interacted with the Indian contingent that participated in the Asian Para Games 2026 at Indira Gandhi Sports Complex in New Delhi. Speaking on the occasion, the Prime Minister stated that he had been eagerly waiting to meet the Para-Asian Games athletes after interacting with the Asian Games contingent a few weeks ago, and noted that their magnificent performance reflects India's rapid emergence as a major global sporting power. Congratulating the players on behalf of 140 crore citizens and felicitating their families, trainers, and coaches for their vital contributions, he stated that the athletes have won both medals on a grand stage and the hearts of millions across the nation.

Contrasting past eras when India's sporting participation was treated as a mere formality and the country lagged in para-sports with just one gold and 14 total medals at the 2010 Para Asian Games, the Prime Minister highlighted the contingent's historic leap to 114 medals comprising 30 gold, 35 silver, and 49 bronze alongside five world records and nine Asian records. Noting that 34 of the 56 female athletes won medals, Indian players swept all three podium spots in four events, and the contingent clinched nine gold medals on the final day alone, he praised their relentless drive to keep winning until the very end of the tournament. “This journey from 14 to 114 medals is the result of the pinnacle of your hard work,” observed PM Modi.

Spotlighting maiden gold medals won by Indian athletes in several events where the country had never succeeded before, the Prime Minister noted that Mona Agarwal set a world record in para shooting while Haney broke his own previous world record. “Through their performance, Himanshu, Ravi, and Jehan showed the world how physical challenges are to be defeated,” noted Shri Modi.

Observing that while the world witnesses the brilliance of individual or collective victory, the grand edifice of success rests on years of unseen toil, sweat, and unwavering penance, the Prime Minister recalled how athlete Rinku maintained his courage after losing his mother just two months before the Asian Para Games and honored her memory by lifting her photograph upon winning gold. “That moment made all of us emotional,” remarked PM Modi.

Describing the athletes' struggles and triumphs as deeply inspiring, the Prime Minister pointed out the close parallel between their personal journeys and the nation's own developmental trajectory. “Today your efforts and the country's efforts are coming together to become an unstoppable force,” affirmed Shri Modi.

the Prime Minister stated that just as the athletes refused to bow before adversity, the nation resolved to overhaul the system so youth talent would not go to waste, instilling confidence among young athletes that the country stands firmly behind them. Pointing to India's growing dominance in archery, athletics, shooting, swimming, table tennis, badminton, judo, and powerlifting, he noted that 36 of the 61 debutants at the Asian Para Games won medals while Sandeep set a world record on his debut. “This participation of the youth is both a picture of today's India and a proclamation of the India of the future,” asserted PM Modi.

Emphasizing that the government views sports not merely as national and international tournaments but as a vital medium for personality development and nation-building, the Prime Minister stated that athletics imparts essential life values to young citizens. “It is sports alone that teach the youth how to win after losing and explain the meaning of discipline and team spirit,” remarked Shri Modi.

Detailing efforts to build a modern sports ecosystem through school and grassroots campaigns, numerous Khelo India Centres, and Olympic-standard training under the TOPS scheme, the Prime Minister recalled his recent call from the Red Fort inviting youth to participate in a nationwide talent hunt campaign with an eye on the Olympics. “With this very vision, we are building a modern sports ecosystem for the country,” asserted PM Modi.

Highlighting that para-sports receive equal priority within these national initiatives to help athletes shine at major global events, the Prime Minister pointed to the tangible outcomes achieved at the recent tournament. “In this competition, players receiving assistance from TOPS won 41 medals, and Khelo India players won 19 medals, which shows that our efforts are moving forward in the right direction,” noted Shri Modi.

Observing that India's modern sports policies are generating wide-ranging youth opportunities beyond the playing field, the Prime Minister pointed to the rapid expansion of sports infrastructure construction, equipment manufacturing, and the broadcasting economy. “Today modern policies regarding sports in India are creating numerous new opportunities for the youth in the world of sports even outside the field,” observed PM Modi.

Noting the recent approval of the Khelo India Sports Goods Manufacturing Scheme worth over 1,800 crore rupees, the Prime Minister called upon the domestic sports manufacturing industry to ensure that athletes worldwide step onto the field wearing Made-in-India gear, apparel, and footwear, thereby strengthening MSMEs and creating jobs in small towns and rural areas. “We want India to produce world-class players and also manufacture world-class sports equipment,” asserted Shri Modi.

Urging the athletes during their upcoming visits to schools, colleges, and institutions to mentor youth on both on-field victory and off-field sports careers while highlighting government initiatives for Divyangjans, the Prime Minister noted the recent Cabinet decision increasing disability pensions, lowering the eligibility threshold from 80 percent to 40 percent, and extending pension coverage from birth rather than age 18, alongside creating a 10,000-word Indian Sign Language dictionary, providing sign-language schoolbooks, and making public spaces accessible under the Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan. “Our effort is that every Divyang brother and sister of the country gets respect, gets equal opportunities, and can move forward in life on the strength of their capability,” affirmed PM Modi.

Reminding the contingent that the Aichi-Nagoya podium is a launching pad rather than the final destination as India sets its sights on the Los Angeles 2028 Games, for which Avani and Manish have already secured quotas, the Prime Minister urged the athletes to celebrate their triumph and immediately begin preparations to ensure record participation and medal hauls in 2028 before concluding with his best wishes. “The country is with you, and the entire country is waiting for your next victory,” affirmed Shri Modi.

2333279.title: Department of Posts Takes Special Campaign 6 to the Last Mile-  Exceeds Targets
2333279.body_html:
Ministry of Communications
Department of Posts Takes Special Campaign 6 to the Last Mile- Exceeds Targets
Cleaned 1,50,000 Sites
Resolved 1,50,000 Public Grievances and Disposed off 1,500 Appeals
Disposed over 8 lakh kg of scrap and 58,514 kg of e-waste worth ₹3.01 crore
Posted On: 05 NOV 2026 7:49PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Posts, Ministry of Communications, successfully conducted Special Campaign 6 from 2nd to 31st October 2026, across its extensive nationwide network, reaffirming its commitment to institutionalising Swachhata, improving administrative efficiency, promoting environmental sustainability and strengthening citizen-centric service delivery.

The campaign witnessed significant achievements across its key focus areas. The Department resolved 1,50,000 public grievances and disposed of 1,500 appeals during the campaign. Against the target of cleanliness activities at 1.35 lakh sites, the Department covered 1,50,000 sites across the country. The campaign also resulted in freeing up 2,03,570 sq. ft. of office space for productive utilisation.

Swachhata: Taking the Last-Mile Approach

The Department adopted a comprehensive approach to Swachhata, covering cleanliness, efficient record management, disposal of redundant material, scientific waste management, optimum space utilisation and process simplification. Cleanliness drives were conducted across Post Offices, including Branch Post Offices, mail offices and administrative establishments, with a focus on public-facing and common areas.

The campaign also promoted Waste to Wealth through reuse of discarded materials, plantation and beautification initiatives. Notably, Mail Motor Services, Kolkata, renovated an office chamber using recycled wooden scrap, showcasing innovative resource utilisation.

Scientific Waste Management and Environmental Sustainability

A major thrust of Special Campaign 6 was the scientific management of scrap and e-waste. The disposal of over 8.03 lakh kg of scrap and 58,514 kg of e-waste generated revenue of approximately ₹3.01 crore during the campaign, while also contributing to better space utilisation and environmentally responsible disposal practices.

Postal Circles undertook several innovative initiatives to promote environmental sustainability. Assam Circle introduced Vertical Green Walls at its N-Gen Post Offices by converting discarded plastic waste and containers into planters, with participation from students. Mail Motor Services, Naraina, New Delhi, inducted 16 electric vehicles into its fleet on 29th October 2026, reinforcing the Department's commitment to greener transportation.

Other initiatives included plantation drives, awareness programmes on waste segregation and composting, and community participation in supporting clean surroundings.

    Dibrugarh University, Assam Postal Circle, N-Gen PO wall transformed into
an air-purifying green wall using up-cycled materials.

 

      

    Mail Motor Services, Naraina, New Delhi, Inducts 16 Electric Vehicles into its Fleet   

Jan Sampark – Dak Chaupal: Bringing Government Services to Citizens

Under Special Campaign 6, the Department organised Dak Chaupals to strengthen citizen engagement and bring Government services closer to the people. The initiative focused on digital interface and financial inclusion with particular emphasis on last-mile delivery. Citizens were sensitised about Postal Life Insurance (PLI), Rural Postal Life Insurance (RPLI), India Post Payments Bank, Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT), e-commerce, export services, and various Government welfare schemes.

These interactions offered an opportunity to address public grievances, obtain citizen feedback, and improve awareness about the range of services offered by India Post.              

 

                  Dak Chaupal organised at Balipatna SO, Bhubaneswar Postal Division, Odisha Circle

Dedicated One-Day Nationwide Activities under Special Campaign 6

In response to the initiative of the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG), the Department of Posts organised a dedicated one-day nationwide programme on 23rd October 2026. A total of 1,861 Dak Chaupals were organised across the country in which 76,343 citizens including 31,728 women took part and cleanliness activities were undertaken at approximately 55,952 sites. The programme also saw the resolution of 9,007 public grievances. 

Special Campaign 6 also featured innovative community engagement activities. At Nehru Place Post Office a calligraphy activity on Swachhata and environmental awareness was organised for school children while, at Vasant Kunj Post Office, children took part in clay pot painting and plantation activities. These events were aimed at inculcating the concept of Swachhata and environmental responsibility among young minds.   

 

                  

                Nehru Place Post Office, New Delhi,                          Vasant Kunj Post Office, New Delhi

                           a calligraphy activity                                      children participated in clay pot painting

Promoting Citizen Feedback and Digital Initiatives

The Department also encouraged technology-driven initiatives to strengthen Swachhata of processes, improve accessibility and enhance citizen experience. An important initiative in this direction is DigiPost, launched in collaboration with Gujarat Police, a unique phygital mail service under which traffic e-challans issued by Gujarat Police are digitally transmitted and physically delivered to citizens. The initiative leverages the extensive reach of India Post to facilitate the delivery of digitally generated citizen services through its physical postal network.

The Department also encouraged the adoption of technology-driven initiatives to strengthen transparency and improve service delivery. Odisha Circle and Jammu & Kashmir Postal Circles introduced a QR code-based customer feedback mechanisms, enabling customers to submit feedback in multiple languages, upload photographs and highlight service-related issues.

Further, India Post's Insurance Management Solution (IMS) facilitates online exploration of PLI/RPLI plans, comparison of premiums and benefits, online policy applications and payment of the first premium, making insurance services more accessible to citizens.

 

                                                                

             Odisha Postal Circle introduced a                                J&K Circle promoting cleanliness by 

      QR Code-Based Customer Feedback System                displaying QR codes at various Post Offices      

 

           

                   Gujarat police and India Post                   India Post's Insurance Management Solution (IMS)      

               sign digipost MOU for e-challans.                 facilitates online exploration of PLI/RPLI plans

 

Towards Sustainable and Institutionalised Swachhata

Special Campaign 6 has further strengthened the Department of Posts' efforts towards institutionalising cleanliness, improving administrative efficiency, promoting environmental sustainability and enhancing citizen-centric service delivery.

Through measurable outcomes, innovative initiatives and active participation of postal employees and communities, the Department continues to transform its establishments into cleaner, more efficient and customer-friendly spaces. The Department remains committed to sustaining these practices beyond the campaign period and embedding Swachhata and efficiency as an integral part of its everyday functioning.

2333276.title: DRDO conducts successful flight-test of quasi-ballistic missile ‘Pralay’
2333276.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
DRDO conducts successful flight-test of quasi-ballistic missile ‘Pralay’
Posted On: 05 NOV 2026 7:47PM by PIB Delhi

Defence Research & Development Organisation (DRDO) conducted the successful flight-test of quasi-ballistic missile ‘Pralay’ from Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Island off the coast of Odisha at around 1110 hrs on November 5, 2026. All the test objectives were fully met as confirmed by the test data captured by various range instruments deployed by Integrated Test Range, Chandipur.

Research Centre Imarat, Hyderabad, along with other DRDO laboratories, has indigenously developed the missile. Bharat Dynamics Limited, one of the Development-cum-Production-Partners, has produced the system. The flight-test was conducted in the presence of senior officials from DRDO, representatives from the industry and the Defence Forces, as part of user evaluation trials. With this successful test, the induction of the system has become imminent.

Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh complimented DRDO, Defence Forces and industry partners on the successful flight-test. He stated that the missile equipped with advanced technologies will further enhance the technological capabilities and operational preparedness of the military against emerging threats.

Defence Secretary and Secretary, Department of Defence R&D and Chairman, DRDO Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh congratulated the teams associated with the successful flight-test.

On the basis of the results of the Civil Services (Main) Examination, 2026 held by the Union Public Service Commission from 21st August 2026 to 30th August 2026, the candidates, as given below, have qualified for the Personality Test (Interview) for selection to the Indian Administrative Service, Indian Foreign Service, Indian Police Service and other Central Services (Group ‘A’ and Group ‘B’).

2.  Candidature of these candidates is provisional subject to them being found eligible in all respects. The candidates will be required to produce the original certificates in support of their eligibility/reservation claims viz. age, educational qualifications, community, economically weaker section, Person with Benchmark Disability (PwBD) and other documents such as TA Form etc. at the time of their Personality Test (Interview). They are, therefore, advised to keep the said documents ready with them. The candidates seeking reservation/relaxation benefits available for SC/ST/OBC/EWS/PwBD/Ex-servicemen etc., must also produce original certificate(s) issued by the closing date of the application of the Civil Services (Preliminary) Examination, 2026 i.e. 27.02.2026.

3.  Dates of Personality Tests (Interviews) of these candidates will be notified in due course, which will be held at the Office of the Union Public Service Commission at Dholpur House, Shahjahan Road, New Delhi-110069. The schedule of Personality Tests (Interviews) will be made available accordingly. The e-Summon Letters of Personality Tests (Interviews) of the candidates qualified for the same, will be made available in due course, which may be downloaded from the Commission’s Website https://www.upsc.gov.in & https://upsconline.nic.in. 4.  No request for change in the date and time of the Personality Test (Interview) intimated to the candidates will ordinarily be entertained.

2333270.title: Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah inaugurates Martyrs’ Memorial of First War of Independence of 1857 in Ambala, Haryana
2333270.body_html:
Ministry of Home Affairs
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah inaugurates Martyrs’ Memorial of First War of Independence of 1857 in Ambala, Haryana
Under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, our government has brought about fundamental transformation in Haryana
Ambala Cantonment is the same land where, on 10 May 1857, revolutionary heroes sounded the bugle of armed revolution against British rule
The spark of 1857 revolution spread across the entire country, leaving the world astonished, this was the struggle that shook the foundations of the British Empire on which the sun never set
Leftist historians called 1857 a ‘revolt’, but Veer Savarkar had spoken the truth — for every child of Mother India, this was not a revolt but a freedom struggle
In 90 years from 1857 to 1947, countless martyrs sacrificed everything, on that very foundation, today under the leadership of Modi Ji, we are able to dream of a developed India
A country that does not understand the value of its independence and does not inscribe the blood of its martyrs in golden letters on the pages of history can never progress
Built at a cost of ₹594 crore and spanning 22 acres, this martyrs' memorial will serve as a source of patriotic inspiration for the younger generation across the country
Haryana has become the country’s first smoke-free state, and it is also the first state in the nation to procure 24 crops at MSP
By formulating an online transfer policy in Haryana, our government has completely eradicated the 'transfer industry' from the state
In Punjab, farmers are still struggling for a guarantee of MSP, Opposition Party made them a false promise; elect our government—we do what we say
Haryana has geared up for a drug-free state, and Prime Minister Modi has accorded priority to Haryana
Posted On: 05 NOV 2026 7:35PM by PIB Delhi

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah today inaugurated the Martyrs’ Memorial of the First War of Independence of 1857 in Ambala, Haryana. On this occasion, Haryana Chief Minister Shri Nayab Singh Saini and Union Minister Shri Manohar Lal, along with many other dignitaries, were present.

On this occasion, in his address, Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Minister Shri Amit Shah said that on this very land, on 10th May 1857, the revolutionary heroes had sounded the bugle of armed revolution against British rule, and from here that revolution had spread like fire, leaving the entire world astonished. British-inspired historians of leftist ideology termed the freedom struggle of 1857 a mere revolt. It may have been a revolt for the British, but Veer Savarkar had said that the revolution of 1857 was not a revolt for the children of Mother India, but a freedom struggle. It was the revolution of 1857 that ignited the flame of freedom in the heart of every citizen of this vast country stretching from the Himalayas to Kanyakumari and from Gangasagar to Somnath.

Shri Amit Shah said that in this great struggle of 90 years from 1857 to 1947, countless martyrs sacrificed everything they had, and only then did we get the good fortune to see present-day India and Mother India. On the foundation of those martyrs’ sacrifices, today under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, we can envision a developed India. Building on the sacrifices of those martyrs and strengthening democratic institutions for 80 years, we stand with dignity before the entire world. The warriors of the 1857 revolution — Nana Saheb Peshwa, Rani Lakshmibai, Tatya Tope, Begum Hazrat Mahal,  and many other fighters — displayed their valour and made the supreme sacrifice.

Union Home Minister said that no country truly understands the value of its freedom until it glorifies the martyrs who shed their blood for it. A country that does not rewrite the blood-stained pages of history in golden letters can never progress. This Martyrs’ Memorial built today in Ambala will become a source of boundless patriotic inspiration for our coming generations of youth and adolescents.

Shri Amit Shah stated that the Saraswati once flowed across this very sacred land, and it was from here—in the region extending as far as the Ganga-Yamuna Doab—that the Vedas and Upanishads were composed. On this very land, Lord Shri Krishna recited the Gita. On this brave land, Maharaja Agrasen gave the Indian model of administration. On this brave land, Raja Nahar Singh and Rao Tula Ram fought the freedom struggle, and continuing that tradition, today a small state like Haryana contributes the highest number of soldiers to the Army. In India’s sports medal tallies, Haryana consistently ranks number one. When the country needed to become self-reliant in food grains, the farmers of Haryana filled the nation’s granaries. Haryana has also made a very significant contribution to the White Revolution.

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Minister said that today, on the land of Haryana, a magnificent memorial of the 1857 revolution has been built on 22 acres at a cost of ₹594 crore, featuring 22 galleries. Shri Shah stated that this memorial represents a remarkable effort to weave together historical documents and the diverse art forms of Haryana, utilizing modern technology such as virtual reality, holography, and interactive projection. With Phulkari and Sarkanda craftsmanship, an open-air theatre seating 2,500 people, and a light-and-sound show, the memorial has been designed to transport visitors back to 1857. This memorial has become a vibrant space that awakens pride in the glory, sacrifice and honour of the 1857 revolution and a sense of duty towards the nation. An appeal is made to the youth of the entire country: to understand the people because of whom we stand where we are today, please visit this memorial in Ambala and also pay homage to the martyrs.

Shri Amit Shah said that today a National Highway built at a cost of ₹1,260 crore was also inaugurated, and through this highway Haryana will become a state with excellent connectivity. Under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, our government has brought about fundamental transformation in Haryana. With the delivery of gas cylinders to every household, Haryana became the country’s first smoke-free state. Haryana is the only state in India that procures 24 crops at MSP. It became the first state to implement the new criminal codes and increase the conviction rate by 40%. Haryana became the first state to operate a hydrogen train. The country’s first elevated railway track was also started in Haryana. Under the Haryana Antyodaya Parivar Parivahan Yojana (HAPPY), an initiative was also implemented in Haryana to provide 1,000 kilometers of free travel to poor families. The country’s largest Transgender Welfare Board was set up in Haryana. The practice of having fully literate panchayats was also pioneered in Haryana. An online transfer policy was formulated in Haryana, and our government completely eliminated the transfer industry from the state. Haryana is the only state in the entire country where there is no longer any ‘Lal Dora’ in the villages. Haryana has become an anaemia-free state, the country’s first Ayush school was established here, it became the first state to issue ‘Parivar Pehchan Patra’, and it is also the first state to stand with farmers of horticultural crops through the Bhavantar scheme. Haryana also pays the highest wages under MGNREGA. Over the past 60 years, Haryana has made remarkable progress. The state has also geared up for a drug-free Haryana, and Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has given priority to Haryana.

2333271.title: MINISTRY OF CULTURE SIGNS MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING WITH GOOGLE ARTS & CULTURE TO DIGITISE AND SHARE INDIA’S CULTURAL HERITAGE
2333271.body_html:
Ministry of Culture
MINISTRY OF CULTURE SIGNS MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING WITH GOOGLE ARTS & CULTURE TO DIGITISE AND SHARE INDIA’S CULTURAL HERITAGE
Posted On: 05 NOV 2026 7:33PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Culture, Government of India, today signed a Memorandum of Understanding with Google Arts & Culture to bring India’s cultural heritage to the public through cutting-edge digital tools. The MoU was signed at a virtual ceremony in the presence of Shri Vivek Aggarwal, Secretary, Ministry of Culture, and Mr Amit Sood, Vice President and Founder, Google Arts & Culture.

The partnership will reflect the civilisational breadth of India: the monuments and archaeological sites protected by the Archaeological Survey of India and the collections they hold, the holdings of the national museums, the manuscript heritage being documented under Gyan Bharatam, and the crafts, performing arts and living traditions sustained by the Ministry’s institutions across the country.

At its centre is the Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum, taking shape in the North and South Blocks of New Delhi as a museum of India’s history across the ages. Its digitisation will create a lasting record of the buildings and the wealth of artefacts they will house, and offer the public an early window onto one of the most significant cultural undertakings of our time.

The MoU is part of the Ministry’s wider effort to strengthen accessibility and expand its digital initiatives, so that India’s heritage can be explored in Indian languages and on any device. It reflects a whole-of-Ministry approach in which preservation, public access and the growth of India’s creative economy advance together, drawing on institutions of every scale and partners from across sectors.

Commenting on the partnership, Shri Vivek Aggarwal, Secretary, Ministry of Culture, said: “India’s cultural heritage is a living inheritance. It belongs to every citizen and speaks to the whole world. Our partnership with Google Arts & Culture brings technology to bear on documenting, preserving and sharing that inheritance, from our ancient manuscripts and monuments to the collections of our national museums and the upcoming Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum. By making these treasures available in Indian languages and to audiences across the globe, we hope to bring more people closer to the story of Indian civilisation, and to safeguard it for generations to come.”

Google Arts & Culture has had a long association with the Ministry’s institutions, including the Archaeological Survey of India, the National Museum and the National Gallery of Modern Art, whose collections it has helped bring to wider audiences over the years.

Mr Amit Sood, Vice President and Founder, Google Arts & Culture, said: “For the past 15 years, Google Arts & Culture has been deeply inspired by India’s millennia of storytelling, artistic mastery and vast heritage. Our partnership with the Ministry of Culture represents a shared commitment to preserve India’s timeless treasures with the help of cutting-edge technologies. Whether supporting the vision for the Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum or preserving historic manuscripts, we are honoured to deploy our technologies to bridge ancient heritage with modern accessibility, making these collections freely discoverable to educate, inspire, and delight curious minds everywhere.”

The MoU reaffirms the Ministry’s commitment to preserving India’s civilisational heritage, championing its creative economy through enduring partnerships, and sharing its culture with the widest possible networks at home and across the world.

*****

2333261.title: IPRD-2026 CONCLUDES WITH FOCUS ON COOPERATIVE OCEAN GOVERNANCE AND RESPONSIBLE MARITIME TECHNOLOGIES
2333261.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
IPRD-2026 CONCLUDES WITH FOCUS ON COOPERATIVE OCEAN GOVERNANCE AND RESPONSIBLE MARITIME TECHNOLOGIES
Posted On: 05 NOV 2026 7:20PM by PIB Delhi

The three-day Indo-Pacific Regional Dialogue 2026 (IPRD-2026), the Indian Navy’s annual apex-level international strategic dialogue, concluded on 05 Nov 2026 in New Delhi. Organised in association with the National Maritime Foundation (NMF), the conference examined ‘Science, Technology and Academic Cooperation in the Indo-Pacific’ through five professional thematic sessions and senior-level interactions intended to identify practical pathways for regional maritime cooperation.

The concluding day opened with a Special Address by Gen NS Raja Subramani, Chief of Defence Staff, after which the CDS had an engaging interaction with the audience. This was followed by a session on ‘Collaborative Approaches to Ocean Governance and Maritime Resilience’, moderated by VAdm Sanjay Jasjit Singh (Retd), Director-General, United Service Institution of India.  In this session, Professor Deo Florence Onda of the University of the Philippines addressed a cooperative plan to share Filipino experience and expertise in ocean governance. Dr Marie Bourrel-McKinnon, former Chief of Staff in the International Seabed Authority, examined equitable deep-sea research partnerships and resource governance. Mr Ramraj Narasimhan, from the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (CDRI), provided an overview of the implementation of the Infrastructure for Resilient Island States (IRIS) programme, while Ms Sofia Furstenberg-Stott of Future Maritime, Sweden, considered how the interface between marine science and shipping operations could be strengthened. The session brought together four dimensions of a common challenge: the need to link scientific capability with governance, make research partnerships more equitable, strengthen the resilience of vulnerable island states, and ensure that scientific knowledge informs the decisions of maritime industry and public institutions.

The final session of IPRD-2026 was centred on the theme, ‘Transformative Maritime Technologies and Dual-Use Implications’.  This session was moderated by Rear Admiral Guninder Singh Jawanda (Retd), Indian Navy. In this session, speakers addressed distinct facets of the sessional theme. Ms Dongyoun Cho of the International Institute for Strategic Studies (IISS), Germany, examined a practical framework for Indo-Pacific cooperation on artificial intelligence and quantum technologies in the maritime domain. Dr Eva Pejsova from the Brussels School of Governance addressed EU–Indo-Pacific mechanisms for the responsible governance of dual-use maritime technologies. Captain Mark Blaine (Retd), South African Navy, from Stellenbosch University discussed a cooperation roadmap to help small and medium navies adapt to these technologies, while Commodore Arun Golaya (Retd) considered operational Navy-to-Navy cooperation for their responsible adoption.  The discussions reflected the dual character of emerging maritime technologies and examined the potential for collaborative research, practical capacity-building and institutional arrangements that allow partners with differing resources and requirements to participate meaningfully in technological change. 

The Valedictory Address by Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh, Defence Secretary, Government of India, brought the mega three-day conference to a fitting and memorable closure. Over its three days, the IPRD-2026 witnessed participation by a wide spectrum of military practitioners, policy makers, representatives from the maritime industry, diplomats from India and friendly foreign countries, academia, media, eminent citizens, and New Delhi’s vibrant student community. Over forty experts and distinguished speakers from twenty countries shared their perspectives on the IPRD’s unifying theme of ‘Science, Technology and Academic Cooperation in the Indo-Pacific’, providing greater specificity to actionable outcomes under the Science, Technology and Academic Cooperation pillar of the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative.  The conference also bolstered the Indian Navy’s committed stance on enhancing regional maritime security and promoting collaborative approaches to strengthen maritime resilience, thus providing a clearer expression to India’s maritime vision of MAHASAGAR (Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions).

*****

2333260.title: A Journey Towards Academic Achievement Through the NFSC Fellowship
2333260.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
 A Journey Towards Academic Achievement Through the NFSC Fellowship
Posted On: 05 NOV 2026 7:18PM by PIB Delhi

For 33 year Rahul Kumar (name changed), the NFSC Scheme has been an important source of support in his pursuit of academic excellence and research advancement. His experience highlights the role of targeted fellowship assistance in reducing financial barriers, promoting inclusive access to higher education and enabling scholars to contribute to the nation through research and knowledge creation.

Rahul Kumar, a resident of Janjgir-Champa district in Chhattisgarh, is pursuing his Ph.D. with the aspiration of becoming an outstanding researcher and contributing to the holistic progress of the nation.

Coming from a Below Poverty Line (BPL) family, he faced significant financial constraints and a lack of resources that made it difficult to pursue advanced research. His academic journey was further affected by challenges arising from misleading information and institutional practices, including the imposition of regulations outside the University Grants Commission (UGC) framework.

A significant turning point came in July 2023, when he began receiving assistance under the National Fellowship for Scheduled Caste Students (NFSC) Scheme of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. The fellowship provided financial assistance, including fellowship support and House Rent Allowance (HRA), amounting to ₹45,700. This support offered much-needed financial stability and helped address the challenges that had been hindering his pursuit of research.

The assistance, which he describes as far beyond his expectations, enabled him to focus more effectively on his doctoral studies and research goals. The financial support helped ease resource-related constraints and provided him with greater scope to pursue his academic work with dedication. It addressed several of the difficulties that had previously come in the way of undertaking quality research.

The fellowship has added immense value to his research and personal life. With financial barriers eased, Mr. Kumar has been able to continue working towards his Ph.D. and strengthen his academic pursuits. His journey reflects how timely educational assistance can help scholars from economically weaker backgrounds continue higher studies and work towards their aspirations.

6. Policy Initiatives/Industry Initiatives

The Ministry of Steel has granted QCO compliance exemption for 162 grades of semi-finished stainless steel products covered under IS 14650, valid until 31 March 2027. The measure aims to address MSME concerns and facilitate the availability of intermediate materials for stainless steel manufacturing.

SAIL reported strong financial performance for H1 FY27, driven by improved profitability, operational resilience and a continued focus on cost optimisation. Sales volume grew by 5% to 5.16 Mt in Q2 FY27 over the corresponding period last year, while Profit After Tax (PAT) surged by approximately 315% to ₹1,774 crore. The company has also approved a ₹1,714-crore expansion and modernisation plan for its Alloy Steels Plant, Durgapur, to expand production of high-grade alloy and special steels for the defence, railway and automotive sectors.

NMDC achieved iron ore production of 5.04 Mt in October 2026, registering an 18% year-on-year increase. Cumulative production during April–October FY27 reached 32.32 Mt, reflecting a 22% year-on-year growth.

MOIL registered improved financial performance in H1 FY27, with manganese ore sales volume rising by 9.67% year-on-year to 0.78 Mt and Profit After Tax (PAT) increasing by 22.5% to ₹149.39 crore, supported by higher sales and improved profitability.

7. International Co-operation

A Ministry of Steel delegation led by the Secretary (Steel) visited Sydney for IMARC 2026 conference, wherein he addressed the Ministerial and Government Global Opportunity Programme on the growth of India’s steel sector and inaugurated the Ministry of Steel Pavilion. He also delivered the keynote address at the Australia-India Business Meet 2026, organised by the Consulate General of India in Sydney. The delegation met the Premier of New South Wales, the NSW Minister for Natural Resources and Austrade to discuss cooperation in mining, steel, critical minerals, raw material security, investment and technology, reaffirming the shared commitment towards stronger partnerships between India and Australia across the mining and steel value chain.

The delegation also met officials from Invest New Zealand and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (MFAT) officials in Auckland. The discussions focused on strengthening India-New Zealand cooperation in investment, trade and the steel sector, and on exploring new avenues for collaboration and partnership.

NMDC Limited has opened a Sydney office, inaugurated by Secretary (Steel), to facilitate engagement with Australian government agencies and industry partners and to strengthen India-Australia cooperation in the minerals sector.

8. Green Steel Initiatives

Under the Ministry of Steel’s Green Steel Initiative, 108 distinct steel producers have been issued Green Steel Certificates across the lists issued till October 2026. The certification covers products including TMT bars, HR/CR coils, plates, wire rods, pipes and other steel products, with a large majority of certified products receiving 5-star ratings, reflecting the growing adoption of lower-emission steelmaking practices across India’s steel industry.

Source: Provisional JPC data for Oct 2026. Mt = Million Tonnes; Mtpa = Million Tonnes Per Annum; MoM = Month-on-Month; YoY = Year-on-Year; CPLY = Corresponding Period Last Year.

2333254.title: Department of Fisheries successfully concludes Special Campaign 6 for institutionalising Swachhata and reducing pendency
2333254.ministry: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
2333254.body_html:
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
Department of Fisheries successfully concludes Special Campaign 6 for institutionalising Swachhata and reducing pendency
Department of Fisheries records significant achievements in cleanliness, grievance redressal and records management under Special Campaign 6
Posted On: 05 NOV 2026 6:55PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying, successfully concluded its participation in Special Campaign 6, conducted from 2nd to 31st October 2026, under the guidance of the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG). The campaign focused on institutionalising Swachhata, reducing pendency in Government offices, improving records management and promoting efficient utilisation of office space and resources.

Demonstrating its commitment to efficient and citizen-centric governance, the Department achieved its target of conducting 40 cleanliness campaigns. Significant progress was also made in grievance redressal, with all 100 public grievances and all 30 public grievance appeals disposed of during the campaign. Further, 4 references received from Members of Parliament and 3 PMO references were disposed of.

A focused exercise was undertaken for records management and digitisation. A total number of 800 files physical files were reviewed out of which 745 files were weeded out, contributing to better record management and streamlining of administrative processes. In respect of e-files, 25 out of 45 files put up for review were closed during the campaign.

The campaign also contributed to the effective utilisation of office space and disposal of redundant materials. Through scrap disposal, the Department and its offices freed up approximately 1,150 square feet of office space. Further, the Department undertook an e-waste management exercise covering 308 items across various categories of electronic and electrical equipment.

The Department also leveraged social media effectively, with over 120 posts shared across X, Facebook, Instagram, Threads, Linkedin, Truth Social, Bluesky and Youtube showcasing various activities undertaken during the campaign and reinforcing public awareness of the Department’s initiatives.

The successful implementation of Special Campaign 6 reflects the Department of Fisheries' continued commitment to promoting cleanliness, improving administrative efficiency, strengthening accountability and creating a more organised, productive and citizen-friendly work environment. The campaign has further reinforced the importance of institutionalising Swachhata and adopting effective practices for better governance and resource optimisation.

2333248.title: From Substance Dependence to a Healthier, More Independent Life
2333248.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Substance Dependence to a Healthier, More Independent Life
Sultanpur UP’s Amit’s Journey of Recovery and Rehabilitation Through DDAC
Posted On: 05 NOV 2026 6:44PM by PIB Delhi

For Amit 23 year Amit (name changed), the District De-Addiction Centre, Sultanpur, Uttar Pradesh has been an important source of support in his journey towards recovery and self-reliance. His journey highlights the significance of accessible de-addiction and rehabilitation services in helping individuals overcome substance dependence, regain confidence and reintegrate into society with dignity and renewed hope.

Amit, a graduate from Sultanpur district, was facing significant personal, social and financial challenges due to substance dependence. His condition had begun to adversely affect his physical health, daily routine, emotional well-being and personal relationships.

Despite being a graduate and working as a part-time employee, he struggled to maintain consistency in his professional life and faced financial difficulties. The impact of addiction extended beyond his personal circumstances, straining his relationships with family members and the surrounding community.

Social stigma and limited support further affected his confidence and ability to lead a stable life. He aspired to overcome substance dependence, regain control over his life, achieve financial independence and rebuild his relationships with dignity.

A significant turning point in his life came on 30 May 2025, when he received rehabilitation support through the District De-Addiction Centre (DDAC), Sultanpur, under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment's rehabilitation services.

The centre provided him with comprehensive assistance, including medical treatment, timely medicines, healthcare facilities, safe accommodation, nutritious food and vocational guidance. Alongside medical care, he received continuous emotional and psychological support through counselling sessions, motivational activities, yoga and regular interactions with caregivers and centre staff.

The structured rehabilitation programme helped Amit gradually improve his health, develop discipline and regain his confidence. Regular counselling and continuous encouragement played an important role in strengthening his emotional well-being and improving his social behaviour. The supportive environment at the centre also helped him work towards rebuilding relationships with his family members and reintegrating into the community.

Today, Amit has made significant progress in his recovery and is leading a healthier and more disciplined life. He has resumed regular work, started supporting himself financially and is gradually rebuilding trust within his family and community. His progress reflects how timely medical intervention, comprehensive rehabilitation and sustained emotional support can help individuals overcome substance dependence and move towards an independent and dignified life.

2333249.title: Union Minister Shri G. Kishan Reddy Calls for Accelerated Coal Sector Reforms, Coal Gasification and Technology-Driven Mining to Strengthen India's Energy Security
2333249.body_html:
Ministry of Coal
Union Minister Shri G. Kishan Reddy Calls for Accelerated Coal Sector Reforms, Coal Gasification and Technology-Driven Mining to Strengthen India's Energy Security
At the 4th Conference of Mining Ministers, Minister Highlights Coal Gasification, Critical Minerals, AI-driven Technologies and Stronger Centre-State Collaboration
Posted On: 05 NOV 2026 6:44PM by PIB Delhi

The Union Minister of Coal and Mines, Shri G. Kishan Reddy, addressing the 4th Conference of Mining Ministers on Reforms in the Mines and Coal Sector in Goa, highlighted the transformative journey of India's coal and mining sectors under the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. He emphasised that sustained reforms have enhanced transparency, efficiency and professionalism, strengthening the sectors' contribution to national economic growth and energy security.

Focusing on the priorities of the coal sector, Shri G. Kishan Reddy underscored the need to accelerate Coal Gasification for the optimum utilisation of India's abundant coal resources. He highlighted its potential to unlock the economic value of domestic coal, promote industrial diversification, generate employment and strengthen the country's long-term energy security.

Highlighting the strategic importance of Critical Minerals in the evolving global geopolitical landscape, the Minister stressed the need to strengthen domestic exploration, mining, processing, refining and recycling capabilities. He emphasised that developing a self-reliant mineral ecosystem is essential to reducing import dependence and strengthening India's strategic and economic resilience.

Emphasising the transformative role of technology, Shri Reddy called upon State Governments to harness Artificial Intelligence (AI), digitalisation and advanced technological solutions across exploration, mine operations and mineral recovery. He highlighted that technology-driven practices would improve productivity, operational efficiency and sustainability in the mining and coal sectors.

The Minister urged States to expedite the operationalization of auctioned mines, accelerate the auction of new blocks, expand exploration activities and adopt technology-driven practices to unlock the full potential of their mineral resources. He also highlighted how mining sector reforms have strengthened State economies, attracted investments, generated employment opportunities and enhanced revenue generation, while promoting development in mining-affected regions.

Reaffirming the spirit of Cooperative Federalism, Shri G. Kishan Reddy called for stronger coordination between the Centre and States to unlock India's mineral and coal potential, strengthen the mining ecosystem and ensure sustainable and inclusive growth. He expressed confidence that collective efforts and a shared roadmap would take India's mining and coal sectors to new heights, contributing significantly to the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.

Addressing the conference, Union Minister of State for Coal and Mines, Shri Satish Chandra Dubey, stated that the mining sector is a key pillar of the country's economic progress, industrial development and energy security. He highlighted the wide-ranging reforms being undertaken by the Central Government, including transparent auction processes, promotion of investment, creation of new employment opportunities and efforts to accelerate mining activities.

He emphasized the importance of prioritizing sustainable and responsible mining, environmental protection, mine rehabilitation and the welfare of communities residing in mining-affected areas. He stated that plans for post-mining rehabilitation and the creation of alternative livelihood opportunities for local communities should be incorporated from the very beginning of mining operations to ensure that environmental and social interests are protected alongside development.

He also stressed the need to increase coal production while promoting safe and modern mining technologies, coal gasification, innovations in coal utilisation and initiatives such as First Mile Connectivity. Furthermore, he called upon States to share their experiences and best practices and work towards addressing challenges in the mining sector.

Addressing the conference, Secretary, Ministry of Coal, Shri Vikram Dev Dutt, highlighted the significant progress made by India's coal sector and its vital role in strengthening the country's energy security and driving economic growth.

He noted that domestic coal production had surpassed one billion tonnes for the second consecutive year, marking a significant achievement in India's journey towards energy self-reliance and reducing dependence on imported coal.

Shri Vikram Dev Dutt emphasised the importance of continued structural reforms to make the coal sector more competitive, transparent, efficient and investment-friendly. Highlighting key initiatives such as Commercial Coal Mining, the revised SHAKTI framework and Coal SETU, he underlined the need to promote greater private sector participation, simplify processes and accelerate the operationalisation of coal mines.

He highlighted Coal Gasification as a major opportunity for value addition, industrial diversification and employment generation. He urged coal-bearing States to actively facilitate investments, support infrastructure development and accelerate project implementation to realise the sector's immense potential.

Stressing the importance of technology, digitalisation, sustainable mining practices and efficient logistics, the Secretary called for stronger Centre-State collaboration to unlock the full potential of India's coal and mineral resources.

He reiterated that the next phase of growth in the coal sector must move beyond extraction towards value creation, positioning the sector as a catalyst for industrial development, stronger State revenues, employment generation and the vision of Viksit Bharat.

At the conference, Ms. Rupinder Brar, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Coal, delivered a detailed and comprehensive presentation highlighting the recent reforms undertaken in the coal sector, their role in enhancing Ease of Doing Business, and the key challenges and expectations from States. The presentation outlined how these reforms are simplifying procedures, improving transparency, facilitating investments and creating a more business-friendly environment for stakeholders. It also emphasised the importance of stronger Centre-State collaboration in addressing emerging challenges and accelerating the pace of reforms. These initiatives are paving the way for a more efficient, competitive and sustainable coal sector, thereby contributing to India's energy security and economic growth.

The Ministry of Mines, Government of India, organised the 4th Conference of Mining Ministers on 5–6 November 2026 in Goa, bringing together Mining Ministers from various States and senior officials from the Central and State Governments. The conference provided an important platform for interaction and exchange of views on various aspects of the mining sector. Discussions focused on the progress, opportunities and challenges in the sector, while encouraging States to share their experiences, initiatives and best practices.

The deliberations at the 4th Conference of Mining Ministers reaffirmed the importance of continued reforms and coordinated efforts between the Central and State Governments in strengthening India's coal sector.

With a focus on accelerating coal gasification, promoting commercial coal mining, leveraging advanced technologies, facilitating investments and ensuring sustainable mining practices, the Ministry of Coal remains committed to unlocking the full potential of India's domestic coal resources. The emphasis on value addition, operational efficiency, private sector participation and cooperative federalism will play a crucial role in positioning India's coal sector as a key driver of industrial growth, energy security, employment generation and economic development.

2333245.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
INDIAN NAVAL SHIP TARKASH CONCLUDES PORT CALL AT PORT LOUIS, MAURITIUS
Posted On: 05 NOV 2026 6:38PM by PIB Delhi

INS Tarkash concluded an enriching and emotive port call at Port Louis, Mauritius, on 03 Nov 2026.

The Commanding Officer called on Mrs Kan Oye Fong, Secretary of Home Affairs, and Mr Rampersad Sooroojebally, PMSM, Commissioner of Police, Mauritius. The latter also visited onboard to interact with the ship’s crew.

The ship hosted a cultural exchange onboard to commemorate Aapravasi Diwas 2026, with Dr the Hon Mahend Gungapersad, Minister of Education and Human Resource, Government of Mauritius, as the Guest of Honour. HE Shri Anurag Srivastava, High Commissioner of India to Mauritius, and other distinguished guests were in attendance. The ship also participated in events commemorating the 192nd Aapravasi Diwas on 02 Nov 2026.

The ship’s crew undertook cross-training of Mauritius Coast Guard personnel and an outreach activity at Hospice Saint Jean de Dieu. Following an engaging stay, the ship participated in a PASSEX with CGS Valiant and undertook joint EEZ surveillance with the Mauritius Coast Guard, supported by a Dornier aircraft.

INS Tarkash has now proceeded for the next phase of operational deployment.

The port call reaffirms the longstanding maritime partnership and strengthening bilateral ties between the two countries.

2333238.title: India Advances Global Diamond Industry Agenda Ahead of Kimberley Process Plenary
2333238.body_html:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
India Advances Global Diamond Industry Agenda Ahead of Kimberley Process Plenary
India’s Observer Status in ADPA Strengthens Engagement with Diamond-Producing Countries
Posted On: 05 NOV 2026 6:32PM by PIB Delhi

India, as Chair of the Kimberley Process (KP) for 2026, convened a stakeholder consultation in Luanda, Angola, on 3 November 2026, bringing together the Chairs and Vice-Chairs of KP Working Groups and Committees (KP Working Bodies), the KP Vice-Chair, Republic of Ghana, and the former KP Chair, United Arab Emirates. The consultation, led by KP Chair and Additional Secretary, Department of Commerce, Shri Yashvir Singh, focused on key priorities concerning the global diamond industry, including responsible rough diamond sourcing, institutional governance, compliance and consumer confidence. Representatives of Observers and partner organisations, including the World Diamond Council, KP Civil Society Coalition, Diamond Development Initiative (DDI) at RESOLVE and the African Diamond Producers’ Association (ADPA), also participated. The engagement formed part of India's outreach ahead of the KP Plenary to be held in New Delhi from 30 November to 4 December 2026. The consultation was held on the sidelines of the 20th anniversary celebrations of ADPA (ADPA@20), held in Luanda on 3–4 November 2026.

India has Observer status in ADPA, providing an institutional platform for engagement with African diamond-producing countries. This offers opportunities for cooperation in securing rough diamond supply chains, technical knowledge exchange, value addition, market access and the promotion of ethical and sustainable practices.

The Chairs and Vice-Chairs of the KP Working Bodies shared updates on progress against their respective work plans and outlined matters proposed for consideration at the Plenary. These included draft Administrative Decisions, initiatives relating to responsible rough diamond sourcing, improvements to the statistical reporting platform, and measures to strengthen institutional governance and participant compliance. The consultation also provided an opportunity to identify matters requiring further coordination and areas where early convergence could support the work of the Plenary.

Reaffirming India's KP Chairship theme of Confidence, Compliance and Credibility, the consultation provided an opportunity for an open exchange on the status and evolving priorities of the global diamond industry. Discussions covered the sustainability of diamond-producing countries and communities, sustainable funding and continuity of the KP Secretariat, digitalisation of certification and statistical processes, and strengthening compliance with the Kimberley Process Certification Scheme. Participants also exchanged views on the reform of the conflict diamond definition, responsible sourcing, artisanal and alluvial diamond production, consumer confidence and the importance of effective reporting and peer-review mechanisms.

Additional Secretary, Department of Commerce, and KP Chair, Shri Yashvir Singh, said, “India’s Chairship places emphasis on Confidence, Compliance and Credibility. The consultation in Luanda provided an opportunity to engage directly with the leadership of the KP Working Bodies, the KP Vice-Chair and Observers on issues that are important to the future of the Process and the diamond industry. Our endeavour is to build a shared understanding of the issues before the New Delhi Plenary and to advance practical outcomes through constructive dialogue and consensus-based decision-making.”

The African Diamond Producers’ Association (ADPA), established on 4 November 2006 in Luanda, Angola, seeks to enhance cooperation among African diamond-producing nations. ADPA comprises 15 effective member countries and 8 Observers, including two non-African Observers, namely the Russian Federation and India. Its member countries collectively account for over 60 per cent of global diamond production. ADPA is currently chaired by the Republic of Sierra Leone, represented by Minister of Mines and Mineral Resources, Hon. Julius Daniel Mattai. On 4 November 2026, Botswana was admitted as an Observer Member of ADPA during the 13th Extraordinary Meeting of the ADPA Council of Ministers held in Luanda.

On 4 November 2026,  Shri Yashvir Singh, participated in the Council of Ministers and main commemoration programme of ADPA@20 and delivered a presentation titled “Partnering for the Future: A Global Industry Perspective on Africa’s Diamond Future”. Speaking as KP Chair (India) 2026, he underlined the central place of African producing countries in the global diamond value chain and outlined how partnership between producers, manufacturing centres and consumer markets can support the long-term sustainability of the natural diamond sector. Drawing on India’s vision of the 3Cs – Confidence, Compliance and Credibility – he highlighted that consumer confidence in natural diamonds, robust compliance with KP minimum requirements and a credible, inclusive Kimberley Process are essential to ensuring that diamond resources continue to contribute to development in producing countries.

The programme brought together representatives of African diamond-producing countries, industry and other stakeholders to mark ADPA’s two decades of engagement. Sessions included discussions on the ADPA Sustainable Diamond Standard and the ADPA Business Council, perspectives on sustainability and audit practices, and deliberations on protecting the integrity of natural diamonds, industry advocacy, market differentiation and consumer confidence.

The 13th Extraordinary Meeting of the ADPA Council of Ministers, held alongside the 20th anniversary celebrations, approved a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the Gem & Jewellery Export Promotion Council (GJEPC), India, and ADPA. The MoU seeks to strengthen cooperation between the Indian gem and jewellery industry and African diamond-producing countries, including through capacity building and skills development in diamond sorting, valuation and manufacturing, exchange of technical expertise, and the promotion of trade and investment linkages across the diamond value chain.

The discussions in Luanda will advance preparations for the KP Plenary in New Delhi, scheduled from 30 November to 4 December 2026 at Bharat Mandapam. The KP Plenary will be preceded by the New Delhi Diamond Dialogue (KP Forum) on 29 November 2026, with associated programme engagements extending through 5 December 2026. India will host the KP Plenary for the third time, following its previous Chairships in 2008 and 2019.

The Kimberley Process Certification Scheme (KPCS), established pursuant to United Nations General Assembly Resolution 55/56 (2000), is an international initiative aimed at preventing conflict diamonds from entering the legitimate rough diamond trade. The KP operates through a tripartite framework comprising Governments, the diamond industry and civil society. It currently has 60 Participants representing 86 countries, with the European Union and its Member States participating as a single entity. The Chairship of the Kimberley Process rotates annually among its participating countries, and India assumed the Chairship on 1 January 2026.
