2333225.title: English rendering of PM's speech during interaction with India’s Asian Para Games Champions
2333225.body_html:
Prime Minister's Office
English rendering of PM's speech during interaction with India’s Asian Para Games Champions
Posted On: 05 NOV 2026 6:22PM by PIB Delhi

My colleagues in the Cabinet, Shri Mansukh Mandaviya ji and Smt. Raksha Khadse ji, all representatives of the Paralympic Committee of India and the National Sports Federations, other distinguished guests, all medal-winning athletes, ladies and gentlemen.

I had been eagerly waiting to meet all of you. Just a few weeks ago, I met the athletes who participated in the Asian Games, and now I have got the opportunity to meet all of you energetic companions who participated in the Para Asian Games. Your outstanding performance shows that India is rapidly emerging as a major power in the world of sports. On such a large platform, you have not only won medals, but you have also won the hearts of crores of Indians. Once again, all of you para-athletes have demonstrated that the highest flights are achieved through determination and courage. On behalf of 140 crore countrymen, I congratulate all of you wholeheartedly.

Your families, trainers, and coaches have also played a crucial role in this achievement. I congratulate them as well. And as I have said before, the amount of effort a coach has to put in for an athlete is immense, but for a Paralympic athlete, many times more effort is required. Only then do such remarkable results emerge. Therefore, I extend special congratulations and appreciation to them.

Friends,

There was a time when India's participation in most sports was considered merely a formality. In para-sports too, the country was far behind. At the 2010 Asian Para Games, India won only one gold medal. Altogether, we managed to win just fourteen medals in that tournament. Fourteen. This time, however, our athletes have returned with one hundred and fourteen medals. Just think about this journey from fourteen to one hundred and fourteen. It is the result of the highest level of your hard work. It is the outcome of your dedication to sports and the ecosystem that has developed around it. This time, with thirty golds, thirty-five silvers, forty-nine bronzes, five new world records, and nine Asian records, you have filled the entire nation with pride. Out of fifty-six women athletes, thirty-four daughters became medal winners. And in four events, all three podium positions belonged to India. India won the gold, and in the same event, India also won the silver and the bronze. Even on the last day of the competition, you performed wonders by winning nine gold medals. It seemed as though you had decided that as long as the Games continued, the medal-winning streak would not stop.

Friends,

This time, our athletes won gold medals in disciplines where India had never achieved such success before. Mona Agarwal created a world record in para shooting. Honey broke his own previous world record. Himanshu, Ravi, and Jehan showed the world through their performances how physical challenges can be overcome.

Friends,

Whether it is the personal achievement of an athlete or the collective success of a nation, the world sees only the shine of victory. But the years of hard work behind that moment, the sweat shed day and night, and the unwavering dedication and perseverance required to reach that point are what form the foundation on which the towering structure of success stands. For example, Rinku ji lost her mother just two months before the Asian Para Games. Even amidst such great sorrow, she maintained her courage. And when she won the gold medal, she raised her mother's photograph and dedicated that medal to her. That moment touched the hearts of all Indians.

Friends,

Your struggles and achievements are an inspiration to every Indian. And in this journey, your path and the nation’s path have been very similar. That is why today, your efforts and the efforts of the nation are combining and creating an even greater force together.

Friends,

After 2014, when the country began its journey towards bigger goals, the situation was very different. Most parents were afraid to send their children into sports and the children themselves were often hesitant. There was disorder in the system, a lack of resources, a lack of support, and a lack of transparency. People used to say that nothing could change in such a system. They had accepted it as a reality. But just as you never accepted defeat before any challenge, the country too kept its eyes fixed only on its goals. We resolved that we would not allow the talent of our youth to go to waste. Therefore, we decided to change the very system that prevented young people like you from moving forward. As a result, a new approach towards sports emerged. Today, if a young athlete has faith in his or her talent, that athlete also believes that the country stands with them. Our para-sports ecosystem itself is one of the biggest examples of this. In sports where India’s representation was once extremely limited, our presence is now growing stronger. In archery, athletics, shooting, swimming, table tennis, badminton, judo, powerlifting, and many other sports, new young athletes are emerging. We are discovering new champions. This time, sixty-one of our athletes participated in the Asian Para Games for the first time. Sixty-one completely new athletes. And among those first-time participants, thirty-six returned home with medals. Sandeep even created a world record in his debut itself. This participation of young athletes reflects the India of today and announces the India of the future.

Friends,

We do not view sports merely as a collection of national and international events. For us, sports are also a powerful medium for character-building and nation-building. It is sports that teach young people how to win after losing. Sports teach discipline and the meaning of team spirit.

Friends,

With this vision, we are building a modern sports ecosystem for the country. Campaigns are being run at schools and at the grassroots level. A large number of Khelo India Centres have been established. We also launched the TOPS Scheme so that athletes could receive Olympic-level training. Keeping the Olympics in mind, I called upon young people from the Red Fort this time to come forward through the Talent Hunt campaign.

Friends,

Para-sports are being given equal importance in all these efforts. As a result, athletes like you are emerging with excellence and bringing glory to the nation at major events. We saw this once again in the recently concluded Para Games. In this competition, athletes receiving support under TOPS won forty-one medals, while Khelo India athletes won nineteen medals. This shows that our efforts are moving in the right direction.

Friends,

Today, modern sports policies in India are creating many new opportunities for young people, even beyond the playing field. Sports infrastructure development, sports equipment production, and the sports broadcasting economy are all expanding rapidly.

Friends,

Just a few days ago, the government approved the Khelo India Sports Goods Manufacturing Scheme worth more than ₹1,800 crore. Now it is time for our sports goods manufacturing industry to achieve new milestones. When an Indian or foreign athlete steps onto a field anywhere in the world, their sports gear should also be Made in India. Their clothing and footwear should also be Made in India. We want India to produce not only world-class athletes but also world-class sports equipment. We want Indian sports products to reach markets across the world. This will strengthen India’s MSME sector and create new opportunities in small towns and rural areas.

Friends,

After today’s event, all of you will also be invited to schools, colleges, and various institutions, where young people will want to listen to you and learn from you. When you speak with them, teach them the secrets of winning on the field, but also tell them about the opportunities connected with sports beyond the field. And you should also explain to them the extensive efforts being made by the country to make life easier for our differently-abled brothers and sisters. Just a few days ago, the Cabinet took an important decision regarding pensions for persons with disabilities. We increased the pension amount. The disability benchmark that was previously 80 percent has been reduced to 40 percent. Earlier, a person had to be eighteen years old to become eligible for a pension. Now, the path for pensions has been opened even for eligible children with disabilities from birth. Similarly, significant efforts have been made to promote Indian Sign Language. A sign language dictionary containing more than ten thousand words has been developed. School textbooks are also being made available in sign language. Through the Accessible India Campaign, public places are being made more accessible for persons with disabilities. Our effort is to ensure that every differently-abled person in the country receives both dignity and equal opportunities, and is able to move forward in life on the strength of their own abilities.

Friends,

The podium at Aichi-Nagoya is not the final destination of your journey. Keep that in mind. You should use this success as a launching pad for even bigger goals. The next target for India, and for most of you athletes, is L.A. 2028. Avani and Manish have already secured their quota places for Los Angeles. Our goal should be to ensure that as many Indian athletes as possible participate in L.A. 2028 and bring home as many medals as possible. Therefore, celebrate this moment wholeheartedly, but also begin preparing for the next challenge right away. The country stands with you, and so do I. The entire nation is waiting for your next victory. Once again, many congratulations and best wishes to all of you.

The grand festival of Diwali has already begun. This time, celebrate Diwali with great pride, enthusiasm, and splendour. But along with celebrating Diwali, also set your next goal in your mind and move forward with a new resolve. My very best wishes to all of you.

Thank you very much.

DISCLAIMER: This is the approximate translation of the Prime Minister’s address. Original address was delivered in Hindi.

2333193.title: Department of Science and Technology Successfully Concludes Special Campaign 6 with Significant Achievements in Swachhata, Record Management, reducing Pendency, improving Record Management and Optimising Office Space
2333193.body_html:
Ministry of Science & Technology
Department of Science and Technology Successfully Concludes Special Campaign 6 with Significant Achievements in Swachhata, Record Management, reducing Pendency, improving Record Management and Optimising Office Space
Posted On: 05 NOV 2026 5:40PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Science and Technology (DST) has successfully concluded Special Campaign 6, conducted from 2nd to 31st October, 2026, reaffirming its commitment to institutionalising Swachhata, reducing pendency, strengthening record management, and optimising office space across the Department and its Autonomous Institutions, Subordinate offices, Missions, Technology Innovation Hubs (TIHs). The campaign was implemented in accordance with the guidelines of the Department of Administrative Reforms & Public Grievances (DARPG).

Major Achievements of Special Campaign 6

During the campaign, a total of 906 cleanliness sites have been cleared across the Department and its Autonomous Institutions and Subordinate Organisations, significantly surpassing the target of 584 campaigns. These initiatives covered offices, laboratories, campuses and public spaces, promoting cleanliness and creating a sustainable workplace environment.

The Department achieved 100% disposal of all 12 Members of Parliament (MP) References received during the campaign period. It also resolved164 Public Grievances and disposed of 21 Public Grievance Appeals, demonstrating its commitment to responsive and citizen-centric governance.

The campaign resulted in the generation of₹25.96 lakh through disposal activities and the release of 1,72,798 square feet of office space through the systematic disposal of obsolete records, scrap, unused furniture and other redundant materials.

Under the Record Management initiative, the Department reviewed 15,665 physical files, substantially exceeding the target of 9,199 files, while achieving 100% review of all 2,516 identified e-files. As a result, 13,031 physical files were weeded out and 1,786 e-files were closed, taking the total number of files weeded out or closed to 14,817. These eﬀorts have significantly improved record management, reduced pendency and enhanced administrative efficiency.

Recognising the importance of public outreach and stakeholder engagement, the Department extensively showcased the activities undertaken under Special Campaign 6 through its official digital and social media platforms. More than 690 social media posts highlighting cleanliness drives, record management initiatives, e-waste disposal, space optimisation and other best practices were disseminated through X, Facebook, LinkedIn and YouTube, ensuring wider public awareness and encouraging greater participation by its Autonomous Institutions, Subordinate offices, Missions, Technology Innovation Hubs (TIHs).

The successful completion of Special Campaign 6 reflects the Department of Science and Technology's continued commitment to transparent, efficient and accountable governance. Through sustained eﬀorts in cleanliness, scientific waste

management, record management, timely disposal of public grievances and references, and eﬀective public outreach, the Department has further strengthened administrative efficiency while creating cleaner, more organised and citizen-centric workplaces.

2333194.title: TRAI Assesses Mobile Network Quality Across Ratnagiri District, Maharashtra LSA
2333194.body_html:
Ministry of Communications
TRAI Assesses Mobile Network Quality Across Ratnagiri District, Maharashtra LSA
Posted On: 05 NOV 2026 5:40PM by PIB Delhi

The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has released findings of Independent Drive Test (IDT) conducted across Ratnagiri District, Maharashtra LSA, during the month of September 2026, for information of general telecom consumers. The purpose of this drive test is to assess and verify real time quality of mobile network services (both voice & data) provided by Telecom Service Providers (TSPs). During the IDT, TRAI captures performance of TSPs for key Quality of Service (QoS) parameters like Coverage, Call Drop Rate (CDR), Call Setup Success Rate (CSSR), data Download (DL) and Upload (UL) throughput etc., which are then published to inform Consumers and encourage TSPs to improve their services.

These IDTs have been designed to capture on ground mobile network performance of all TSPs across diverse usages environment like cities, hotspots, public transport hubs, etc. In this type of drive testing, live data and voice sessions are established using SIM cards from all TSPs over 2G, 3G, 4G, and 5G networks. Multiple advanced test handsets are used, and the sessions are monitored and analysed in real-time using advanced Software Systems.

TRAI, through its appointed agency, conducted drive tests across City drive – 346.1 KMs, Hotspot locations - 11, Walk Test – 7.6 KMs and Highway drive of – 131.8 KMs in Ratnagiri District during 08th September to 11th September 2026 in Maharashtra LSA. These tests were conducted under the supervision of the TRAI Regional Office Bengaluru. The observations presented in drive test reports represent the performance of the TSPs on the area/ route under test on the day/ time of conducting the drive test.

Drive Test Route Map: The following map provides overview of drive test routes indicating City drive, Inter-operator calling, Hotspots and Walk tests, as per the legends shown on the map:-

Key Parameters Assessed

  1. Coverage Gap: Percentage of samples, for which signal strength observed less than the minimum prescribed signal strength for respective technology (2G/ 3G/ 4G/ 5G).
  2. Voice Services: Call Setup Success Rate (CSSR), Drop Call Rate (DCR), Call Setup Time, Call Silence Rate, Speech Quality (MOS).
  3. Call Silence Instance: Number of call silence instance occurred during the calls.
  4. Data Servies: Download/ Upload Throughput, Latency, Jitter, Packet Drop Rate           

The overall mobile network performance in Ratnagiri District for the key parameters has been summarised below:-

1. Ratnagiri District

a)    Coverage Gap - The signal strength observed during voice testing on the drive test route in auto-selection mode (5G/4G/3G/2G), measured as the number of samples having poor signal strength out of the total samples collected, was 5692/33673 for Airtel, 1484/40900 for BSNL, 1184/42801 for RJIL and 4823/38305 for VIL. Details of the coverage gaps have been provided in the map Annexed.

b)    Dropped Calls - Dropped calls, measured as the number of dropped calls out of the number of successfully established calls, were 15/301 for Airtel, 32/338 for BSNL, 10/387 for RJIL and 12/339 for VIL. Details of the dropped call locations have been provided in the map Annexed.

c)    Call Silence Instance - Call silence instances, measured as the total number of silence instances observed for > 3 seconds out of the total calls established, were 15/282 for Airtel, 11/310 for BSNL, 23/355 for RJIL and 6/306 for VIL. Details of the call silence instance locations have been provided in the map Annexed.

d)    Data Download and Upload Throughput:

i)   Data Download performance (Overall): Average download speed was observed as 113.81 Mbps for Airtel (5G/4G), 4.42 Mbps for BSNL (4G), 134.77 Mbps for RJIL (5G/4G) and 38.93 Mbps for VIL (5G/4G/2G). Detail of Download throughput has been provided in the map Annexed.

ii)  Data Upload performance (Overall): Average upload speed was observed as 17.46 Mbps for Airtel (5G/4G), 2.62 Mbps for BSNL (4G), 134.77 Mbps for RJIL (5G/4G) and 38.93 Mbps for VIL (5G/4G/2G). Detail of Upload throughput has been provided in the map Annexed.

Locations of Dropped Calls and Call Silence instances can be seen by clicking red dot on the map Annexed.

2.  Highway Drive – Ratnagiri to Kolhapur

a)    Coverage Gap - The signal strength observed during voice testing on the drive test route in auto-selection mode (5G/4G/3G/2G), measured as the number of samples having poor signal strength out of the total samples collected, was 333/11280 for Airtel, 381/11135 for BSNL, 100/11954 for RJIL and 185/11656 for VIL. Details of the coverage gaps have been provided in the map Annexed.

b)    Dropped Calls - Dropped calls, measured as the number of dropped calls out of the number of successfully established calls, were 6/56 for Airtel, 14/57 for BSNL, 2/59 for RJIL and 7/62 for VIL. Details of the dropped call locations have been provided in the map Annexed.

c)    Call Silence Instance - Call silence instances, measured as the total number of silence instances observed for > 3 seconds out of the total calls established, were 3/55 for Airtel, 1/59 for BSNL, 6/62 for RJIL and 1/61 for VIL. Details of the call silence instance locations have been provided in the map Annexed.

d)    Data Download and Upload Throughput:

i)   Data Download performance (Overall): Average download speed was observed as 124.67 Mbps for Airtel (5G/4G), 6.77 Mbps for BSNL (4G), 269.13 Mbps for RJIL (5G/4G) and 53.05 Mbps for VIL (5G/4G/2G). Detail of Download throughput has been provided in the map Annexed.

ii)  Data Upload performance (Overall): Average upload speed was observed as 19.77 Mbps for Airtel (5G/4G), 6.57 Mbps for BSNL (4G), 12.27 Mbps for RJIL (5G/4G) and 14.17 Mbps for VIL (5G/4G/2G). Detail of Upload throughput has been provided in the map Annexed.

Locations of Dropped Calls and Call Silence instances can be seen by clicking red dot on the map Annexed.

Details of drive test route and area covered during the IDT is as under:-

a)  City - The areas covered in the city drive are Devale, Kosumb, Navadi, Kurdhunda, Hathkhamba, Mirjole, Jakadevi, Jaigad, Undi, Ganpatipule, Basani, Tilak Ali, Bhatye, Purnagad, Adivare, Rajapur, Dasur, Satavali, Lanja, Punas and Nachane etc.

b)   Highway - Teli Aali, Karwanchiwadi, Nanij, Kondgaon, Amba, Malkapur, Bambavade and Kerle etc.

c)         Hotspot - The hot spot locations, capturing stationary user experience, are Bhatye Beach, District Collector Office, Ratnagiri, Lanja ST Bus Stand / Main Town Centre, Rajapur Government Hospital, Rajapur ST Bus Stand, Ratnadurg Fort / Bhagwati Fort, Ratnagiri Fish Market and Fisherman Docking Station, Ratnagiri ST Bus Stand, Superintendent of Police Office, Ratnagiri, Thiba Point, and Zilla Parishad, Ratnagiri.

d)         Walk Test - The walk tests conducted on 08th and 11th September 2026, Ganpatipule Beach, Rajapur Market Area, Ratnagiri Main Market, and Ratnagiri Railway Station.

The findings of this IDT report have been shared with respective TSPs for taking further necessary action at their end. Detailed reports of IDT are made available on the TRAI website at www.trai.gov.in. For any clarification or additional information, an email can be sent to adv.bengaluru@trai.gov.in or Regional Office of TRAI at Bengaluru RO can be contacted on telephone No. +91-80-22865004.

2333041.title: Dr Jitendra Singh to formally Launch Nationwide Digital Life Certificate Campaign 5
2333041.ministry: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
2333041.body_html:
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
Dr Jitendra Singh to formally Launch Nationwide Digital Life Certificate Campaign 5
Nationwide DLC Campaign 5 to Cover Over 2,000 Cities and Towns Across India
Posted On: 05 NOV 2026 3:13PM by PIB Delhi

Dr. Jitendra Singh, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences and Minister of State in the Prime Minister’s Office and the Ministries of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, will formally launch the Nationwide Digital Life Certificate (DLC) Campaign 5 on 6th November 2026 at the National Media Centre, Raisina Road, New Delhi.

Organised by the Department of Pension & Pensioners’ Welfare (DoPPW), Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions, the month-long campaign will continue until 30th of November 2026, covering over 2,000 cities and towns across the country. The initiative aims to make the submission of life certificates more accessible, convenient and hassle-free for pensioners through digital technology, particularly face authentication using the Jeevan Pramaan app.

The campaign is being conducted in collaboration with Public Sector Banks, India Post Payments Bank (IPPB), UIDAI, MeitY, Pensioners’ Welfare Associations, and key Ministries and Departments, including Defence, Railways and Posts, along with the Department of Telecommunications, Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation and State Governments.

Special emphasis is on facilitating super-senior pensioners aged 80 years and above, women pensioners and those facing health-related difficulties. Doorstep and home-based services will also be facilitated for pensioners unable to visit campaign locations due to age or infirmity.

During the launch programme, Dr. Jitendra Singh will also release the Compendium Booklet and Coffee Table e-Book documenting the achievements and initiatives undertaken during Nationwide DLC Campaign 4.0.

Senior officials from participating Ministries, Departments, banks and other stakeholder organisations are expected to attend the launch along with representatives from Pensioners Associations.

2332985.title: Union Health Minister reviews progress of AIIMS Awantipora; directs expeditious completion of remaining construction works and early operationalisation
2332985.ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
2332985.body_html:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Union Health Minister reviews progress of AIIMS Awantipora; directs expeditious completion of remaining construction works and early operationalisation
Timely completion of AIIMS Awantipora will strengthen access to quality tertiary healthcare in Jammu & Kashmir: Union Health Minister
Union Health Minister commends stakeholders for completing major buildings despite challenging terrain
OPD services targeted to commence before December 2026, followed by IPD services and academic activities in July 2027
Posted On: 05 NOV 2026 2:06PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Health and Family Welfare and Chemicals and Fertilizers, Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda, today reviewed the progress of construction and operationalisation of the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), Awantipora, Jammu and Kashmir.

During the review, the Union Health Minister assessed the status of infrastructure development, procurement of medical equipment and furniture, recruitment of faculty and other personnel, and preparedness for commencement of medical and academic activities at the Institute.

The Minister was informed that construction of AIIMS Awantipora is nearing completion, with all major buildings completed. Appreciating the efforts of CPWD and all concerned agencies and stakeholders, Shri Nadda commended their dedicated efforts in advancing the project despite the challenges posed by the site's terrain and other constraints. He emphasised that AIIMS Awantipora is a priority project and directed the concerned agencies to maintain the momentum and complete the remaining construction works by March 2027.

The Minister reviewed the phase-wise construction and handover plan. It was informed that the Phase-I buildings, including the OPD Registration Block, OPD Block, residential buildings and designated hostels, have been completed, with inventory verification and formal handover processes underway. The remaining academic, administrative, hospital, residential and hostel infrastructure is being taken up in a phased manner.

Emphasising the need for early operationalisation of the Institute, Shri Nadda directed HITES and the Executive Director, AIIMS Awantipora, to work in close coordination and expedite the procurement of medical equipment, OPD instruments, laboratory equipment and medical and administrative furniture. He stressed that all essential procurements required for commencement of OPD services must be completed on priority.

It was informed that procurement approval has been conveyed for 180 medical equipment items amounting to ₹59.41 crore, of which Notices of Award have been issued for 140 items. Procurement processes for OPD instruments, laboratory furniture and medical and administrative furniture are also at various stages of progress.

The Union Health Minister also reviewed preparedness for commencement of medical services and directed that all requisite arrangements, including equipment, diagnostic facilities, manpower and other operational requirements, be completed in advance. The OPD services at AIIMS Awantipora are targeted to commence before December 2026. The IPD services are proposed to begin in July 2027, subject to completion of the requisite infrastructure and operational arrangements. Academic activities, including commencement of MBBS classes, are proposed for the academic session 2027–28, beginning June–July 2027.

Reviewing the recruitment status, the Minister appreciated the efforts of the Executive Director and the Institute's team in taking forward the recruitment process. The Minister directed that the recruitment process be fast-tracked to ensure the availability of qualified faculty at the earliest. He also emphasised expediting recruitment against non-faculty positions and engagement of the requisite manpower for operationalisation of OPD and other services.

The Ministry has approved the engagement of essential manpower for operationalisation of the OPD and related services, including hospital attendants, housekeeping and sanitation personnel, and security staff. The proposed manpower arrangements cover 652 positions across various categories, including 150 security personnel.

The Minister further reviewed institutional readiness and support arrangements, including campus security, transport connectivity, website development and operational partnerships. He emphasised the need for effective coordination among AIIMS Awantipora, CPWD, HITES and the local administration to address security and other operational issues and ensure the smooth functioning of the Institute.

Reiterating the Government's commitment to strengthening healthcare infrastructure across the country, Shri Nadda emphasised that the timely completion and operationalisation of AIIMS Awantipora would be an important step towards expanding access to quality tertiary healthcare and specialised medical services in Jammu and Kashmir. The Institute will also strengthen medical education and contribute to the development of healthcare capacity in the region, in keeping with the vision of Hon'ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi to ensure accessible and quality healthcare for all.

2332947.title: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) organised an awareness workshop on SRI Fund for supporting Women-Led MSMEs
2332947.body_html:
Ministry of Micro,Small & Medium Enterprises
Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) organised an awareness workshop on SRI Fund for supporting Women-Led MSMEs
Ministry of MSME highlights the role of SRI Fund in mobilising Growth Capital for Women-Led Enterprises under Yashashvini Campaign
SRI Fund leverages nearly ₹48,000 Crore in Private Investment, supports 824 MSMEs
Posted On: 05 NOV 2026 1:37PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME), Government of India, organised an “Awareness Workshop on the Self-Reliant India (SRI) Fund for Supporting Women-Led MSMEs” on 4 November 2026 at Kartavya Bhawan 3, New Delhi, as part of the Yashashvini Campaign for promoting women entrepreneurship. The event was chaired by Shri Bharat Khera, Secretary (MSME).

The workshop brought together over 60 women entrepreneurs from across the country, along with senior officials from the Ministry of MSME, representatives of industry associations, NSIC Venture Capital Fund Limited (NVCFL). SBI Ventures Limited (SVL), Daughter Funds under the SRI Fund, Women Entrepreneurship Platform (WEP) of NITI Aayog and Atal Incubation Centre ALEAP Women Entrepreneurs Hub.

Dr. Rajneesh, Additional Secretary & Development Commissioner, Ministry of MSME, gave an overview of the journey of the SRI Fund. He explained that the Fund was conceived to extend equity support to MSMEs beyond traditional debt, with a ₹10,000 crore commitment from the Government of India, and an expectation that private investors would contribute four times that amount. He noted that, in several cases, investee enterprises associated with the SRI Fund had grown their turnover three to four times within two to three years, and had gone on to raise further capital from private sources. He urged the associations present to carry the message about the Fund to their members.

In his inaugural address, Shri Bharat Khera said that registrations on the Udyam and Udyam Assist portals had crossed 10 crore on 30 October 2026, which had bridged the formalisation gap. Of these, 37.6 per cent were women-owned enterprises, and now, let us aspire to take this share to 50 per cent. He noted that formalisation now placed a greater responsibility on the Ministry to help MSMEs scale up – for which, growth capital is critical.

Shri Khera shared that, under the SRI Fund, commitments of ₹8,305 crore had been made against the ₹10,000 crore corpus, and that nearly ₹48,000 crore had been leveraged from private venture capital and private equity funds. 72 Daughter Funds have been empanelled, and investments of ₹21,330 crore have already been made in 824 MSMEs, of which about 74 per cent are micro enterprises. Of the enterprises supported, 77 have moved up to a larger category, six have been listed on stock exchanges, and 32 exits have been completed with profits. He added that Daughter Funds take investment decisions on commercial lines, looking at viability, growth trajectory over the last three years, and a business plan with positive cash flows. The Government maintains an arm’s length from their day-to-day operations and does not play any role in Daughter Funds’ investment decisions.

Secretary also stressed that credit and equity must go together. He said that MSME credit outstanding had grown from about ₹10 lakh crore in 2014 to over ₹40 lakh crore, with the non-performing assets for MSME sector falling to about 3.5 per cent. He highlighted that an additional ₹2,000 crore has been provided to the SRI Fund in Union Budget 2026-27, for micro enterprises. He also drew attention to the newly rolled out ₹10,000 crore SME Growth Fund, which will invest directly in small and medium enterprises. He advised entrepreneurs to maintain proper financial records and adopt a suitable legal structure, and said that bringing in equity also improves an enterprise’s access to debt.

In Session I, titled ‘The growth journey of women-led MSMEs – why growth capital matters’, representatives of industry associations shared their experience of working with women entrepreneurs. They pointed out that many women-led enterprises that are early-stage require support through smaller tickets, investment-readiness programmes in Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities, support in accounting and business valuation, and flexibility for women entrepreneurs who may lack collateral or long balance-sheet histories. They also stressed the need to link capital with market access, including through the Government e-Marketplace (GeM), ONDC and exports, and emphasized the importance of organizing such workshops regularly.

In Session II, on the ‘Overview of the SRI Fund and the role of Daughter Funds’, Shri Praveen Kumar, Additional Development Commissioner, Ministry of MSME, explained the structure of the Fund, in which the Mother Fund invests only through Daughter Funds, and the Daughter Funds invest in MSMEs. Shri Subhransu Sekhar Acharya, Chairman-cum-Managing Director, NSIC, spoke on the gaps in the MSME ecosystem and advised entrepreneurs on the benefits of equity funding. Shri Prem Prabhakar, MD and CEO of SBI Ventures Limited, the investment manager of the SRI Fund, said that equity is of strategic value for growing enterprises as it does not require collateral and because investors provide sector specific mentorship and hand-holding. The Daughter Funds explained the investment criteria such as a strong market, a capable team, a scalable model, audited financials, governance readiness, including a private limited company structure, and a clear use of capital. They advised entrepreneurs on the common steps for acquiring equity funding, from screening to due diligence and documentation.

In Session III, the focus was on support available through ecosystem partners. Representatives from the Atal Incubation Centre ALEAP Women Entrepreneurs Hub and the Women Entrepreneurship Platform (WEP), NITI Aayog, presented the range of support available to women entrepreneurs, including incubation, mentorship, market access, access to information on government schemes, and compliance support. Technical support for the conceptualisation, planning, and execution of the workshop was provided by the ecosystem partner MicroSave Consulting (MSC).

The final session was an interactive Q&A where participants broached subjects such as approaching Daughter Funds, investment-readiness for proprietorship-run enterprises, sector-specific funds, and technology and infrastructure support. It was shared that details of the 72 Daughter Funds, including their sector focus and contacts, are available on the website of NSIC Venture Capital Fund Limited, the special purpose vehicle for the SRI Fund.  The workshop concluded with the Ministry of MSME assuring continued support to women entrepreneurship through the Yashashvni Campaign in the future.

2332944.title: TRAI Assesses Mobile Network Quality across Nuh & Palwal cities and adjoining areas (in Haryana LSA) during the month of July 2026
2332944.body_html:
Ministry of Communications
TRAI Assesses Mobile Network Quality across Nuh & Palwal cities and adjoining areas (in Haryana LSA) during the month of July 2026
Posted On: 05 NOV 2026 1:28PM by PIB Delhi

The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has released findings of Independent Drive Test (IDT) conducted across Nuh & Palwal cities and adjoining areas (in Haryana LSA), during the month of July 2026, for information of general telecom consumers. The purpose of this drive test is to assess and verify real time quality of mobile network services (both voice & data) provided by Telecom Service Providers (TSPs). During the IDT, TRAI captures performance of TSPs for key Quality of Service (QoS) parameters like Coverage, Call Drop Rate (CDR), Call Setup Success Rate (CSSR), Packet loss rate, data Download (DL) and Upload (UL) throughput etc., which are then published to inform Consumers and encourage TSPs to improve their services.

These IDTs have been designed to capture on ground mobile network performance of all TSPs across diverse usages environment like cities, hotspots, public transport hubs, etc. In this type of drive testing, live data and voice sessions are established using SIM cards from all TSPs over 2G, 3G, 4G, and 5G networks. Multiple advanced test handsets are used, and the sessions are monitored and analysed in real-time using advanced Software Systems.

TRAI, through its appointed agency, conducted drive tests across City drive – 295.2 KMs, Walk test-1.8 KMs & Hotspot locations - 06 across Nuh & Palwal cities and adjoining areas during 13th  July to 15th July 2026 in Haryana LSA. These tests were conducted under the supervision of the TRAI Regional Office Jaipur. The observations presented in the drive test reports represent the performance of the TSPs on the area/ route under test on the day/ time of conducting the drive test.

Drive Test Route Map: The following map provides overview of drive test routes indicating City drive, Inter-operator calling, Hotspots and Walk tests, as per the legends shown on the map: -

Key Parameters Assessed

  1. Coverage Gap: Percentage of samples, for which signal strength observed less than the minimum prescribed signal strength for respective technology (2G/ 3G/ 4G/ 5G).
  2. Voice Services: Call Setup Success Rate (CSSR), Drop Call Rate (DCR), Call Setup Time, Call Silence Rate, Speech Quality (MOS).
  3. Call Silence Instance: Number of call silence instance occurred during the calls.
  4. Data Servies: Download/ Upload Throughput, Latency, Jitter, Packet Drop Rate.           

The overall mobile network performance in Nuh & Palwal cities and adjoining areas of the districts for the key parameters has been summarised below:

  1. Nuh District:
  1. Coverage Gap - The signal strength observed during voice testing on the drive test route in auto-selection mode (5G/4G/3G/2G), measured as the number of samples having poor signal strength out of the total samples collected, was 346/15867 for Airtel, 4021/15424 for BSNL, 784/15626 for RJIL and 327/15836 for VIL. Details of the coverage gaps have been provided in the map Annexed.
  1. Dropped Calls - Dropped calls, measured as the number of dropped calls out of the number of successfully established calls, were 0/142 for Airtel, 5/140 for BSNL, 1/141 for RJIL and 0/143 for VIL. Details of the dropped call locations have been provided in the map Annexed.
  1. Call Silence Instance - Call silence instances, measured as the total number of silence instances observed for > 3 seconds out of the total calls established, were 13/136 for Airtel, 35/131 for BSNL, 5/135 for RJIL and 20/139 for VIL. Details of the call silence instance locations have been provided in the map Annexed.
  2. Packet Loss rate (Downlink & Uplink):
  1. Packet Loss rate (Downlink): Downlink Packet loss rate measured for  Airtel as 1.84 %, for BSNL as 5.35%, for RJIL as 2.11%  and  for VIL as 3.33 %.
  2. Packet Loss rate (uplink): Uplink Packet loss rate measured for  Airtel as 2.06%, for BSNL as 3.12%, for RJIL as 2.84%  and  for VIL as 2.21 %.
  1. Data Download and Upload Throughput:
  1. Data Download performance (Overall): Average download speed was observed as 75.70 Mbps for Airtel (5G/4G), 6.78 Mbps for BSNL (4G/3G/2G), 130.28 Mbps for RJIL (5G/4G) and 20.03 Mbps for VIL (5G/4G/2G). Detail of Download throughput has been provided in the map Annexed.
  1. Data Upload performance (Overall): Average upload speed was observed as 14.26 Mbps for Airtel (5G/4G), 6.21 Mbps for BSNL (4G/3G/2G), 9.71 Mbps for RJIL (5G/4G) and 10.84 Mbps for VIL (5G/4G/2G). Detail of upload throughput has been provided in the map Annexed.
  1. Palwal District :
  1. Coverage Gap - The signal strength observed during voice testing on the drive test route in auto-selection mode (5G/4G/3G/2G), measured as the number of samples having poor signal strength out of the total samples collected, was 279/30406 for Airtel, 2239/29643 for BSNL, 768/29489 for RJIL and 241/30350 for VIL. Details of the coverage gaps have been provided in the map Annexed.
  2. Dropped Calls - Dropped calls, measured as the number of dropped calls out of the number of successfully established calls, were 1/272 for Airtel, 3/268 for BSNL, 1/251 for RJIL and 0/269 for VIL. Details of the dropped call locations have been provided in the map Annexed.
  3. Call Silence Instance - Call silence instances, measured as the total number of silence instances observed for > 3 seconds out of the total calls established, were 10/259 for Airtel, 11/258 for BSNL, 9/250 for RJIL and 17/265 for VIL. Details of the call silence instance locations have been provided in the map Annexed.
  4. Packet Loss rate (Downlink & Uplink):
  5. Packet Loss rate (Downlink): Downlink Packet loss rate measured for  Airtel as 0.79 %, for BSNL as 2.57%, for RJIL as 1.62%  and  for VIL as 1.22%.

 

  1. Packet Loss rate (uplink): Uplink Packet loss rate measured for  Airtel as 0.96%, for BSNL as 1.40%, for RJIL as 1.78%  and  for VIL as 1.35%.
  1. Data Download and Upload Throughput:
  1. Data Download performance (Overall): Average download speed was observed as 105.00 Mbps for Airtel (5G/4G), 13.92 Mbps for BSNL (4G/3G/2G), 212.03 Mbps for RJIL (5G/4G) and 40.70 Mbps for VIL (5G/4G/2G). Detail of Download throughput has been provided in the map Annexed.
  1. Data Upload performance (Overall): Average upload speed was observed as 20.96 Mbps for Airtel (5G/4G), 7.20 Mbps for BSNL (4G/3G/2G), 14.52 Mbps for RJIL (5G/4G) and 13.03 Mbps for VIL (5G/4G/2G). Detail of upload throughput has been provided in the map Annexed.

Locations of Dropped Calls and Call Silence instances can be seen by clicking red dot on the map Annexed.

Details of drive test route and area covered during the IDT are as under: -

Nuh District- Tauru, Rewasan, Ghasera, Nuh, Akera, Nagina, Mandkhera, Mohlaka, Sakras, Ferozpur and Jhirka etc.

 Palwal District- Mandkola, Palwal Rural, Dhal, Baghola, Alawalpur, Deeghot, Khatela Sarai, Banchari, Hodal, Singar, Punhana and Phangwan etc.

The findings of this IDT report have been shared with respective TSPs for taking further necessary action at their end, if required. Detailed report of IDT is made available on the TRAI website at www.trai.gov.in. For any clarification or additional information, an email can be sent to Regional office of TRAI at Jaipur on Email id adv.jaipur@trai.gov.in Regional Office of TRAI at Jaipur RO can be contacted on telephone no.  0141-2701919.

2332934.title: Inter-Ministerial Group Recommends Asset Monetisation Proposals Worth Over ₹1,100 Crore for Approval by Cabinet-Delegated Alternative Mechanism
2332934.body_html:
Ministry of Finance
Inter-Ministerial Group Recommends Asset Monetisation Proposals Worth Over ₹1,100 Crore for Approval by Cabinet-Delegated Alternative Mechanism
Recommendations Cover Surplus Land and Building Assets of CPSEs; IMG Reviews Progress of Asset Monetisation Initiatives Facilitated by NLMC
Posted On: 05 NOV 2026 1:16PM by PIB Delhi

The Inter-Ministerial Group (IMG), chaired by the Secretary, Department of Public Enterprises (DPE), and co-chaired by the Secretary, Department of Telecommunications (DoT), has recommended asset monetisation proposals involving assets valued at over ₹1,100 crore for consideration and approval by the Alternative Mechanism (AM).

The proposals primarily relate to surplus land and building assets of Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) identified for monetisation. The recommendations mark an important milestone in the Government of India's efforts to unlock value from surplus and underutilised public assets and facilitate their productive utilisation.

The recommendations reflect the growing momentum of the Government's asset monetisation programme, which seeks to enable CPSEs and other Government entities to realise the economic potential of surplus assets through systematic assessment, professional transaction preparation and competitive price discovery.

The recommended proposals will be placed before the Cabinet-delegated Alternative Mechanism for consideration and approval. Following the requisite approvals, further monetisation activities will be undertaken in accordance with prescribed procedures.

As the Government's specialised institution for monetisation of surplus land and other non-core assets, NLMC plays a key role in facilitating asset assessment, due diligence, valuation, transaction structuring and market-facing monetisation processes, working closely with concerned Ministries, Departments and asset-owning entities.

The initiative reinforces the Government of India's commitment to efficient public asset management, transparent and value-maximising monetisation, and productive utilisation of surplus assets to support investment and economic development.

About NLMC

The National Land Monetization Corporation (NLMC) is a wholly owned Government of India company under the administrative control of the Department of Public Enterprises, Ministry of Finance. Established pursuant to the Union Budget 2021–22 announcement, NLMC facilitates the monetisation of surplus land and other non-core assets of CPSEs and Government entities through professional transaction advisory, due diligence, valuation and transparent, competitive monetisation processes.

Website: https://nlmc.dpe.gov.in

2332932.title: Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare achieves 100% of targets under Special Campaign 6
2332932.ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
2332932.body_html:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare achieves 100% of targets under Special Campaign 6
Special Campaign 6 undertaken at over 1.62 lakh sites across institutions and offices under the Department of Health and Family Welfare
Over 1.20 lakh physical files weeded out; 5.82 lakh sq. ft. of office space reclaimed
12,840 public grievances and 119 MP References disposed of; scrap and e-waste disposal generates over ₹1 crore in revenue
Posted On: 05 NOV 2026 1:12PM by PIB Delhi

Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has successfully achieved 100% of the targets set for the Department of Health and Family Welfare (DoHFW) under Special Campaign 6, conducted from 2nd to 31st October, 2026. The campaign was undertaken with a focus on institutionalising Swachhata, reducing pendency and strengthening administrative efficiency across Government offices.

The campaign was implemented across the Department's Headquarters, Central Government Hospitals, Attached and Subordinate Offices, Autonomous Bodies and Central Public Sector Undertakings (CPSUs) across the country. It reaffirmed the Ministry's commitment to promoting a culture of cleanliness, effective records management and improved working environments across its institutions.

  

  

Shri J. P. Nadda, Hon’ble Union Minister of Health & Family Welfare visited AIIMS, New Delhi to review cleanliness, waste management and patient amenities during Special Campaign 6

Under the guidance of the Union Minister of Health and Family Welfare and the Union Health Secretary, the progress of the campaign was regularly reviewed to ensure the timely achievement of targets. During the campaign, cleanliness drives were undertaken at 1,62,325 sites across offices and institutions under the Department.

Significant achievements were also recorded in addressing public grievances and reducing administrative pendency. A total of 12,840 public grievances and 6,026 associated appeals were disposed of, while 119 references received from Members of Parliament were addressed. The campaign also facilitated the simplification of 19 rules and processes, contributing to streamlined administrative procedures.

As part of Special Campaign 6, Shri Prataprao Jadhav, Hon’ble Minister of State for Health & Family Welfare visited the health check-up camp at Kartavya Bhawan-1, New Delhi and interacted with Safai Mitras, appreciating their contribution to cleanliness and hygiene

As part of the records management exercise, 1,25,114 physical files were reviewed, of which 1,20,115 files were weeded out. In addition, 37,481 e-files were reviewed, with 32,542 e-files closed. These initiatives resulted in the reclamation of 5,82,449 square feet of office space. The disposal of scrap and e-waste also generated revenue exceeding ₹1 crore, while promoting the responsible management of obsolete materials.

Union Health Secretary reviewed the progress of Special Campaign 6 and preparedness for dedicated one-day activity “Kayakalp Activities (Sanitation & Hygiene)” held on 27th October, 2026

The progress and achievements under the campaign were regularly uploaded on the Special Campaign portal of the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG) at https://scdpm.nic.in. Social media updates, PIB statements and best practices were also shared on the portal to document and highlight the initiatives undertaken across the Department.

AIIMS, Jodhpur promotes “Waste-to-Art” by reusing plastic drums and bottles as planters and creating decorative pots and wall hangings carrying “No Tobacco” and “No Smoking” messages

Lady Hardinge Medical College, New Delhi: “Waste-to-Art” activity

Through the successful implementation of Special Campaign 6, the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has further strengthened its efforts towards institutionalising Swachhata, promoting efficient office management, minimising administrative pendency and ensuring responsive public service delivery. Achievement of 100% of the prescribed targets, with performance exceeding targets across several parameters, reflects the Department's sustained commitment to efficient, accountable and citizen-centric governance.

2332894.title: NRAA, ICAR-NBSS&LUP and DoLR Organise National-Level Consultation to Strengthen Science-Based Watershed Management
2332894.body_html:
Ministry of Rural Development
NRAA, ICAR-NBSS&LUP and DoLR Organise National-Level Consultation to Strengthen Science-Based Watershed Management
Shri. Dilip Kumar, Secretary, DoLR calls for balancing scientific rigour with practical implementation, flexibility and community participation
National Technical Guidelines to provide a scientific and practical framework for future watershed development programmes
Posted On: 05 NOV 2026 12:19PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Land Resources (DoLR), Ministry of Rural Development, The National Rainfed Area Authority (NRAA), Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, in collaboration with the ICAR–National Bureau of Soil Survey and Land Use Planning (ICAR-NBSS&LUP), Nagpur, has organised a two-day , 3rd National Level Consultation Meeting on the Draft National Technical Guidelines (NTG) for Improved Watershed Management under World Bank Assisted “Rejuvenating Watersheds for Agricultural Resilience through Innovative Development (REWARD)” Programme on November 4–5, 2026, at ICAR-NBSS&LUP, Nagpur. The consultation brings together senior policymakers, technical experts, development partners, researchers and representatives of various States to deliberate on strengthening watershed development through scientific, technology-driven, cost-effective and participatory approaches.

The inaugural session was attended by Shri Dilip Kumar, IAS, Secretary, Department of Land Resources, Dr. Chandra Sekhar Kumar, IAS, CEO, National Rainfed Area Authority (NRAA), Shri Nitin Khade, IAS, Joint Secretary, Department of Land Resources, Ms. Priti Kumar, Senior Agriculture Specialist and Task Team Leader, World Bank, Dr. Susama Sudhishri, Technical Expert (Watershed Development) NRAA and Dr. N.G. Patil, Director, ICAR-NBSS&LUP, along with other distinguished delegates.

Addressing the inaugural session, Secretary, DoLR, Shri Dilip Kumar emphasised the need to strike a balance between scientific rigour and practical implementation in watershed development programmes. He observed that technical guidelines should not become so rigid that they create difficulties for field-level implementation. Flexibility must be provided to States, taking into account their institutional capacities, technical capabilities and varying administrative arrangements.

Highlighting the importance of efficient financial management, he stressed that funds allocated to the Department should be utilised effectively and speedily by the States.

Shri Dilip Kumar emphasised the importance of identifying a set of essential parameters to be followed uniformly by all States, while allowing flexibility in adopting other desirable parameters according to local requirements. He called for robust baseline data and comprehensive impact assessments to evaluate the outcomes of WDC-PMKSY 2.0, identify implementation gaps and draw lessons for the effective design and execution of WDC-PMKSY 3.0.

He further stressed that watershed development should remain focused on tangible outcomes for farmers and communities. Scientific interventions must translate into practical, location-specific solutions that can be effectively implemented at the grassroots level. He also called for recognising and motivating well-performing States and field-level officers to strengthen institutional commitment and improve implementation.

Shri Dilip Kumar observed that the proposed National Technical Guidelines should be finalised with a practical and implementable approach. He expressed confidence that achieving 80–90 per cent of the intended objectives through a flexible and realistic implementation framework would be more meaningful than adopting overly rigid standards.

Dr. C.S. Kumar, CEO, NRAA, highlighted the critical importance of data accessibility and availability for effective planning and implementation of watershed development programmes. He stressed the need for comprehensive capacity building of stakeholders at different levels and advocated effective utilisation of legacy datasets and existing scientific information. He also emphasised the development of a harmonised national-level Decision Support System, incorporating the best features of the systems developed by Odisha and Karnataka, to facilitate effective and integrated watershed planning.

Speaking on the occasion, Shri Nitin Khade highlighted the importance of finalising the National Technical Guidelines (NTGs) in a time-bound manner, stating that the consultation was an important step towards completing the draft guidelines. He emphasised that the guidelines would serve as a foundational framework  for future watershed development programmes.

Referring to India's vision of becoming a developed nation by 2047, Shri Khade highlighted the aspiration to contribute towards building a drought-resilient India through the scientific treatment of rainfed areas.

Emphasising the importance of Land Resource Inventory (LRI), he stated that LRI-based scientific data, digital soil libraries and Decision Support Systems (DSS) can transform watershed planning and implementation. These tools can enable village communities and individual farmers to make informed decisions regarding soil and water conservation plans, cropping patterns and nutrient management through accessible digital platforms.

He appreciated the contribution of ICAR-NBSS&LUP and the Soil and Land Use Survey of India (SLUSI) in developing digital soil mapping databases covering large areas. He emphasised that the extent of LRI coverage under future watershed development programs should be determined by considering the availability of existing datasets, implementation timelines, cost-effectiveness and field-level feasibility.

Shri Khade also highlighted the need to accelerate project implementation under WDC PMKSY 2.0. He noted that project timelines had progressively been reduced from seven years under WDC-PMKSY 1.0 to five years under WDC-PMKSY 2.0.

He further emphasised the need for appropriate use of GIS, remote sensing, high-resolution satellite imagery and drone technology, depending on local requirements.

Highlighting the importance of community participation, he stressed the need to strengthen Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs), User Groups ( UGs),Self-Help Groups (SHGs) and other community-based institutions for livelihood enhancement, value addition and better market access. He also underlined the need to strengthen community ownership and participation in the maintenance of water harvesting structures beyond the project period.

Dr. N.G. Patil, Director, ICAR-NBSS& highlighted the significance of Land Resource Inventory as a holistic, science-based approach for integrated watershed planning and landscape development.

The consultation is witnessing participation from representatives of the Department of Land Resources, NRAA, World Bank, REWARD project States of Odisha and Karnataka, NGOs, consortium partners including ICRISAT, WASSAN, NRSC and MANAGE, NABARD and various ICAR institutes.

The two-day consultation provides a platform for detailed technical deliberations and knowledge sharing on LRI, hydrological assessments, GIS and remote sensing applications, Decision Support Systems, community participation, livelihood interventions and monitoring and evaluation mechanisms.

The deliberations are expected to contribute towards finalising the National Technical Guidelines under the World Bank-assisted REWARD programme. These guidelines will also serve as an important technical input for WDC-PMKSY 3.0, facilitating science-based, cost-effective, scalable and participatory watershed planning, implementation and monitoring across States.

The consultation reaffirms the collective commitment of national and State-level institutions towards building climate-resilient landscapes, strengthening water security and improving the livelihoods of farming communities through scientific and sustainable watershed management.

2332844.title: Department of Rural Development and DAHD Join Hands to Boost Fodder Production, Strengthen Livestock Infrastructure and Support Rural Livelihoods under VB–G RAM G
2332844.body_html:
Ministry of Rural Development
Department of Rural Development and DAHD Join Hands to Boost Fodder Production, Strengthen Livestock Infrastructure and Support Rural Livelihoods under VB–G RAM G
Centre Issues Joint Advisory to States/UTs to Improve Fodder Availability and Promote Livestock Development in Rural Areas
22 Permissible Works Identified for Fodder Cultivation, Pasture Development, Dairy Infrastructure and Veterinary Facilities
Viksit Gram Panchayat Plans to Drive Fodder Security, Livestock Development and Sustainable Rural Livelihoods
Posted On: 05 NOV 2026 10:22AM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Rural Development (DoRD), Ministry of Rural Development, and the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying (DAHD), Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, have jointly issued an advisory to all States and Union Territories to strengthen fodder security, pasture development and livestock-supportive infrastructure through convergence under the Viksit Bharat–Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin): VB–G RAM G Act, 2025.

The initiative adopts a whole-of-government approach to address fodder scarcity, strengthen livestock-related infrastructure and support the livelihoods of rural households, particularly small and marginal farmers and landless families dependent on livestock and dairy activities. It seeks to align rural employment and asset creation with the requirements of the livestock sector, while ensuring compliance with the provisions and planning framework of the Act.

The VB–G RAM G Act, which came into force on 1 July 2026, provides a statutory guarantee of 125 days of wage employment per rural household and focuses on the creation of durable assets across four thematic areas, including livelihood-related infrastructure and mitigation of extreme weather events. The joint advisory seeks to leverage this framework to promote fodder production, develop community pastures and strengthen livestock-supportive infrastructure.

22 Permissible Works Identified for Fodder and Livestock-Related Infrastructure

The advisory identifies 22 relevant works from the list of 375 permissible works under the VB–G RAM G framework. These cover interventions relating to fodder cultivation and storage, pasture development, livestock shelters, dairy infrastructure and veterinary health facilities.

Key interventions include:

  • Fodder cultivation for individual households and communities.
  • Development of community fodder resources, pastures, grazing lands and silvipasture.
  • Fodder storage facilities, fodder banks, silage units and other eligible fodder-related assets.
  • Construction, repair and maintenance of livestock shelters for eligible beneficiaries and communities, including cattle, goat, piggery and poultry shelters, as specified in the approved list.
  • Construction and repair of community milk collection centres.
  • Construction and repair of community veterinary health centres.
  • Construction of community cattle and animal troughs.
  • Construction of Azolla tanks for individual beneficiaries, as included in the approved list.

These interventions are intended to improve fodder availability, strengthen livestock-supportive infrastructure and contribute to more sustainable livestock-based livelihoods. All works will be undertaken in accordance with the approved list of permissible works and the applicable provisions of the Act, Rules and Guidelines.

Viksit Gram Panchayat Plans to Drive Local Priorities

The advisory emphasises decentralised, bottom-up and Panchayati Raj Institution (PRI)-led planning, with fodder development and livestock-supportive infrastructure integrated into Viksit Gram Panchayat Plans (VGPPs) and aligned with local development priorities approved through the Gram Sabha.

States and Union Territories are encouraged to endeavour to progressively increase expenditure on fodder and livestock-supportive works towards at least 5% of total programme expenditure, wherever supported by local needs, approved plans and applicable guidelines.

A need-based saturation approach is also encouraged to identify eligible households and communities requiring fodder and livestock-related assets. Gram Panchayats may give particular attention to areas with significant livestock dependence, including Gram Panchayats where more than 30% of the population is livestock-dependent, based on local requirements and priorities.

State-specific Fodder Resource Development Plans prepared by the ICAR–Indian Grassland and Fodder Research Institute (ICAR–IGFRI) may serve as guiding documents for planning at the district and block levels. The advisory also encourages attention to climate-resilient interventions, including suitable fodder varieties, perennial grasses and integrated crop–livestock systems, wherever relevant and covered under the permissible works.

Interdepartmental Convergence and Monitoring

The advisory calls upon States and Union Territories to prepare comprehensive State Action Plans for fodder security and livestock infrastructure through convergence among the Departments of Rural Development, Animal Husbandry, Agriculture and other relevant sectors.

The coordinated approach is intended to improve planning, facilitate effective use of available resources and ensure that investments respond to local requirements and support sustainable livestock-based livelihoods.

Strict Compliance with Statutory Safeguards

The advisory reiterates that all fodder development and livestock-supportive works must adhere to the applicable provisions of the VB–G RAM G Act, 2025. These include decentralised and PRI-led planning, compulsory social audit, the district-level ceiling of 40% on the material component, selection of individual beneficiaries in accordance with provisions under Schedule I, weekly public disclosure and grievance redressal.

States and Union Territories have also been urged to ensure that the approved advisory is disseminated among the concerned departments, Panchayati Raj Institutions and field functionaries to facilitate effective planning and implementation.

The advisory underscores the importance of coordinated action by State Governments and Union Territoriesto ensure that fodder security and livestock-supportive infrastructure receive due attention in rural development planning.

Strengthening Rural Livelihoods towards Viksit Bharat @2047

The joint advisory marks an important step towards integrating rural employment, natural resource management and livestock development. By linking permissible works under VB–G RAM G with local fodder and livestock infrastructure needs, the initiative seeks to improve fodder availability, support dairy and animal husbandry activities and strengthen livelihood opportunities for rural households.

Through convergence, decentralised planning and coordinated implementation, the initiative aims to help States and Panchayati Raj Institutions create durable assets that respond to local needs, support climate-resilient rural development and contribute to the broader vision of Viksit Bharat @2047.

2332796.title: Union Health Ministry Proposes Immediate Suspension of Manufacturing Licences for Drugs Found Not of Standard Quality on Specified Critical Parameters
2332796.ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
2332796.body_html:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Union Health Ministry Proposes Immediate Suspension of Manufacturing Licences for Drugs Found Not of Standard Quality on Specified Critical Parameters
Proposed Amendments to Drugs Rules, 1945 Aim to Strengthen Regulatory Oversight and Ensure Prompt Action Against Substandard Medicines
Manufacturing Licences of Drugs Found Deficient in Assay, Dissolution, Related Substances, Impurities or Sterility Proposed to be Suspended Immediately
Restoration of Suspended Licences to be Permitted Only After Verified Corrective and Preventive Action by Manufacturers
Enhanced Reporting Mechanism Proposed to Facilitate Timely Regulatory Coordination and Strengthen Accountability
Posted On: 04 NOV 2026 8:57PM by PIB Delhi

In a significant step towards strengthening the regulatory framework for ensuring the quality and safety of medicines in the country, the Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has proposed amendments to the Drugs Rules, 1945, to provide for immediate suspension of manufacturing licences in respect of drugs declared Not of Standard Quality (NSQ) on specified critical quality parameters.

The proposed amendments seek to enable prompt regulatory intervention upon detection of substandard medicines, prevent their continued manufacture and distribution, and strengthen the mechanism for ensuring compliance with prescribed quality standards, in the interest of patient safety and public health.

Under the existing provisions of the Drugs Rules, 1945, suspension or cancellation of a manufacturing licence is preceded by the prescribed regulatory procedure, including issuance of a show-cause notice. This may result in a time gap between the declaration of a drug as NSQ and initiation of regulatory action. During this period, the concerned drug may continue to remain in circulation, posing potential risks to public health and making effective recall more challenging.

To address this regulatory concern, the Ministry has proposed a provision for immediate suspension of the manufacturing licence of the concerned drug by the Central Licensing Approving Authority or the State Licensing Authority, as the case may be, upon receipt of a Government Analyst's report declaring the drug as NSQ with respect to Assay, Dissolution, Related Substances, Impurities or Sterility.

These parameters are critical to determining the quality of medicines. The proposed provision aims to ensure that instances of non-compliance involving these specified parameters are met with prompt regulatory action, thereby minimising potential risks to patients.

The proposed amendment also provides for mandatory corrective measures before revocation of the suspension. The suspension shall continue until the manufacturer undertakes an effective Root Cause Analysis to identify the reasons for the quality failure and implements appropriate Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) to the satisfaction of the concerned Licensing Authority.

Revocation of the suspension shall be permitted only after implementation of the requisite corrective and preventive measures and their due verification by the Licensing Authority. This mechanism is intended to ensure that identified quality deficiencies are adequately addressed and necessary safeguards are put in place to prevent their recurrence.

To further strengthen regulatory coordination and facilitate timely action, consequential amendments have also been proposed to Form 13, relating to the test report of the Government Analyst.

Under the proposed mechanism, the Government Analyst's report would be endorsed to the Drugs Controller General of India (DCGI), the concerned State/UT Licensing Authority under whose jurisdiction the manufacturing site is located, as well as the manufacturer and marketer of the concerned drug.

The proposed arrangement is aimed at ensuring timely communication of NSQ findings to the relevant authorities and stakeholders, thereby facilitating coordinated regulatory action and strengthening accountability across the drug manufacturing and marketing chain.

The proposed amendments follow deliberations at the 65th meeting of the Drugs Consultative Committee (DCC), held on 20 December 2024, and recommendations of the 92nd meeting of the Drugs Technical Advisory Board (DTAB), held on 24 April 2025.

The amendments are expected to strengthen post-marketing regulatory surveillance, facilitate timely action against substandard medicines, promote greater accountability among manufacturers and marketers, and reinforce public confidence in the quality of medicines available in the country.

The initiative reflects the Government of India's continued commitment to strengthening the drug regulatory framework and ensuring the availability of safe, effective and quality medicines for the public.

The draft amendments have been notified for public consultation, inviting objections and suggestions from stakeholders and members of the public within 30 days from the date on which copies of the Gazette of India containing the draft rules are made available to the public.

Objections and suggestions, if any, may be addressed to the Under Secretary (Drugs), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India, U-6, Work Hall-C Wing, First Floor, Kartavya Bhawan-1, New Delhi – 110001, or sent by email to drugsdiv-mohfw[at]gov[dot]in.

The draft Gazette notification may be accessed through the official e-Gazette portal at:

https://egazette.gov.in/(S(tqlgzgdze5s0ylovnh4l0ej1))/ViewPDF.aspx

2332794.title: PM Surya Ghar Has Truly Transformed into a Mass Movement: Shri Pralhad Joshi
2332794.ministry: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
2332794.body_html:
Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
PM Surya Ghar Has Truly Transformed into a Mass Movement: Shri Pralhad Joshi
Five Country Partners deepen bilateral clean energy ties across hydrogen, offshore wind and financing
BRE Summit and Expo 2026 Charts India’s Technology-Led Clean Energy Future
Posted On: 04 NOV 2026 8:54PM by PIB Delhi

“The PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana has truly transformed into a mass movement, ultimately ensuring welfare and savings for the people, the states, and the entire country”, said Union Minister for New and Renewable Energy, Education and Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, Shri Pralhad Joshi at a fireside chat during the 3rd day of a Bharat Renewable Energy Summit & Expo 2026 here today.

Union Minister Shri Joshi highlighted that India is now completing approximately one lakh rooftop solar installations every six days because of the rooftop solar initiative. He noted that this is not only reducing emissions but also strengthening India's energy security during peak hours. Emphasising the tangible benefits, he stated that millions of households are achieving zero electricity bills and generating substantial collective income by selling surplus power back to the grid. He further highlighted India's exponential growth in solar energy, with installed capacity increasing from a mere 3 GW in 2014 to 172 GW today.

The Next Terawatt Diplomatic Dialogue, addressed by Minister of State for New and Renewable Energy Shri Shripad Yesso Naik, underscored that the next terawatt of clean energy will require collective collaboration across countries, technologies and institutions. The minister also sought the views of the diplomats on country partnerships, investment, technology, implementation and capacity building.

A parallel CEO Caucus convened by the International Solar Alliance, CEEW and Energiva Ventures mapped the international clean energy implementation architecture for the decades ahead, with the ISA High-Level Assembly and a SIDS Ministerial Roundtable adding further diplomatic weight. Country sessions with Norway, Japan, Australia, the United Kingdom and France deepened bilateral ties across hydrogen, offshore wind and financing, while Karnataka, Delhi, Uttarakhand, Bihar, Gujarat and Chhattisgarh each presented their renewable energy investment pipelines to a global audience.

The 4th International Conference on Green Hydrogen, held alongside BRE Summit and Expo 2026, highlighted progress under the National Green Hydrogen Mission, which targets 5 million tonnes of annual green hydrogen production capacity by 2030. Sessions across the day examined electrolyser manufacturing, hydrogen in mobility, fuel cell technologies and sustainable aviation fuels, reinforcing India’s hydrogen economy as a key pillar of the broader energy transition.

Industry leaders, researchers, manufacturers and knowledge partners are using the platform to explore technology collaborations, research partnerships and opportunities to strengthen domestic supply chains.

The Wind Plenary examined India’s onshore and offshore wind trajectory, a battery storage plenary focused on building domestic giga-scale manufacturing capacity and the RE for AI plenary explored how machine intelligence can strengthen grid forecasting and energy security. A dedicated policy session on women in renewable energy asked how India can better mobilise resources, commitment and intent to improve gender participation across the sector.

The RTSE Vendor Buddy tool, developed by C-STEP with support from Bloomberg Philanthropies and in association with the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy, was also launched today. The platform helps rooftop solar vendors assess roof layouts, design 3D solar systems, and generate technical drawings and bills of materials in a single workflow.

India’s solar manufacturing sector has expanded significantly, with module manufacturing capacity crossing 200 GW and solar cell manufacturing reaching approximately 45 GW. The country is also advancing wind energy manufacturing, with domestic capabilities now covering a significant share of the turbine value chain. BRE Summit and Expo 2026 is providing a platform for manufacturers, technology companies, investors and policymakers to explore pathways for deeper domestic and international collaboration across the clean energy manufacturing ecosystem.

As renewable energy capacity expands, energy storage and transmission infrastructure are becoming central to grid stability and the reliable integration of variable renewable power. The Summit is bringing together technology providers, developers and industry stakeholders to advance discussions on battery energy storage systems, pumped storage and grid modernisation, with India’s efforts in both areas creating growing opportunities for investment and technology partnerships.
