2332630.title: Ministry of Minority Affairs Organises ‘Samavesh Se VIKAS’ to Review PM VIKAS Implementation and Strengthen Stakeholder Engagement
2332630.body_html:
Ministry of Minority Affairs
Ministry of Minority Affairs Organises ‘Samavesh Se VIKAS’ to Review PM VIKAS Implementation and Strengthen Stakeholder Engagement
MoUs with four institutions to expand industry-oriented training and traditional skill development opportunities for youth from minority communities
Posted On: 04 NOV 2026 5:28PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Minority Affairs organised “Samavesh Se VIKAS – Implementation Review and Stakeholder Dialogue” on 4 November 2026 at Samrasta Hall, Dr. Ambedkar International Centre, New Delhi. The event brought together over 80 participants, in the presence of Shri Shyama Prasad Roy, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Minority Affairs, and Ms. Neha Giri, Director, Ministry of Minority Affairs. Representatives of Project Implementing Agencies (PIAs) and other stakeholders participated in discussions focused on reviewing the progress of Pradhan Mantri Virasat Ka Samvardhan (PM VIKAS), addressing implementation-related challenges and identifying measures to strengthen training quality, placements and overall outcomes under the scheme.

 

Addressing the gathering, Shri Shyama Prasad Roy, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Minority Affairs, emphasised the importance of ensuring that skill development translates into meaningful employment opportunities and a better future for beneficiaries.

 

 

“The theme is 'Samavesh Se VIKAS', and it is not a mere slogan. Our expectation is that every beneficiary, whether a girl, a school dropout or any trainee, completes skilling with a certificate in hand, gets a job and moves towards a brighter future. That is the plan,” he said.

The event also marked the signing of Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) under PM VIKAS with Pithampur Auto Cluster (PAC), the Centre of Excellence in Maritime & Shipbuilding (CEMS), and the Institute of Entrepreneurship Development (IED). These partnerships aim to expand access to skill development and industry-oriented training for youth from minority communities across different sectors and regions.

 

 

The partnership with PAC will facilitate skill training for 2,400 candidates in Madhya Pradesh in job roles aligned with emerging industry requirements, including Electric Vehicle Service Technician, CNC Milling Programmer, Warehouse Associate and Supply Chain Executive (Sustainability).

The MoU with CEMS will facilitate skill training for 6,300 candidates across Karnataka, Puducherry, Maharashtra, Telangana, West Bengal, Odisha and Gujarat. The training will cover several job roles, including Business Analyst, Warehouse Supervisor, AI Technocrat and Guest Service Executive (Front Office), among others.

 

Under the partnership with IED, 900 candidates in Uttar Pradesh will receive skill training in the Solar PV Installer (Suryamitra) job role. The initiative aims to equip young people with industry-relevant skills and prepare them for emerging employment opportunities in the renewable energy sector, contributing to the development of a skilled workforce for India's growing green energy ecosystem.

In another development under PM VIKAS, the Ministry of Minority Affairs signed an MoU with the Central University of Kashmir on 3 November 2026 for the implementation of training under the Traditional Skill component of the scheme. Under this initiative, 120 candidates will receive training as willow craft artisans in Ganderbal district, Jammu & Kashmir, through a 390-hour training programme. The initiative aims to preserve traditional craftsmanship while helping participants develop skills that can support sustainable livelihood opportunities.

 

 

During the event, Ms. Neha Giri, Director, Ministry of Minority Affairs, made a presentation on the progress of PM VIKAS, highlighting its implementation status, key areas requiring attention and priorities for the way forward. She stressed the need for PIAs to give greater attention to employment outcomes and maintain closer engagement with employers.

“We expect all our PIAs to place a much sharper focus on placement outcomes, employer engagement and timely reporting of verified placement data,” she said.

 

 

A key session of the event was the PIA-wise implementation review, during which progress under PM VIKAS was examined alongside issues and challenges faced by implementing agencies. The review provided a platform for detailed discussions on implementation-related concerns, identifying areas requiring attention and exploring practical measures to strengthen coordination, training delivery, placement outcomes and monitoring mechanisms. The discussions also focused on improving accountability and ensuring that training programmes lead to meaningful employment opportunities for beneficiaries.

The event further included discussions on strengthening quality assurance through independent monitoring by the Quality Council of India (QCI) and Indian Institute of Management Bangalore (IIM Bangalore). Technology-driven solutions were also discussed, including BlueDot for improving placement outcomes and Voice AI for collecting candidate feedback, as presented by EkStep Foundation. The discussions also covered the role of the National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC) in the skill development ecosystem, with emphasis on strengthening industry linkages and employment opportunities.

A presentation by ITIHAAS – Indian Traditions and Heritage Society on “Upskilling for Youth in Heritage and Tourism” highlighted opportunities for developing skills among young people in the heritage and tourism sectors. The presentation focused on connecting skill development with India's cultural heritage and creating livelihood opportunities through tourism-related activities.

The event concluded with an interactive dialogue involving Ministry officials, stakeholders and PIAs, providing an opportunity to share field-level experiences, discuss implementation concerns and challenges, and offer recommendations for strengthening the delivery and effectiveness of PM VIKAS.

The Ministry of Minority Affairs remains committed to improving access to quality skill development, strengthening industry linkages and creating sustainable livelihood opportunities for youth from minority communities through PM VIKAS.

2332613.title: Novel silicon chip allowing terahertz waves to pass through barriers could enable future 6G networks
2332613.body_html:
Ministry of Science & Technology
Novel silicon chip allowing terahertz waves to pass through barriers could enable future 6G networks
Posted On: 04 NOV 2026 5:22PM by PIB Delhi

A new silicon chip that allows terahertz waves to pass through an engineered barrier with little loss, while carrying data at 100 Gbit/s, points to compact terahertz circuits for future 6G communication technologies.

Future sixth-generation (6G) wireless networks are expected to use terahertz frequencies, which lie between microwaves and infrared light and offer wide bandwidth. Guiding these waves through compact circuits is challenging, as bends, junctions and abrupt changes in a waveguide can scatter or reflect part of the signal, weakening it as it travels.

By arranging triangular holes in a carefully designed pattern in a silicon slab, researchers can create a photonic crystal that guides terahertz waves along the boundary between two regions. Such boundary channels resist certain kinds of backscattering, but a practical circuit must also tolerate deliberately introduced obstacles and changes in geometry.

Researchers at the Jawaharlal Nehru Centre for Advanced Scientific Research (JNCASR), an autonomous institute of the Department of Science and Technology (DST), approached this challenge through topological photonics and demonstrated data transmission at up to 100 gigabits per second (Gbit/s) across an engineered barrier. A single barrier added only about 1–2% loss, and two barriers in sequence about 2–3%. In a conventional, non-topological waveguide, a comparable barrier markedly reduces transmission.

The team designed a silicon photonic crystal whose structure mimics the honeycomb lattice of graphene, and created a barrier by changing the sizes of the triangular holes over a short section of the waveguide.

Transmission remained close to its barrier-free level as long as the barrier strength stayed below a characteristic coupling strength of the crystal. Because the barrier is set by hole geometry, this offers a practical design rule for such devices.

The researchers tested the concept in three devices fabricated on high-resistivity silicon, a material compatible with established semiconductor manufacturing: one with two barriers in sequence, one with an omega-shaped route containing four sharp bends and a central barrier, and a power splitter with a barrier in one of its two branches.

Measurements across 310–360 GHz agreed closely with simulations. In the splitter, the two output signals were nearly identical, showing that the barrier had little effect on transmission.

Figure 1. Artistic illustration of photonic Klein tunnelling in a silicon valley photonic crystal chip. A terahertz signal carrying high-speed data crosses the engineered barrier (blue) without significant loss, supporting 100 Gbit/s data transmission for 6G communication.

 

In high-speed data tests, the double-barrier and omega-shaped devices carried 48 and 60 Gbit/s, respectively. The splitter supported 100 Gbit/s using QAM-32 modulation, which encodes information in the signal’s amplitude and phase. At this rate, a 5-gigabyte high-definition film could in principle be transferred in under half a second.

Figure 2. The research team in the Meta Optics Laboratory (MetoLab), JNCASR, with the fabricated silicon chip used to demonstrate photonic Klein tunnelling.

 

The study was led by Dr Abhishek Kumar, Assistant Professor at JNCASR, where he heads the Meta Optics Laboratory (MetoLab), with Samina Mulla and Sangram Kumar Sadhu of JNCASR as joint first authors. Collaborators included Asif Iqbal M and N. S. Vidhyadhiraja (JNCASR); Siddhartha Lal (IISER Kolkata); Anshuman Kumar (IIT Bombay); Zhonghua Gu and Prakash Pitchappa (Institute of Microelectronics, A*STAR, Singapore, and Pascal Szriftgiser and Guillaume Ducournau (University of Lille and CNRS, France).

“Showing that terahertz waves can cross a barrier created simply by changing the hole geometry, while carrying 100 gigabits per second, suggests that this effect can become a useful design tool for terahertz chips,” said Dr Abhishek Kumar.

The results could help researchers develop terahertz circuits that route and split signals on a single chip with low loss. The team next plans to tune the barriers electrically, thermally or mechanically, which could allow a device to redirect signals between paths on demand. The work has been published in the journal Advanced Materials.

Publication Link: DOI: https://doi.org/10.1002/adma.75322

2332607.title: Advanced protective coatings to improve machining of critical superalloys can help aerospace, energy & petrochemical sectors
2332607.body_html:
Ministry of Science & Technology
Advanced protective coatings to improve machining of critical superalloys can help aerospace, energy & petrochemical sectors
Posted On: 04 NOV 2026 5:21PM by PIB Delhi

An advanced surface-engineering approach developed by scientists can help improve the durability of cutting tools used for machining super alloys.

This could help aerospace, energy and petrochemical sectors, where nickel-based superalloys are indispensable for components operating under extreme conditions.

Machining of super alloys for use in aircraft engines, power plants and petrochemical systems is a major manufacturing challenge. Nickel-based superalloys such as Inconel 718 (IN718), IN625 and IN617 possess exceptional strength and hardness which make them difficult to cut or shape. Rapid work hardening, poor thermal conductivity and strong chemical interaction with cutting tools accelerate tool wear, reduce productivity and increase manufacturing costs.

Scientists from the International Advanced Research Centre for Powder Metallurgy and New Materials (ARCI), Hyderabad, an autonomous R&D Centre of the Department of Science and Technology (DST) have developed and evaluated two nanocomposite protective coatings—Titanium Aluminium Silicon Nitride (TiAlSiN) and Chromium Aluminium Silicon Nitride (CrAlSiN)—on widely used tungsten carbide cutting tools.

The coatings were deposited in-house using cathodic-arc physical vapour deposition and this helped evaluate the performance of tools for milling of IN718, IN625 and IN617. The study examined both tool life and the mechanisms governing coating performance.

The research revealed an important finding: there is no single coating that performs best for every superalloy. The effectiveness of a protective coating depends significantly on the chemistry of the material being machined and its interaction with the coating.

For IN718, the TiAlSiN-coated tool improved tool life by about 80% compared with an uncoated tool, while for IN625, the improvement was about 60%. For IN617, however, CrAlSiN proved remarkably superior, increasing tool life by more than 200%. The results demonstrate that one coating may be better suited to IN718 and IN625, while another can perform substantially better for IN617. The findings provide a scientific basis for selecting coatings according to the specific alloy being machined.

Fig 1: Advanced nanocomposite coatings significantly improve the life of tungsten carbide cutting tools. The results show that the optimum coating depends on the specific nickel-based superalloy being machined.

 

The researchers also investigated how cutting tools failed. A major cause of damage was repeated adhesion of workpiece material to the tool surface. During machining, a layer of the superalloy can stick to the cutting edge and, when it subsequently breaks away, it pulls tiny fragments from the tool, progressively causing chipping. The coatings helped delay this damage and extend tool life. Chipping and progressive wear were identified as the major failure modes, with abrasion, adhesion and attrition contributing to the overall wear process.

Fig2: A Scanning Electron Microscope image of a cutting-tool edge showing workpiece adhesion, abrasion, chipping and lateral cracks—key mechanisms responsible for tool failure during machining of nickel-based superalloys.

 

The researchers also examined the metal chips generated during machining. The chips exhibited characteristic shear bands and serrated or saw-tooth patterns, reflecting the intense thermo-mechanical conditions during cutting. The degree of chip segmentation was related to tool performance, providing further insight into the complex machining behaviour of these advanced alloys.

Longer-lasting cutting tools can reduce downtime, improve productivity and lower the cost of machining high-value engineering components.

More significantly, the study points towards a science-based, application-specific approach to protective coatings. Rather than seeking a universally superior coating, manufacturers can select or design coatings based on the composition and behaviour of the particular alloy being machined. This can contribute to more efficient, reliable and cost-effective manufacturing of components made from advanced materials.

The research carried out at ARCI's Centre for Engineered Coatings, has been published in the journal Materials Today Communications.

The study demonstrates that the key to improving the machining of some of industry's most demanding materials lies not merely in developing a better coating, but in matching the right coating to the right material.

Link to Publication:

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.mtcomm.2024.109101

2332614.title: Ministry of Coal Achieves 130% Target in Site Cleaning and 162% in Scrap Disposal Under Special Campaign 6
2332614.body_html:
Ministry of Coal
Ministry of Coal Achieves 130% Target in Site Cleaning and 162% in Scrap Disposal Under Special Campaign 6
Scrap Disposal Generates ₹61.41 Crore, with 100% Disposal of Public Grievances and PMO References
CPSEs Promote Innovative Waste-to-Wealth Initiatives for Sustainable Resource Management
Posted On: 04 NOV 2026 5:20PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Coal and its CPSEs demonstrated extraordinary over-achievement across all key parameters during Special Campaign 6, establishing exemplary benchmarks in institutional clean-up and administrative reform.

The Ministry cleaned 2,035 sites against a target of 1,565 (130% achievement) and cleared over 14.84 million sq. ft. of area against the planned 10.18 million sq. ft. (146% achievement). Alongside these physical accomplishments, the Ministry recorded perfect 100% disposal rates in successfully resolving 253 out of 253 Public Grievances and clearing 52 out of 52 PMO references.

Overall scrap disposal reached 17,686 metric tons against a target of 10,909 metric tons (162% achievement), yielding a total revenue of ₹61.41 crore. Furthermore, the Ministry made monumental strides in streamlining file operations by reviewing 1,79,793 physical and E-files against a target of 59,593 and total files weeding out and closed are 1,70,336. These operational successes were amplified by social media outreach that featured 16,424 tweets and 38 PIB releases issued.

Prominent best practices executed during the campaign include:

  1. NLC India Limited (NLCIL) developed a Waste-to-Wealth Children's Eco Park at Mine-I, Neyveli, inaugurated on 22 October 2026. The park showcases sustainable resource utilisation through the reuse of 2.5 MT of iron scrap, 3,000 solid blocks and salvaged timber, including wood recovered from trees felled during Cyclone Thane.

 

  1. Eastern Coalfields Limited (ECL), has transformed a large room previously used for storing junk and discarded materials into a beautiful, fully equipped crèche facility at its headquarters here in Sanctoria, demonstrating how effective space utilisation can contribute to employee welfare and workplace improvement.

Before

After

 

  1. Scrap oil drums in the Krishnashila Area, Northern Coalfields Limited (NCL) were creatively upcycled and repurposed to construct an aesthetic welcome sign board for “Krishnakunj”. By repainting the discarded drums in vibrant colors and mounting lettering on them, waster material was effectively transformed into an attractive entrance installation.

 

  1. Some notable work from South Eastern Coalfields Limited (SECL) includes:

Singhali Underground Mine in the Korba Area, workers constructed a working model of the Paste-Fill Mining System from scrap materials to demonstrate how fly ash and industrial waste can backfill mined voids to enhance structural stability and prevent land subsidence.

At the Kusmunda Area, employees built a replica of Tiger Hill featuring soldier figures and the National Flag to honor the sacrifices of the Indian Armed Forces during Operation Vijay in the 1999 Kargil War.

Bhatgaon Area introduced a ‘Kabaad Se Jugaad’ installation centered around a miner figure to advocate waste reduction, recycling, and sustainable lifestyle practices.

 

  1. The Mandamarri Area, SCCL creatively transformed waste scrap materials into two distinct artworks: a Shiv Ling idol adorned with sacred symbols and traditional elements, and a separate Trishul artwork. The initiative promotes the Waste to Wealth concept through innovative scrap reuse while reducing scrap accumulation on the premises.

 

Through these comprehensive clean-up operations, innovative waste-to-wealth initiatives, and robust administrative reforms, the Ministry of Coal has set a high standard for public sector efficiency and sustainability. By combining record-breaking physical achievements with creative employee-welfare and environmental practices, the Ministry continues to demonstrate its steadfast commitment to governance excellence, resource optimization, and the broader goals of Swachh Bharat.

2332576.title: NITI Aayog and GIZ India Sign Implementation Agreement under Nationally Determined Contribution-Transport Initiative for Asia Phase II (NDC-TIA II) to Accelerate Road Freight Decarbonisation
2332576.body_html:
NITI Aayog
NITI Aayog and GIZ India Sign Implementation Agreement under Nationally Determined Contribution-Transport Initiative for Asia Phase II (NDC-TIA II) to Accelerate Road Freight Decarbonisation
Posted On: 04 NOV 2026 5:00PM by PIB Delhi

NITI Aayog and the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH signed an Implementation Agreement under the Nationally Determined Contribution–Transport Initiative for Asia Phase II (NDC-TIA II) on 3rd November 2026. NDC-TIA II is a regional initiative supported by the German Government's International Climate Initiative (IKI). World Resources Institute (WRI) India, International Council on Clean Transportation (ICCT) India and Agora Energiewende are among the initiative's implementing partners.

Decarbonising road freight is an important component of India's transition towards a sustainable, energy-efficient and low-carbon transport system. However, the electrification of medium- and heavy-duty freight vehicles remains at an early stage, highlighting the need for adequate charging infrastructure, innovative financing mechanisms and an enabling regulatory framework. The Agreement formalises the collaboration between the project partners for accelerating the decarbonisation of India's road freight sector. The initiative will contribute to India's broader efforts to achieve its Nationally Determined Contribution targets and long-term climate goals.

2332572.title: Shram Samvad: Indore & Dhar Region Level Capacity-Building and Awareness Programme on Labour Codes
2332572.body_html:
Ministry of Labour & Employment
Shram Samvad: Indore & Dhar Region Level Capacity-Building and Awareness Programme on Labour Codes
Posted On: 04 NOV 2026 4:54PM by PIB Delhi

A District Level Capacity-Building and Awareness Programme, “Shram Samvad”, on Labour Codes, Labour Welfare and Social Protection, was jointly organized by Ministry of Labour & Employment (MoLE), Government of India (GoI) and Labour Department, Government of Madhya Pradesh in collaboration with Association of Industries Madhya Pradesh and Pithampur Audhyogik Sangathan at Indore, Madhya Pradesh on 3rd November, 2026.

The programme aimed at enhancing awareness among employers, HR, Legal and Finance professionals regarding the Labour Codes and rules made thereunder. It also focused on strengthening awareness and institutional capacity on labour reforms, welfare and social protection, promoting Centre-State coordination and stakeholder engagement. Sushri Sheetala Patle, IAS, Labour Commissioner, Madhya Pradesh presided over the programme and participants included senior officials from MoLE, Labour Department, GoMP, Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) , Employees' State Insurance Corporation (ESIC), Chief Labour Commissioner (Central) [CLC(C)], Directorate General Labour Welfare (DGLW) along with more than 150 participants from employers, industry representatives, legal, HR and finance professionals

The programme featured a series of technical sessions designed to provide participants with practical insights into the Labour Codes, employer obligations, and key social security initiatives of the GoI.

Shri S.R. Datta, Director, MoLE presented the keynote address highlighting the key features of the Labour Codes. Various sessions were conducted by officials from MoLE, focusing on the key compliance requirements for employers under each of the four Labour Codes and Central Rules notified under the Labour Codes. The sessions provided practical guidance on statutory obligations and compliance responsibilities, enabling participants to better understand the operational aspects of the new labour codes. 

Representatives from EPFO and DGLW also led sessions on Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana (PMVBRY) and Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maandhan (PM-SYM) Scheme, respectively.

To facilitate the employers and compliance professionals in effective implementation of the Labour Codes and Rules, ‘Handbook of Compliance for Employers’ and ‘Compilation of Frequently Asked Questions’ developed by MoLE were also shared with the participants.

An engaging Question and Answer session was also held, enabling participants to address their queries and gain greater clarity on the Labour Codes, compliance requirements, and social security provisions. By bringing together Central Government and State Government authorities and industry representatives, the event contributed to enhanced awareness, improved understanding, and stronger stakeholder engagement, thereby supporting the effective adoption and implementation of the New Labour Codes.

2332557.title: A Rulebook Alone Cannot Guarantee Dignity; Every Hand in Aviation Must Ensure It: Manmeet Kaur Nanda
2332557.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
A Rulebook Alone Cannot Guarantee Dignity; Every Hand in Aviation Must Ensure It: Manmeet Kaur Nanda
Posted On: 04 NOV 2026 4:44PM by PIB Delhi

“Merely framing rules, enforcing them or having a handbook will make no difference unless the last person dealing with a passenger with a disability understands and implements what is written in it.” Emphasizing the need to translate accessibility commitments into ground-level action, Ms. Manmeet Kaur Nanda, Additional Secretary, Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (DEPwD), called for making continuous sensitization and training an integral part of India's aviation ecosystem to ensure safe, dignified and independent air travel for persons with disabilities.

Highlighting the human cost of inaccessible air travel, Ms. Nanda recounted the experience of a para-athlete who had to travel to Egypt and compete in an international sporting event using a broken wheelchair after her original wheelchair was damaged by an airline. Despite this ordeal, the athlete went on to win a medal. Describing such experiences as barriers that the entire aviation ecosystem must collectively eliminate, she stressed that airlines, airport operators, ground-handling personnel, security agencies, customs and immigration officials must undergo regular induction and refresher training. She underlined that the Handbook's coverage of all 21 specified disabilities, including invisible disabilities, would help build greater sensitivity and preparedness among frontline personnel. Calling for measurable accountability, she advocated accessibility performance indicators, time-bound grievance redressal mechanisms and dedicated dashboards to monitor the performance of airlines and airports. Reiterating the principle of “Nothing About Us Without Us”, she emphasized the active involvement of persons with disabilities as trainers and partners in shaping and evaluating aviation services.

Ms. Stuti Kacker, Former Secretary, DEPwD and Advisor, Asia-Pacific Network for Accessibility (APNA), highlighted the significant contribution of civil society organizations, disability rights activists, the media and the judiciary in advancing India's accessibility movement. Acknowledging the pioneering efforts of disability rights advocates, she observed that accessibility is a fundamental right, not an act of charity. She emphasized that Universal Design, inclusive mobility and sustained collaboration are essential to ensuring dignity, independence and equal opportunities.

Shri S. Govindraj, Commissioner, Office of the Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities, highlighted the need to extend priority assistance to passengers with disabilities during deplaning, just as it is provided during boarding, to ensure a seamless and dignified travel experience. Mr. Prateek Sen of IndiGo emphasized that accessible physical infrastructure must be complemented by adequately trained personnel equipped with the right knowledge, attitude and soft skills. Reiterating the airline's philosophy of “Customers are the Core”, he stressed the importance of comprehensive sensitization and training across aviation services.

The “Sensitization and Training Handbook: Further Advancing the Accessibility of India’s Aviation Services” was officially launched on 4 November 2026 at the India International Centre, New Delhi. Developed by Samarthyam Centre for Universal Accessibility under the aegis of the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (DEPwD), Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, in collaboration with the Ministry of Civil Aviation, the Handbook aims to strengthen institutional capacity and promote an inclusive, safe and passenger-friendly aviation ecosystem.

The Handbook provides practical guidance to airline personnel, airport operators, security staff and other aviation stakeholders on the rights and requirements of persons with 21 specified disabilities under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016, relevant Civil Aviation Requirements (CAR), end-to-end passenger assistance, safety protocols, accessible communication and identification of barriers throughout the air travel journey. The launch was accompanied by a panel discussion featuring representatives from the Ministry of Civil Aviation, Airports Authority of India, Indian Aviation Academy, Office of the Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities and IndiGo Airlines. Passengers with diverse disabilities also shared their lived experiences and perspectives, bringing the voice of the traveler to the center of the deliberations.

In her welcome address, Dr. Anjlee Agarwal, Founder Trustee, Samarthyam Centre for Universal Accessibility and Co-founder, Asia-Pacific Network for Accessibility (APNA), highlighted the pivotal role played by civil society in shaping India's journey towards accessibility and disability inclusion. She emphasized the importance of translating advocacy into institutional action through awareness, capacity building and sustained stakeholder engagement. Samarthyam, a not-for-profit organization working for the past 36 years to advance universal accessibility, inclusive mobility and disability rights through advocacy, capacity building and accessibility audits, has been instrumental in advancing this agenda. The initiative marks an important step towards transforming accessibility commitments into everyday practices, ensuring that every passenger can travel with confidence, dignity, independence and equal opportunity.

2332535.title: From Substance Dependence to a Healthier and More Stable Life
2332535.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Substance Dependence to a Healthier and More Stable Life
Tengana’s Suresh Kumar’s Journey Towards Recovery and Rehabilitation
Posted On: 04 NOV 2026 4:24PM by PIB Delhi

For 30 year Suresh Kumar (name changed), the support provided under the NAPDDR Scheme has marked an important step towards recovery, economic stability and a renewed sense of purpose.

His journey highlights the importance of timely intervention, sustained counselling, family participation and structured rehabilitation in helping individuals overcome substance dependence and rebuild their lives with dignity and confidence.

Mr Suresh Kumar, a resident of Karimnagar district in Telangana, faced significant personal, social and financial challenges due to prolonged alcohol and tobacco consumption. His journey towards substance dependence began during his late teenage years, largely influenced by peer pressure and emotional stress. Over time, his dependence intensified, adversely affecting his physical and mental health, family relationships and professional life.

The decline in his confidence, reduced motivation, irregular work attendance and financial instability further complicated his situation. His relationships with family members became strained, and he gradually withdrew from social interactions. Despite these difficulties, his family continued to support him and remained committed to helping him overcome his dependence.

A significant turning point came on 12 November 2025, when he received support at the Integrated Rehabilitation Centre for Addicts (IRCA), operated by Prakriti Environment Society in Karimnagar, Telangana, under the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR) Scheme of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.

Through the intervention, he received comprehensive assistance, including individual counselling, group therapy, family counselling, motivational interviewing and relapse prevention therapy. Medical supervision and emotional support helped him address the challenges associated with substance dependence. Vocational guidance and rehabilitation services further supported his efforts to rebuild his confidence and reintegrate into family and social life.

With continued counselling, family involvement and structured rehabilitation, Mr. Kumar gradually regained control over his life. The intervention helped him develop healthier coping mechanisms, strengthen family relationships and work towards sustained recovery. The combined support of professional counselling and family participation played an important role in his progress towards a healthier lifestyle.

Today, Mr. Kumar is maintaining sobriety and leading a healthier and more stable life. He has resumed regular employment, actively participates in family and social activities, and has regained his confidence and motivation. His improved employment stability has also strengthened his financial position. From a phase of irregular earnings and financial difficulties, he is now earning approximately ₹15,000 per month.

2332534.title: The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) Launches Network Anubhav Platform
2332534.body_html:
Ministry of Communications
The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) Launches Network Anubhav Platform
Posted On: 04 NOV 2026 4:21PM by PIB Delhi

The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) today launched the Network Anubhav Platform – A geospatial and analytical dashboard for user test data and TRAI independent drive test data and to provide DND web interface. User test data comprises of the test results from MySpeed and MyCall apps of TRAI. The platform delivers insights on various network parameters to consumers, service providers and TRAI.

Key Features of the Geo-Spatial Maps

Geo-Spatial maps allow consumers to:-

  • View test results categorised as Cellular or Fixed broadband, further segregated service provider-wise and technology-wise, based on parameters, including download and upload speeds.
  • Navigate and zoom the map to examine the location and distribution of consumer-generated test observations.
  • Use filters, legends, supporting tables and downloadable reports to interpret the displayed results.

The platform reports percentile values calculated from tests conducted by users in a given area:

  • P50 (median speed): Half of the tests recorded a speed at or above this value.
  • P80 (for Mobile Broadband): 80% of the tests recorded a speed at or above this value.
  • P90 (for Fixed Broadband): 90% of the tests recorded a speed at or above this value.

Though these values based on user tests do not represent comprehensive assessment of network quality based on standard methodology, they provide valuable information to users regarding experience of other users at various locations. The maps also facilitate a geospatial appreciation of independent drive tests for various locations. Together, these data sets and their geospatial visualization provide valuable information to users about experience of other users and results of Independent Drive Tests.

Empowerment of Consumers

Consumers can report spam and test internet speeds. Aggregated results from TRAI Apps, web interface, and Independent Drive Tests are available on the Network Anubhav dashboard. Consumers can view location-specific results of tests conducted by other users.

Insights for TSPs and TRAI

Through a secure interface, Telecom service providers can view data of call quality, coverage and internet tests conducted by consumers. Along with location, date, time, and values of technical parameters, TSPs can identify geographic locations for further analysis and can use it for network improvement.

TRAI can use the aggregated insights for evidence-based monitoring of consumer experience and use this data for improvement in network performance.

MySpeed SDK

TRAI's MySpeed SDK enables eligible third-party apps to integrate connectivity-measurement capabilities. Wider integration can expand participation and the volume of real-world measurements contributing to the platform.

DND Services

With Anubhav portal access to the DND is now available through web interface. Consumers can use the available DND facilities to exercise preference for commercial communication, submit complaints relating to unsolicited commercial communication, track complaint status and view consolidated and service-provider-wise complaint information.

Speaking on the occasion, Shri Anil Kumar Lahoti, Chairman, TRAI, said:

“The Network Anubhav Platform brings greater transparency to observed network tests conducted by Consumers and TRAI. It empowers consumers to analyse location and service provider specific tests, enables TSPs to identify areas for network optimisation and strengthens TRAI’s efforts for network improvement.”

Consumers are encouraged to contribute regularly through the TRAI MySpeed and MyCall apps. Wider participation will improve the coverage and utility of the platform’s information.

Access the Platform

Network Anubhav portal: https://anubhav.trai.gov.in

For additional queries, please contact: Ms. Archna Ahlawat, Advisor (IT), at advisorit@trai.gov.in.

2332530.title: Resolution adopted at the Conference of Chairpersons of Public Accounts Committees of Parliament of India and State/UT Legislatures
2332530.body_html:
Lok Sabha Secretariat
Resolution adopted at the Conference of Chairpersons of Public Accounts Committees of Parliament of India and State/UT Legislatures
Thiruvananthapuram, Keralam 3-4 November, 2026
Posted On: 04 NOV 2026 4:20PM by PIB Delhi

Taking into account the deliberations held in the plenary session of the conference on Audit, accountability and good governance- The evolving role of public accounts committee, we hereby resolve

  • To uphold rigorous examination standards to assess that public funds disbursed are legally available for the exact service or purpose to which they have been charged thereby safeguarding the public exchequer;

· to establish robust mechanism for continuous peer learning, exchange of best practices and sharing of procedural innovations between Public Accounts Committees of Parliament and State/UTs by creating a digital portal;

· to formulate an action plan for prescribing standardised timelines for submission of Action Taken Notes on audit paras as well as Public Accounts Committees’ recommendations in all States/UTs;

· to ensure development of a digital oversight system such as the Audit Para Monitoring System (APMS)in all State/UT PACs;

· enhance the institutional capacity of PAC Secretariats by conducting regular trainings/ orientations by specialised training institutes and equip members with analytical tools for examining complex technical and financial issues;

· to consider holding a minimum of three sittings each month and constituting Sub-Committees in State/UT Legislatures PACs to examine and clear pending audit observations;

· to strengthen collaboration with the O/o C&AG to leverage advanced forensic tools and identify high-risk areas of governance requiring immediate legislative oversight; and,

· to utilise digital solutions effectively while maintaining integrity and sanctity of the due process of the legislature.

Adopted by the Chairpersons and Members of the Public Accounts Committees of Parliament and State UT Legislatures on this 4th day of November, 2026, atThiruvananthapuram, Kerala.

2332524.title: Cabinet creates a pathway for all Agniveers to be absorbed in Defence Forces
2332524.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
Cabinet creates a pathway for all Agniveers to be absorbed in Defence Forces
Performance assessment by the Defence Forces over last four years of the Agniveers yields positive feedback
Based on merit, 25% of Agniveers to be offered regular employment in the Defence Forces as envisaged earlier
Remaining Agniveers to be offered another engagement period of two years based on their willingness
Post completion of this two-year engagement period, all Agniveers to be enrolled as regular soldiers subject to their willingness and meeting selection criteria
Posted On: 04 NOV 2026 4:14PM by PIB Delhi

An objective assessment in terms of organisational requirements and operational efficiency has brought out the outstanding performance of Agniveers in terms of skills, motivation levels, physical fitness and technological prowess. As envisaged earlier, based on merit, 25% of Agniveers will be offered regular employment in the Defence Forces.

Further, for the remaining 75% Agniveers, on the recommendations of the Indian Defence Forces, another engagement period of 2 years has been approved by the Cabinet. After completion of this two-year engagement period, all Agniveers will be offered enrollment as regular soldiers subject to their willingness and their meeting selection criteria.

The introduction of another engagement period of two years for the willing 75% Agniveers has been done after deliberate, reasoned and elaborate evaluation and feedback with the fundamental aim of aligning the aspirations of Agniveers and organisational efficiency.

Achievements of Agnipath Scheme

After four years of implementation of the Agnipath Scheme, detailed feedback about its efficacy and the performance of Agniveers was obtained. Some of the salient achievements of the scheme include:

  • Increased footprint of recruitment of Agniveers across districts of the country
  • More standardised and transparent recruitment process
  • Very high level of physical fitness, morale, motivation, competitive spirit and discipline
  • Enhancement of skills, technological adaptability and education in the service
  • Opening up of various branches of the Defence Forces for women

Based on these achievements, the Agnipath scheme shall continue. The second engagement period will have higher remuneration, enhanced Seva Nidhi package and seniority benefits.

With the introduction of another engagement period of two years followed by induction of all Agniveers as regular soldiers, the Cabinet has created a pathway for absorption of all Agniveers into Defence Forces.

2332315.title: IndiaAI Mission Released Indigenous Foundation Models EKA-1 by Soket and Dhīr 2B & Dhīr 5B by ZenteiQ Under the IndiaAI Innovation Centre Pillar
2332315.body_html:
Ministry of Electronics & IT
IndiaAI Mission Released Indigenous Foundation Models EKA-1 by Soket and Dhīr 2B & Dhīr 5B by ZenteiQ Under the IndiaAI Innovation Centre Pillar
EKA-1 by Soket Features 26.3 Billion Parameters Trained on Approximately 7.5 Trillion Tokens Across All 22 Scheduled Indian Languages and English for Math, Code, Reasoning & Agentic Use
ZenteiQ Introduces Open-Source Dhīr 2B and Dhīr 5B Multilingual Assistants Supporting English and 10 Indian Languages for Secure, On-Premise, Offline-Capable Deployment Across Critical Sectors
Posted On: 03 NOV 2026 10:02PM by PIB Delhi

The IndiaAI Mission, under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), today released the indigenous foundation models EKA-1 and Dhīr (Dhīr 2B & Dhīr 5B) developed by Soket Labs Technology and Research Private Limited and ZenteiQ AiTech Innovations respectively.

The release was unveiled today at a press event in New Delhi, in the presence of Shri S. Krishnan, Secretary, Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India, and senior officials of MeitY and IndiaAI, alongside the leadership teams of Soket and ZenteiQ. These indigenous models are a key milestone under the IndiaAI Mission, showcasing India's progress in creating home-grown AI technology.

Marking the occasion, Shri S. Krishnan, Secretary, Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), said, The development of such indigenous models strengthens India’s technological and strategic autonomy in Artificial Intelligence. It also opens up opportunities to improve productivity and efficiency across government, industry, research and education. These resources have supported the development of models such as EKA-1 and Dhīr, each addressing distinct and relevant use cases. Through platforms such as AIKosh, these models can be made accessible to researchers, students, innovators and the wider public, encouraging further experimentation and innovation.

Speaking on the advancement of indigenous AI capabilities, Shri Sudeep Shrivastava, COO, IndiaAI, said, "IndiaAI Mission's comprehensive support ecosystem is dedicated to making artificial intelligence more accessible and tailored to India's unique landscape. Breakthrough models like Dhīr and EKA-1 showcase the nation's multi-layered progress in AI ranging from lightweight solutions optimized for everyday devices to robust powerhouses engineered for complex enterprise applications."

Soket AI and ZenteiQ are among the teams selected under the IndiaAI Innovation Centre (Foundation Models) pillar of the IndiaAI Mission to build indigenous foundation AI capabilities and Large Language Models. Access to subsidized national AI compute infrastructure and support for ancillary research expenses under the mission enabled the development of these models, highlighting how public AI infrastructure can accelerate homegrown innovation.

EKA-1 by Soket: Open, Sparse Hybrid Language Model Across All 22 Scheduled Indian Languages

Soket Labs Technology and Research Private Limited has developed EKA-1, a powerful Foundation Model featuring 26.3 billion parameters and trained on approximately 7.5 trillion tokens.

EKA-1 demonstrates advanced capabilities, spanning all 22 scheduled Indian languages alongside English. Built as an open, sparse hybrid language model, EKA-1 is designed for math, code, reasoning, and agentic use.

Speaking at the release, Abhishek Upperwal, CEO, Soket Labs Technology and Research Private Limited, said,  “With the support of the IndiaAI Mission, we have developed an advanced AI model specifically tailored to India's unique banking, financial services and cybersecurity landscape. It is designed to address sector-specific requirements, understand India's evolving digital ecosystem, and deliver solutions aligned with the country's needs and priorities.”

Dhīr 2B & Dhīr 5B by ZenteiQ: Secure, On-Premise Multilingual Assistants for Critical Sectors

ZenteiQ AiTech Innovations has introduced the Dhīr 2B and Dhīr 5B open-source models. These models can be deployed as secure, on-premise, multilingual assistants supporting English and 10 Indian languages.

Dhīr 2B and Dhīr 5B enable offline-capable, document-grounded automation, knowledge retrieval, and citizen or enterprise services across defence, government, industrial, and educational sectors particularly in low-connectivity or sensitive environments.

Speaking at the release, Prof. Sashikumar, CEO, ZenteiQ AiTech Innovations, said, “Models like Dhīr 2B and Dhīr 5B offer the flexibility to run across different computing platforms, including GPUs and TPUs. Their lightweight architecture also enables on-device deployment on mobile phones, without dependence on cloud connectivity. This allows users to access AI capabilities locally while keeping data on their devices, enhancing privacy, security and accessibility.”

About the IndiaAI Mission

Based on the Hon'ble Prime Minister's vision to democratize the use of technology, India's AI strategy aims to address India-centric challenges, create economic and employment opportunities for all Indians, and position the nation as a global leader in artificial intelligence. Guided by the vision of “Making AI in India and Making AI Work for India”, the Union Cabinet approved the IndiaAI Mission on March 7, 2024. The mission operates across seven key pillars to establish a robust and inclusive AI ecosystem aligned with India's development goals: IndiaAI Compute Capacity, IndiaAI Innovation Centre, IndiaAI Datasets Platform (AIKosh), IndiaAI Application Development Initiative, IndiaAI FutureSkills, IndiaAI Startup Financing, and Safe & Trusted AI.

2332312.title: CSIR-NIScPR Successfully Concludes the International Conference on CDTK-2026, marking 25 years of the Indian Journal of Traditional Knowledge (IJTK)
2332312.body_html:
Ministry of Science & Technology
CSIR-NIScPR Successfully Concludes the International Conference on CDTK-2026, marking 25 years of the Indian Journal of Traditional Knowledge (IJTK)
CDTK Fosters Experiential Learning and Knowledge Exchange with Researchers and Traditional Knowledge holders
Distinguished Talk by Padma Shri awardee Seed Conservationist Smt. Rahibai Soma Popere
Posted On: 03 NOV 2026 9:57PM by PIB Delhi

The final day of the International Conference on Communication and Dissemination of Traditional Knowledge (CDTK) commenced with a dedicated scientific session entitled, “Challenges and Opportunities in Scholarly Communication in Traditional Knowledge: Celebrating 25 Years of Indian Journal of Traditional Knowledge (IJTK)”. The session opened with a commemorative video documenting the inception, advancements, and key milestones of the IJTK over its 25 years journey. Following the visual presentation, Dr Geetha Vani Rayasam, Director, CSIR-NIScPR, officially released the IJTK 25th anniversary issue.

Dignitaries releasing IJTK-25th anniversary issue

The first keynote address of the session (online) was delivered by Dr Ina Vandebroek, Professor of Ethnobotany, University of the West Indies, Mona. In her talk, she shared her expertise on working with local communities of the biodiversity hotspots of the Caribbean deep forests in Jamaica emphasising the necessity of becoming stronger community ally. Chairperson and Keynote speaker of the session Prof. Pulok Mukherjee, Jadavpur University, and Executive Editor, IJTK, emphasised translating traditional knowledge into global evidence through omics integration, highlighting Lok Swasthya Parampara and sustainable impact. Dr H. R. Nagendra, Chief Editor, IJTK, highlighted the journal’s evolution and scientific indexing milestones. Former Editors Dr N. R. Mankad, Dr T. K. Mukherjee and Dr K. P. Singh recalled IJTK’s inception, 25-year scholarly journey and editorial legacy. Dr Charu Verma, CSIR-NIScPR, emphasised digitization for global accessibility, while Dr R. N. Padaria, ICAR-IARI, stressed community ownership and participatory frameworks benefiting Traditional Knowledge holders.

The fifth scientific session, titled “Challenges and Opportunities in Popularising Traditional Knowledge,” was chaired by Shri P. A. Vivekananda Pai, Secretary General, Vijnana Bharati, Kerala. In his address, he highlighted India’s foundational contributions to Mathematics, specifically the Kerala School of Mathematics and Madhava’s work on calculus, alongside core scientific frameworks like Panchamahabhuta and Panchikarana. He insisted on overcoming colonial and anthropocentric mindsets, and scaling indigenous technologies to strengthen local economies and sustainability.

Dr Pramod Grover, Director, Science City, Kolkata, highlighted the role of National Council of Science Museum (NCSM) in science communication via interactive exhibits, and teacher training. He recommended establishing collaboration between NCSM and SVASTIK, establishing a traditional knowledge hub to extend scientific outreach to rural communities and elevate public understanding. Dr V. V. Binoy, Associate Professor, National Institute of Advanced Studies, Bengaluru addressed on contextual and participatory models of science communication, emphasising engagement with traditional knowledge holders. He recommended integrating indigenous epistemologies into science classrooms and exploring India’s historical scientific contributions within modern fields like AI.

The final scientific session of the conference, titled, “Sustainable Innovation and Development: Experiential Learning from Social Researchers and Traditional Knowledge Holders” was chaired by Dr Arvind C Ranade, Director, National Innovation Foundation, Gandhinagar. He in his address outlined three key pillars of sustainable innovation namely environmental sustainability, economic viability and fair benefit-sharing with traditional knowledge holders. Dr Gajanan Dange, Founder & President, YOJAK, highlighted how India’s traditional knowledge systems promote a holistic approach to biodiversity and breed conservation, sustainable agriculture, and the preservation of local ecological practices. Shri Krishna Nath, Indian Folk Herbalist, Jorhat, Assam, addressed about the rich legacy of traditional healing practices in Assam, drawing on generations of indigenous knowledge of medicinal plants and remedies.

Distinguished talk by Smt. Rahibai Soma Popere, Padma Shri, Farmer and Seed Conservationist

Smt. Rahibai Soma Popere, Padma Shri, Farmer and Seed Conservationist from Maharashtra, shared her inspiring journey of conserving indigenous seeds and reviving traditional farming practices. She highlighted the importance of protecting native seeds, restoring soil health and moving towards chemical-free agriculture. Emphasising the value of traditional wisdom, she called for a return to nature-based farming to ensure that every household has access to toxin-free vegetables and safe, nutritious food, paving the way for a healthier and more sustainable future. The two days of conference conducted 40 oral and 60 poster presentations from participants across the country and abroad.

The valedictory session featured a welcome address by Dr Naresh Kumar, Chairperson, CDTK-2026, and closing remarks by Dr Geetha Vani Rayasam, Director, CSIR-NIScPR, who highlighted ethical engagement, community sensitisation, documentation and benefit-sharing in Traditional Knowledge. Prof B N Jagatap, Former Senior Professor at IIT Bombay, highlighted the importance of formalising Indian Knowledge Systems, showcasing India's original scientific contributions, and incorporating diverse forms of evidence. The dignitaries also presented Best Poster Presentation Awards. Dr Charu Lata, Organising Secretary, CDTK-2026, proposed the vote of thanks. The conference reaffirmed the importance of scientific validation, ethical dissemination and community participation in preserving and promoting Traditional Knowledge.

2332277.title: Union Home and Cooperation Minister Shri Amit Shah addresses the closing ceremony of the Chhattisgarh Rajyotsav in Raipur today
2332277.body_html:
Ministry of Home Affairs
Union Home and Cooperation Minister Shri Amit Shah addresses the closing ceremony of the Chhattisgarh Rajyotsav in Raipur today
Congratulations to all the people of the state—especially our tribal brothers and sisters—on a Naxal-free Chhattisgarh; Bow to the CAPFs and the Chhattisgarh Police for this achievement
5 lakh Peepal trees will be planted in Naya Raipur, transforming it into a 'Peepal City'—the world's largest eco-friendly city
The people of Chhattisgarh brought us to power; we pledged to eliminate the Naxal menace within two months, and we have succeeded in making the state Naxal-free
I ask those who support Naxalism in the name of human rights: do human rights belong only to those who wield guns to obstruct development, and not to the poor tribal people?
Modi government is providing artificial limbs to those who lost their arms or legs due to Naxalite violence, helping them stand on their own feet once again
The opposition party has consistently supported Naxalites
A former Home Minister once suggested that Naxalites need not lay down their arms—they should simply refrain from causing chaos. We said, lay down arms and join the mainstream; else, security forces will engage deal with you, 90% of the Naxalites surrendered
Opposition party has always stood by unconstitutional establishments—such as 'Janatana Sarkar' established by Naxalites, which executed innocent journalists, social activists, and students
The same opposition leader who once supported the Naxalites' 'Janatana Sarkar', is now mocking our Parliament by creating a 'mock parliament'
The conduct of the Leader of the Opposition is unconstitutional, yet he walks around carrying a copy of the Constitution
Because of Naxalism, what should have been a 'cultural corridor' in Chhattisgarh turned into a 'Red Corridor'; children who should have held pens in their hands were forced to carry guns. Instead of the school bell ringing, the school itself was blown up
Those who write articles on how to tackle Naxalism should no longer live in fear; come here, witness the development and write about the suffering of these tribals
Modi government is ready to discuss every issue—if the opposition has the courage, it should allow Parliament to function; the public will then see who speaks the truth and who tells lies
Chhattisgarh government has fulfilled over 70% of the guarantees made by PM Modi
In the near future, a Naxal-free Chhattisgarh will rank among the top three tourism states in the country
It was once said that while the land of Chhattisgarh is rich, its people are poor; within 10 years, both the land and its people will be prosperous
Our government will lead Chhattisgarh from a state of fear to one of trust, and from mere resources to true prosperity—we will build a thriving Chhattisgarh, home to a proud people and a bountiful land
Posted On: 03 NOV 2026 8:35PM by PIB Delhi

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah today addressed the concluding ceremony of the Chhattisgarh Rajyotsav in Raipur. On this occasion, Chhattisgarh Chief Minister Shri Vishnu Deo Sai and Deputy Chief Minister Shri Vijay Sharma, along with several other dignitaries, were present.

Addressing the programme, Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that on behalf of the entire people of Chhattisgarh, he extends thanks and pays tributes to former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee Ji, because it was Atal Ji who established the state of Chhattisgarh in the year 2000. He said that we knew that as soon as the state was formed, leaders of the opposition party could become the Chief Minister, yet we did not worry about it. Shri Shah said that injustice had been meted out to Chhattisgarh and the development of this region had been stalled. He said that Atal Ji created Chhattisgarh and Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi ji has nurtured it.

Shri Amit Shah, while extending best wishes to the people of Chhattisgarh, especially the tribal community, said that today Chhattisgarh is moving forward on the path of development after becoming Naxal-free. He also congratulated the Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF) and the Chhattisgarh Police for this achievement. He said that today is a day of pride, achievement and resolve. We take pride in the legacy of Atal Ji, who gave Chhattisgarh the identity of a separate state. It is the fulfilment of the resolutions that had been taken for so many years — the resolutions to make a Naxal-free Chhattisgarh and a Naxal-free India have been realised. And along with this, there is the resolve to build a developed Chhattisgarh under the leadership of Modi Ji and Vishnu Deo Ji.

Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that today people from various fields who have made significant contributions to the development of Chhattisgarh were honoured. He said that the message of Guru Ghasidas and the message of service, equality and truth of Guru Nanak Dev Ji — these are the values of Chhattisgarh. Shri Shah said that to keep the folk culture of Chhattisgarh alive, our government organises Chhattisgarh Pandum and Bastar Olympics. The government of Vishnu Deo Sai has given a new identity to cultural heritages like Panthi, Pandavani, Raut, Nacha, Karma and Saila dances, arts such as Dhokra art, Bell Metal, wood craft and Kosa, and the unique 75-day tradition of Bastar Dussehra. Through Bastar Pandum and Bastar Olympics, lakhs of youth have participated in tribal games and revived their culture. Bastar Pandum has once again brought to life the attire, cuisine, songs and dances of this region. At the same time, work is now underway to fulfill the long-pending vision of development of the tribal areas.

Shri Amit Shah said that the people of Chhattisgarh removed the opposition party and gave a mandate to our party, and within just two months of that we took the resolve to eliminate Naxalism. He said that where a cultural corridor should have existed, a Red Corridor was created. In the forests where mahua, tendu leaves and folk songs should have been, landmines were laid. The child who should have held a pen in his hand was abducted from school and handed a gun. Where the school bell should have rung, the school building itself was blown up, and the person who was to build the road meant to bring development was burnt alive in front of his family. He questioned those who support Naxalism in the name of human rights: Does human rights belong only to those who take up guns and halt development? Do the poor tribals not have human rights? Shri Shah said that the Modi government has shown that poor tribals too have human rights. He said that those whose hands and feet were blown off in bomb blasts over the past 30 years have been provided artificial limbs in an effort to make their lives easier. The Home Minister said that those who sit far away and write long articles offering advice did not have the courage to come here and stay even for a single day. He said that he invites such people not to be afraid — no one will kill them here now. Come and experience the breeze of development. If Shri Ram awakens in your heart, then write a couple of articles on their pain.

Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that the opposition party had always supported Naxalism. He stated that in 2010, a senior minister in the opposition party's central government had said that Naxalites did not need to surrender their weapons; they simply needed to stop creating disturbances. Shri Shah said that violence cannot be stopped in this manner. Union Home Minister stated that he had clearly declared in Parliament that anyone wishing to surrender should lay down their arms and surrender, and the government would bring them into the mainstream. Otherwise, security personnel would confront them. He said that the appeal to armed Naxalites to surrender had yielded positive results: only 10 per cent of the Naxalites were killed, while 90 per cent surrendered. Today, the entire country has become free of Naxalism. This is the policy of Shri Narendra Modi-led government. He further stated that those who abide by the law will be treated as ordinary citizens. However, anyone who violates the law, whether in Bastar, the Northeast or Kashmir, will be dealt with firmly by security forces to protect citizens.

Shri Amit Shah said that the opposition party had always supported unconstitutional establishments and mock parliaments. He stated that the Naxalites had established a parallel government called the Jantana Sarkar in Chhattisgarh. It had its own Home Minister, Chief Minister, Finance Minister and other officials. Shri Shah questioned which Constitution permitted a parallel government such as the Jantana Sarkar and who had authorised them to deliver justice. He said that several innocent journalists, social workers and students had been hanged from trees by the Naxalites. He alleged that opposition leaders had continued to support such activities in Parliament. He said that earlier, the opposition had supported the fake Jantana Sarkar and other unconstitutional governments, and now it had gone a step further by creating a mock parliament and making a mockery of Parliament itself. He accused the opposition of organising a mock parliament and staging a debate merely for show. The Home Minister told the Leader of the Opposition that the Modi government was ready to discuss every issue. He said that the government was willing to convene a special session of Parliament to discuss SIR and challenged the opposition to demonstrate its courage by debating the issue before the people of the country. He further said that carrying a copy of the Constitution in one's hand does not amount to respecting it; one's conduct must reflect constitutional values. He accused the opposition of repeatedly disrupting Parliament and bringing its proceedings to a standstill. He urged the opposition to allow Parliament to function and engage in a direct debate. He said that the people of the country would then be able to judge who was speaking the truth and who was spreading falsehoods.

Union Home Minister said that the leadership trio comprising the Chief Minister and both Deputy Chief Ministers of Chhattisgarh had fulfilled more than 70 per cent of the guarantees made by the Modi government in a very short period. He stated that the 33rd installment under the Mahtari Vandan Yojana had been transferred to the mothers and sisters of Chhattisgarh. Paddy procurement is underway, while sectors such as agriculture, forest produce, animal husbandry and MSMEs are achieving their targets. He said that Chhattisgarh is now Naxal-free and expressed confidence that, in the coming years, the state would rank among the top three states in the tourism sector. He highlighted the tourism potential of Chhattisgarh, mentioning Chitrakote Falls, Tirathgarh Falls, Kanger Valley National Park, Maa Bamleshwari Temple, Maa Danteshwari Temple in Dantewada and the Bastar Dussehra festival. He said that all these destinations and cultural attractions have the potential to attract tourists from across the world to Chhattisgarh.

Shri Amit Shah said that it was often said in the past that the land was rich, but its people were poor. However, within the next 10 years, both the land and its people will be prosperous. This is Modi Ji's guarantee. He said that the goal is to build a prosperous and happy society alongside a prosperous and flourishing land. He stated that the state's annual budget had increased 30-fold, while per capita income had risen 17-fold. The Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP) of a state like Chhattisgarh had grown 25-fold. He further highlighted the expansion of educational infrastructure, stating that the number of ITI institutions had doubled, engineering colleges had tripled, polytechnic colleges had increased six-fold, and colleges and universities had also grown six-fold. He said that his government had increased the state's literacy rate from 65 per cent to 79 per cent. He said that our government’s fourth term in office in the state would take the people of Chhattisgarh from fear to trust and from resources to prosperity. By transforming possibilities into achievements, the government would work towards building a prosperous and happy Chhattisgarh.

2332276.title: MY Bharat's ‘Yuva Samvad: Know Your Vote’ Campaign Reaches Over 59,000 Youth Across 30 States/UTs
2332276.ministry: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
2332276.body_html:
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
MY Bharat's ‘Yuva Samvad: Know Your Vote’ Campaign Reaches Over 59,000 Youth Across 30 States/UTs
311 Yuva Samvads conducted so far; 91 programmes held across 24 States/UTs on Tuesday
Posted On: 03 NOV 2026 8:33PM by PIB Delhi

Mera Yuva Bharat (MY Bharat), under the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, organised 91 Yuva Samvads across 24 States/UTs today as part of its nationwide ‘Viksit Bharat Yuva Samvad: Know Your Vote’ campaign, aimed at promoting electoral awareness and encouraging informed and responsible participation of young people in democracy. The programmes brought together 15,453 youth, 90 Youth Icons and public representatives for discussions on voting rights, democratic values and civic responsibilities.

The events covered Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Delhi, Haryana and Uttar Pradesh in the north, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Karnataka and Puducherry in the south, Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Mizoram, Sikkim and Tripura in the North-East, Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha and West Bengal in the east, Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh in central India, and Gujarat, Maharashtra and Rajasthan in the west.

With today's programmes, the campaign has reached a cumulative 311 Yuva Samvads across 30 States/UTs, engaging 59,408 young people and 310 Youth Icons. The initiative provides students with an opportunity to understand democratic processes, interact with elected representatives and develop a better understanding of their rights and responsibilities as citizens.

 

 

 

In Delhi, Dr. Satyapal Singh, retired IPS officer, highlighted the importance of lifelong learning and the power of voting rights in shaping democracy. In Mandi, Himachal Pradesh, Leader of Opposition Shri Jai Ram Thakur and MLA Shri Puran Chand Thakur urged students to stay informed about current affairs, think critically and distinguish facts from rumours and misinformation. At Dharamshala, Member of Parliament from Kangra and Chamba Dr. Rajeev Bhardwaj responded to students' questions during an interactive discussion.

In Gujarat, programmes in Bhavnagar, Patan and Surat provided students, particularly first-time voters, an opportunity to seek clarity on voting rights and electoral procedures. In Rajasthan, local representatives and Youth Icons engaged with students in Hanumangarh, Pali and Sikar. The Hanumangarh programme also featured discussions on free and fair voting, a question-and-answer session and the Loktantrik pledge.

 

 

In Uttar Pradesh, the Ballia programme combined an orientation on MY Bharat activities, including the Viksit Bharat Young Leaders Dialogue 2027 and Viksit Bharat Young Professionals, with a discussion on ‘Know Your Vote’ and the Loktantrik pledge. In Bihar, programmes featured presentations and discussions on democratic participation. In Khagaria and Purnea, public representatives encouraged young people to become informed voters and contribute to a stronger democracy, while participants in Begusarai, Patna and Saharsa took the Loktantrik Shapath, reaffirming their commitment to responsible citizenship.

In Chhattisgarh, programmes in Dantewada and Jashpur highlighted the role of young people in democracy and nation-building. In Dantewada, MLA Shri Chaitram Atami attended the programme, while Youth Icon Ms. Nandani Dixit delivered a presentation on voting rights and responsible citizenship. In Jashpur, MLA Smt. Raimuni Bhagat urged young people to contribute towards building a Viksit Bharat, exercise independent judgement and remain alert to fake news and misinformation.

 

 

 

Yuva Samvads were held in Ashoknagar, Dewas, Dhar, Indore, Rajgarh, Satna, Shahdol, Tikamgarh and Umaria districts of Madhya Pradesh. In Dewas, Youth Icon Muskan Khare led an interaction with students, while athletes Mahi Verma and Adnan Mohammad Badshah were felicitated for their sporting achievements. In Rajgarh, Member of Parliament Shri Rodmal Singh Nagar engaged with participants, while MLA Smt. Neena Vikram Verma attended the programme in Dhar.

In Karnataka, State MLC Shri C.T. Ravi attended the programme in Bangalore Rural and responded to students' questions. Participants took the Loktantrik pledge and registered on the MY Bharat portal. In Kolar, the programme included an orientation on MY Bharat, a presentation by the Youth Icon and a pledge-taking ceremony.

2332260.title: Sarbananda Sonowal Outlines Plan to Double Coastal & Waterway Freight Share to 12% by 2047
2332260.ministry: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
2332260.body_html:
Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
Sarbananda Sonowal Outlines Plan to Double Coastal & Waterway Freight Share to 12% by 2047
Paradip Port, Govt of Odisha team up to Develop Puri International Cruise Terminal with Rs 1,500 crore: Sarbananda Sonowal
Coastal Cargo Promotion Scheme and Cruise Bharat Mission expected to create more than 560,000 jobs and save 16 million tons of carbon dioxide emissions
India's maritime sector is undergoing massive transformations: Sonowal at Consultative Committee meeting in Puri
Posted On: 03 NOV 2026 8:04PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways (MoPSW), Sarbananda Sonowal, said at a Consultative Committee meeting in Puri, Odisha, that the government is working to double the share of coastal and inland waterway shipping in India's freight movement from 6% to 12% by 2047, and to attract 1 million sea cruise passengers by 2029, through two proposed initiatives: the Coastal Cargo Promotion Scheme and the Cruise Bharat Mission.

The Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal also announced that Puri International Cruise Terminal will be developed by Paradip Port Authority (PPA) in partnership with the Government of Odisha. The project is likely to be developed at a cost of Rs 1,500 crores.

Sonowal chaired a meeting of the ministry's Consultative Committee on strengthening coastal and cruise shipping. Minister of State of MoPSW Shantanu Thakur and eight members of Parliament attended. The ministry's secretary introduced the topic by outlining measures to promote coastal and cruise shipping.

"In the last 12 years under PM Narendra Modi, India's maritime sector has undergone massive transformations," Sonowal said.

India has more than 11,000 kilometers (6,800 miles) of coastline, a natural advantage for moving freight over long distances more cleanly. Coastal cargo at Indian ports has surged from 74 million metric tons to 177 million metric tons over the past 12 years, growth of about 140%, Sonowal said.

“Under Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s dynamic leadership, our coastline and our rivers are being turned into engines of growth. The Coastal Cargo Promotion Scheme and the Cruise Bharat Mission will move more cargo by sea and bring more visitors to our shores, creating jobs and protecting the environment,” Sarbananda Sonowal said.

The Coastal Cargo Promotion Scheme, announced in the 2026-27 budget, will offer incentives to cargo owners, coastal vessel operators and multimodal transport operators, who move cargo by more than one means of transport, such as ship, rail and road.

Sea cruises are also growing fast, Sonowal said. In the 2025-26 fiscal year, India recorded 462,661 ocean cruise passengers and 212 vessel calls, a 5.5-fold rise in passenger traffic and a 2.1-fold rise in vessel calls since 2013-14. The Cruise Bharat Mission, launched in September 2024, targets 1 million sea cruise passengers and 400,000 jobs by March 2029.

Twenty river cruise circuits across 16 National Waterways are already operating, and 51 more have been identified for development in phases. Sonowal said 143 river cruise terminals and landing points are operational. The two initiatives together are expected to generate more than 560,000 jobs and save 16 million metric tons of carbon dioxide emissions, Sonowal said.

Sonowal highlighted the development of National Waterway No. 5 in Odisha, estimated to cost more than Rs 13,000 crore. The waterway is meant to link the state's industrial and mining centers, including Talcher and Kalinganagar, with ports on the east coast.

Members of Parliament praised the government's efforts to develop the maritime sector and offered suggestions on maritime infrastructure in different parts of the country.

"I extend my deep gratitude to the MPs for their valuable insights and suggestions, which will help shape this journey," Sonowal said. "Led by PM Modi's vision, we are steadily advancing towards a competitive, sustainable and thriving maritime ecosystem for a Viksit Bharat.”
