2332256.title: Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 Celebrates India's Cultural Diversity Through Traditional Art, Craft and Cultural Performances
2332256.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 Celebrates India's Cultural Diversity Through Traditional Art, Craft and Cultural Performances
Artists from Different Corners Come Together Every Evening to Showcase India's Rich Cultural Heritage
Dr. Virendra Kumar Visits Stalls, Interacts with Artisans and Appreciates Their Traditional Craftsmanship
Stalls Showcase Handicrafts, Handloom Products and Creative Talent at Dilli Haat INA
Posted On: 03 NOV 2026 8:01PM by PIB Delhi

The Shilp Samagam Mela 2026, being organised by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment at Dilli Haat, INA, New Delhi, is bringing together India's rich artistic traditions, traditional craftsmanship and cultural diversity on a common platform.

Alongside showcasing handicrafts, handloom products and indigenous art forms, the 15-day Mela is emerging as a vibrant celebration of India's inclusive participation.

Organised around the theme ‘प्रकाश और परंपरा – ज्योति से ज्योति जलाएँ’, the Mela celebrates India's traditional crafts, festive lighting and cultural heritage.

The Mela has been curated around seven thematic zones, each offering a distinctive experience showcasing India's crafts, traditions, food and cultural expressions. कला आँगन features live craft demonstrations; प्रकाश चौक showcases lamps and lights; पूजा पथ presents devotional products; सजावट बाज़ार focuses on home décor; घराना features textiles and fashion; स्वाद चौक offers food; and मंच hosts cultural activities and performances.

The Ministry has been organising Shilp Samagam Melas since 2022. Through 15 such fairs, more than 1,000 artisans from Scheduled Castes, Other Backward Classes and Safai Karamcharis have benefited from opportunities to exhibit and market their products.

After inauguration of the Mela on Monday evening, the Hon'ble Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment, Dr. Virendra Kumar, visited the stalls and interacted with stall managers and visitors, taking keen interest in the products and traditional crafts on display.

The Minister’s interaction with the participating artisans provided an opportunity to appreciate their creativity, skills and entrepreneurial efforts.

Dr Kumar’s visit also highlighted the importance of providing artisans from various communities with financial constraints, with platforms to showcase their products, connect with consumers and expand their livelihood opportunities.

A special attraction of the Mela is the series of cultural activities and programmes organised during the evening hours, where artists and performers from different States come together to present their respective art forms and cultural traditions.

The visitors are mesmerized with the cultural programmes wherein artists and performers present their colourful cultural presentations.

Through music, dance and other artistic performances, these programmes offer visitors an opportunity to experience the diverse cultural expressions of different regions of the country on one platform.

The evening programmes provide a common stage for artists from different parts of India to share their artistic heritage, celebrate regional identities and promote cultural exchange.

These performances add to the festive atmosphere of the Mela while highlighting the richness and diversity of India's traditional and contemporary cultural expressions.

The Mela brings together traditional craftsmanship, handloom products, live craft demonstrations and cultural performances, while promoting entrepreneurship, livelihood generation and inclusive participation.

The Mela features more than 130 stalls showcasing handicrafts, handloom products and creative works by artisans and beneficiaries belonging to Scheduled Castes, Other Backward Classes, Safai Karamcharis and persons with disabilities.

A key component of the Mela is Bharat TULIP, which seeks to connect artisans with wider markets through e-commerce platforms, enabling them to expand their reach and strengthen their economic opportunities. The initiative also contributes to preserving India's traditional arts and crafts by providing artisans with greater visibility and access to consumers.

Through Purple Fest, the Mela further celebrates the creativity, abilities and contributions of persons with disabilities, encouraging equal opportunities, participation and inclusion in society.

The participating beneficiaries are supported by the National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC), National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC) and National Divyangjan Finance and Development Corporation (NDFDC). They are being provided free stalls along with facilities such as travel expenses, daily allowance and transportation of goods to facilitate their participation.

Through this initiative, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment continues its efforts to strengthen livelihood opportunities, promote traditional craftsmanship, encourage entrepreneurship and foster inclusive economic growth while celebrating India's rich cultural heritage.

The Mela invites visitors to explore India's traditional crafts, support artisan communities and experience the country's vibrant cultural diversity through its art, craftsmanship, music and performances.

The Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 will remain open to visitors at Dilli Haat, INA, New Delhi, until November 15, 2026.

2332293.title: BRE Summit and Expo 2026 Brings Global Investors and Industry Leaders Together
2332293.ministry: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
2332293.body_html:
Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
BRE Summit and Expo 2026 Brings Global Investors and Industry Leaders Together
Country Partners and 13 States and Union Territories Showcase Investment and Collaboration Opportunities
Odisha Signs 18 MoUs Worth ₹1.17 Lakh Crore
Posted On: 03 NOV 2026 8:00PM by PIB Delhi

On the second day of the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit and Expo 2026, Union Minister of New and Renewable Energy Shri Pralhad Joshi, Union Minister of Power and Housing and Urban Affairs Shri Manohar Lal Khattar and Minister of State for New and Renewable Energy and Power Shri Shripad Yesso Naik participated in “The Next Terawatt” ministerial plenary, a high-level dialogue convened by the International Solar Alliance, CEEW and Energiva Ventures. The plenary brought together senior government and industry voices to map the international renewable energy implementation architecture for the decades ahead.

The discussions deliberated on four key priority areas critical to accelerating the next phase of global renewable energy expansion: integrated energy planning, supply and storage; energy infrastructure expansion and resilience; terawatt-scale financing of projects and ecosystems; and digitalisation and AI for secure and affordable energy. The discussions outlined a strategic roadmap from now to 2050, aligned with India’s vision of Viksit Bharat by 2047.

Odisha witnessed the signing of 18 Memorandum of Understanding (MoUs), representing a total proposed investment of approximately ₹1.17 lakh crore, in the presence of Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi and Deputy Chief Minister Kanak Vardhan Singh Deo.

In a separate development, Bondada Engineering Ltd., part of the Bondada Group, signed an MoU with the Goa Investment Promotion and Facilitation Board (Goa-IPB), committing a proposed investment of approximately ₹3,000 crore towards renewable energy projects in Goa.

BRE Summit & Expo 2026 has brought together representatives from over 130 countries, including more than 40 Ministers, senior policymakers, investors, financial institutions and industry leaders. Australia, Denmark, the European Union, France, Germany, the Netherlands, Norway, Sweden and the United Kingdom are participating as Country Partners, providing opportunities to strengthen bilateral cooperation and facilitate investment and technology partnerships across the clean energy value chain.

Thirteen States and Union Territories are also showcasing their renewable energy potential, project pipelines, manufacturing capabilities and policy initiatives, highlighting the breadth and diversity of investment opportunities across India.

The day also featured the first leg of Watts Next: Innovators’ Ideas for India’s Energy Security, Agenda 2047, a by-invite ideas forum curated in partnership with BloombergNEF. Moving beyond conventional panel discussions, the session brought together leading innovators, entrepreneurs and industry leaders to present bold, actionable ideas on technology, finance and policy that could shape India’s energy system as the country approaches its centenary of independence. Speakers included Sumant Sinha (Founder, Chairman and CEO, ReNew), Shreya Mishra (Co-Founder and CEO, SolarSquare), Girish R Tanti (Co-Founder, Suzlon Group), Prof. Ashok Jhunjhunwala (IIT Madras) and Meredith Annex (Head of Clean Power Research, BloombergNEF).

India’s renewable energy expansion will require sustained investment in generation capacity, energy storage, transmission networks, domestic manufacturing and supporting infrastructure. The Summit is providing a platform for public and private sector stakeholders to explore innovative financing models, strengthen investment partnerships and identify solutions to accelerate project implementation.

DAHD Successfully Concludes Special Campaign 6.0
Posted On: 03 NOV 2026 7:37PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying (DAHD), Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Government of India, actively participated in Special Campaign 6.0, conducted from 2nd October, 2026 to 31st October, 2026 with the objective of strengthening cleanliness practices and ensuring the timely disposal of pending matters. During Special Campaign 6.0, the Department demonstrated commendable performance, achieving or exceeding 100% of targets in several key areas, including State Government references, disposal of public grievances and appeals, review of physical files, cleanliness of sites, and scrap disposal. Notably, 247 sites were cleaned against a target of 226, and revenue of ₹25,93,896 was generated through scrap disposal, reflecting the Department’s strong commitment to efficient administration, improved record management and workplace cleanliness.

2332241.title: Ministry of Labour & Employment Successfully Concludes Special Campaign 6
2332241.body_html:
Ministry of Labour & Employment
Ministry of Labour & Employment Successfully Concludes Special Campaign 6
Posted On: 03 NOV 2026 7:31PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Labour & Employment has successfully concluded Special Campaign 6, reaffirming its commitment to administrative efficiency, cleanliness, transparency and improved public service delivery. The campaign witnessed active participation from the Ministry and its attached, subordinate and autonomous organizations across the country.

Key Achievements

1. Disposal of Pending Matters: The Ministry and its associated organizations disposed of 2,42,042 public grievances against a target of 2,07,000, achieving 116.93% of the target (16.93% above target). Similarly, 11,001 PG Appeals were disposed of against a target of 5,758, achieving 191.06% (91.06% above target), while 844 PMO references were disposed of against a target of 807, achieving 104.58% (4.58% above target).

2. Efficient File Management: More than 2 lakh physical files were reviewed, resulting in the weeding out of 98,500 files. Additionally, 70,191 e-files were reviewed against a target of 41,180, achieving 170.45% of the target (70.45% above target). A total of 14,589 e-files were closed, strengthening records management and administrative efficiency.

3. Space Optimization: Approximately 2,18,106 sq. ft. of office and outdoor space was reclaimed, reorganized and beautified, contributing to a cleaner and more productive working environment.

4. Revenue Generation: Disposal of scrap and obsolete materials generated revenue of ₹49,48,896, facilitating better resource utilization.

5. Cleanliness and Environmental Improvement: Cleanliness drives were conducted at more than 2,700 sites, promoting hygiene and environmental sustainability.

Special One-Day Event and Outreach Activities

As part of the campaign, the Ministry organized a dedicated One-Day Event on 9th October 2026 across all its attached, subordinate and autonomous offices throughout the country. Activities included extensive cleanliness and plantation drives, weeding out of obsolete records and redressal of public grievances. Dental and eye health check-up camps were also organized by the Ministry as part of the initiative.

The campaign's progress was regularly monitored at various levels within the Ministry. Mass pledge-taking activities and other awareness initiatives were also conducted to encourage collective participation.

The successful conclusion of Special Campaign 6 reflects the Ministry's continued commitment to good governance, efficient administration, employee well-being and citizen-centric service delivery.

2332200.title: From Financial Assistance To Academic Excellence
2332200.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Financial Assistance To Academic Excellence
How The NFSC Scheme Supports A Scholar’s Journey
Posted On: 03 NOV 2026 6:50PM by PIB Delhi

For 30 year Dr. Anirudh Pradhan (name changed), the NFSC Scheme has been an important source of support in translating his academic aspirations into professional achievement.

The fellowship enhanced his academic progress, improved his professional opportunities and strengthened his confidence and financial stability. His journey reflects the role of financial assistance in enabling students to pursue higher education and build meaningful careers.

Dr. Anirudh Pradhan, a resident of Sambalpur district in Odisha, aspired to gain knowledge and achieve excellence in his chosen field of study. However, financial constraints and the lack of proper guidance posed challenges to his pursuit of higher education. His family also faced limited access to educational and livelihood opportunities, making it difficult to meet the financial requirements of advanced studies.

A significant support in his academic journey came through the National Fellowship for Scheduled Caste Students (NFSC) Scheme of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. His fellowship assistance commenced on 27 December 2019.

Under the scheme, he received fellowship support of Rs 31,000 per month, along with contingency assistance, which helped address financial barriers and enabled him to focus on his Ph.D. research.

With the support of the fellowship and his continued academic efforts, Dr. Pradhan successfully completed his Ph.D. He is currently working as an Assistant Professor of Sociology at Model Degree College, Nuapada, Khariar, Odisha, with a basic pay of Rs 63,000.

The financial assistance provided under the NFSC Scheme helped him pursue his doctoral studies without significant financial burden. It enabled him to devote greater attention to his research and academic goals, while strengthening his confidence and providing greater financial stability during his higher education.

2332192.title: Union Health Ministry has proposed amendments to Drugs Rules, 1945 to mandate Authorisation of qualified personnel for drug batch release
2332192.ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
2332192.body_html:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Union Health Ministry has proposed amendments to Drugs Rules, 1945 to mandate Authorisation of qualified personnel for drug batch release
Amendments to the Drugs Rules, 1945 seek to strengthen accountability and documentation in batch release
Posted On: 03 NOV 2026 6:43PM by PIB Delhi

Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has proposed amendments to the Drugs Rules, 1945, to mandate drug manufacturers to formally authorise a person with appropriate qualifications and experience for batch release of drugs and maintain prescribed records for every batch manufactured.

The proposed amendments aim to strengthen accountability in the drug manufacturing process by introducing an explicit regulatory requirement for the authorisation of personnel responsible for batch release. While manufacturing licences currently require manufacturers to furnish details of competent technical staff responsible for manufacturing and testing, there is no specific provision for mentioning the person authorised to undertake batch release.

Under the proposed framework, applicants seeking manufacturing licences under the relevant provisions of the Drugs Rules, 1945, would be required to designate a suitably qualified and experienced person for batch release and maintain batch-release records in accordance with the prescribed requirements. The amendments also propose to introduce a prescribed format for the Batch Release Certificate under the Rules.

Batch release is a critical stage in the pharmaceutical manufacturing process, involving an overall review of the relevant quality parameters and documentation before a batch is released for distribution. The proposed requirements are intended to establish clear responsibility for this function, ensure traceability of batch-release decisions and provide an additional level of oversight of product quality.

The proposed amendments are also expected to support manufacturers in strengthening their compliance with applicable Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) and reinforce the regulatory framework governing the quality assurance of drugs.

Objections and suggestions, if any, on the proposed amendments may be submitted to the Under Secretary (Drugs Regulation), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India, U-6, Work Hall, C Wing, First Floor, Kartavya Bhawan-1, New Delhi – 110001, or sent by email to drugsdiv-mohfw[at]gov[dot]in.

2332184.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
Indian Coast Guard and Sri Lanka Coast Guard hold 9th High-Level Meeting
Posted On: 03 NOV 2026 6:30PM by PIB Delhi

The 9th High-Level Meeting (HLM) between the Indian Coast Guard (ICG) and the Sri Lanka Coast Guard (SLCG) was held at Mirissa, Sri Lanka, on 03 November 2026.

The Indian delegation was led by Director General Paramesh Sivamani, Director General, Indian Coast Guard, while the Sri Lankan delegation was headed by Rear Admiral Ruwan Rupasena, Director General, Sri Lanka Coast Guard.

The meeting focused on strengthening bilateral cooperation in key areas of mutual interest, including Marine Pollution Response, Maritime Search and Rescue (SAR), and Maritime Law Enforcement. Discussions also explored avenues for enhancing capacity building and technical assistance initiatives to further strengthen operational cooperation between the two Coast Guards.

During the deliberations, both delegations reaffirmed their commitment to working closely towards addressing emerging maritime challenges and enhancing cooperation in ensuring maritime safety, security and environmental protection across the shared maritime domain.

The meeting highlighted the shared resolve of the Indian Coast Guard and Sri Lanka Coast Guard to further strengthen bilateral engagement, promote coordinated responses to maritime contingencies and advance regional cooperation for a safe, secure and clean maritime environment in the Indian Ocean Region.

2332175.title: IPRD-2026 COMMENCES AT NEW DELHI, TRANSLATING SCIENTIFIC ADVANCEMENT INTO REGIONAL COOPERATION
2332175.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
IPRD-2026 COMMENCES AT NEW DELHI, TRANSLATING SCIENTIFIC ADVANCEMENT INTO REGIONAL COOPERATION
Posted On: 03 NOV 2026 6:18PM by PIB Delhi

The Indo-Pacific Regional Dialogue 2026 (IPRD-2026), the Indian Navy’s annual apex-level international strategic dialogue, commenced on 03 Nov 2026 at New Delhi. Organised in association with the National Maritime Foundation (NMF), the Navy’s knowledge partner, the three-day conference is examining ‘Science, Technology and Academic Cooperation in the Indo-Pacific’, with particular emphasis on translating scientific advancement and institutional partnerships into practical regional cooperation.

The opening day of IPRD-2026 established the central question of the dialogue: ‘How the Indo-Pacific can turn scientific knowledge and technological innovation into enduring institutional cooperation, stronger maritime capabilities and shared regional resilience.’

The proceedings began with the Inaugural Address by Adm Dinesh K Tripathi (Retd), Chairman NMF, and former Chief of the Naval Staff. This was followed by a Special Address by VAdm Biswajit Dasgupta (Retd), National Maritime Security Coordinator, Govt of India.

The first session of IPRD-2026 focused upon the theme, ‘Academic Networks, Research, and Human Capital Development’.  This session was moderated by VAdm Sanjay Mahindru (Retd), former Deputy Chief of the Naval Staff, and featured perspectives from France, Indonesia, Japan and Maldives. It explored the potential for a wider Indian Ocean academic network, including cooperation among universities in Indo-Pacific coastal cities, and examined social-science research networks in the Indian Ocean. The session also explored closer links among think tanks, universities and governments. A monograph entitled, ‘Sea Blindness and Maritime Heritage in India’, was also released upon culmination of this session.

The second professional session of the day, ‘Maritime Situational Awareness and Protection of Critical Maritime Infrastructure’, highlighted the breadth of the contemporary maritime-awareness challenges associated with the protection of seaborne trade and critical undersea infrastructure. Moderated by VAdm Tarun Sobti (Retd), former Deputy Chief of the Naval Staff, it examined the opportunities and challenges associated with the Indo-Pacific Partnership for Maritime Domain Awareness (IPMDA), particularly the practical requirements of information-sharing, and explored the development of cooperative Indo-Pacific architecture for underwater domain awareness. The session also included views from the Indian Ocean Commission (IOC) on cooperative approaches to the protection of critical maritime infrastructure.

Together, the two professional sessions examined how technological systems and scientific partnerships can be made operationally useful by strengthening maritime information-sharing, safeguarding critical infrastructure, improving access to oceanographic knowledge, and enabling a more coordinated response to climate-related risks.

The day’s programme also featured ‘Sahyog Ka Samvaad’, a special ambassadorial interaction with HE Ms Mahishini Colonne, High Commissioner of Sri Lanka; HE Mr Josel F Ignacio, Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary, Embassy of the Philippines; and HE Mrs May-Elin Stener, Ambassador of the Kingdom of Norway. This interaction was hosted and moderated by VAdm Pradeep Chauhan (Retd), Director-General, NMF.

The first day of IPRD-2026 ended on a highly optimistic note, with enthusiastic participation from the audience, that presented several actionable policy recommendations on fostering regional cooperation in science and technology, and knowledge sharing through academic collaboration.

Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava, Secretary, Union Health Ministry, selects part-time members of National Dental Commission and its Autonomous Boards through draw of lots as per procedure prescribed under the National Dental Commission Act, 2023
Ten part-time members representing State/UT Governments and nine representing State Dental Councils selected to the National Dental Commission for a two-year tenure; second part-time members of three Autonomous Boards also selected
Posted On: 03 NOV 2026 6:17PM by PIB Delhi

Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has undertaken the selection of part-time members of the National Dental Commission (NDC) and its three Autonomous Boards through a draw of lots, in accordance with the provisions of the National Dental Commission Act, 2023, and the Rules framed thereunder. Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava, Secretary, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, participated in the selection process.

The appointments, made for a tenure of two years, comprise ten part-time members representing State/UT Governments and nine part-time members representing State Dental Councils. The process also included the selection of the second part-time member for each of the three Autonomous Boards of the Commission.

The ten part-time members representing State/UT Governments have been selected from Sikkim, Jharkhand, Keralam, Uttarakhand, Mizoram, Rajasthan, Arunachal Pradesh, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh and Jammu & Kashmir.

The nine part-time members representing State Dental Councils have been selected from Nagaland, Tamil Nadu, Madhya Pradesh, Meghalaya, Karnataka, Telangana, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Puducherry.

In addition, the second part-time member for each of the three Autonomous Boards of the National Dental Commission has been selected from among the nine members representing State Dental Councils, in accordance with Section 17(5) of the National Dental Commission Act, 2023. The selections are as follows:

  • Under-Graduate and Post-Graduate Dental Education Board: Telangana
  • Dental Assessment and Rating Board: Karnataka
  • Ethics and Dental Registration Board: Madhya Pradesh

The selection process through a draw of lots follows the statutory procedure prescribed under the National Dental Commission Act, 2023, for appointment of part-time members to the Commission and its Autonomous Boards.

2332174.title: Union Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh Inaugurated Microbiology Laboratory, Launched Churpi Traceability Initiative and Fodder Plus FPO Products in Sikkim
2332174.ministry: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
2332174.body_html:
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
Union Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh Inaugurated Microbiology Laboratory, Launched Churpi Traceability Initiative and Fodder Plus FPO Products in Sikkim
Sikkim recorded 79% growth in milk production over the last decade; dairy cooperative societies increased by 88%
Centre of Excellence for indigenous Siri cattle and modernisation of Mangan dairy plant announced
Posted On: 03 NOV 2026 6:14PM by PIB Delhi

Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh (Alias Lalan Singh), Hon’ble Union Minister of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Government of India, participated in a programme organised by the Sikkim Milk Union (SMU) at Gangtok, Sikkim, on 3 November 2026. The programme focused on strengthening dairy infrastructure, expanding cooperative networks and promoting value addition in the dairy sector.

The Hon’ble Union Minister inaugurated the Microbiology Laboratory of the Sikkim Milk Union under the National Programme for Dairy Development (NPDD). The facility was aimed at strengthening microbiological testing and quality assessment, thereby contributing to improved quality assurance and food safety in the dairy sector. He also inspected the exhibition stalls showcasing dairy products and other initiatives of the Sikkim Milk Union.

The programme commenced with a welcome address by the Chairman of the Sikkim Milk Union, followed by the felicitation of the Hon’ble Union Minister and other dignitaries. The Microbiology Laboratory at Karfectar was also virtually inaugurated. The Churpi Traceability initiative was inaugurated to strengthen traceability and promote the identity and marketability of the traditional dairy product. The Hon’ble Union Minister also witnessed the launch of Fodder Plus products developed by Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs), highlighting the importance of fodder availability, farmer collectives and diversified income opportunities in the livestock sector.

Registration certificates were distributed to five newly established Dairy Cooperative Societies (DCSs), marking another step towards strengthening the cooperative dairy network in Sikkim and expanding the reach of organised dairy institutions at the grassroots level.

Sikkim recorded 79% growth in milk production over the last decade

Addressing the gathering, the Hon’ble Union Minister congratulated the Government of Sikkim and stakeholders on the significant progress made in the dairy sector. He highlighted that milk production had increased by 79%, from 1.37 lakh litres to 2.45 lakh litres per day, while the number of dairy cooperative societies had grown by 88%, from 389 in 2014–15 to 733 in 2025–26. Daily milk supply to consumers had also doubled from 28,000 litres to 56,000 litres.

Emphasising the need to accelerate dairy development, he called upon NDDB to intensify its efforts and deploy additional human resources to help Sikkim achieve self-reliance in milk production and procurement. He underlined the role of dairy cooperatives in ensuring milk quality, preventing adulteration and securing fair returns for farmers.

Citing the example of Varanasi, he highlighted how NDDB's intervention had increased milk collection from 14,000 litres per day in 2022 to approximately 2.5 lakh litres per day. The price received by farmers had also increased from ₹28–30 to ₹42 per litre, with additional income opportunities through cow dung utilisation in biogas plants under the GOBARdhan initiative.

Centre of Excellence for indigenous Siri cattle

Referring to his visit to Mangan, where local cattle yielded an average of approximately three litres of milk per day, the Hon’ble Minister announced that the Central Government would sanction funds for establishing a Centre of Excellence for the conservation and development of indigenous Siri cattle. The proposed centre would promote advanced breeding technologies, including IVF, to improve the genetic potential and milk productivity of the breed. He invited the State Government to submit a formal proposal for consideration.

Modernisation of Mangan dairy plant

The Hon’ble Minister further stated that NDDB would finance and undertake the comprehensive modernisation of the existing dairy processing plant in Mangan district, following the successful model implemented in Mizoram.

Concluding his address, he reiterated the Central Government’s commitment to Sikkim's dairy and agricultural development, stating that the State's economic progress was integral to strengthening the North Eastern region and advancing the Prime Minister’s vision of an Aatmanirbhar North East.

2332169.title: Seminar on Cyber-Enabled Cognitive Warfare by CENJOWS & HQIDS Concludes in New Delhi
2332169.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
Seminar on Cyber-Enabled Cognitive Warfare by CENJOWS & HQIDS Concludes in New Delhi
Posted On: 03 NOV 2026 6:10PM by PIB Delhi

The two-day seminar on “Cyber-Enabled Cognitive Warfare”, organised by the Centre for Joint Warfare Studies (CENJOWS) under the aegis of Headquarters Integrated Defence Staff (HQ IDS), concluded in New Delhi on November 03, 2026. The Chief of the Air Staff, Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, delivered a special address and emphasised the importance of synergised and coordinated functioning among all stakeholders to enhance operational efficacy and situational awareness.

The second day of the seminar focused on evolving approaches to deterrence in the cyber-enabled cognitive domain, with particular emphasis on the credibility of response options training, simulation and capacity building, alongside digital governance, ethical considerations and legal frameworks for addressing emerging threats. The deliberations were held on the convergence of cyber capabilities, Artificial Intelligence, information manipulation and psychological influence, and the challenges they pose to national security. Discussions also highlighted issues relating to attribution, strategic signalling, coordinated responses and the development of institutional capabilities to counter hostile activities in the cognitive domain. 

The seminar underscored the need for a coordinated, multi-domain approach to national security, recognising that cyber-enabled cognitive threats extend beyond conventional technological vulnerabilities to influence perceptions, decision-making and institutional trust. The deliberations aimed to strengthen joint and inter-agency understanding, foster collaboration among defence, government, scientific and academic communities, and contribute towards developing effective capabilities and response frameworks to address the evolving security environment.

The seminar featured a special address by General Anil Chauhan (Retd), former Chief of Defence Staff and Director, Vivekananda International Foundation. The seminar brought together stakeholders from the defence forces, government, academia, technology and media to deliberate on emerging challenges in the cognitive domain and explore strategies to strengthen national preparedness through deterrence, inter-agency coordination and capacity building.

***

2332168.title: India Committed to Protecting Integrity of Sports, says Dr. Mandaviya at 10th WAADS QA Managers’ Meeting 2026
2332168.ministry: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
2332168.body_html:
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
India Committed to Protecting Integrity of Sports, says Dr. Mandaviya at 10th WAADS QA Managers’ Meeting 2026
Union Sports Minister Launches NDTL Extramural Research Grant Policy
“Athlete Education and Doping Prevention is our Priority,” Dr. Mandaviya Links Clean Sport to 2030 CWG, 2036 Olympic Dreams
Posted On: 03 NOV 2026 6:05PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Youth Affairs & Sports Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya, on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, launched the Extramural Research Grant Policy of the National Dope Testing Laboratory (NDTL) at the 10th World Association of Anti-Doping Scientists (WAADS) Quality Assurance Managers’ Meeting 2026 in New Delhi.


The two-day meeting that began on November 2 was organised by NDTL and brought together international stakeholders from the sports and scientific communities. Dr. Mandaviya, as the chief guest, also oversaw the launch of the NDTL Newsletter at the meet.

The Union Sports Minister Outlined India’s zero tolerance policy for doping. He said, “Friends, India has zero tolerance for doping. Our responsibility is to ensure that every victory is earned through talent, discipline, and hard work.



 

“Over the last two years, under the leadership of our Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, sports has been recognised as an important pillar of nation-building,” said Dr. Mandaviya. “India’s sporting journey has entered a new phase.”

Highlighting India’s commitment towards further anti-doping research and education, the Union Minister said, “Today we launched the important Extramural Research Grant Policy, which aims at promoting research and development in areas of advanced detection and prevention. This initiative will strengthen the scientific foundation of our anti-doping efforts.”



 

With India set to host Commonwealth Games 2030 and harbouring ambitions of hosting the 2036 Olympics, education and awareness about doping play a vital role in India’s fight towards preventing it.

Dr. Mandaviya said, “Our approach, therefore, combines stronger testing infrastructure with education, awareness, and prevention. As India prepares to host the Commonwealth Games in 2030 and with our dreams of hosting the 2036 Olympics as well, anti-doping testing, athlete education, and international cooperation are a priority for us.

“Athletes, coaches, and medical professionals must understand the implications of prohibited substances, the risks associated with supplements, and their responsibilities under anti-doping rules,” said Dr. Mandaviya.



 

The Union Sports Minister stated that India has already taken major steps towards becoming a sporting nation, and the recent performances of its athletes at the 2026 Asian Games prove that.

“Through initiatives such as Khelo India, which translates to Play India, Fit India, and the target Olympic podium scheme, we have strengthened the sporting ecosystem and created greater opportunities for our youth to excel,” said Dr. Mandaviya. 



 

“At the recently concluded Asian Games 2026, our athletes delivered one of their best performances, finishing fourth in the final medal tally. Our para-athletes have also scripted history at the Asian Para Games 2026, securing a record 114 medals, our highest ever medal tally at the games,” he said.

Over the two days, the meeting was also attended by Secretary (Sports) Shri Hari Ranjan Rao, along with International delegates, Dr. Osquel Barroso, Senior Associate Director (Laboratory Science and Medicine), WADA, Dr. Dorota Kwiatkowska, President, WAADS, Prof. (Dr.) P. L. Sahu, Director, NDTL, and other eminent Scientists.

 

*****

 

Ayushman Kumar

2332152.title: NITI Aayog and TEXMiN Sign Joint Statement of Intent to Strengthen India’s Critical Minerals Ecosystem
2332152.body_html:
NITI Aayog
NITI Aayog and TEXMiN Sign Joint Statement of Intent to Strengthen India’s Critical Minerals Ecosystem
Prof. Gobardhan Das highlights the strategic importance of critical minerals for national security, technological self-reliance and Viksit Bharat 2047
Posted On: 03 NOV 2026 5:50PM by PIB Delhi

NITI Aayog and TEXMiN (Technology Translation Research Park), an initiative of the Department of Science and Technology (DST), Government of India, at IIT (ISM) Dhanbad, signed a Joint Statement of Intent (SoI) to strengthen collaboration in the critical and strategic minerals sector.

The collaboration aims to advance indigenous technological capabilities, promote research & innovation and support the development of resilient and sustainable critical mineral value chains in India. It aligns with the objectives of the National Critical Mineral Mission (NCMM) and the vision of an Aatmanirbhar and Viksit Bharat.

The SoI was signed during the visit of Prof. Gobardhan Das, Member, NITI Aayog, to IIT (ISM) Dhanbad, where he inaugurated the National Symposium on Critical Minerals and Rare Earths (CMRE 2026) on 31 October 2026, organised as part of the 45th Annual National Conference of the Indian Council of Chemists.

Addressing the symposium, Prof. Das highlighted the importance of critical minerals as strategic enablers of national security, technological self-reliance and India’s vision of Viksit Bharat 2047. Drawing on India’s rich metallurgical heritage, he emphasised the need to build indigenous technological capabilities through research, innovation and industry collaboration.

He stressed the need to move beyond a mine-centric approach towards an integrated value chain encompassing exploration, processing, refining, advanced materials and recycling. He also highlighted the potential of recovering critical minerals from secondary resources such as coal fly ash, red mud, mine tailings and electronic waste, while underscoring the importance of translating research into commercially viable technologies and promoting sustainable resource utilisation.

The Joint Statement of Intent between NITI Aayog and TEXMiN envisages cooperation in four key areas: collaborative research and technology development; technical and strategic studies; policy and institutional support; and capacity building and knowledge exchange.

The collaboration aims to strengthen indigenous capabilities, facilitate technology translation and promote stronger linkages among government, academia, research institutions and industry.

The symposium brought together policymakers, researchers, technology developers and industry representatives to deliberate on strengthening India’s critical minerals and rare earths ecosystem.

The initiative is expected to contribute to India’s efforts towards building resilient critical mineral supply chains and advancing technological self-reliance.Ll

2332151.title: Ministry of MSME observes Vigilance Awareness Week 2026 on the Theme of “Probity for Prosperity”
2332151.body_html:
Ministry of Micro,Small & Medium Enterprises
Ministry of MSME observes Vigilance Awareness Week 2026 on the Theme of “Probity for Prosperity”
Nukkad Natak Organised to promote Integrity and Preventive Vigilance during Vigilance Awareness Week 2026
Posted On: 03 NOV 2026 5:49PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) observed Vigilance Awareness Week 2026 from 26th October to 1st November 2026, in accordance with the guidelines issued by the Central Vigilance Commission (CVC). This year’s theme was “Probity for Prosperity” (सत्यनिष्ठा से समृद्धि). In line with the Commission’s advisory, the Ministry also undertook a three-month preventive vigilance campaign from 17th August to 16th November 2026, focusing on expeditious disposal of pending complaints and cases, capacity-building programmes, digital initiatives, and contract management.

The week-long observance commenced on 26th October 2026 with the Secretary, Ministry of MSME, Shri Bharat Khera, administering the Integrity Pledge to the officers and staff of the Ministry at Kartavya Bhawan-3, New Delhi. More than 500 officials from the Ministry and its organisations participated in the pledge-taking ceremony in hybrid mode, reaffirming their commitment to integrity, transparency and probity in public service.

As part of the observance, Quiz and Slogan Writing competitions were organised for the officials of the Ministry on 26th October 2026. The competitions witnessed enthusiastic participation and aimed at fostering greater awareness of integrity, transparency, probity and ethical conduct in the discharge of official responsibilities.

The central event marking the culmination of the week-long observance was held on 30th October 2026 under the Chair of Secretary. The event was attended by more than 300 officials of the Ministry and its organisations and field offices across the country through hybrid mode. On the occasion, the Chief Vigilance Officer (CVO), MSME, made a presentation highlighting the preventive vigilance initiatives undertaken by the Ministry during the three-month campaign. Secretary (MSME) also felicitated the winners of the Quiz and Slogan Writing competitions and emphasised the importance of imbibing the values of integrity, transparency and accountability embodied in the theme “Probity for Prosperity”.

Further reinforcing the message of vigilance and ethical conduct, a Nukkad Natak was staged by a team from the National School of Drama (NSD) on 30th October 2026 at Kartavya Bhawan-3, New Delhi. Based on the theme “Probity for Prosperity”, the performance highlighted the importance of adherence to Conduct Rules, continuous upgradation of knowledge and effective use of the whistleblower mechanism in preventing and combating corruption. More than 300 officials from various Ministries and Departments witnessed the performance.

Through the observance of Vigilance Awareness Week 2026 and the ongoing preventive vigilance campaign, the Ministry of MSME reiterated its commitment to strengthening transparency, accountability and integrity in governance. The initiatives undertaken during the period reaffirm the Ministry’s resolve to promote a culture of ethical conduct and preventive vigilance, contributing towards a transparent, accountable and prosperous nation.

***

2332234.title: وزیر دفاع نے  دہلی ڈیفنس ڈائیلاگ 2026 میں کہاکہ  اکیسویں صدی میں فوجی تیاری کے لیے دفاعی شعبے کی اہم صلاحیتوں کی مقامی سطح پر تیاری اور ان کے آزادانہ استعمال کی استعداد ناگزیر ہے
2332234.body_html:
रक्षा मंत्रालय
وزیر دفاع نے  دہلی ڈیفنس ڈائیلاگ 2026 میں کہاکہ  اکیسویں صدی میں فوجی تیاری کے لیے دفاعی شعبے کی اہم صلاحیتوں کی مقامی سطح پر تیاری اور ان کے آزادانہ استعمال کی استعداد ناگزیر ہے
’’دفاعی اصلاحات، خود انحصاری، باہمی تعاون اور برآمدات،  وکست بھارت  2047 کے باہم مربوط ستون ہیں‘‘
جناب راج ناتھ سنگھ نے اختراع کو فروغ دینے کے لیے عملی ضروریات اور تحقیق کی آزادی کے درمیان توازن قائم کرنے پر زور دیا
’’خود انحصاری کا مطلب دنیا سے کنارہ کشی اختیار کرنا نہیں، بلکہ یہ  ہندوستان  کوعالمی تعاون کے لیے زیادہ بہتر ماحول فراہم کرتی  ہے‘‘
وزیر دفاع نے مشترکہ ترقی، مشترکہ پیداوار اور اختراع میں شراکت داری کی بنیاد پر بین الاقوامی تعاون کی وکالت کی
प्रविष्टि तिथि: 03 NOV 2026 5:44PM by PIB Delhi

وزیر دفاع جناب راج ناتھ سنگھ نے اہم دفاعی سازوسامان اور ٹیکنالوجیز کی ملک کے اندر تیاری اور انہیں آزادانہ طور پر برقرار رکھنے کی صلاحیت پیدا کرنے پر زور دیتے ہوئے کہا کہ ’’اکیسویں صدی میں فوجی تیاری کا انحصار بنیادی طور پر تکنیکی اور صنعتی صلاحیتوں پر ہے۔‘‘ وہ 3 نومبر 2026 کو منوہر پاریکر انسٹی ٹیوٹ فار ڈیفنس اسٹڈیز اینڈ اینالیسز (ایم پی-آئی ڈی ایس اے) میں منعقدہ دہلی ڈیفنس ڈائیلاگ کے تیسرے ایڈیشن سے خطاب کر رہے تھے۔ انہوں نے اس بات پر زور دیا کہ ’آتم نربھرتا‘ کو تکنیکی خود مختاری کی جستجو کے طور پر دیکھا جانا چاہیے، کیونکہ خود انحصاری کا مطلب یہ یقینی بنانا ہے کہ ملک کی اہم دفاعی ضروریات بیرونی انحصار کی محتاج نہ رہیں۔ انہوں نے کہا کہ حقیقی خود انحصاری اسی وقت حاصل ہوتی ہے جب ملک کے پاس دفاعی نظام کا خاکہ تیار کرنے کا علم، اسے تیار کرنے کی ٹیکنالوجی، اس میں بہتری لانے کے لیے دانشورانہ ملکیت کے حقوق اور اس کی پوری مدتِ استعمال کے دوران اسے برقرار رکھنے کی صلاحیت موجود ہو۔

اس سال کے ڈائیلاگ کے موضوع ’دفاعی اصلاحات، خود انحصاری، باہمی تعاون اور برآمدات‘ پر اپنے خیالات کا اظہار کرتے ہوئے وزیر دفاع نے ان چاروں عناصر کو 2047 تک ہندوستان کو ترقی یافتہ ملک بنانے کے ہدف کے باہم مربوط پہلو قرار دیا۔ انہوں نے کہا کہ اصلاحات کے ذریعے ایسا سازگار ادارہ جاتی ماحول پیدا کیا جانا چاہیے جو ترقی کی راہ ہموار کرے، خود انحصاری سے ملک کی مقامی تکنیکی صلاحیتوں کو مستحکم کیا جانا چاہیے، باہمی تعاون کے ذریعے جدید ٹیکنالوجیز تک رسائی کو تیز کرنے اور مشترکہ ترقی کو ممکن بنانے کی ضرورت ہے، جبکہ برآمدات کے ذریعے پائیدار صنعتی نظام کے لیے درکار پیداواری وسعت، مسابقتی صلاحیت اور عالمی شراکت داریوں کو فروغ دیا جانا چاہیے۔ انہوں نے کہا کہ یہ چاروں عناصر ہندوستان کی  اسٹریٹجک خود مختاری کی جستجو کے ایک دوسرے کو تقویت دینے والے ستون ہیں۔

جناب راج ناتھ سنگھ نے اس بات پر زور دیا کہ اصلاحات ملک کی تبدیلی کے لیے آمادگی، خود انحصاری اس کے تخلیقی عزم، باہمی تعاون دنیا کے ساتھ شراکت داری کے اعتماد اور برآمدات عالمی سطح پر مقابلہ کرنے کی تیاری کی علامت ہیں۔ انہوں نے کہا کہ ان چاروں عناصر کو ایک ساتھ آگے بڑھنا چاہیے، کیونکہ اصلاحات، بین الاقوامی تعاون اور برآمدات کے بغیر خود انحصاری ہندوستان کے تکنیکی امکانات، صنعتی وسعت اور عالمی مسابقتی صلاحیت کو محدود کر دے گی۔

وزیر دفاع نے نشاندہی کی کہ دنیا بھر میں حالیہ تنازعات نے جنگ کی نوعیت میں بنیادی تبدیلی کو نمایاں کیا ہے۔ اب میدانِ جنگ خشکی، سمندر اور فضا سے آگے بڑھ کر خلا، سائبر اسپیس اور ڈیجیٹل شعبے تک پھیل چکے ہیں۔ انہوں نے کہا کہ روایتی اور غیر روایتی جنگ کے درمیان فرق بتدریج ختم ہوتا جا رہا ہے، جبکہ نسبتاً کم لاگت والے ڈرونز اور خودکار نظام جدید اور مہنگے فوجی سازوسامان کے لیے چیلنج بن رہے ہیں۔ انہوں نے مزید کہا کہ جدید ہتھیاروں کے نظام رکھنے کے ساتھ ساتھ تیزی سے اختراع کرنے، بڑے پیمانے پر پیداوار کرنے اور دفاعی صلاحیتوں کو دوبارہ بحال کرنے کی استعداد بھی اب اتنی ہی اہم ہو گئی ہے۔

جناب راج ناتھ سنگھ نے اس بات پر زور دیتے ہوئے کہ تکنیکی اور پیداواری صلاحیتوں کے فروغ کے لیے سازگار ادارہ جاتی ماحول، ترقی پسندانہ پالیسیاں اور مؤثر طریقۂ کار ضروری ہیں، گزشتہ ایک دہائی کے دوران ہندوستان کے دفاعی صنعتی ڈھانچے کو مضبوط بنانے کے لیے کیے گئے اقدامات کی تفصیلات پیش کیں۔ ان اقدامات میں دفاعی صنعتی راہداریوں کا قیام اور سابقہ آرڈیننس فیکٹری بورڈ کو سات دفاعی سرکاری شعبے کے اداروں (ڈی پی ایس یوز) میں تبدیل کرنا شامل ہے، جن کا مقصد دفاعی پیداوار کے شعبے میں خود مختاری، کارکردگی اور مسابقتی صلاحیت کو بڑھانا ہے۔

وزیر دفاع نے جدید دفاعی پلیٹ فارمز اور نظاموں کی تیاری اور پیداوار میں نجی شعبے کی زیادہ سے زیادہ شمولیت کی حوصلہ افزائی کے لیے حکومت کے عزم کا اعادہ کیا۔ انہوں نے کہا کہ ایڈوانسڈ میڈیم کامبیٹ ایئرکرافٹ، پروپلشن سسٹمز، اے ٹی اے جی ایس، توپ خانے کے گولہ بارود اور جہاز سازی جیسے منصوبوں میں نجی شعبے کی شرکت کے مواقع سے مقامی سطح پر ترقی کے عمل میں تیزی آئے گی، پیداواری صلاحیت میں وسعت پیدا ہوگی اور عالمی دفاعی منڈی میں ہندوستان کی پوزیشن مضبوط ہوگی۔ انہوں نے کہا کہ ان اقدامات سے نجی صنعتوں، چھوٹی، بہت چھوٹی اور درمیانہ درجے کی صنعتوں (ایم ایس ایم ایز)، اسٹارٹ اپس اور تعلیمی اداروں کی وسیع تر شمولیت کے مواقع پیدا ہو رہے ہیں۔

جناب راج ناتھ سنگھ نے بتایا کہ وزارتِ دفاع میں 2025 کو اصلاحات کا سال قرار دیا گیا تھا، جس میں مشترکہ کارروائی، انضمام، ابھرتی ہوئی ٹیکنالوجیز، اختراع اور ملک کے دفاعی صنعتی نظام کو مضبوط بنانے پر توجہ مرکوز کی گئی۔ انہوں نے کہا کہ پالیسیوں، ادارہ جاتی ڈھانچوں، ٹیکنالوجی کی ترقی، حصولیابی کے طریقۂ کار اور کاروبار کرنے میں آسانی سے متعلق شروع کی گئی اصلاحات کے مثبت نتائج سامنے آ رہے ہیں۔ مالی سال 2025-26 میں دفاعی پیداوار ریکارڈ سطح پر پہنچ کر تقریباً 1.78 لاکھ کروڑ روپے ہو گئی، جبکہ دفاعی برآمدات بڑھ کر 38,424 کروڑ روپے تک پہنچ گئیں۔ انہوں نے مزید کہا کہ ہندوستانی دفاعی مصنوعات اب 80 سے زائد ممالک تک پہنچ رہی ہیں، جو سرکاری شعبے کے اداروں، نجی صنعتوں، چھوٹی، بہت چھوٹی اور درمیانی درجے کی صنعتوں اور اسٹارٹ اپس کے بڑھتے ہوئے تعاون کی عکاسی کرتی ہیں۔

وزیر دفاع نے دفاعی برآمدات کو ہندوستان کے خود انحصاری کے ایجنڈے کا ایک اہم پہلو قرار دیتے ہوئے کہا کہ برآمدات سے ملک کے مقامی صنعتی نظام کی پختگی، مقامی ٹیکنالوجیز کی مسابقتی صلاحیت اور ہندوستان کی استعداد پر بین الاقوامی شراکت داروں کے اعتماد کا اظہار ہوتا ہے۔ انہوں نے اس ترقی کا سہرا پالیسیوں میں مسلسل نرمی، طریقۂ کار کو آسان بنانے اور معیاری بنانے کے اقدامات کو دیا، جن کی بدولت ہندوستانی صنعت کار، بالخصوص چھوٹی، بہت چھوٹی اور درمیانہ  درجے کی صنعتیں، بین الاقوامی مواقع سے زیادہ مؤثر انداز میں فائدہ اٹھانے کے قابل ہوئے ہیں۔

جناب راج ناتھ سنگھ نے دفاعی برآمدات کے دائرہ کار کو وسیع کرتے ہوئے اس میں دیکھ بھال، مرمت، تربیت، رسد اور تکنیکی تعاون کو بھی شامل کرنے پر زور دیا۔ انہوں نے کہا کہ ہر کامیاب برآمد کو ایک دیرپا  اسٹریٹجک شراکت داری کی بنیاد بننا چاہیے۔ انہوں نے 2029 تک دفاعی پیداوار کو 3 لاکھ کروڑ روپے اور دفاعی برآمدات کو 50,000 کروڑ روپے تک پہنچانے کے حکومتی عزم کا اعادہ کیا۔ انہوں نے کہا کہ ان اہداف کے حصول کے لیے ملک کی دفاعی صنعت کو اپنی پیداواری صلاحیت میں اضافہ، معیار میں بہتری اور عالمی سطح پر مسابقتی صلاحیت کو مضبوط بنانا ہوگا۔

وزیر دفاع نے اس بات پر زور دیا کہ دفاعی افواج کو تحقیق و ترقی کے عمل میں اہم شراکت دار بنے رہنا چاہیے، کیونکہ ان کا عملی تجربہ اور میدانِ جنگ کی صورتِ حال سے متعلق ان کی سمجھ، تحقیقی ترجیحات کے تعین اور ابھرتی ہوئی ٹیکنالوجیز کی افادیت کا جائزہ لینے میں غیر معمولی اہمیت رکھتی ہے۔ اس کے ساتھ ہی انہوں نے تحقیق کے عمل میں آخری صارف کی فوری ضروریات سے آگے بڑھ کر سوچنے کی ضرورت پر بھی زور دیا۔ انہوں نے کہا کہ اگر تحقیق کو فوری عملی ضروریات کے نقطۂ نظر تک محدود کر دیا جائے تو اس کا نتیجہ صرف پہلے سے معلوم مسائل کے حل تک محدود ہو سکتا ہے، جبکہ ان امکانات کی کھوج نہیں ہو پائے گی جن کا ابھی تصور بھی نہیں کیا گیا ہے۔ انہوں نے کہا کہ تحقیق و ترقی کے عمل کو قائم شدہ مفروضات پر سوال اٹھانے، غیر روایتی خیالات پر کام کرنے اور ایسی ٹیکنالوجیز دریافت کرنے کی آزادی ہونی چاہیے جن کے استعمال کے امکانات فوری طور پر واضح نہ ہوں۔

جناب راج ناتھ سنگھ نے اس بات پر زور دیا کہ عملی ضروریات کو تحقیق کی سمت متعین کرنے میں رہنمائی فراہم کرنے کا موقع دیتے ہوئے اختراع کے لیے ضروری آزادی اور فکری گنجائش کو بھی برقرار رکھا جانا چاہیے، تاکہ دونوں کے درمیان مناسب توازن قائم ہو سکے۔ انہوں نے تجربات کی حوصلہ افزائی اور اس بات کو یقینی بنانے کی اہمیت بھی اجاگر کی کہ کامیاب اختراعات تجربہ گاہوں اور ابتدائی نمونوں تک محدود نہ رہیں، بلکہ انہیں پیداوار اور عملی استعمال کے مرحلے تک پہنچایا جائے۔ انہوں نے کہا کہ مقصد ایسا نظام تشکیل دینا ہونا چاہیے جس میں اختراع کی حوصلہ افزائی ہو، سرمایہ کاری کا تسلسل برقرار رہے اور کامیاب خیالات کو عملی صلاحیتوں میں تبدیل کیا جا سکے۔

بین الاقوامی دفاعی تعاون کے حوالے سے وزیر دفاع نے واضح کیا کہ ہندوستان کی خود انحصاری کی کوششوں کا مطلب دنیا سے کنارہ کشی اختیار کرنا نہیں ہے، بلکہ یہ ایک ایسے پراعتماد اور تکنیکی طور پر باصلاحیت ہندوستان کی علامت ہے جو بین الاقوامی شراکت داروں کے ساتھ تعاون کے لیے پہلے سے بہتر پوزیشن میں ہے۔ انہوں نے کہا کہ اگرچہ روایتی شراکت داریاں، جن کی بنیاد دفاعی سازوسامان کی خریداری، لائسنس کے تحت تیاری اور ٹیکنالوجی کی منتقلی پر رہی ہے، ہندوستان کی صنعتی صلاحیتوں کو فروغ دینے میں معاون ثابت ہوئی ہیں، تاہم مستقبل کی ضروریات اس سے زیادہ بلند عزائم پر مبنی ایسے طریقۂ کار کا تقاضا کرتی ہیں جس کی بنیاد مشترکہ ترقی، مشترکہ پیداوار اور اختراع میں شراکت داری ہو۔

جناب راج ناتھ سنگھ نے کہا، ’’ایسی شراکت داریوں کے ذریعے ڈیزائن اور ترقی کے عمل میں ہندوستان کی بامعنی شرکت، اہم ٹیکنالوجیز تک رسائی، دانشورانہ ملکیت کے حقوق کی مناسب تقسیم اور ہندوستانی کمپنیوں کے لیے عالمی سپلائی چین میں شرکت کے مواقع یقینی بنائے جانے چاہئیں۔ ہماری وسیع ملکی منڈی، پھیلتا ہوا صنعتی ڈھانچہ اور سائنسی و انجینئرنگ کے شعبوں میں باصلاحیت افراد کی بڑی تعداد بین الاقوامی کمپنیوں کو ہندوستانی صنعتوں کے ساتھ شراکت داری کے لیے اہم مواقع فراہم کرتی ہے۔‘‘

اپنے خطاب کے اختتام پر وزیر دفاع نے دفاعی افواج، سرکاری ملازمین، سائنس دانوں، صنعت کاروں، تعلیمی اداروں اور بین الاقوامی شراکت داروں سے اپیل کی کہ وہ ہندوستان کے دفاعی عزائم کی تکمیل کے لیے اجتماعی عزم کا مظاہرہ کریں۔ انہوں نے کہا کہ ملک کا مقصد دفاعی ٹیکنالوجیز کی خریداری سے آگے بڑھ کر انہیں خود تیار کرنے، ملکی ضروریات کے لیے پیداوار سے آگے بڑھ کر عالمی منڈیوں میں مقابلہ کرنے اور بین الاقوامی دفاعی شراکت داریوں میں محض حصہ لینے کے بجائے عالمی دفاعی ٹیکنالوجی کے مستقبل کی تشکیل میں بامعنی کردار ادا کرنے کی جانب پیش قدمی کرنا ہونا چاہیے۔ انہوں نے اعتماد ظاہر کیا کہ دہلی ڈیفنس ڈائیلاگ میں ہونے والی تبادلۂ خیال کی نشستوں سے اس وژن کی تکمیل کے لیے قیمتی خیالات اور قابلِ عمل تجاویز سامنے آئیں گی۔

اپنے استقبالیہ کلمات میں ایم پی-آئی ڈی ایس اے کے ڈائریکٹر جنرل، سفیر سجان آر چنائے نے اس بات کو اجاگر کیا کہ دہلی ڈیفنس ڈائیلاگ 2026 دفاعی اصلاحات، مقامی صلاحیتوں، بین الاقوامی تعاون اور دفاعی برآمدات کے حوالے سے مختلف نقطہ ہائے نظر کے تبادلے کے لیے ایک پلیٹ فارم فراہم کرے گا۔ انہوں نے پروپلشن سسٹمز اور دفاعی برآمدات کے موضوعات پر ایم پی-آئی ڈی ایس اے کی جانب سے منعقدہ دو ابتدائی گول میز کانفرنسوں کے علاوہ پہلی آسیان-انڈیا ڈیفنس تھنک ٹینک فورم کا بھی ذکر کیا، جن سے ادارے کے بین الاقوامی روابط مزید مستحکم ہوئے ہیں۔

اس موقع پر چیف آف انٹیگریٹڈ ڈیفنس اسٹاف (سی آئی ایس سی)، ایئر مارشل تیجندر سنگھ، ایڈیشنل سکریٹری محترمہ دیپتی موہل چاولہ، دیگر سینئر حاضر سروس اور ریٹائرڈ افسران کے علاوہ غیر ملکی معززین بھی موجود تھے۔

دہلی ڈیفنس ڈائیلاگ کے بارے میں

ایم پی-آئی ڈی ایس اے کے زیر اہتمام 3 اور 4 نومبر 2026 کو منعقد ہونے والا یہ دو روزہ ڈائیلاگ ہندوستان اور بیرونِ ملک سے تعلق رکھنے والے پالیسی سازوں، دفاعی افواج کے نمائندوں، دفاعی صنعت، تعلیمی اداروں، تھنک ٹینکس اور  اسٹریٹجک امور کے ماہرین کو ایک پلیٹ فارم پر جمع کرتا ہے، تاکہ ہندوستان کی بدلتی ہوئی دفاعی ترجیحات اور بین الاقوامی تعاون کے امکانات پر تبادلۂ خیال کیا جا سکے۔

اس ڈائیلاگ میں ہونے والی گفتگو کا محور ایسی قابلِ عمل پالیسی تجاویز پیش کرنا ہے جو ہندوستان کی دفاعی تیاری کو مضبوط بنانے، مقامی تکنیکی صلاحیتوں کو فروغ دینے اور بین الاقوامی دفاعی تعاون کے مواقع کو وسعت دینے میں معاون ثابت ہوں۔ اس ڈائیلاگ کا مقصد حکومت، صنعت، اصل سازوسامان تیار کرنے والی کمپنیوں (او ای ایمز)، چھوٹی، بہت چھوٹی اور درمیانہ  درجے کی صنعتوں (ایم ایس ایم ایز)، اسٹارٹ اپس اور تحقیقی اداروں کے درمیان زیادہ سے زیادہ رابطے اور تعاون کو فروغ دینا ہے۔ توقع ہے کہ اس کے نتائج پالیسی سازی کے لیے اہم معلومات اور تجاویز فراہم کریں گے اور خود انحصار و تکنیکی طور پر ترقی یافتہ دفاعی نظام کے ہندوستان کے  اسٹریٹجک وژن کو آگے بڑھانے میں معاون ہوں گے۔

2332136.title: Launch of “India S&T Scoreboard” on 3rd November 2026 in New Delhi
2332136.body_html:
NITI Aayog
Launch of “India S&T Scoreboard” on 3rd November 2026 in New Delhi
Posted On: 03 NOV 2026 5:37PM by PIB Delhi

NITI Aayog launched the “India S&T Scoreboard” on 3rd November 2026 at the Civil Services Officer’s Institute (CSOI), KG Marg, New Delhi. The Scoreboard was unveiled by Shri Ashok Kumar Lahiri, Vice Chairman, NITI Aayog. Developed as a key NITI Aayog initiative, the Scoreboard is an interactive platform that provides an integrated se se view of the science & technology landscape of Indian States and UTs. It has been designed to facilitate evidence-based policymaking and benchmarking across States/ UTs. Prof. Vivek Kumar Singh, Senior Adviser, NITI Aayog, welcomed the participants and set out the context and objectives of the exercise. He added that the Scoreboard has been built to go beyond the volume of output and capture quality, impact and collaboration, so that States can identify expertise and areas for focused action.

Prof. Umesh V. Waghmare, Secretary, Department of Science and Technology noted that the Scoreboard adds a valuable State-level picture to the national evidence base on science and technology, and highlighted the role of State S&T Councils and State universities in widening India’s research base. Dr. T. Srinivasa Kumar, Secretary, Ministry of Earth Sciences underscored that earth sciences are closely linked to every State, and that local capacity in science and technology is essential for States to make effective use of forecasts, early warnings and opportunities in the ocean sector.

Prof. Abhay Karandikar, Member (S&T), NITI Aayog emphasized that sound policy in science and technology must rest on reliable and comparable evidence. He observed that data on research and innovation has so far remained fragmented across multiple sources, making it difficult for States to assess where they stand. The Scoreboard addresses this gap by bringing ecosystem, publication and patent data together on a single interactive dashboard, with trends over years, so that States can track their progress over time.

Shri Ashok Kumar Lahiri, Vice Chairman, NITI Aayog emphasized that India’s further progress in science and technology requires a more active role by the States. Guided by the principle of cooperative and competitive federalism, he noted that the Scoreboard will help States identify their strengths and gaps, learn from one another, and design better programmes and policies in science and technology. He urged all States and UTs to make full use of the platform.

The Scoreboard brings together data on the S&T ecosystem, including higher education institutions, R&D institutions, deep tech startups, and incubators, along with S&T outputs like research publications and patents. Going beyond the volume of output, it presents indicators of research quality, impact, collaboration and open access across priority research areas and three sectors, namely Academia, Government R&D Labs and Industry. It also enables side by side comparison of States/ UTs and provides detailed State profiles, including State policies and best practices.

The launch was followed by a walkthrough of the Scoreboard and a technical session on its methodology and data sources. Distinguished invitees from state government and academia shared their observations and suggestions for the further development of the platform. Representatives of states noted that the platform will support their planning, and help build institutional capacity and skilled human resources in science and technology at the state level. The deliberations reaffirmed that a reliable and comparable evidence base on science and technology at the State level will play an important role in strengthening State S&T ecosystems and in advancing India’s journey towards the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047.

Access the India S&T scorecard here: www.sts.niti.gov.in

2332134.title: NHRC, India takes suo motu cognizance of the reported sale and trafficking of girl children from border districts of Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan to cities in Maharashtra
2332134.body_html:
National Human Rights Commission
NHRC, India takes suo motu cognizance of the reported sale and trafficking of girl children from border districts of Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan to cities in Maharashtra
​​​​​​​
Reportedly, parents sell their daughters to middlemen for Rs. 3 lakh to Rs. 5 lakh due to poverty and other reasons
The Commission issues notices to the Chief Secretaries and Directors General of Police of Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Maharashtra, calling for detailed reports on the matter within two weeks
Posted On: 03 NOV 2026 5:36PM by PIB Delhi

The National Human Rights Commission has taken suo motu cognizance of a media report that a large number of minor girl children are being sold for Rs. 3 lakh to Rs. 5 lakh by their parents to middlemen in several districts along the borders of Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan. Subsequently, these small girls are trafficked by middlemen with the help of false documents showing them as their adopted children. On gaining adulthood, they are sold for Rs. 35 lakh to Rs. 40 lakh in different cities of Maharashtra for sex trade after changing their personal details to hide their identities.

The Commission has observed that the contents of the news report, if true, raise serious issues of violation of the human rights of the victim girl children. Therefore, it has issued notices to the Chief Secretaries and Directors General of Police of Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Maharashtra, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks.

According to the media report, carried on 30th October 2026, parents sell their girl child due to poverty and other reasons. The media report has quoted four specific cases of such trafficked girls.

2332122.title: Devotees Offer Prayers and Pay Homage to Sacred Relics of Lord Buddha at Tawang Monastery
2332122.body_html:
Ministry of Culture
Devotees Offer Prayers and Pay Homage to Sacred Relics of Lord Buddha at Tawang Monastery
Large Numbers of Devotees Gather at Tawang Monastery to Seek Blessings of Holi relics
Special Exhibitions at the Monastery Showcase the Archaeological, Historical and Cultural Legacy of Buddhism
Posted On: 03 NOV 2026 5:28PM by PIB Delhi

The Sacred Exposition of the Holy Relics of Shakyamuni Buddha at Gaden Namgyal Lhatse (Tawang Monastery) has become a significant occasion of spiritual devotion and reverence for devotees from  Tawang and neighbouring regions of Arunachal Pradesh. During the first three days of the exposition, the monastery witnessed a large gathering of devotees, with long queues of people waiting to have a glimpse of the sacred relics, offer prayers and pay homage. The participation reflects the deep faith and devotion of the people towards Lord Buddha and his timeless teachings.

The exposition has been made accessible to Buddhist monks, senior citizens and the general public, providing devotees with an opportunity to pay homage to the sacred relics and experience their spiritual significance. It has also offered a rare opportunity for people to reconnect with the Buddha's enduring message of compassion, peace, wisdom and universal brotherhood.

Alongside the sacred exposition, visitors are being provided an opportunity to explore the rich heritage and diverse dimensions of Buddhist civilization through two special exhibitions. The exhibition titled ‘Unearthing the Sacred Piprahwa: The Story of the Holy Buddha Relics and Their Discovery’ Conducted by The International Buddhist Confederation (IBC), traces the archaeological history of the Piprahwa relics, highlighting their discovery in 1898 and their significance in Buddhist history. Another exhibition, ‘Crossroads of Dhamma: Classical Legacies, Living Art, and Anthropological Perspectives’, curated by the National Museum, New Delhi, showcases the historical, artistic and cultural evolution of Buddhism. Together, these exhibitions provide visitors with deeper insights into the rich and enduring legacy of Buddhism.

The sacred relics of Shakyamuni Buddha, brought from the National Museum, New Delhi, were ceremonially received by the Chief Minister of Arunachal Pradesh, Shri Pema Khandu, at the historic Tawang Monastery. The occasion was attended by Union Minister of Culture and Tourism, Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, along with venerable Buddhist monks, religious leaders and devotees, marking the commencement of the exposition in the state.

The exposition will continue at Tawang Monastery until November 7, 2026. Thereafter, the sacred relics will be taken to TGL Monastery (Lower Gompa), Bomdila, where they will be open for public veneration from November 8 to 13, 2026. The exposition will subsequently move to the Golden Pagoda, Namsai, from November 14 to 20, 2026. The sacred relics are scheduled to return to the National Museum, New Delhi, on November 21, 2026.

***

M Annadurai

2332107.title: NLMC Organises Pre-Bid Meeting for E-Auction of 5.119-Acre HIL (India) Limited Land Parcel in New Delhi
2332107.body_html:
Ministry of Finance
NLMC Organises Pre-Bid Meeting for E-Auction of 5.119-Acre HIL (India) Limited Land Parcel in New Delhi
Third e-auction publicly advertised by NLMC in the last two months reflects the Government's continued thrust on monetisation of surplus public sector land assets
Strategically located land parcel on Rohtak Road carries a reserve price of ₹829.69 crore and offers development potential of FSI 400 under applicable TOD provisions
Posted On: 03 NOV 2026 5:11PM by PIB Delhi

The National Land Monetization Corporation (NLMC), under the administrative control of the Department of Public Enterprises (DPE), Ministry of Finance, Government of India, organised a Pre-Bid Meeting in New Delhi today, in connection with the proposed e-auction of a strategically located land parcel owned by HIL (India) Limited.

The meeting was organised to familiarise prospective bidders with the property's location, key features, development potential, applicable land-use provisions, eligibility requirements and the terms and conditions governing the e-auction. Representatives from NLMC, HIL (India) Limited and CBRE India, the transaction advisor, participated in the meeting and provided detailed information to prospective bidders regarding the property and the bidding process.

The Pre-Bid Meeting provided a platform for prospective participants to interact with the concerned officials, seek clarifications on the Request for Proposal (RFP), understand the technical and financial bid submission requirements and obtain information necessary for informed participation in the e-auction.

Third E-Auction by NLMC in Two Months: Advancing the Government's Land Monetisation Agenda

The proposed monetisation of the HIL (India) Limited land parcel marks the third e-auction publicly advertised by NLMC in the last two months. This reflects the sustained efforts being undertaken by the Government of India to accelerate the monetisation of surplus and underutilised land and other non-core assets of Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs).

Through these successive e-auctions, NLMC is facilitating the identification, structuring and monetisation of public-sector land assets, with the objective of unlocking their economic value and enabling their productive utilisation through transparent and competitive processes.

The initiative is aligned with the Government's broader asset monetisation programme, which seeks to unlock the value of existing public assets, encourage private-sector participation and facilitate the generation of resources for further economic development.

Speaking on the occasion, Mr. Rohan Chand Thakur (IAS), Chief Executive Officer, National Land Monetization Corporation (NLMC), said, "The Government of India has accorded significant priority to the monetisation of surplus and underutilised land assets of Central Public Sector Enterprises. The third e-auction publicly advertised by NLMC within the last two months reflects our continued efforts to translate this priority into tangible outcomes. Our endeavour is to unlock the economic value of public assets through transparent, structured and competitive processes while facilitating their productive utilisation. The HIL land parcel, given its strategic location and development potential, presents an opportunity for eligible participants to explore its future utilisation. The Pre-Bid Meeting is an important step towards ensuring clarity, transparency and informed participation in the bidding process."

Mr. Kuldeep Singh, Chairman and Managing Director, HIL (India) Limited, stated,

"The land parcel being offered for outright sale is strategically located on Rohtak Road, Shivaji Marg, New Delhi, and represents a significant asset of HIL (India). Spread over approximately 5.119 acres, the property offers substantial development potential, with an FSI of 400 along with the applicable FSI based on TOD provisions, subject to the prescribed statutory conditions and approvals. Through this monetisation initiative, we seek to facilitate the productive utilisation of the asset while providing prospective developers and eligible bidders an opportunity to participate in its future development. We encourage interested participants to examine the auction documents and actively participate in the competitive bidding process."

Strategic Location and Development Potential

The land parcel being offered for outright sale measures approximately 5.119 acres and is situated in the Najafgarh Industrial Area, along Rohtak Road, Shivaji Marg, New Delhi. The property enjoys a prominent location with approximately 140 metres of frontage along Rohtak Road, offering visibility and connectivity to key parts of the National Capital.

The site also benefits from connectivity through the Delhi Metro's Green Line, providing convenient public transport access. Its location, accessibility and surrounding urban infrastructure make it a significant property with potential for suitable redevelopment and future utilisation, subject to applicable regulations and statutory approvals.

The property has an indicated development potential of FSI up to 400 along with the applicable FSI based on TOD provisions, subject to the applicable provisions of the Master Plan for Delhi 2021, relevant redevelopment policies, statutory requirements and approvals from the competent authorities. The reserve price for the land parcel has been fixed at ₹829.69 crore.

Key Features and Auction Parameters

During the meeting, prospective bidders were apprised of the important features and participation conditions of the proposed e-auction, including:

  • Property Area: Approximately 5.119 acres.
  • Location: Najafgarh Industrial Area, Rohtak Road, Shivaji Marg, New Delhi.
  • Road Frontage: Approximately 140 metres along Rohtak Road.
  • Development Potential: FSI of 400 under applicable TOD provisions, subject to statutory conditions and approvals.
  • Reserve Price: ₹829.69 crore.
  • Mode of Sale: Outright sale through an online e-auction.
  • Bidding Parameter: Highest auction price, with bidding in multiples of ₹1 crore per acre.
  • Consortium Participation: Permitted, with a maximum of three members.
  • EMD Payment: Through Bank Guarantee or NEFT/RTGS, as stipulated in the RFP.
  • Land Use: Industrial use, with conversion permissible subject to applicable norms and approvals.
  • Applicable Policy: Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) Policy, as applicable.

The participants were also briefed on the process for registration, submission of technical bids, compliance with eligibility criteria, payment of the Earnest Money Deposit (EMD) and participation in the online auction. The meeting provided an opportunity to clarify procedural and technical aspects of the transaction and familiarise prospective bidders with the prescribed bidding framework.

NLMC's Role in Advancing Public Asset Monetisation

The National Land Monetization Corporation (NLMC) is a wholly owned Government of India company functioning under the administrative control of the Department of Public Enterprises, Ministry of Finance. It has been established to undertake and facilitate the monetisation of surplus land and building assets of Central Public Sector Enterprises and other Government agencies.

NLMC works in coordination with concerned CPSEs and other stakeholders to identify surplus and underutilised assets, undertake the necessary transaction structuring and facilitate their monetisation through transparent and competitive mechanisms.

The ongoing series of e-auctions, including the proposed HIL (India) Limited land parcel sale, represents the continued operationalisation of the Government's asset monetisation agenda. These initiatives are aimed at unlocking the value of public assets, promoting efficient asset management and encouraging private-sector participation in their productive utilisation.

E-Auction and Bid Submission Details

The e-auction is being conducted through the designated NLMC e-auction portal.

Interested and eligible bidders can access the detailed Request for Proposal (RFP), property particulars, eligibility conditions, auction terms and other relevant documents through the following portal:

  • E-Auction Portal: https://nlmc.enivida.com
  • Last Date for Submission of Technical Bids: 19 November 2026
  • Time: 1400 hours

Prospective bidders are encouraged to review the RFP and all accompanying documents carefully and complete the registration and bid submission formalities within the stipulated timeline.

Through the proposed monetisation, NLMC and HIL (India) Limited aim to facilitate the optimal utilisation of a strategically located public-sector land asset while providing eligible participants an opportunity to participate in its future development.

About National Land Monetization Corporation (NLMC)

The National Land Monetization Corporation (NLMC) is a Government of India entity under the administrative control of the Department of Public Enterprises, Ministry of Finance. NLMC has been established to undertake the monetisation of surplus land and building assets of Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) and other Government agencies. It plays an important role in the Government's asset monetisation programme by facilitating the identification, aggregation and monetisation of surplus and underutilised public assets.

For further information:

National Land Monetization Corporation (NLMC)
Department of Public Enterprises
Ministry of Finance, Government of India

Website: https://nlmc.dpe.gov.in
E-Auction Portal: https://nlmc.enivida.com
