2332088.title: Union Minister Dr Virendra Kumar to Launch ‘Vayo Samman Rashtriya Abhiyan’, a National Intergenerational Bonding Campaign, Tomorrow in National Capital
2332088.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Union Minister Dr Virendra Kumar to Launch ‘Vayo Samman Rashtriya Abhiyan’, a National Intergenerational Bonding Campaign, Tomorrow in National Capital
Campaign to promote sustained intergenerational engagement through the ‘5C’ model of Connect, Converse, Co-create, Contribute and Continue
Vayo SAATHI Volunteer Initiative To Mobilise Citizens Aged 18 Years And Above For The Welfare, Care And Social Inclusion Of Senior Citizens
Handbook Outlining The Campaign Framework And Implementation Roles Of States, Districts And Community Institutions To Be Released
Department To Sign MoUs With Shri Ram Chandra Mission And Adhyatma Vigyan Satsang Kendra, Jodhpur, To Promote Wellness And Intergenerational Engagement Among Senior Citizens
Posted On: 03 NOV 2026 4:54PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, will launch the ‘Vayo Samman Rashtriya Abhiyan’ – National Intergenerational Bonding Campaign under the Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY), in National Capital here tomorrow. 

Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment, Dr. Virendra Kumar, will formally launch the campaign, marking an important step towards strengthening intergenerational solidarity and promoting a society that values the experience, wisdom and contribution of senior citizens.

A Senior Official in the Ministry said the national campaign seeks to institutionalise meaningful and sustained engagement between senior citizens and younger generations, fostering mutual respect, understanding, companionship and shared responsibility.

He said the Vayo Samman Rashtriya Abhiyan is not merely a welfare campaign, but a nationwide social movement to institutionalise intergenerational solidarity, recognise senior citizens as contributors to society and mobilise youth participation in the cause of dignified ageing.

The Official added the Campaign envisages intergenerational bonding as a community-driven movement, encouraging families, educational institutions, youth organisations, voluntary organisations and local institutions to create opportunities for meaningful interaction and collaboration between generations.

The Ministry Official said the Vayo Samman Rashtriya Abhiyan seeks to respond to the emerging challenges by creating an enabling environment in which the younger generation can learn from the life experiences, knowledge, skills and cultural heritage of senior citizens, while older persons can benefit from the energy, technological awareness and contemporary perspectives of youth.

 

The initiative recognises senior citizens not merely as beneficiaries of welfare programmes but as active contributors, mentors and valuable repositories of knowledge, culture and social experience, he added.

The Official noted that India is undergoing a significant demographic transition, with the population of senior citizens steadily increasing adding the population aged 60 years and above is projected to grow from approximately 10 crore in 2011 to 23 crore by 2036, with its share in the total population rising from 8.4 per cent to 14.9 per cent.

Alongside this demographic shift, urbanisation, migration, changing family structures and evolving social patterns have, in many instances, reduced opportunities for regular interaction between generations, he said.

The Official said these developments underline the need for a structured and sustained approach to addressing social isolation, strengthening community support systems and ensuring that senior citizens remain active, respected and meaningfully connected with society.

He further said the Abhiyan is structured around an innovative ‘5C’ model – Connect, Converse, Co-create, Contribute and Continue, which provides a practical framework for building meaningful relationships between generations and sustaining them through regular community participation.

The five components seek to Connect by creating opportunities for senior citizens and younger generations to interact through community platforms, educational institutions and social initiatives, Converse to encourage dialogue, storytelling, exchange of experiences and mutual understanding between generations, Co-create to facilitate joint activities, creative initiatives and collaborative projects drawing upon the complementary strengths of senior citizens and youth, Contribute to enable both generations to contribute their knowledge, skills, time and capabilities towards community welfare and social development and Continue to ensure that intergenerational engagement evolves into a regular, sustained and community-led practice rather than remaining limited to one-time activities.

The Official informed that the Campaign will be implemented across twelve thematic areas, offering diverse opportunities for participation and collaboration. These include ‘30 Minutes Together’, ‘Teach Me – I'll Teach You’, ‘My Story, My India’, ‘Digital Dada-Dadi / Digital Saathi’, ‘Generation Health & Wellness’ and ‘Silver Skills – Seniors as Mentors’, among other activities.

He said through these themes, the Abhiyan will promote companionship, oral history and cultural exchange, digital literacy, health awareness, wellness, skill-sharing and mentorship.

It will also encourage young people to assist senior citizens in navigating digital services and identifying potential cyber fraud, thereby strengthening their confidence and safety in an increasingly technology-driven environment, he said.

The Official elaborated that a key component of the launch will be the introduction of Vayo SAATHI – Support, Awareness, Assistance, Training, Health and Inclusion, a digitally enabled volunteer initiative designed to mobilise citizens and institutions in support of the welfare, dignity and social inclusion of senior citizens.

He said the initiative seeks to develop a nationwide network of volunteers who can contribute their time, skills and resources to support older persons at the grassroots level. It is open to all citizens aged 18 years and above, including students, young professionals, community volunteers, civil society organisations and institutional partners, he further said.

Under the initiative, volunteers will be encouraged to serve as friends, facilitators, connectors and support persons for senior citizens, helping them access relevant information, welfare services, community activities, digital assistance and other forms of support, the Official said. He added that the framework will complement and strengthen existing institutional and community-based support systems.

The Ministry Official said the interested citizens can register as Vayo SAATHI volunteers through the Senior Citizens Welfare (SCW) SAMAVESH Portal or the JEEVAN App. Registered volunteers will also receive a Vayo SAATHI Certificate in recognition of their participation and contribution.

Through this initiative, the Ministry seeks to transform volunteerism into a structured, accessible and scalable mechanism for community participation in senior citizens' welfare, he added.

Union Minister is also scheduled to release a Handbook on Vayo Samman Rashtriya Abhiyan on the occasion. The Handbook will serve as a guiding document for the campaign, detailing its objectives, implementation framework, thematic activities and mechanisms for community participation.

It will also delineate the roles and responsibilities of States, Districts and community institutions, facilitating coordinated implementation and wider outreach across the country. The Handbook is intended to support the adoption of the campaign at different administrative and community levels and encourage active participation by educational institutions, youth groups, voluntary organisations and other stakeholders.

As part of the launch programme, the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment will sign two Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) with Shri Ram Chandra Mission (SRCM) and Adhyatma Vigyan Satsang Kendra (AVSK), Jodhpur.

These partnerships aim to promote the holistic wellbeing of senior citizens through meditation, yoga and other wellness-oriented programmes. They will also support intergenerational engagement through community-based activities and sensitisation initiatives, including pledge drives and walkathons, encouraging greater public awareness and collective responsibility towards the welfare of older persons.

These collaborations reflect the Ministry’s commitment to engaging civil society organisations and other institutional partners in expanding the reach of senior citizens' welfare initiatives and promoting healthy, active and dignified ageing.

The Vayo Samman Rashtriya Abhiyan represents a broader effort to strengthen the social fabric through intergenerational solidarity and collective participation. By bringing senior citizens and youth together on common platforms, the campaign seeks to promote a culture in which experience and innovation complement each other, traditional wisdom is valued, and older persons remain integral to community life.

The Department of Social Justice and Empowerment invites citizens, educational institutions, universities, youth organisations, NGOs, resident welfare associations, community institutions and Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) partners to actively participate in the campaign and register as Vayo SAATHI volunteers.

Through sustained public participation, institutional partnerships and community-led initiatives, the Abhiyan aspires to build a society in which senior citizens lead lives marked by dignity, respect, security, active participation and inclusion, while younger generations develop a deeper appreciation of their responsibilities towards older persons.

The campaign seeks to reinforce the principle that the welfare of senior citizens is not merely a governmental responsibility but a shared social commitment, requiring the active participation of every generation.

It is pertinent to mention that Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY) is a flagship initiative of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment aimed at promoting the welfare, care, protection and empowerment of senior citizens. Through its various interventions, the scheme seeks to facilitate an enabling environment for older persons to lead healthy, active, dignified and productive lives, with access to appropriate support services and opportunities for social participation.

2332003.body_html:
Prime Minister's Office
Text of PM’s address at the Foundation Stone Laying Ceremony of Pune Metro Projects
Posted On: 03 NOV 2026 2:29PM by PIB Delhi

महाराष्ट्र के राज्यपाल जिष्णु देव वर्मा जी, मुख्यमंत्री श्री देवेंद्र फडणवीस जी, केंद्रीय मंत्रिमंडल के मेरे साथी मनोहर लाल जी, महाराष्ट्र के डिप्टी सीएम एकनाथ शिंदे जी, श्रीमती सुनेत्रा अजित पवार जी, सभी मंत्री, सांसद और विधायकगण, अन्य जन-प्रतिनिधि, और पुणे के मेरे प्यारे भाइयों और बहनों!

दिवाली अगदी जवल आली आहे, सर्वप्रथम तुम्हा सर्वांना, दिवालीच्या खूप खूप शुभेच्छा!

साथियों,

त्योहारों की खुशियां तब और बढ़ जाती हैं, जब जीवन में कोई नई सुविधा जुड़ती है। आज पुणे के लोगों के लिए ऐसा ही एक सुखद अवसर है। मुझे खुशी है कि आज पुणे मेट्रो की एक और लाइन का लोकार्पण हो रहा है।10 वर्ष पहले मुझे पुणे में पहले चरण के काम का, शिलान्यास का अवसर मिला था। अब हिंज़वडी से शिवाजीनगर के बीच मेट्रो शुरु होने से,पुणे के एक बड़े आईटी हब को बेहतर कनेक्टिविटी मिलेगी। आज जिस नई लाइन पर काम शुरु हुआ है, उससे पुणे के पुराने और नए इलाकों के बीच कनेक्टिविटी और मजबूत होगी। मैं पुणे और महाराष्ट्र के सभी लोगों को बहुत-बहुत बधाई देता हूं।

साथियों,

पुणे शहर हमेशा से ऐसे विचारों का केंद्र रहा है, जिनसे राष्ट्र को, समाज को नई दिशा मिली है। आज पुणे, विकसित भारत की नई ऊर्जा को भी दिशा दे रहा है। आईटी, ऑटोमोबाइल, फार्मा, स्टार्टअप्स, इनोवेशन से लेकर मैन्युफेक्चरिंग तक, पुणे, देश के युवाओं के लिए सपनों और संकल्प का स्थान है। और ऐसे में मजबूत होती यहां की मेट्रो कनेक्टिविटी, पुणे शहर के विकास को नई गति देने जा रही है।

साथियों,

पुणे मेट्रो का लोकार्पण, इसका विस्तार, ये दिखाता है कि विकसित भारत के लिए, हम कैसे शहरों का निर्माण कर रहे हैं। पहले किसी शहर की पहचान, उसके उद्योगों से होती थी। या वहां के किसी प्रसिद्ध खान-पान या फल-फसल से होती थी। लेकिन आज शहरों की पहचान के साथ, दो और कसौटियां जुड़ गई हैं। एक, कोई शहर कितना कंपीटिटिव है, और दूसरा, वहां ईज़ ऑफ लिविंग का क्या स्तर है? मेट्रो प्रोजेक्ट, इन दोनों कसौटियों में किसी भी शहर को और बेहतर बनाता है। पुणे मेट्रो का जितना विस्तार हो रहा है, उससे समय भी बच रहा है और पुणे वासियों को ज्यादा सुविधा भी मिल रही है। और हम सब जानते हैं, जब शहर का समय बचता है, तो शहर की Productivity बढ़ती है। जब शहर की Productivity बढ़ती है, तो देश की Economy को गति मिलती है। और जब इकॉनॉमी बढ़ती है, तो गरीब और मिडिल क्लास, दोनों को उसका फायदा होता है।

साथियों,

आज का ये दिन प्रो-पीपल, प्रो एक्टिव गुड गवर्नेंस का भी उदाहरण है। हमारे देश में पहली मेट्रो 1984 में चली थी। उसके बाद के 30 साल में, सिर्फ दो सौ अड़तालीस किलोमीटर मेट्रो लाइन बनी, Two Hundred and Forty Eight Kilometre. 2014 तक देश में सिर्फ 5 शहरों में मेट्रो चल रही थी। अगर वही पुरानी सोच चलती, पुरानी सरकार रहती, पुरानी कार्यसंस्कृति रहती, तो पुणे में मेट्रो को पहुंचने में कई दशक और लग जाते। लेकिन 2014 में जब देश ने NDA को सेवा का मौका दिया, तो हम एक संकल्प लेकर चले। ये संकल्प था, शहर में रहने वाले मिडिल क्लास की ईज़ ऑफ लिविंग, ईज ऑफ ट्रांसपोर्टेशन, और इसका नतीजा आज हम देख रहे हैं। बीते 12 वर्षों में देश में मेट्रो ट्रांसपोर्ट का कायाकल्प हो चुका है। 2014 में जहां दो सौ अड़तालीस किलोमीटर मेट्रो रूट था, अब ये बढ़कर करीब 1200 किलोमीटर हो चुका है। 2014 में जहां सिर्फ 5 शहरों में मेट्रो चल रही थी, अब देश के 26 शहरों में मेट्रो चलने लगी है। अब हर रोज मेट्रो में एक करोड़ से ज्यादा लोग ट्रेवेल कर रहे हैं। आज भारतीय मेट्रो नेटवर्क, दुनिया के टॉप थ्री मेट्रो नेटवर्क में गिना जाता है।

साथियों,

जैसी स्थिति बाकी देश में थी, वही हालात महाराष्ट्र के भी थे। 2014 में जब पहली बार NDA की डबल इंजन सरकार बनी, तब महाराष्ट्र में 10-11 किलोमीटर ही मेट्रो लाइन चालू थी। आज महाराष्ट्र में, करीब पौने दो सौ किलोमीटर की मेट्रो लाइन सेवा में है। 680 किलोमीटर से अधिक की मेट्रो लाइन्स पर काम हो रहा है। आज सिर्फ मेट्रो इंफ्रास्ट्रक्चर पर ही महाराष्ट्र में, ढाई लाख करोड़ रुपए से अधिक का निवेश किया जा रहा है। ये पैसा, श्रमिक की जेब में जा रहा है, ये पैसा, इंजीनियर्स को रोजगार दे रहा है। ये पैसा, दुकानों में, फैक्ट्रियों में रोजगार बना रहा है।

साथियों,

ये मेट्रो प्रोजेक्ट, एक और कारण से भी विशेष है। इस मेट्रो लाइन का निर्माण, पीपीपी मॉडल से हुआ है। यानी ये सरकार और प्राइवेट सेक्टर के साझा प्रयासों से बना है। ये विकास का एक ऐसा मॉडल है, जिसकी सफलता से देश की प्रगति को और गति मिलेगी।

साथियों,

आज विकसित भारत बनाने के लिए, भारत का एक-एक नागरिक, भारत का हर युवा बेटा-बेटी पूरी ताकत से जुटे हैं। आज हर कोई बड़े आत्मविश्वास से कह रहा है- We Will Do It. We Will Do It. ये भाव, पूरे देश में है। बीते 12 वर्षों में देश की ऊर्जा, गांव की सड़कों, हाईवे-एक्सप्रेसवे, नई रेल लाइनों का बिजलीकरण, लंबी-लंबी टनल, ऊंचे-ऊंचे पुल, इनके निर्माण में अनेक विविध योजनाएं नए-नए प्रकल्प साकार कर रही है। अब आने वाले वर्षों में इसके साथ ही, देश अपनी ऊर्जा. अपने शहरों को दुनिया के Best शहरों में से एक बनाने में लगाने वाला है।

साथियों,

हमारे शहर केवल रहने की जगह नहीं हैं। ये देश की Economic Activity के बड़े केंद्र भी हैं। हमें देश के सैकड़ों छोटे शहरों को, Growth Hubs भी बनाना है इसी विजन के साथ इस साल फरवरी में, Urban Challenge Fund को स्वीकृति दी गई थी। इस Fund के लिए, एक लाख करोड़ रुपए की मदद केंद्र सरकार दे रही है। इससे आने वाले वर्षों में देश के शहरों में, लाखों करोड़ रुपए का निवेश जुटाने का लक्ष्य है। मैं स्थानीय निकायों को, प्राइवेट सेक्टर के साथियों को, सभी को आगे आने का आग्रह करता हूं। हम सभी को मिशन मोड पर जुटना है। मुझे विश्वास है, कि महाराष्ट्र इसमें अपनी भूमिका का और विस्तार करेगा।

साथियों,

आज दो और कारणों से दुनिया में भारत की बहुत चर्चा हो रही है। एक, भारत ने मुश्किल वैश्विक परिस्थितियों में भी, दुनिया में सबसे तेज़ विकास की गति जारी रखी है। और दूसरा, भारत में सिर्फ 10-12 वर्षों के भीतर ही 50 करोड़ लोगों ने भीषण गरीबी को परास्त किया है। ये वर्ल्ड बैंक की ताज़ा रिपोर्ट में सामने आया है। देश की अनेक पीढ़ियां, गरीबी हटाने के वादों और दावों के बीच ही बड़ी हुई हैं। पहले, गरीबी से लड़ाई सिर्फ नारों में थी, आज भारत गरीबी को धरातल पर पराजित कर रहा है।

साथियों,

आज भारत वो देश है, जो Fastest Growing Economy भी है, और Fastest Poverty reducer भी है। ये दोनों सिद्धियां एक दूसरे से जुड़ी हुई हैं। भारत की अर्थव्यवस्था तेज़ी से बढ़ रही है, भारत का बजट बढ़ रहा है, देशवासियों पर ज्यादा निवेश हो रहा है, पहले जो पैसा, घोटालों और भाई भतीजावाद में लीकेज में जाता था, अब सीधा लाभार्थी तक पहुंच रहा है। जब देश के खज़ाने का पैसा, रोड, रेल, एयरपोर्ट, मेट्रो में लगता है, जब सरकार, बिजली, पानी, गैस पाइपलाइन पर निवेश बढ़ाती है, तब लोगों का जीवन भी सुधरता है और उनके लिए रोजगार के मौके भी बढ़ते हैं।

साथियों,

गरीबों के घर, टॉयलेट, हर घर जल, गैस कनेक्शन, ऐसी सुविधाओं से लोगों का आत्मविश्वास बढ़ा है, उनका समय बच रहा है। और ये समय, अपने परिवार के लिए अतिरिक्त कमाई में उपयोग हो रहा है।

साथियों,

पिछले महीने ही मुझे आप सब के आशीर्वाद से सरकार के मुखिया के तौर पर काम करते हुए 25 वर्ष पूरे हुए हैं। हमारी सरकार का हमेशा से मंत्र रहा है कि गरीब को सशक्त करो तो गरीब में अपनी गरीबी से बाहर निकलने का साहस आ जाता है। मुझे याद है, जब मैं गुजरात में मुख्यमंत्री था, तो इसी सोच के साथ मैंने गरीब कल्याण मेले की परंपरा शुरु की थी। इन मेलों में गरीब कल्याण की स्कीमों की डिलिवरी पर फोकस होता था। गरीबों को मंच पर आमंत्रित किया जाता था। वे गरीबी को परास्त करने का संकल्प लेते थे, एक आत्मविश्वास लेकर आयोजन से लौटते थे।

साथियों,

वो जो काम 25 साल पहले मैंने शुरू किया, वो आज तक अनवरत चल रहा है। इसी को मैं, पावर टू एंपावर कहता हूँ। पावर टू एंपावर, यही सुशासन है। यानी ये परिवर्तन एकदम नहीं आया है। सरकारें नारे लगाते लगाते थक चुकी हैं  भूतकाल में। हमने एक-एक कड़ी को जोड़ा है। एक-एक जिंदगी के सपनों को बुना है। ये वर्षों के सोचे-समझे और योजनाबद्ध प्रयासों का परिणाम है। और इसलिए, 50 करोड़ भारतीयों ने गरीबी को पराजित किया है।

साथियों,

जब गरीबी घटती है, तो फायदा केवल उन परिवारों को नहीं होता, जो इस कुचक्र से बाहर निकलते हैं। ये देश की इकॉनमी में एक नई जान फूंकता है। ये एक नए मिडिल क्लास को जन्म देता है। नियो मिडिल क्लास नए सपने लेकर के आता है। जिसकी परचेज़िंग पावर, बाज़ार को गति देती है। दुकानों से लेकर फैक्ट्रियों तक नई संभावनाएं बनती हैं। यानी भारत में कम होती गरीबी, भारत की अर्थव्यवस्था को नई ऊंचाई पर ले जा रही है।

साथियों,

विकसित भारत की इस यात्रा में, हमारे किसान भाई-बहनों की भी बड़ी भूमिका रहती है। और इसलिए हमारी सरकार, किसान बहनों-भाइयों को निरंतर सशक्त कर रही है। हालांकि महाराष्ट्र में मौसम की बेरुखी के कारण, अनेकों किसान परिवारों को इस समय मुश्किल हो रही है। पिछले कुछ सालों में, देवेंद्र फडणवीस जी के नेतृत्व में, जल संरक्षण का बहुत सारा काम हुआ है। लेकिन इस प्राकृतिक आपदा ने बड़ी परेशानी पैदा कर दी है। मैं महाराष्ट्र के प्रत्येक किसान भाई-बहन को ये भरोसा देता हूं, कि संकट के इस समय में एनडीए सरकार, पूरी संवेदनशीलता के साथ किसानों के साथ खड़ी है। महाराष्ट्रातील दुष्काड़ाची मला माहिती आहे. राज्य सरकारने आगाऊ मदत सुद्धा दिली आहे. मी पीएम किसानचा निधी जमा केला. अजिबात काड़जी, करु नका, आम्ही सारे शेतकड़यांसोबत आहोत.

साथियों,

मैं देशवासियों से भी कहूंगा, ये तीज-त्योहार का समय है। हमें अपने किसान बहन-भाइयों को याद रखना है। उनके घर भी दीवाली की खुशियां बनी रहे, इसका हमें ध्यान रखना है। ये सामाजिक जिम्मेदारी भी है, जो हमारे सूखा पीड़ित नागरिक हैं, किसान भाई-बहन हैं, जो अन्य लोग गांवों में रहते हैं, उनकी तकलीफों को भी हमें नहीं भूलना है। हम सब मिलकर ही इस आपदा का सामना करेंगे।

साथियों,

सबका प्रयास, एकजुट प्रयास, यही विकसित भारत की प्राणवायु है। इसी भावना से हमें देश के विकास में जुटे रहना है। एक बार फिर, आप सभी को मेट्रो परियोजनाओं की शुभकामनाएं। आने वाले त्योंहारों की बहुत-बहुत शुभकामनाएं। आपका बहुत-बहुत आभार! पुणेवासी मेरे साथ बोलिये, जोर से पूरी ताकत से, दोनों हाथ ऊपर करके बोलिये -

भारत माता की जय!

भारत माता की जय!

भारत माता की जय!

2331985.title: From Alcohol Addiction To A Healthier Life
2331985.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Alcohol Addiction To A Healthier Life
 NAPDDR Enabled Pedhapalli Telangana’s Ramesh Kumar’s Recovery and Rehabilitation
Posted On: 03 NOV 2026 1:59PM by PIB Delhi

For Ramesh Kumar (name changed), the NAPDDR Scheme represents more than access to de-addiction treatment. It has provided an opportunity to overcome addiction, restore his confidence and rebuild his life with dignity.

His journey reflects the importance of timely intervention, professional rehabilitation, family support and sustained follow-up care in helping individuals overcome substance dependence and reintegrate into society.

The 40 year Ramesh Kumar, a resident of Pedhapalli district of Telangana, faced significant personal, family and professional challenges due to alcohol addiction. His alcohol consumption began during his early adult years, influenced by peer pressure and negative social influences, and gradually developed into addiction. Over time, this adversely affected his health, family relationships, behaviour and employment.

He experienced emotional distress, withdrew from social activities and struggled to maintain financial and professional stability. Despite these difficulties, he remained willing to seek treatment and rebuild his life, while his family continued to extend support throughout his journey towards recovery.

A significant turning point came through the intervention under the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR) Scheme of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. Through the Integrated Rehabilitation Centre for Addicts (IRCA), operated by Prakriti Environment Society in Pedhapalli, Telangana, he received comprehensive de-addiction treatment and rehabilitation services.

The support included medical supervision, individual and family counselling, group therapy, motivational enhancement, relapse prevention therapy and regular follow-up sessions.

The rehabilitation programme helped him develop effective coping mechanisms, regain self-confidence and address the emotional and psychological challenges associated with addiction. He also received vocational guidance, medical intervention and support for social reintegration. Continuous counselling and family participation played an important role in strengthening his commitment to recovery and helping him maintain a healthier lifestyle.

The intervention has brought a positive transformation in his personal and professional life. Ramesh has successfully overcome alcohol dependence and is now sober and regularly employed.

His employment has become more stable, and he currently earns approximately Rs 12,000–15,000 per month. The improvement in his health, emotional well-being and financial stability has also contributed to better family circumstances.

2331966.title: SUVIKALP- Mine Repurposing Tool; Transforming Closed and Abandoned Mines into Productive Assets
2331966.body_html:
Ministry of Coal
SUVIKALP- Mine Repurposing Tool; Transforming Closed and Abandoned Mines into Productive Assets
Posted On: 03 NOV 2026 1:30PM by PIB Delhi

Mine closure is an integral part of the mining lifecycle. However, the responsibility towards a mining region does not end with the completion of mining operations. Ensuring productive utilisation of post-mining land, environmental restoration and sustainable socio-economic development requires a structured approach to mine repurposing. Recognising this need, the Coal Controller Organisation (CCO), under the Ministry of Coal, Government of India, has developed SUVIKALP – Mine Repurposing Tool, a digital decision-support platform aligned with the Mining Plan Guidelines for Coal and Lignite Mine, 2025.

SUVIKALP aims to establish a scientific, transparent and standardised framework for identifying suitable post-mining land-use opportunities. It addresses the challenges associated with fragmented assessments, independent evaluation of multiple parameters and limited integration of community priorities in conventional mine repurposing decisions.

Scientific and Data-Driven Assessment

SUVIKALP brings together geo-mining characteristics, environmental conditions, infrastructure availability, resource constraints, financial considerations and socio-economic factors within a unified digital platform. Users can create a comprehensive site profile by entering relevant mine-specific information, enabling systematic assessment of potential repurposing alternatives against the characteristics and constraints of individual mine sites.

The platform employs a Multi-Criteria Decision-Making (MCDM) methodology based on TOPSIS (Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution) to evaluate and rank potential repurposing options. This approach facilitates objective comparison of alternatives against multiple parameters, providing stakeholders with transparent, consistent and evidence-based recommendations.

The assessment process follows a structured sequence comprising factor selection, generation of potential options, integration of community priorities, suitability assessment and final ranking. This enables mine owners, project proponents and government agencies to make informed decisions based on site-specific conditions rather than relying exclusively on subjective assessments.

Integrating Community Priorities through RECLAIM

Sustainable mine repurposing must address the aspirations of communities residing in mining regions. Accordingly, SUVIKALP integrates RECLAIM – Community Engagement and Development Framework to incorporate local priorities into the project evaluation process.

The framework facilitates systematic consideration of community preferences alongside technical feasibility, environmental suitability and economic considerations. This helps ensure that proposed redevelopment initiatives are aligned with local development needs, employment generation, livelihood opportunities, infrastructure development and long-term community benefits.

By bringing community perspectives into the decision-making process, SUVIKALP promotes a participatory approach to post-mining development, strengthening the linkage between mine closure, regional development and inclusive growth.

From Project Identification to Implementation: PRISM

A distinguishing feature of SUVIKALP is its PRISM (Post-Mining Repurposing Implementation Strategic Model), which extends the platform beyond the identification and ranking of potential projects.

PRISM provides a structured approach to exploring implementation pathways, including project vision, repurposing strategies, investment dynamics, strategic structuring and monitoring. It is supported by an integrated knowledge repository comprising project concept notes, national and international case studies, sample tender documents, details of implementation agencies and best-practice resources.

This integrated approach enables stakeholders to move from identifying suitable opportunities towards understanding the practical requirements for project development and execution. It also facilitates knowledge sharing and provides reference materials to support informed planning and implementation.

   

 

Way Forward: Building an Implementation-Oriented Framework

The next phase of SUVIKALP will focus on expanding its adoption and strengthening the transition from project recommendations to implementation. Key priorities include:

  1. Wider Adoption: Expand SUVIKALP across closed and abandoned coal and lignite mines.
  2. Project Development: Convert recommendations into site-specific feasibility studies, concept notes and DPRs.
  3. Institutional Convergence: Strengthen coordination among government, industry, experts and implementation agencies.
  4. Investment Mobilisation: Explore funding and partnerships for viable mine repurposing projects.
  5. Knowledge and Capacity Building: Share best practices and build stakeholder capacity.
  6. Monitoring and Evaluation: Track implementation and assess environmental, economic and community benefits. Towards a Sustainable Post-Mining Future

SUVIKALP represents an important step towards institutionalising scientific and participatory decision-making in mine repurposing. By integrating technical assessment, community priorities, objective project ranking and implementation guidance within a single digital ecosystem, it provides a structured foundation for sustainable post-mining land-use planning.

The long-term vision is to evolve SUVIKALP into a scalable national knowledge and decision-support ecosystem, adaptable to diverse mining conditions and regional development priorities. The success of this initiative will ultimately be reflected not merely in the identification of suitable projects, but in their successful implementation and the lasting benefits delivered to mining communities.

Through SUVIKALP, the objective is to transform the legacy of mining from resource extraction into an opportunity for environmental restoration, economic diversification and sustainable regional development.

2331955.title: Raksha Mantri chairs meeting of Consultative Committee of Ministry of Defence on ‘Modernisation of Indian Defence Forces’ in Jaisalmer
2331955.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
Raksha Mantri chairs meeting of Consultative Committee of Ministry of Defence on ‘Modernisation of Indian Defence Forces’ in Jaisalmer
Govt is committed to building a technologically empowered military equipped to meet present-day & emerging challenges: Shri Rajnath Singh
“We aim to achieve Rs 3 lakh crore defence production & Rs 50,000 crore defence exports by 2029”
Posted On: 03 NOV 2026 1:08PM by PIB Delhi

Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh chaired the meeting of the Consultative Committee of the Ministry of Defence on ‘Modernisation of Indian Defence Forces’ in Jaisalmer, Rajasthan on November 3, 2026. The meeting witnessed comprehensive deliberations on the emerging security challenges, warfare paradigms, technological advancements and the imperative of building a future-ready, technologically empowered and operationally agile military. The key focus areas emerging from the meeting include:

  • Capability Development & Force Modernisation: Accelerating the induction of next-generation platforms, weapon systems and technologies to enhance combat effectiveness and operational preparedness.

  • Jointness & Integration: Strengthening Tri-service integration, joint operational planning and synergised application of capabilities across multiple domains.

  • Indigenous Defence Manufacturing: Giving further impetus to Make-in-India and Aatmanirbhar Bharat through indigenous research, design, development and manufacturing, with greater participation of domestic industry, start-ups and academia.

  • Emerging & Disruptive Technologies: Harnessing artificial intelligence, autonomous systems, unmanned platforms, cyber, space, electronic warfare and advanced communications to prepare for the character of future conflicts.

  • Defence Research & Innovation: Strengthening collaboration among the Defence Forces, DRDO, Defence Public Sector Undertakings, private industry and academic institutions to accelerate the transition from innovation to operational capability.

  • Resource Optimisation & Implementation: Establishing clear priorities, institutional mechanisms and measurable milestones to ensure that modernisation initiatives translate into tangible operational outcomes.

Emphasising the need for the Defence Forces to remain prepared for present-day and emerging challenges, Raksha Mantri enumerated the steps taken by the Government, under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, across three key dimensions - ‘Budget & Capital Acquisition and Self-reliance’, ‘Technology’ and ‘Human Capital’ - to equip the military to meet the evolving demands of technology-driven modern warfare. He highlighted the Government's sustained focus on budgetary support and capital acquisition to meet the modernisation requirements, stressing that adequate financial resources, coupled with effective utilisation and prioritisation of critical needs of the Services, are essential to strengthening military capabilities.

Shri Rajnath Singh stated that the defence budget for the Financial Year (FY) 2026-27 was increased to a record Rs 7.85 lakh crore, including a capital outlay of Rs 2.19 lakh crore earmarked for modernisation and capital procurement, reflecting the commitment to meeting the operational requirements of the Defence Forces while bolstering domestic defence industries and manufacturing capabilities.

On the growing Aatmanirbharta in defence, Raksha Mantri said that defence production has risen from Rs 46,429 crore in FY 2014-15 to a record Rs 1.78 lakh crore in FY 2025-26, with defence exports, which stood at less than Rs 2,000 crore in 2014, growing to approximately Rs 40,000 crore. “We aim to achieve defence production worth Rs 3 lakh crore and defence exports worth Rs 50,000 crore by 2029,” he added.

Shri Rajnath Singh underlined the transformative role of technology in modern warfare, stating that technological advancements are integral to the changing character of conflicts. He highlighted the initiatives undertaken by DRDO in developing advanced weapons, missiles and systems, adding that the Government is providing a level playing field to the private sector, enabling greater participation of entities ranging from MSMEs to large corporations in the defence ecosystem. Describing it as a 'whole-of-the-nation' approach, he expressed satisfaction at the growing contribution of private industry towards strengthening the defence capabilities of the country.

Underscoring the importance of human capital, Raksha Mantri stated that the strength of a military is determined not merely by technology and financial resources, but also by the capabilities & preparedness of personnel. “The rapidly evolving nature of warfare necessitates that our Defence Forces remain aligned with the changing requirements of modern warfare. Keeping this in mind, all three Services have continuously refined their structures and formations. The Indian Army’s new formations, including the ‘Asani’, ‘Bhairav’ and ‘Shaktiban’ platoons, are proving highly effective in addressing contemporary operational requirements and adapting to the changing dynamics of the battlefield,” he said.

Shri Rajnath Singh emphasised that modernisation is not just about procuring new weapons and equipment, it entails enhancing the operational preparedness of the Defence Forces, equipping them with modern technologies and developing indigenous capabilities for the long term. Underlining the significance of ‘Aatmanirbhar Bharat’ in the context of national security, he highlighted that the focus is to build a robust domestic defence ecosystem that aligns technological development with military requirements, encourages greater participation of Indian industry and reduces the country’s strategic dependence on foreign sources. Strategic autonomy and indigenous technological capabilities are essential to safeguarding national security, he said.

Raksha Mantri underscored that modernisation is a continuous process, necessitating sustained efforts to enhance operational preparedness in response to evolving technologies, shifting security challenges and changing requirements. He emphasised the need to build long-term capabilities that would enable the Defence Forces to remain operationally effective and self-reliant. He called for sustained promotion of research and development, indigenous technologies, greater industrial participation and innovation to strengthen the country's defence capabilities.

The meeting witnessed valuable suggestions by Members of Parliament from both the Rajya Sabha and the Lok Sabha. Their diverse perspectives and insights enriched the consultative process, bringing in important legislative, strategic and national perspectives. The deliberations translated into a clear roadmap for action, with emphasis on prioritising critical capabilities, strengthening coordination among stakeholders, streamlining acquisition and development processes, and periodically assessing progress against defined objectives.

Emphasising the need to translate intent into implementation, the meeting highlighted the importance of a structured and phased approach to modernisation. The objective is to build a military capable of responding effectively to conventional, sub-conventional and multi-domain security challenges.

Raksha Rajya Mantri Shri Sanjay Seth, Defence Secretary Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh, Secretary (Defence Production) Shri Sanjeev Kumar, Secretary (Ex-servicemen Welfare) Smt Sukriti Likhi, Secretary (Defence Finance) Shri Vishvajit Sahay and other senior civil & military officials attended the meeting. 

***

2331941.title: TRAI releases “The Telecommunication Interconnection (Third Amendment) Regulations, 2026”
2331941.body_html:
Ministry of Communications
TRAI releases “The Telecommunication Interconnection (Third Amendment) Regulations, 2026”
Posted On: 03 NOV 2026 12:37PM by PIB Delhi

The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) today released “The Telecommunication Interconnection (Third Amendment) Regulations, 2026”. These regulations will take effect from 1st January, 2027.

Interconnection in telecommunications refers to the technical, operational, and commercial arrangements that connect two or more telecom networks, allowing telecommunications traffic to flow between them and enabling users of different service providers to communicate seamlessly. Section 11(1)(b) of the TRAI Act, 1997, inter alia, empowers TRAI to prescribe the terms and conditions of interconnection between service providers, and ensure technical compatibility and effective interconnection between different service providers.

To ensure that the existing regulatory framework governing interconnection matters remains relevant, transparent, and conducive to efficient interconnection between service providers, TRAI initiated the review of the regulatory framework through a Pre-Consultation Paper on the “Review of the existing TRAI Regulations on Interconnection matters”, dated 03.04.2025. Through this Pre-Consultation Paper, stakeholders’ comments were sought, inter alia, to review the Telecommunication Interconnection Regulations, 2018.

Subsequently, a Consultation Paper on the “Review of the existing TRAI Regulations on Interconnection matters”, providing the background information and taking into account the stakeholders’ comments received during the pre-consultation process, was issued on 10.11.2025. Through the Consultation Paper, stakeholders’ comments were sought, inter alia, to review the Telecommunication Interconnection Regulations, 2018. After extension, the last dates for furnishing written comments and counter-comments were 15.12.2025 and 29.12.2025, respectively.

In response to the issues raised in the Consultation Paper, seventeen stakeholders submitted their comments, while nine stakeholders submitted counter-comments. As part of the consultation process, an Open House Discussion (OHD) on the Consultation Paper was held on 28.01.2026. Based on the comments received from stakeholders during the consultation process, and their analysis, TRAI has finalised the Telecommunication Interconnection (Third Amendment) Regulations, 2026.

The salient points of the amendment regulations are given below:

  1. Interconnection at LSA/ Service Area level: The amendment enables interconnection providers and seekers to mutually agree on locations for handing over or taking over telecommunication traffic. It modernises the existing interconnection regulatory framework to align with contemporary network architectures and facilitate a transition from the existing interconnection at Long Distance Charging Area (LDCA) and Short Distance Charging Area (SDCA) level to the Licensed Service Area (LSA) level of interconnection. The shifting of traffic to LSA-level POIs would simplify routing and support more efficient management of scarce numbering resources, and would also result in benefits such as lower latency, and enhanced service reliability.
  2. Migration of existing traffic at the SDCA/ LDCA-level POIs: Existing traffic, in terms of Minutes of Usage (MoUs), at the LDCA/SDCA-level points of interconnection (POIs) shall be migrated to LSA-level POIs within three years, in a phased manner. Thereafter, all traffic shall be handed over or taken over at the LSA or Service Area level POIs.
  3. Migration to IP-based interconnection: The amendment regulations provide for establishment of IP-based interconnection by service providers. All new interconnections established after these regulations come into force shall be IP-based interconnections. All existing POIs working on E1/ TDM-based interconnection shall be migrated to IP-based interconnection within a period of three years, in a phased manner. The migration to IP-based interconnection improves bandwidth efficiency, call quality and end-to-end call performance.
  4. Capacity augmentation framework for IP-based interconnection: For IP-based interconnection, maximum call-handling capacity at a POI shall be determined having regard to the concurrent session-handling capability and link bandwidth, while maintaining the desired Quality of Service in accordance with the TRAI’s relevant Regulations.
  5. Procedure for surrender of POIs: A specific regulatory framework has been introduced for surrender of POIs. Earlier, the regulations had only the provision of “disconnection” of a POI, which is for stoppage of exchange of traffic at the POI. This is a step taken by a service provider for reasons attributable to the other service provider, in exceptional circumstances arising out of differences between them. On the other hand, the process for surrender is intended for voluntary surrender of a POI by a service provider for its own operational requirements, such as on account of reduction in traffic, withdrawal of services from an area or re-routing of traffic, thereby improving financial efficiency.
  6. Rationalisation of bank guarantee provisions: The existing bank guarantee framework has been retained; however, the validity of bank guarantees furnished on reassessment, and the interval for such reassessment, have been extended from six months to twelve months. A revised methodology has also been introduced for determining the ceiling on bank guarantees for POIs, including IP-based interconnection.
  7. Interest on delayed payment of interconnection-related charges: A specific provision has been introduced to address delayed payment of interconnection charges or interconnection usage charges. The rate of interest shall be mutually agreed between service providers, subject to a ceiling of the State Bank of India’s one-year Marginal Cost of Funds-based Lending Rate (MCLR) plus two percent.
  8. Reporting requirements: The amendment regulations prescribe reporting requirements for monitoring the shifting of traffic from LDCA/SDCA-level POIs to LSA-level POIs, and migration from E1/TDM-based to IP-based interconnection.
  9. Graded framework for financial disincentives: For effective implementation of the regulations, a graded financial disincentive framework has been prescribed for contravention of provisions of these regulations. This revision makes the enforcement of regulatory framework more effective, proportionate and commensurate with the nature and seriousness of the contraventions covered under these Regulations.

The provisions for interest on delayed payment, reporting requirements and financial disincentives will enable effective enforcement of the regulations. The amendment regulations align the regulatory provisions with technological advancements and sectoral developments. They are expected to strengthen the interconnection framework and facilitate seamless communication across telecom networks. The regulatory framework aims to provide greater regulatory certainty to service providers while upholding the principles of effective interconnection, transparency, non-discrimination and fair competition.

The full text of “The Telecommunication Interconnection (Third Amendment) Regulations, 2026”, along with the Explanatory Memorandum, is available on TRAI’s website www.trai.gov.in.

For any clarification/ information, Shri Sameer Gupta, Advisor (Networks, Spectrum & Licensing-I), TRAI may be contacted at email ID: adv-nsl1@trai.gov.in or telephone number +91-11-20907752.

2331935.title: VELC on board Aditya-L1 reveals asymmetric expansion of solar eruption that could impact space weather
2331935.body_html:
Ministry of Science & Technology
VELC on board Aditya-L1 reveals asymmetric expansion of solar eruption that could impact space weather
Posted On: 03 NOV 2026 12:17PM by PIB Delhi

India’s first space-based solar observatory, Aditya-L1 has helped scientists take a peek into the nature of expansion of a solar eruption or a coronal mass eruption (CME) and gain new insights into it. This could be important for space-weather studies and thereby affecting our satellites and communication networks. 

Aditya L 1 satellite launched in September 2023 is now operational at the Sun–Earth L1 point, providing continuous observations of the Sun. It carries 7 payloads, of which the Visible Emission Line Coronagraph (VELC), the primary payload, is an internally occulted coronagraph designed to observe the solar corona simultaneously in various modes.

By combining data from the Visible Emission Line Coronagraph on Aditya-L1 with complementary observations from NASA’s SDO spacecraft and three-dimensional modeling, scientists from the Indian Institute of Astrophysics (IIA), an autonomous institution of the Department of Science and Technology (DST) were able to reconstruct the full 3-D geometry and dynamics of solar eruptions.

Their study published in Astrophysical Journal Letters, showed, for the first time, that the CME did not expand outward from the Sun like a simple symmetric bubble, as previously thought. Instead, it underwent non-uniform expansion and developed an asymmetric shape. These differences in CME expansion can affect its speed as it travels towards Earth causing space-weather disturbances. 

The VELC studies nascent CMEs through spectroscopy in the 530.3 nm wavelength green emission line due to highly ionized iron atoms in the corona. This line emission captures hot coronal plasma which is at temperatures of around 1.8 million Kelvin. The Doppler shift, or the change in the wavelength of this emission line provides information about plasma velocity along the line of sight, and close to the solar disk.

The VELC, with this unique capability, was designed and fabricated by the IIA at its MGK Menon Lab for Space Sciences on the CREST campus in Hosakote, with substantial support from ISRO.

“We observed the CME that occurred on 5 August 2024 using the VELC as well as data from the Atmospheric Imaging Assembly (AIA) onboard NASA’s Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO)”, explained Saurabh Tripathi, a PhD student at IIA, and lead author of the study. The CME was launched from an active region near the western limb of the Sun. VELC’s spectroscopic data show an unusual yet distinct Doppler pattern of blueward and red-ward shifted emission, which arises from plasma moving towards and away from us, respectively.

 “Our results show that the CME did not expand uniformly. The AIA images captured how the CME propagated across the sky, while VELC revealed the motion of the expanding CME bubble towards and away from us,” Tanmoy Samanta, a solar astronomer at IIA and the corresponding author of the study elaborated. Together, these observations reveal that the CME did not expand like a simple spherical bubble. Instead, its uneven expansion caused it to develop an asymmetric shape.

“To understand the unusual spectral pattern observed by VELC, we then developed a 3-D geometric-kinematic model of an expanding CME”, said Jayant Joshi of IIA and a co-author. The model was used to test how the CME’s orientation and uneven sideways expansion could produce the spectral structures observed by VELC. A model with symmetric expansion could not reproduce the observed pattern. Instead, a model of an inclined CME axis and asymmetric lateral expansion produced a spectral pattern and temporal evolution similar to those observed by VELC. The researchers plan to use this technique on other CMEs, to reconstruct their motion without relying entirely on multi-viewpoint imaging from telescopes in space. This complementarity is particularly valuable in the lower corona, where CMEs evolve rapidly, and their motion along the line of sight cannot be obtained from imaging alone.

Fig. (Left) Composite image of the Sun’s corona combining data from India's Aditya-L1/VELC (outer part, 1.05–1.5 solar radii) and NASA’s SDO/AIA (inner disk). (Top right) Aditya-L1/VELC spectra recorded during the eruption, showing two distinct branches of emission — one shifted toward shorter wavelengths (plasma moving toward us) and one toward longer wavelengths (plasma moving away) — the spectral signature of a three-dimensional, asymmetric solar eruption. (Bottom right) Model spectra reproducing the observed pattern, confirming asymmetric lateral expansion of the CME in the inner corona

“The asymmetric shape of an early CME can have important implications for how it interacts with the solar wind and experiences drag during its propagation through the heliosphere. Such effects can influence the CME’s speed and, ultimately, its arrival time at Earth”, said Joshi.

Publication link: https://doi.org/10.3847/2041-8213/aea295

2331901.title: Commerce and Industry Minister Shri Piyush Goyal Chairs Roundtable on Strengthening India’s Biopharma Startup Ecosystem and Accelerating Bioeconomy Growth
2331901.body_html:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
Commerce and Industry Minister Shri Piyush Goyal Chairs Roundtable on Strengthening India’s Biopharma Startup Ecosystem and Accelerating Bioeconomy Growth
Roundtable Urges Regulatory Reforms and Shared Infrastructure to Boost Biopharma Startups
Posted On: 03 NOV 2026 11:06AM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal chaired a high-level roundtable on “India’s Bioeconomy Opportunity: Role of Startups in Driving Innovation and Growth” at Vanijya Bhawan, New Delhi. Organised by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), in collaboration with NITI Aayog and NITI Frontier Tech Hub, the roundtable brought together policymakers, industry leaders and biopharma startups to deliberate on measures to accelerate the growth of India’s bioeconomy.

In his address, Shri Piyush Goyal emphasised the need to leverage India’s scientific capabilities and entrepreneurial talent to position the country as a global leader in the bioeconomy. He underscored the importance of faster approvals, improved access to finance, shared infrastructure and stronger industry–academia–Government collaboration. He also called for time-bound action on the recommendations emerging from the roundtable.

The discussions focused on strengthening the biopharma startup ecosystem through streamlined regulations, faster approvals, a proposed Regulatory Sandbox, Single Window Clearance, global regulatory alignment and simplified patent application processes.

The importance of Biopharma SHAKTI, announced in the Union Budget 2026–27, was also discussed, along with the need to develop shared infrastructure, including laboratories, testing facilities and clinical trial facilities, to reduce costs and enable startups to scale their innovations.

Distinguished Fellow, NITI Aayog, Ms. Debjani Ghosh, highlighted the importance of collaboration among startups, industry, academia and Government in building a globally competitive bioeconomy. Member, NITI Aayog, Prof. Gobardhan Das, stressed the need to strengthen research capabilities and translate scientific discoveries into commercially viable products.

The roundtable also discussed measures to strengthen indigenous life sciences manufacturing, expedite customs clearance for laboratory equipment and reagents, and simplify access to Government schemes and regulatory support. Participants emphasised the need for stronger inter-ministerial coordination to facilitate coherent policy interventions and ensure faster resolution of sector-specific challenges.

***

Abhishek Dayal/ Abhijith Narayanan/ Ishita Biswas

2331900.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
OPENING CEREMONY OF EXERCISE TIGER TRIUMPH 2026
Posted On: 03 NOV 2026 11:02AM by PIB Delhi

The Opening Ceremony of the 5th edition of the India–US Bilateral Tri-Service Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR) Exercise, Tiger Triumph 2026, was held at Maritime Warfare Centre (MWC), Visakhapatnam on 02 Nov 2026. The exercise, which is being conducted as a Tabletop Exercise (TTX) this year, aims to enhance coordination, joint planning and interoperability between the Armed Forces of both countries during large-scale HADR operations. The Opening Ceremony was presided over by RAdm Vishal Bishnoi, Flag Officer Commanding Eastern Fleet, and RAdm Joaquin J Martinez de Pinillos, Vice Commander, US Pacific Fleet.

The exercise reflects the deepening convergence of India–US strategic maritime interests and the growing defence partnership between the two nations. The present edition aims to further enhance interoperability and facilitate the conduct of Combined Joint All-Domain Operations, with a focus on planning and coordination for large-scale HADR operations.

Participating units from the Indian side include specialists from all domains of maritime operations from the Indian Navy, ground forces from the Indian Army and representatives from various units of the Indian Air Force, as well as Special Forces personnel from all three Services. A team from the NDRF will also participate for the first time in the 5th edition of Tiger Triumph 2026.

The US Joint Force comprises specialist representatives from various domains of the US Armed Forces, including the Air Force, Army, Marine Corps and Navy, as well as specialists in Space, Cyber, Medical and Explosive Ordnance Disposal.

2331879.title: Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare proposes expansion of authorised Import gateways for Drugs, Medical Devices and Cosmetics
2331879.ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
2331879.body_html:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare proposes expansion of authorised Import gateways for Drugs, Medical Devices and Cosmetics
Proposed amendment to Drugs Rules, 1945, seeks to add additional Inland Container Depots, Special Economic Zones and an international airport to facilitate efficient import and clearance of healthcare products
Posted On: 03 NOV 2026 9:54AM by PIB Delhi

Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has proposed an amendment to Rule 43A of the Drugs Rules, 1945, to expand the network of authorised entry points for the import of drugs, medical devices and cosmetics into the country. The proposed amendment aims to facilitate smoother import operations, improve logistics efficiency and strengthen the supply chain for healthcare products.

Rule 43A of the Drugs Rules, 1945, specifies the authorised ports, airports, railway stations, road crossings and other entry points through which drugs may be imported into India. With a view to facilitating trade and improving the efficiency of import-related processes, the Ministry has proposed the inclusion of additional Inland Container Depots (ICDs), a Special Economic Zone (SEZ) and an international airport in the list of authorised locations.

The proposed additional locations are ICD Sonipat, Piyala and Harsaru in Haryana; ICD Dadri in Uttar Pradesh; ICD Gandhidham/Mundra in Gujarat; ICD Sanath Nagar and Thimmapur in Hyderabad, Telangana; ICD Whitefield in Bengaluru, Karnataka; SEZ Bommasandra in Karnataka; and Noida International Airport in Uttar Pradesh for the import of drugs by air.

These locations will be added to the existing network of authorised import gateways, which includes ICDs at Dhannad and Tihi in Indore, Madhya Pradesh, along with the airports already notified for the import of drugs.

The proposed expansion is expected to facilitate importers in clearing consignments closer to their manufacturing facilities, warehouses and distribution centres. This is likely to reduce inland transportation distances, optimise logistics costs and minimise delays in the movement of imported consignments. The measure is also expected to improve operational convenience for importers while facilitating more efficient movement of medicines, medical devices and cosmetics across different regions of the country.

Through this proposed amendment, the Ministry seeks to strengthen the supporting infrastructure for the import of healthcare products, promote ease of doing business and contribute towards a more efficient and responsive supply chain, thereby facilitating timely availability of essential healthcare products.

Objections and suggestions, if any, on the proposed amendment may be submitted to the Under Secretary (Drugs Regulation), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India, U-6, Work Hall, C Wing, First Floor, Kartavya Bhawan-1, New Delhi – 110001, or emailed to drugsdiv-mohfw[at]gov[dot]in.

The draft notification containing the proposed amendment to the Drugs Rules, 1945, may be accessed through the Official Gazette at the following link: https://egazette.gov.in/(S(s2ixpktncwy30a02dofwfeqh))/ViewPDF.aspx

2331872.title: INDIAN NAVY SUCCESSFULLY RESCUES HIJACKED FISHING VESSEL ‘AZINI’ OFF THE COAST OF SOMALIA
2331872.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
INDIAN NAVY SUCCESSFULLY RESCUES HIJACKED FISHING VESSEL ‘AZINI’ OFF THE COAST OF SOMALIA
Posted On: 03 NOV 2026 8:45AM by PIB Delhi

In a swift and well-coordinated operation spanning over 48 hours, the Indian Navy successfully liberated the fishing vessel, Azini, from armed pirates. The operation culminated in the safe rescue of all 20 crew members, with no casualties or injuries.

Fishing Vessel Azini was reported to have been hijacked by an armed pirate group earlier last month, off the north-eastern coast of Somalia. The hijacking represented a significant maritime security threat, with the possibility of the vessel being employed as a ‘mother ship’ for launching further pirate attacks against merchant shipping in the region.

Responding to the situation, the Indian Navy tasked a mission-deployed warship to intervene, supported by a maritime reconnaissance aircraft. Working in close coordination, these platforms located the vessel after persistent surveillance, tracked its movements and employed calibrated non-kinetic measures to contain its movement and prevent its escape.

Marine Commandos were augmented through a precision airdrop by an Indian Air Force (IAF) C-17 aircraft.

Executing a swift and well-coordinated tactical intervention, the Indian Navy secured the vessel, overcame the pirate threat and ensured safe release of all 20 crew members.

The successful operation is testament to the Indian Navy’s high operational preparedness and ability to undertake complex maritime security operations through seamless inter-service coordination. It also underscores India’s unwavering commitment to remaining First Responder and Preferred Security Partner in the Indian Ocean Region.

The Indian Navy stands committed to safeguarding seafarers, protecting vital maritime trade routes and ensuring a safe, secure and stable maritime environment in the Indian Ocean Region.

2331870.title: Workshop on “eFiling 3.0: From Process to Practice”- an initiative under eCourts Mission Mode Project
2331870.body_html:
Ministry of Law and Justice
Workshop on “eFiling 3.0: From Process to Practice”- an initiative under eCourts Mission Mode Project
Hon’ble Minister of State (Independent Charge), Ministry of Law and Justice, Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal, to grace the occasion
Posted On: 03 NOV 2026 8:38AM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Justice, Ministry of Law and Justice, Government of India, is organising a Workshop on “eFiling 3.0: From Process to Practice” on 4th November 2026 (Wednesday) from 2:00 p.m. onwards at Hall No. 5, Vigyan Bhawan, Maulana Azad Road, New Delhi. The workshop is an initiative under the eCourts Mission Mode Project. It aims to familiarise Government officials with the eFiling 3.0 platform and forms part of the Department’s continued efforts to advance ease of justice through technology.

The programme will be graced by the presence of Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal, Hon’ble Minister of State (Independent Charge), Ministry of Law and Justice. The Members of the eCommittee, Supreme Court of India, are also expected to be present.

The workshop will feature technical sessions, to be conducted by the National Informatics Centre (NIC), on:

  • Functioning of eCourts: an overview of the applications and services under the eCourts Project;
  • eCourts Single Sign-On (SSO) and the eCourts Services Mobile App;
  • eFiling 3.0: features and functions, including the facilities available to Government Pleaders and Government Departments; and
  • an open discussion with participating officers.

Phase III of the eCourts Project aims at end-to-end digital and paperless courts and citizen-centric judicial eServices, and provides, inter alia, for universal adoption of eFiling across all courts. Government Ministries and Departments, together with their attached and subordinate offices, autonomous and regulatory bodies and Public Sector Undertakings, account for a substantial share of litigation. Their wider adoption of eFiling will improve efficiency and reduce reliance on physical court processes. The workshop seeks to equip designated officers with the practical knowledge required for this purpose.

The event reflects the Government of India’s commitment to a digital, paperless and citizen-centric justice delivery system and to strengthening institutional adoption of technology in the judicial process.

2331839.title: International Buddhist Confederation, in Collaboration with the Ministry of Culture and the Government of Arunachal Pradesh, Organises International Conference on “Buddhism: Dissemination in the Himalayan Region and Beyond” today at Tawang, Arunachal Pradesh
2331839.body_html:
Ministry of Culture
International Buddhist Confederation, in Collaboration with the Ministry of Culture and the Government of Arunachal Pradesh, Organises International Conference on “Buddhism: Dissemination in the Himalayan Region and Beyond” today at Tawang, Arunachal Pradesh
Posted On: 02 NOV 2026 10:06PM by PIB Delhi

The International Buddhist Confederation, New Delhi along with the Ministry of Culture, Government of India and Government of Arunachal Pradesh organised a day long international conference titled “BUDDHISM: DISSEMINATION IN THE HIMALAYAN REGION AND BEYOND” at the Kalawangpo Convention Centre, Tawang, Arunachal Pradesh on today on the sidelines of the Sacred Relics Exposition in Tawang, Arunachal Pradesh.

The conference was attended by monks, scholars, and delegates from India, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Myanmar, Malaysia, Indonesia, and Germany.

The Inaugural session commenced with Mangalacharan (Sacred chanting) by venerable sangha members followed by a welcome address by Secretary General IBC Shartse Khensur Jangchup Choeden Rinpoche. Addressing the gathering, the Secretary General IBC shed light on the theme of this conference which explores how Buddhism was born in the plains of India and spread across the subcontinent and beyond. He conveyed gratitude to the Hon’ble Chief Minister of Arunachal Pradesh for gracing the occasion as the Chief Guest. The SG also expressed appreciation to Arunachal Pradesh administration and Ministry of Culture, Govt. of India for all the support rendered by them for convening the Conference.

The Secretary General IBC mentioned that the occasion holds special significance as it also marks the 14th founding day of the IBC during which the IBC has  continued to serve the Buddha Dhamma. He mentioned that IBC is committed to unite monastic and lay Buddhist organisations worldwide and expressed hope for future collaborations by IBC with the newly formed Arunachal Buddhist Confederation (ABC) in serving the cause of the Buddha Dhamma.

Addressing the conference, the Chief Minister of Arunachal Pradesh, Shri Pema Khandu, Chief Guest at the occasion, congratulated the IBC on its 14th founding day, calling it a befitting coincidence that the International Conference on Buddhism being held in Tawang coincided with IBC’s glorious 14 years of service. He commended the efforts of IBC’s present and former leaders for their dedication and commitment towards Buddhism.

The Chief Minister commented that the conference, jointly organised by the IBC, the Ministry of Culture, Govt. of India and the Government of Arunachal Pradesh, holds special relevance in Tawang owing to the presence of the Sacred Relics. He noted the subject matter themes and subthemes of the discussions at the international conference and recalled how Buddhism that originated in India first transmitted due to efforts of King Ashoka in the 3rd century BCEt. He elaborated on how Buddhism, since the 6th and 7th CE, spread from Himalayan region of India, especially from Arunachal Pradesh, and reached Tibet and other regions attributing the same to Guru Padamasambhava and Shantarakshita. He also emphasized the importance of Tawang as the birth place of the 6th Dalai Lama.

Highlighting Arunachal Pradesh's special place in the larger Buddhist heritage, he said its monasteries are not merely places of worship but a spiritual and cultural legacy. He stressed on the need to ensure development and modernity while preserving cultural values, and to reflect on how the Buddha's message can be carried forward.

He concluded his remarks by thanking the Ministry of Culture, Govt. of India; National Museum; IBC; and Arunachal Pradesh administration for the Holy Relics Exposition and the International Conference. He also thanked the conference delegates, especially the international speakers from several countries, who have come to Tawang to participate in the conference.

The day-long conference featured three thematic sessions, focusing on various aspects of the dissemination, evolution and contemporary relevance of Buddhism in the Himalayan region and beyond.

Session One

During the first session of the conference, on Carrying Forward the Buddha’s Legacy Post His Great Demise (Mahāparinirvāṇa), the panel comprising speakers from Sri Lanka, Myanmar and India explored the Buddha’s enduring legacy following His Mahāparinirvāṇa (the Great Demise) through preservation of material heritage, ritual and institutional renewal. Discussions examined the Four Noble Truths as living heritage and Buddhism’s evolution as a composite cultural tradition shaped by cross-cultural exchange, international collaboration, and the transmission of the Dhamma across generations and societies.

Session Two

In the second session of the conference, on Historical and Doctrinal Continuity of Buddhism, speakers from Nepal, Germany and India, examined the transmission of Buddhist textual and monastic traditions through successive historical periods, with special emphasis on Arunachal Pradesh. It explored the diversity of Buddhist schools and their shared doctrinal foundations, highlighting the roles of language, interpretation, pedagogy and artistic expression in preserving and communicating Buddhist thought.

Session Three

In the last and final session of the day on Buddhism and Right Livelihood, the panel of speakers from Indonesia, Malaysia and India, explored the relevance of Buddhist principles of Right Livelihood in contemporary academic, economic and social contexts. Discussions bridged the intellectual heritage of Nalanda with modern academia and examined cultural tourism, pilgrimage, sustainable prosperity, skill development, geographical interconnectedness and the implications of globalisation and consumerism through a Buddhist perspective.

The conference concluded with a Vote of Thanks by Shri Thupten Kalden, Director, Department of Karmik & Adhyatmik Affairs (DoKAA), Government of Arunachal Pradesh. The event culminated with the sacred Lamp Prayer of Atiśa Dīpaṃkara Śrījñāna, performed by the Monpa group, bringing the conference to a solemn and spiritually uplifting close.

***

2331820.title: Union Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh Alias Lalan Singh Reviews Dairy and Animal Husbandry Initiatives in Sikkim During Two-Day Visit
2331820.ministry: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
2331820.body_html:
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
Union Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh Alias Lalan Singh Reviews Dairy and Animal Husbandry Initiatives in Sikkim During Two-Day Visit
Key initiatives launched for dairy development, indigenous breed conservation and scientific livestock breeding; focus on strengthening livelihoods of farmers and livestock rearers
Posted On: 02 NOV 2026 9:38PM by PIB Delhi

The Hon’ble Union Minister of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh Alias Lalan Singh undertook a two-day visit to Sikkim during 2–3 November 2026 to review the progress of various initiatives and development programmes of the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying (DAHD) in Sikkim of the North Eastern Region (NER). The visit focused on strengthening dairy development, promoting indigenous livestock breeds, improving livestock productivity, expanding dairy cooperative networks and enhancing livelihood opportunities for farmers and livestock rearers.

On 2nd November, the Hon’ble Union Minister visited Tingda Government Primary School, interacted with students and encouraged them to pursue education and learning. He also visited the Ramthang Primary Health Sub-Centre (PHSC) and Wellness Centre to review the available healthcare facilities.

 

The Hon’ble Union Minister visited an exhibition showcasing Siri bulls, Siri cows and related value-added products, where he interacted with farmers and learnt about indigenous breed conservation and livestock-based livelihood opportunities. He also inspected stalls displaying dairy and animal husbandry products and locally grown organic vegetables.

The Hon’ble Union Minister digitally launched the North District Cooperative Milk Producers’ Union Ltd (NDMU). Under White Revolution 2.0 at Mangan, marking an important step towards strengthening the dairy cooperative network and expanding organised dairy activities in North Sikkim. The initiative is expected to facilitate greater participation of dairy farmers in the cooperative network and strengthen institutional support for dairy development.

The Hon’ble Union Minister launched “Minimum Standard Protocol for Semen Production and Standard Operating Procedures for Artificial Insemination Using Liquid Semen in Pigs”. The publication establishes a standardised framework for semen production and artificial insemination (AI) using liquid semen in pigs. The protocols aim to promote scientific breeding practices, improve genetic quality, enhance productivity, strengthen biosecurity and expand the adoption of artificial insemination technology in pig farming.

The initiative is expected to improve reproductive efficiency, reduce the risk of disease transmission and enhance farmers' incomes, particularly in the North-Eastern Region, where pig rearing plays an important role in rural livelihoods.

The Hon’ble Union Minister also digitally launched the Siri Cattle Conservation Programme, aimed at conserving and promoting the indigenous Siri cattle breed, preserving valuable genetic resources and strengthening scientific breeding practices.

Furthermore, he digitally laid the foundation stone of the Siri Bull Mother Farm at Chuchachen in Pakyong district. The proposed facility aims to strengthen the conservation of the indigenous Siri breed, support genetic improvement and promote scientific breeding and multiplication of quality germplasm.
The visit concluded with an address by the Hon’ble Union Minister of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh, who highlighted the importance of strengthening the dairy and livestock sectors, promoting indigenous breeds, adopting modern breeding technologies and creating sustainable livelihood opportunities for farmers and livestock rearers.

During the address the Hon’ble Union Minister announced that DAHD, Government of India will establish a Centre of Excellence for the indigenous Siri cattle breed conservation and development in Sikkim. Hon’ble Union Minister directed for the preparation of a comprehensive Action Plan for Siri cattle conservation and development focusing on breed improvement, genetic conservation and scientific breeding. Further, he emphasised the need to prepare a Work Plan for introducing In Vitro Fertilisation (IVF) technology to accelerate genetic improvement and facilitate the multiplication of superior germplasm.

The Hon’ble Minister congratulated on the inclusion of the North District Cooperative Milk Producers’ Union Ltd. under White Revolution 2.0 and to ensure successful implementation, Hon’ble Minister advised National Dairy Development Board (NDDB) to prepare a comprehensive plan for the modernization of the dairy plant, expansion of the dairy cooperative network, and development of an integrated “Sikkim Milk” brand to drive sustainable growth of the dairy sector in the State.

The Hon’ble Union Minister reiterated the importance of strengthening the dairy and livestock sectors through indigenous breed conservation, modern breeding technologies, dairy infrastructure development and cooperative-led growth to enhance livestock productivity and create sustainable livelihood opportunities for farmers and livestock rearers.

2331804.title: Lending Institutions propose institutional financing of PMAY-G beneficiaries at MoRD–NHB “PMAY-G Reform Samvad” in Lonavala: States, HFCs, SFBs, MFIs and RRBs deliberate a roadmap for affordable institutional credit for rural housing
2331804.body_html:
Ministry of Rural Development
Lending Institutions propose institutional financing of PMAY-G beneficiaries at MoRD–NHB “PMAY-G Reform Samvad” in Lonavala: States, HFCs, SFBs, MFIs and RRBs deliberate a roadmap for affordable institutional credit for rural housing
Posted On: 02 NOV 2026 9:22PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD), jointly with the National Housing Bank (NHB), spearheaded “PMAY-G Reform Samvad”, a one-day stakeholder dialogue on reforms for strengthening rural housing under PMAY-G. It brought together MoRD, NHB, State Rural Development Departments, the World Bank, International Finance Corporation, Sa-Dhan, TCIS Habitat for Humanity International and lending institutions, including Housing Finance Companies (HFCs), Regional Rural Banks (RRBs), Small Finance Banks (SFBs) and Micro Finance Institutions (MFIs).

Departing from the conventional view for rural loans, the discussion witnessed the lenders describing PMAY-G households as a promising and largely untapped segment. They noted that beneficiaries are verified under the scheme, Government assistance covers a substantial part of the cost, and construction is tracked through milestones on the PMAY-G platform, which reduces the cost and risk of lending. They expressed willingness to design dedicated loan products and to work with the Ministry, NHB and States on enabling reforms.

Earlier in the morning, Dr. Rajaram Dighe, Director, Rural Housing, Government of Maharashtra, welcomed the participants. Shri Sanjay Shukla, Managing Director, NHB, underlined the need for affordable institutional credit to help rural families complete their homes. Shri Piyush Srivastava, Senior Economic Advisor (Rural Housing), MoRD, delivered the keynote address, setting the direction for the day. He mentioned that PMAY-G was the world’s largest housing scheme and its achievements in rural housing are a matter of great satisfaction.  He, however, called for greater coordinated push towards the national goal of housing for all where the institutional finance can act as a force multiplier. NHB, the World Bank, Sa-Dhan and TCIS Habitat for Humanity International then presented global and grassroots perspectives on rural housing finance.

Why institutional credit matters for PMAY-G

PMAY-G aims to complete 4.95 crore pucca houses by March 2029. The cost of building a rural house often exceeds the assistance under the scheme, and arranging the balance can delay construction and push households towards high-interest informal lenders. Lenders with last-mile reach, in turn, face funding gaps, perceived credit risk and the absence of standardised rural housing loan products. The Samvad deliberated on:

  • which household segments can be financed responsibly, with loan sizes and repayment suited to seasonal incomes;
  • the barriers to lending, from documentation and appraisal to transaction costs;
  • how PMAY-G data, construction milestones and DAY-NRLM SHG networks can lower these barriers; and
  • the support needed from the Centre, States and NHB, including NHB’s proposed refinance window for rural housing.

Three mixed breakout groups of lenders and State Governments presented their recommendations in plenary, followed by an open forum.

Key Outcomes of the Deliberations

A key takeaway was the keen interest of HFCs, SFBs and MFIs in extending credit to PMAY-G beneficiaries over and above scheme assistance. Lenders cited unclear land titles, restrictions on mortgage of allotted properties, seasonal incomes, high transaction costs and perceived credit risk as the main barriers. To translate this interest into lending at scale, participants recommended:

  • Dedicated rural housing loan products of ₹2–5 lakh, with repayment aligned to seasonal incomes;
  • A pilot of a commercially viable model, possibly anchored by an NHB-supported entity, before wider rollout;
  • Credit guarantee support through a Government-backed partial guarantee mechanism;
  • Affordable lending rates through interest subvention, concessional funding and NHB refinance;
  • Land and property reforms by States, including mortgage of allotted properties and stamp duty concessions;
  • Regulatory treatment suited to rural borrowers, including differentiated NPA and provisioning norms; and
  • Community-based last-mile delivery through Gram Panchayats, DAY-NRLM SHGs and the LokOS platform.

Review of PMAY-G progress

The workshop also reviewed PMAY-G progress in Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Assam and Kerala, including a dedicated session with PFMS to resolve State-specific SNA SPARSH issues.

Way forward

The interest shown by lending institutions marks an important step towards combining Government assistance with institutional credit, so that PMAY-G families can complete quality homes without costly informal borrowing. The Ministry will examine the suggestions emerging from the Samvad and take them forward in consultation with NHB, State Governments, lending institutions and knowledge partners.
