2331704.title: TRAI issues the Telecom Consumers Complaint Redressal (Fourth Amendment) Regulations, 2026
2331704.body_html:
Ministry of Communications
TRAI issues the Telecom Consumers Complaint Redressal (Fourth Amendment) Regulations, 2026
Posted On: 02 NOV 2026 6:08PM by PIB Delhi

The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has today issued the Telecom Consumers Complaint Redressal (Fourth Amendment) Regulations, 2026.

To address the evolving needs related to the upgradation of grievance redressal framework, the Authority released a consultation paper on the Draft Telecom Consumers Complaint Redressal (Fourth Amendment) Regulations, 2026, on 7th May 2026, inviting comments and counter-comments by 12th and 19th June 2026, respectively. A total of 32 comments and 24 counter-comments were received from stakeholders and uploaded to the TRAI website. An online Open House Discussion (OHD) was held on 17th July 2026.

Based on the above consultations, the Authority has finalized the Amendment Regulations. The salient features of the same are given below:

  • The amended regulations shall apply to Internet Service Providers having more than ten thousand subscribers as on the last day of the preceding financial year. The existing alternative criterion based on annual financial turnover exceeding ₹5 crore has been dispensed with thus simplifying the applicability clause.
  • Consumers will now be able to register complaints and appeals, raise service requests, and make service-related queries through the service provider’s mobile application, in addition to the existing channels of the Complaint Centre, website and web portal thus giving wider choice, flexibility and ease to consumers in filing complaint and appeal.
  • Consumer support through Complaint Centres will be available round the clock on all days of the week, instead of the existing 16-hour arrangement. Such support may be provided through human representatives, automated systems, AI agents, other customer-centric technological solutions, or a combination thereof. Human assistance shall be available for at least sixteen hours daily. Technology-based solutions shall function with appropriate human oversight. This will ensure ease and convenience to consumers and gives flexibility to service providers in manning the Complaint Centres.
  • Every service provider shall equip dedicated desks or helplines in their Complaint Centre or Consumer support centres, with personnel or assistive technology capable of receiving calls from persons with disabilities (PwDs). Service providers will ensure that their mobile app, website and portal have accessibility features in accordance with the applicable guidelines or standards on accessibility for Persons with Disabilities issued by the Government of India.
  • The time limit for filing an appeal following disposal of a complaint has been revised from 30 days to 15 days as consumers would normally prefer appeal as soon as possible whereas a longer time allowed unduly increases compliance requirements. Consumers may now file appeals through the service provider’s mobile application, website or portal, in addition to the existing channels of email, post, in person, or through the Consumer Care Number. This will ensure faster resolution of appeal.
  • Also, the Appellate Authority has been made more responsible through the present amendment. It has been mandated that the Appellate Authority shall comprise one or more persons who are regular employees in the management of the service provider and also possess at least five years’ experience. The Appellate Authority shall examine the appeal, take appropriate action for resolution of the grievance, and communicate its final decision within 15 days of receipt of the appeal.
  • The earlier process of resolution of appeal cases through Advisory committee has been dispensed with in order to ensure efficient and time-bound resolution of appeal cases.
  • A new mechanism of “Feedback Survey” has been introduced. Upon resolution or closure of a complaint or appeal, the service provider shall conduct an online feedback survey to assess the consumer’s satisfaction with the resolution. Feedback shall be obtained on a five-point scale, ranging from “Fully Satisfied” (5 points) to “Totally Dissatisfied” (1 point). The service provider shall publish the results of such feedback surveys on its website on a quarterly basis.
  • It has also been mandated that every service provider shall place before its CEO or Board of Directors a quarterly report on the redressal of complaints, appeals and the results of feedback survey. This has been done to ensure suitable review and oversight of the disposal of complaints and appeals by the service providers at the highest level.
  • A new mechanism of Consumer Grievance Redressal Oversight Committee has been introduced. Every Service Provider shall establish a Consumer Grievance Redressal Oversight Committee to oversee and periodically review the functioning of its grievance redressal mechanism. The Committee shall comprise representatives of the Service Provider and at least one representative from each consumer organisation registered with the Authority in the State or Union Territory forming part of the licensed service area.  Service Providers will form such committee taking representation mandatorily from those states and union territories in which their subscriber base is above ten thousand. The Committee shall meet at least once every year to review the grievance redressal mechanism.
  • The amendment introduces a new mechanism of Regulatory Review. The Authority may conduct periodic review of the functioning of the Grievance Redressal Mechanism of the service providers by: -
    • audit and inspection of the records of the service provider,
    • audit and analysis of Quarterly Performance Reports submitted by the service provider,
    • review based on consumer feedback.
  • The amendment introduces the provision of financial disincentives in cases of disposal of complaint or appeal in contravention of the provisions of these regulations observed during the audit, inspection, analysis or review.
  • The provision of financial disincentives has also been introduced for non-submission/ delayed submission of the Quarterly Performance Report.

The amendments strengthen the consumer grievance redressal framework through enhanced digital access available to consumers, round the clock Complaint Centre support, improved accessibility for Persons with Disabilities and faster filing and disposal of complaints and appeals. The Appellate mechanism has been strengthened. Structured consumer feedback surveys, grievance redressal oversight committees, enhanced regulatory review, and financial disincentives for specified instances of non-compliance have been introduced to ensure appropriate supervision and compliance enforcement.

Full text of the Regulation is available on the TRAI's website www.trai.gov.in. For any clarification/information Advisor (Consumer Affairs), TRAI, may be contacted at email ID: adv.ca@trai.gov.in or Telephone +91-11- 26769605.

2331689.title: DoPPW Accelerates Digital Empowerment of Pensioners Through Nationwide Digital Life Certificate Campaign 5
2331689.ministry: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
2331689.body_html:
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
DoPPW Accelerates Digital Empowerment of Pensioners Through Nationwide Digital Life Certificate Campaign 5
DoPPW, SBI Join Hands to Facilitate Hassle-Free Digital Life Certificates for Pensioners
Over Two Crore Digital Life Certificates Targeted Under Nationwide DLC Campaign 5
Posted On: 02 NOV 2026 5:43PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Pension and Pensioners’ Welfare (DoPPW), Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, organised a Mega Camp in collaboration with the State Bank of India (SBI) at the NDCC Convention Centre, New Delhi, on 2 November 2026, as part of the Nationwide Digital Life Certificate (DLC) Campaign 5. The camp witnessed enthusiastic participation from pensioners and senior citizens and aimed to facilitate the submission of Digital Life Certificates through technology-driven, accessible and pensioner-friendly services.

Addressing the gathering, the Secretary, DoPPW, Ms Nivedita Shukla Verma highlighted that digital empowerment of pensioners is an important component of the Government’s commitment to Ease of Living. The Secretary emphasised that technological advancements, particularly face authentication, have transformed the process of submitting life certificates by enabling pensioners to generate their Digital Life Certificates independently through smartphones, without the need to visit banks or other offices.

The Secretary also appreciated SBI’s significant contribution to the initiative, noting that the Bank had facilitated approximately 25 lakh Digital Life Certificates during the previous year’s campaign.

As part of the current campaign, SBI is conducting special DLC camps across 115 cities and extending assistance through its branches and dedicated support teams. The Bank has also undertaken initiatives to expand coverage among its pensioners and facilitate access to digital services, including special arrangements at branches with a substantial pensioner population.

Addressing the gathering Joint Secretary DoPPW Sh Dhrubajyoti Sengupta  urged all pensioners to make use of the facilities available under the campaign and encourage fellow pensioners to adopt digital services, thereby contributing to a more accessible, transparent and citizen-centric pension delivery system.

***

2331682.title: PM-SETU to strengthen North-East's skilling ecosystem through industry-led ITI transformation; Tourism and Hospitality identified as key sectors for global employment opportunities
2331682.ministry: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
2331682.body_html:
Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
PM-SETU to strengthen North-East's skilling ecosystem through industry-led ITI transformation; Tourism and Hospitality identified as key sectors for global employment opportunities
MoU exchanged between MSDE and Government of Assam for setting up of SIIC; Numaligarh Refinery and Oil India Limited clusters declared under PM-SETU
Posted On: 02 NOV 2026 5:32PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), Government of India, organised a programme on Skilling for International Mobility & PM-SETU', with a special focus on the Tourism and Hospitality sector in Guwahati today.

The programme brought together senior representatives of the Central and Assam Governments, industry stakeholders and the skilling ecosystem to deliberate on strengthening the North-Eastern Region's skilling infrastructure, expanding international employment opportunities for its youth and fostering industry-led transformation of Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) under the Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs (PM-SETU).

The programme highlighted the immense potential of the North-Eastern Region in tourism and hospitality, particularly in the context of the growing demand for skilled professionals in domestic and international markets. Discussions focused on aligning skill development programmes with emerging industry requirements, international standards and opportunities for global workforce mobility.

Delivering the keynote address, Shri Jayant Chaudhary, Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship and Minister of State for Education, Government of India, highlighted the importance of aligning India's skilling architecture with the changing requirements of industry and the global economy.

He emphasised that initiatives such as PM-SETU are aimed at bringing industry closer to skill development and training, ensuring that ITIs evolve into modern, demand-driven institutions capable of preparing young people for emerging opportunities.

"India's strength lies in the aspirations and capabilities of its youth. Through PM-SETU, we are working towards transforming our ITIs into modern, industry-responsive institutions that equip young people with skills relevant to the future of work. The North-Eastern Region has enormous potential, particularly in tourism and hospitality, and our endeavour is to ensure that its youth are not only prepared for opportunities within the country but are also equipped to participate confidently in the global workforce."

Shri Biswajit Daimary, Minister for Skills, Employment and Entrepreneurship, Sports and Youth Welfare, Handloom, Textile and Sericulture, and Indigenous and Tribal Faith and Culture, Government of Assam, in his special remarks, highlighted the importance of equipping the youth of Assam with industry-relevant skills and creating pathways to employment opportunities both within India and internationally.

"Assam and the entire North-Eastern Region have tremendous potential in sectors such as tourism and hospitality. Our priority is to ensure that the youth of the region are equipped with the right skills, exposure and opportunities to participate in the emerging global economy. Through stronger collaboration between the Central Government, the State Government and industry, we can build a robust skilling ecosystem that translates the aspirations of our youth into meaningful employment and entrepreneurship opportunities."

Smt. Manasi Sahay Thakur, IAS, Joint Secretary, MSDE, set the context for the programme and highlighted the importance of strengthening institutional and industry partnerships to create a future-ready workforce. She emphasised the need to connect the region's youth with emerging employment opportunities through demand-driven skilling and stronger institutional infrastructure.

CEO of Tourism and Hospitality Skill Council (THSC), spoke about the potential of tourism and hospitality skilling in the North-Eastern Region and the opportunities emerging from the sector's growth. He highlighted the importance of developing industry-relevant competencies to enhance the employability of youth and prepare them for opportunities in the global hospitality ecosystem.

The programme featured a dedicated session on PM-SETU, highlighting opportunities for strengthening the skilling ecosystem in the North-Eastern Region through industry-responsive ITI transformation.

As part of the strategic partnerships announced during the programme, a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was exchanged between the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship and the Government of Assam for setting up of SIIC.

Letters of Intent (LoIs) were signed for two ITI clusters i.e Jorhat and Tinsukhia, supported by Numaligarh Refinery Limited (NRL) and Oil India Limited (OIL), respectively, under the PM-SETU scheme. This marks a significant milestone in strengthening industry participation and fostering industry-led transformation of the vocational education and training ecosystem in the region.

The programme also deliberated on international mobility and WorldSkills as avenues for expanding opportunities for young people from the North-Eastern Region.

The Government of Assam also presented its CM FLIGHT Scheme and the vision for a Global Skill Center, highlighting the State's efforts towards strengthening skill development and connecting its workforce with emerging opportunities.

 

Attended the Northeast Tourism & Hospitality Skill Conclave 2026 in Guwahati, alongside Hon’ble Minister Sh @BiswajitDaimar5. Led by @MSDESkillIndia, with support from @NSDCIndia and the @skillthsc, the Conclave focused on strengthening tourism-led skilling, industry partnerships and international mobility opportunities for the youth of the North-East. The occasion also witnessed the exchange of an MoU between MSDE and the Government of Assam for establishing a Skill India International Centre (SIIC), and the exchange of LoIs of PM-SETU clusters with Numaligarh Refinery Limited and Oil India Limited. These partnerships aim to strengthen industry-aligned skilling infrastructure, create opportunities, and equip the youth of the North-East with skills for emerging domestic and international markets!

— Jayant Singh (@jayantrld) November 2, 2026

2331644.title: Ministry of Mines Concludes Special Campaign 6 with Significant Achievements in E-Waste Management, Cleanliness and Governance
2331644.body_html:
Ministry of Mines
Ministry of Mines Concludes Special Campaign 6 with Significant Achievements in E-Waste Management, Cleanliness and Governance
Posted On: 02 NOV 2026 5:17PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Mines, along with its attached and subordinate offices, Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) and autonomous bodies, has successfully concluded Special Campaign 6, with a particular focus on the effective collection, segregation and disposal of e-waste. The campaign also focused on cleanliness, efficient record management, disposal of pending references, resolution of public grievances and improving administrative efficiency, reaffirming the Ministry's commitment to sustainability and good governance.

A key highlight of Special Campaign 6 was the extensive drive for the collection and disposal of e-waste. During the campaign, a total of 134.92 tonnes of e-waste had been collected/disposed across 96 locations, generating revenue of approx ₹ 1.2 crore. The initiative covered offices of the Ministry of Mines / field offices as well as other government offices, promoting the responsible disposal of electronic waste, resource recovery and environmentally sustainable practices.

During the campaign period, 465 cleanliness campaign were conducted across the Ministry and its organizations. The campaign generated total revenue of approximately 6.19 crore from disposal of scrap and e-waste, and freed approximately 47881 square feet of office space. These efforts contributed to improved workplace conditions, better utilization of office space and the promotion of a culture of cleanliness and sustainability.

Under the record management initiative, 13067 physical files were reviewed, of which 9470 were weeded out. In the electronic records category, 3270 e-files were reviewed and 1812 were closed. Overall 11282 files were weeded out or closed, contributing to streamlined record management and improved administrative efficiency.

The Ministry also achieved its targets in disposing the Public Grievances/ Public Grievances appeals, references received from Members of Parliament, the Prime Minister's Office (PMO), the Inter-Ministerial Committee (IMC) and State Governments reference. In addition, 7 rules/processes were simplified during the campaign to promote ease of governance and administrative efficiency.

Several innovative best practices were undertaken by the Ministry's organisations to promote environmental sustainability and resource conservation. Hindustan Copper Limited (HCL) inaugurated a rainwater harvesting facility at Khetri Copper Complex, Rajasthan, and organised a tree plantation drive at Indian Copper Complex, Jharkhand, under the Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam initiative. NALCO promoted the use of biodegradable bags in township and undertook plantation drives under its One Employee – One Green initiative. The Indian Bureau of Mines (IBM) developed a green park on barren land in Ranchi. Other initiatives included innovative waste-to-wealth activities through the reuse of scrap materials, including the creation of decorative plants and toolkits from discarded materials, demonstrating the potential of recycling and creative reuse.

Through the dedicated efforts of its offices and organisations, the Ministry of Mines has made significant progress in promoting cleanliness, sustainable waste management, better record management and citizen-centric governance. The achievements of Special Campaign 6 reflect the Ministry’s continued commitment to environmental sustainability, efficient use of resources and the adoption of good administrative practices.

***

HQ IDS-CENJOWS Seminar on Cyber-Enabled Cognitive Warfare Commences in New Delhi
Posted On: 02 NOV 2026 4:53PM by PIB Delhi

A two-day seminar on “Cyber-Enabled Cognitive Warfare”, organised by the Centre for Joint Warfare Studies (CENJOWS) under the aegis of Headquarters Integrated Defence Staff (HQ IDS), commenced in New Delhi on November 02, 2026. The seminar aims to deliberate on the emerging security challenges arising from the convergence of cyber operations, Artificial Intelligence (AI), information influence and human cognition, with particular focus on India's evolving threat landscape.

The sessions focused on the cyber-enabled cognitive battlefield and India's evolving threat landscape, the anatomy of influence operations, including the actors, vectors and narratives shaping the information environment. The deliberations also addressed the targeting of military personnel, veterans and their families, alongside the growing convergence of cyber technologies, Artificial Intelligence and digital manipulation. The discussions highlighted the need for a comprehensive understanding of emerging threats, extending beyond their technological dimensions to encompass their psychological, institutional and societal implications.

The seminar brings together senior military leaders, government officials, strategic affairs experts, diplomats, representatives from academia, technology specialists and media representatives, providing a multidisciplinary platform for deliberations on the challenges and implications of cyber-enabled cognitive warfare.

The inaugural session was attended by Rear Admiral Sanjay Sachdeva, Director General, Defence Cyber Agency, Major General Ashok Kumar (Retd), Director General, CENJOWS, Shri Navin Kumar Singh, National Cyber Security Coordinator, Vice Admiral A N Pramod,  Deputy Chief of the Naval Staff, and Air Marshal Tejinder Singh, Chief of Integrated Defence Staff to the Chairman, Chiefs of Staff Committee (CISC).

2331603.title: 1st International Maize Conference 2026 Calls for Higher Productivity, Innovative Breeding and Farmer-Centric Research
2331603.body_html:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
1st International Maize Conference 2026 Calls for Higher Productivity, Innovative Breeding and Farmer-Centric Research
Research and extension must translate into higher farm profitability and improved livelihoods: Dr M.L. Jat, Secretary, DARE  
Dr. Jat advocates Systems-Science Approach to Bridge Yield Gaps and Strategically Target Maize Across Seasons Without Compromising Oilseeds and Pulses
Posted On: 02 NOV 2026 4:50PM by PIB Delhi

The 1st International Maize Conference themed “Maize Revolution for Food, Feed, Fodder, Fuel and Sustainability in the Changing World,” (M4FS) commenced at the JD Convention Centre, Hyderabad today, bringing together scientists, policymakers, agricultural institutions and industry stakeholders to discuss strategies for advancing maize research, productivity and value-chain development.

The conference highlighted high-yielding varieties and hybrids, improved nutritional quality, efficient resource utilisation, mechanisation, robust seed systems and maize’s growing role in food, feed, fodder and energy security.

Addressing the conference Secretary, DARE and DG ICAR Dr. M. L. Jat, congratulated the maize research community on India’s maize production reaching approximately 55 million tonnes, accompanied by substantial productivity gains over the past decade. He called for increasing production to 75 million tonnes over the next decade, alongside a further 1.5-fold increase in productivity through technological innovation, improved crop management and efficient resource utilisation.

Emphasising an expansion of the traditional 4F vision—Food, Feed, Fodder and Fuel—to 5F by placing Farmers at the centre, Dr. Jat stressed that research and extension must translate into higher farm profitability and improved livelihoods. He advocated a systems-science approach to bridging yield gaps, particularly those arising from crop management, and strategic targeting of maize across seasons and agroecological zones without compromising other important crops, particularly oilseeds and pulses. He also underscored the need for affordable, quality seed, especially public-sector hybrids, supported by a robust seed system.

Dr. D. K. Yadav, Deputy Director General (Crop Science), ICAR, described maize as a model crop for food, nutritional and energy security. Acknowledging progress in maize research and extension over the past five years, including the development of 329 maize hybrids, he called for strengthening the All India Coordinated Research Project on Maize (AICRP on Maize). He emphasised breeding for higher yields, improved nutritional quality and resistance to biotic and abiotic stresses, alongside input-use efficiency, mechanisation, capacity development and stronger public-sector hybrid seed production. He also highlighted the need for collaboration among research institutions, universities and industry to realise maize’s potential as an ethanol feedstock.

Padma Shri Dr. S. Vasal, eminent maize scientist and a World Food Laurete associated with CIMMYT, advocated simple, cost-effective breeding approaches to accelerate the development of improved varieties and hybrids suited to farmers’ needs.

Padma Bhushan Dr. R. S. Paroda, former Secretary, DARE, and Director General, ICAR, and Chief Guest, stressed the importance of aligning research priorities with the evolving needs of agriculture and allied sectors. He called for greater use of advanced breeding techniques, systematic germplasm conservation and utilisation, stronger maize value chains, and effective aflatoxin management to ensure maize safety and quality for food and feed.

Earlier, Dr. H. S. Jat, President, Maize Technologists Association of India (MTAI), welcomed the dignitaries and highlighted maize’s strategic importance in India’s agricultural transformation. He called for stronger collaboration among research institutions, agricultural universities, policymakers and industry to address emerging challenges.

Several scientific publications were released during the programme, and awards were presented to eminent scientists and researchers in recognition of their contributions to maize research and development.

The conference underscored the importance of collaborative, farmer-centric research to bridge yield gaps, improve seed access, strengthen breeding programmes, enhance nutritional quality and develop sustainable maize value chains. Being held from 2–4 November, 2026 in Hyderabad, the conference provides a platform for national and international experts to shape a roadmap for a productive, profitable and sustainable maize sector in India.

2331588.title: Indian Railways Observes Rashtriya Ekta Diwas and Swachhata Hi Seva 2026
2331588.body_html:
Ministry of Railways
Indian Railways Observes Rashtriya Ekta Diwas and Swachhata Hi Seva 2026
Railway Board Chairman & CEO Administers Unity Pledge and Felicitates Safai Mitras at Rail Bhawan
Posted On: 02 NOV 2026 4:34PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Railways observed Rashtriya Ekta Diwas and organised activities under Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 – Special Campaign 6.0 at Rail Bhawan, New Delhi, on 30 October 2026.

To mark the 151st birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, the ‘Iron Man of India’, Shri Satish Kumar, Chairman & CEO of the Railway Board, administered the Rashtriya Ekta Diwas Pledge at Vichar (Conference Hall), Rail Bhawan. Members of the Railway Board, Directors General, senior officers and staff of the Ministry of Railways were present on the occasion.

Rashtriya Ekta Diwas is observed every year on 31st October to commemorate the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. He played a pivotal role in the integration of the princely states into the Union of India and made an enduring contribution towards strengthening the unity and integrity of the nation.

As part of Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 – Special Campaign 6.0, various activities were organised at Rail Bhawan to promote cleanliness, hygiene and sanitation. Health check-up camps were organised for Safai Mitras, recognising the importance of their health and well-being.

On the occasion, Chairman & CEO, Railway Board, felicitated Safai Mitras in recognition of their dedicated services and contribution towards maintaining cleanliness at Rail Bhawan. The felicitation acknowledged their hard work and commitment to maintaining cleanliness and upholding the spirit of Swachhata in Indian Railways.

The event recognised the contributions of day-to-day maintenance staff, with senior members of the Railway Board felicitating employees for their dedication and hard work. The felicitation included staff from housekeeping and horticulture, reflecting the deep sense of unity within the Rail family and the spirit of working together as One Family. The occasion also coincided with the felicitation of 11 employees who retired after dedicating a significant part of their lives to the service of Indian Railways and the people of the country.

The celebrations reinforced the message of keeping offices clean and green while fostering a culture of teamwork, mutual respect and collective responsibility. It highlighted the spirit of Indian Railways as One Family, working together as One Team to serve the people of India.

As India moves forward towards the vision of Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat, Indian Railways continues to play a vital role in strengthening the unity and integration of the nation. As the country's national transporter, connecting every part of India and carrying millions of passengers to their destinations every day, Indian Railways remains a symbol of national unity, bringing people, regions and states closer together.

2331586.title: From Financial Support to Career Growth: How NFSC is Empowering a Research Scholar
2331586.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Financial Support to Career Growth: How NFSC is Empowering a Research Scholar
Posted On: 02 NOV 2026 4:33PM by PIB Delhi

At 32, Pavithran S (name changed), a scholar from Ranipet district of Tamil Nadu, aspired to complete his Ph.D. and build a strong academic and professional career. As the first student at his institution to receive the fellowship under the National Fellowship for Scheduled Caste Students (NFSC) Scheme, he encountered certain initial administrative challenges. These included the creation of Maker and Checker IDs at the institutional level to facilitate the processing of fellowship-related formalities.

The NFSC Scheme provided him with timely financial assistance to continue his academic journey. His fellowship support began in March 2023 and included fellowship assistance, House Rent Allowance (HRA) and contingency support. An amount of Rs 5 lakh has been provided to him under the scheme.

The financial assistance helped address an important challenge faced by the scholar during his higher studies. He stated that the support was very helpful in pursuing his Ph.D. and also contributed to the financial stability of his family. By easing financial concerns, the fellowship enabled him to continue working towards his academic goals with greater confidence.

The support under the scheme has also had a positive impact on his professional journey. Pavithran is currently employed full-time and acknowledges that the NFSC fellowship has played a significant role in developing his career. He credits the scheme with providing the support needed to sustain his academic pursuits alongside his professional responsibilities.

For Pavithran, the NFSC Scheme represents more than financial assistance. It has been a meaningful source of encouragement in his pursuit of doctoral education, strengthened his family's financial stability and contributed to his career development. His experience reflects the role of targeted educational support in enabling scholars to pursue higher learning and work towards their aspirations.

2331574.title: Dr Jitendra Singh highlights expansion of disaster preparedness and weather monitoring infrastructure with new Seismological Observatory inaugurated in high seismic region of Kishtwar
2331574.body_html:
Ministry of Earth Sciences
Dr Jitendra Singh highlights expansion of disaster preparedness and weather monitoring infrastructure with new Seismological Observatory inaugurated in high seismic region of Kishtwar
IMD strengthens weather monitoring network in the region from not a single Doppler Weather Radar in 2014 to 4 installed in last 12 years and 4 more being installed making it total 8; Automatic Weather Stations from 3 to 12 out of which 4 for Kishtwar and 2 each for Doda and Ramban; Rainfall monitoring infrastructure expanded with Rain Gauge Stations increased from 9 to 15
Four more Doppler Weather Radars to be commissioned in Doda, Kishtwar, Anantnag and Baramulla; Minister calls for greater public adherence to scientific weather warnings
Dr Jitendra Singh Calls for Greater Public Trust in Scientific Weather Warnings as Meteorological Infrastructure Expands Across Jammu and Kashmir
Posted On: 02 NOV 2026 4:23PM by PIB Delhi

Inaugurating the new Seismological Observatory in the high seismic zone of Kishtwar today through the Ministry of Earth Sciences, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology, Earth Sciences, Minister of State in the Prime Minister's Office, Department of Atomic Energy and Department of Space, Dr Jitendra Singh today highlighted the significant expansion of meteorological and weather monitoring infrastructure in Jammu & Kashmir after 2014, particularly in the erstwhile Doda district, with additional installations brought in after the Chasoti cloudburst tragedy last year.

Addressing the gathering, Dr Jitendra Singh said that the India Meteorology Department (IMD) had strengthened the weather monitoring network in the region from not a single Doppler Weather Radar in 2014 to 4 installed in last 12 years and 4 more being installed making it total 8; Automatic Weather Stations from 3 to 12 out of which 4 for Kishtwar and 2 each for Doda and Ramban.

Dr. Srinivasa Kumar Tummala, Secretary, Ministry of Earth Sciences, Govt of India, Senior Scientist Suresh and others came specially from Delhi for the event.

MLA Padder-Nagseni Constituency and Leader of Opposition, J&K Legislative Assembly, Sh. Sunil Sharma; MLA of the Kishtwar Assembly Constituency and Ms. Shagun Parihar also spoke on the occasion. Deputy Commissioner Kishtwar, Pankaj Sharma and SSP Kishtwar Sunny Gupta were also present among others.

The Minister said, the expansion of scientific and weather monitoring infrastructure has also strengthened the region's disaster preparedness in an area that is vulnerable to earthquakes, landslides and other weather-related challenges.

The new observatory at Kishtwar is equipped with state-of-the-art digital seismic equipment and will transmit data in real time to the 24x7 Earthquake Monitoring Centre of the National Centre for Seismology in New Delhi. With the establishment of the new facility, Jammu and Kashmir now has four Seismological Observatories, including those at Jammu, Srinagar, Udhampur and Kishtwar.

Dr Jitendra Singh said the observatory would continuously monitor earthquake activity in the region and contribute to a better understanding of its seismic hazards. The information generated would also support the district administration and rescue teams in responding more effectively, besides helping in planning safer infrastructure.

Highlighting the transformation in meteorological infrastructure since 2014, Dr Jitendra Singh said that there was no Doppler Weather Radar coverage in the region earlier. After 2014, four Doppler Weather Radars have been installed at Banihal, Jot, Jammu and Srinagar, significantly expanding weather monitoring capabilities.

He further informed that four more Doppler Weather Radars are set to be commissioned in 2027 at Doda, Kishtwar, Anantnag and Baramulla, further strengthening weather surveillance and extending coverage across the region.

The Minister also highlighted the significant expansion of the Automatic Weather Station network. From three Automatic Weather Stations earlier at Udhampur, Kathua and Ramban, nine additional stations have been added, taking the total number to 12. These include four stations in Kishtwar, two each in Doda and Ramban, and one in Kathua.

Dr Jitendra Singh said that the expansion of scientific infrastructure has been guided by the needs and geographical vulnerabilities of the region. He noted that administrative boundaries may change, but geographical challenges remain, making it essential to strengthen weather monitoring and early warning systems across vulnerable areas.

The rainfall monitoring network has also been expanded, with the number of Rain Gauge Stations increasing from nine to 15 across the five districts of the parliamentary constituency. These stations provide regular rainfall information and strengthen local-level weather monitoring.

Highlighting the reach of weather and agromet services, the Minister said that weather forecasts are now disseminated at the Panchayat level across all Panchayats in the five districts. The weather forecast and agromet advisory services have reached 5,467 beneficiaries, enabling wider access to weather-related information.

He also referred to the strengthening of specialised meteorological facilities in the region, including the High-Altitude Cloud Physics Laboratory at Patnitop, Jammu and Kashmir. The meteorological infrastructure in Jammu has also been strengthened with the establishment of a Regional Meteorological Centre to provide weather and early warning services.

Dr Jitendra Singh said that access to timely weather information has made a tangible difference to local administration and disaster preparedness. Referring to recent experiences, he noted that advance weather information helped the district administration plan and manage activities with greater ease.

Emphasising the importance of public cooperation, the Minister said that scientific weather warnings can save lives only when they are taken seriously and acted upon. He recalled an instance when traffic restrictions were imposed following a weather alert and subsequent damage to the highway demonstrated the importance of adhering to timely warnings.

“Information is important, but following the information is equally important,” he emphasised, calling upon citizens to cooperate with the administration during weather alerts and advisories.

Dr Jitendra Singh also spoke about the need to counter unverified and alarmist information with scientific and evidence-based communication. He said that weather-related information and predictions should be understood on the basis of scientific assessment and credible sources.

Highlighting the positive potential of technology and social media, the Minister said that access to digital information and new platforms has created opportunities for young people, including those living in remote areas. He urged the youth to make constructive use of the opportunities and facilities now available to them.

Dr Jitendra Singh also reflected on the wider transformation of the region, referring to improved connectivity and the development of Kishtwar as a major power hub. He said the region's scientific and infrastructure capabilities were being strengthened alongside efforts to improve the safety and well-being of its people.

The event was attended by senior officials, public representatives and other dignitaries.

2331564.title: Under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Government is strengthening institutional framework for management of foreign nationals through expansion of Foreigners Regional Registration Offices (FRROs)
2331564.body_html:
Ministry of Home Affairs
Under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Government is strengthening institutional framework for management of foreign nationals through expansion of Foreigners Regional Registration Offices (FRROs)
Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah has directed to establish FRROs in all state capitals by 2027
Number of FRROs in the country now goes up to 20
Five New FRROs offices set up at Jaipur, Chandigarh, Guwahati, Aizawl, and Amravati; 3 new notified at Kohima, Agartala and Bhubaneswar
FRRO offices aim at boosting service accessibility for foreigners visiting for tourism, medical and education purposes 
35 online services through e-FRRO facilitate registration, visa extensions, conversion and other eligible immigration-related services
Posted On: 02 NOV 2026 4:17PM by PIB Delhi

Under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Government is strengthening institutional framework for management of foreign nationals through expansion of Foreigners Regional Registration Offices (FRROs).

There has been a substantial increase in the number of foreigners visiting India for tourism, medical and education purposes and there is a need to appoint FRROs in all states. This will ensure service accessibility, enhance regulatory compliance and promote India as an attractive destination. Identifying this need, Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation, Shri Amit Shah has directed to establish FRROs in all state capitals by 2027. 

Pursuant to the above directions of the Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah, five new FRROs have been set-up in the capitals of five states since 2025. Three FRRO offices at Jaipur, Chandigarh and Guwahati were established in the year 2025. Earlier, these were under the jurisdiction of the FRRO offices located at Delhi, Amritsar and Kolkata respectively.

This year two new FRRO offices have been established in the state capitals, namely, Aizawl (Mizoram), and Amravati (Andhra Pradesh). Earlier, Aizawl was under the jurisdiction of FRRO, Kolkata whereas Amravati was under the jurisdiction of FRRO, Hyderabad. Recently three new FRRO offices namely Kohima (Nagaland), Agartala (Tripura) and Bhubaneshwar (Odisha) are notified. Earlier, Kohima and Agartala were under the jurisdiction of FRRO, Kolkata whereas Bhubaneshwar was under the jurisdiction of FRRO, Hyderabad.

The total number of FRRO offices in the country has now gone up to twenty (20), located at Ahmedabad, Amravati, Amritsar, Aizawl, Agartala, Bengaluru, Bhubaneswar, Calicut, Chennai, Cochin, Chandigarh, Delhi, Guwahati, Hyderabad, Kolkata, Kohima, Kozhikode, Lucknow, Mumbai and Trivandrum.

The Government of India is pursuing the matter of establishing FRRO’s in remaining States namely Bihar, Goa, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Meghalaya. This will help foreigners visiting India in obtaining various consular services such as visa extension, conversion, immigration compliance and legal safety. The expansion will strengthen local-level institutional capacity, improve coordination with State authorities, facilitate legitimate foreign visitors and reinforce the effective implementation of immigration law and national security requirements.

The expansion of Foreigners Regional Registration Offices (FRROs) has a dual focus on facilitating foreigners’ legitimate travel and stay in India and ensuring effective implementation of immigration laws and security requirements. The Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025, which consolidated four earlier laws relating to immigration and foreigners, provides a unified statutory framework for regulating the entry, stay, movement and exit of foreign nationals. As per this act, the Bureau of Immigration, which mainly performs the immigration function, shall in discharge of its duties, be assisted, among others, by the Foreigners Regional Registration Officer (FRRO) as may be authorized by the Central Government of India.

The Foreigners Regional Registration Office regulates, tracks and facilitates the lawful stay of foreign nationals visiting or residing in India. It administers post-arrival registration for eligible category of foreigners and issues a Registration Certificate (RC)/Residential Permit on registration. It also records changes in a foreigner’s particulars, such as residential address, passport details or travel plans within the country, and grants permission to visit protected and restricted areas. Exit permits are issued to foreigners whose visas have expired, who have overstayed, or who require formal clearance before leaving India. Overall, the FRRO monitors compliance with Indian immigration laws, handles cases of overstay and visa violations, and coordinates legal action or penalties where necessary.

2331454.title: AIR FORCE SCHOOLS ADOPT CHILD DIGITAL SAFETY PROGRAMME
2331454.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
AIR FORCE SCHOOLS ADOPT CHILD DIGITAL SAFETY PROGRAMME
42 Air Force Schools on-boarded; Teachers Certified as Cyber Crime First Responders ScrollControl Project
Posted On: 02 NOV 2026 12:54PM by PIB Delhi

Spearheading the initiative to build cyber safety capability within the Air Force schools community, the Indian Air Force Educational & Cultural Society under the aegis of Air Headquarters on-boarded Air Force Schools across the country onto ScrollControl, a comprehensive Child Digital Safety Programme through Information Sharing and Analysis Center Foundation (ISAC). This initiative coincides with the observance of the National Cyber Security Awareness Month.

Two hundred and sixty-one teachers of forty two Air Force Schools have undergone certification course as Cyber Crime Intervention Officers, to protect children from online grooming and exploitation, misuse of artificial intelligence, gaming-related harms and financial frauds, also enabling them to preserve digital evidence and to act as first responders.

In the era of affordable high-speed internet, smart devices and access to social media, school-going children are extensively exposed to unregulated digital spaces which are primarily designed for adults. To ensure safety of school children in the cyber space, Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) has directed affiliated schools to incorporate cyber safety best practices through the monthly observance of Cyber Jagrookta Diwas. The present initiative enables Air Force Schools to align with this requirement with trained in-house capability.

Through ScrollControl, Air Force Schools will be able to form cyber clubs, certify students on cyber safety, conduct awareness sessions for parents and staff, access age-appropriate content rating platform for families, and be recognised as a Cyber Safe School.

The training and certification of teachers, their empanelment on the National Security Database, and 24x7 victim support through a multi-disciplinary ecosystem of cyber lawyers, cyber psychologists and forensic experts are being provided under this programme through ISAC Foundation

2331429.title: DPIIT Implements Special Campaign 6 to Institutionalise Swachhata and Minimise Pendency Across Offices
2331429.body_html:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
DPIIT Implements Special Campaign 6 to Institutionalise Swachhata and Minimise Pendency Across Offices
DPIIT Disposes of Over 99% of Public Grievances and Closes 83% of Identified E-Files Under Special Campaign 6
Posted On: 02 NOV 2026 12:17PM by PIB Delhi

The Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), along with its attached and subordinate offices, is implementing Special Campaign 6 under the guidance of the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG). The campaign aims to institutionalise Swachhata and minimise pendency in official work across all offices.

During the implementation phase, DPIIT has made significant progress across multiple parameters. All categories of pending references, including those received from the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), Cabinet, Members of Parliament, State Governments and Public Grievances (PG)/PG Appeals, have been identified and are being systematically addressed to ensure their timely and effective disposal.

As of 28 October 2026, DPIIT has successfully disposed of more than 50% of references received from the PMO, around 75% of references from the Cabinet/Inter-Ministerial Committee (IMC) and State Governments, over 99% of Public Grievances and more than 80% of Public Grievance Appeals. The Department has also closed around 83% of the identified e-files, reflecting its efforts towards efficient record management. These initiatives have contributed to improving workplace cleanliness and the overall working environment for officials and staff.

The implementation phase of Special Campaign 6, being conducted from 2 to 31 October 2026, was preceded by a preparatory phase from 15 to 30 September 2026. The campaign has helped raise awareness among government officials about the importance of cleanliness, efficient record management and the timely disposal of pending matters. DPIIT remains committed to institutionalising Swachhata and minimising pendency across its attached and subordinate offices, thereby fostering a cleaner, more efficient and responsive working environment.

2331418.title: Aatmanirbhar Bharat: MoD inks Rs 53,866.50 crore contracts with GRSE & GSL for 8 Next Generation Corvettes for Indian Navy
2331418.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
Aatmanirbhar Bharat: MoD inks Rs 53,866.50 crore contracts with GRSE & GSL for 8 Next Generation Corvettes for Indian Navy
Posted On: 02 NOV 2026 11:53AM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Defence has signed contracts worth Rs 53,866.50 crore with Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers Limited (GRSE) and Goa Shipyard Limited (GSL) for the acquisition of eight Next Generation Corvettes (NGCs) for the Indian Navy. The contracts were inked in the presence of Defence Secretary Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh at Kartavya Bhawan-2, New Delhi on November 02, 2026.

Under the contracts, GRSE will construct five corvettes, while GSL will construct the remaining three. The project marks a significant milestone in India's indigenous warship design and construction capabilities, as it is the first project in which the ships will be indigenously designed by the Indian Navy and constructed by Defence Public Sector Undertakings (DPSUs) selected through a competitive process.

The NGCs will be equipped with state-of-the-art capabilities, including advanced missiles, weapons and sensor suites, enabling them to undertake missions across the air, surface and sub-surface domains. The induction of these ships will significantly enhance the Indian Navy’s operational capabilities in safeguarding maritime trade routes, conducting anti-surface and anti-submarine warfare operations, strengthening coastal defence, undertaking littoral combat operations, and carrying out maritime presence and surveillance missions.

The NGC project will provide a significant impetus to India’s indigenous shipbuilding ecosystem by strengthening collaboration among DPSUs, private shipyards and Indian industrial partners, including MSMEs. The construction of these ships is expected to generate approximately 72 lakh person-days of employment in the shipyards and 460 lakh person-days in ancillary industries and MSMEs over the next ten years.

By promoting the use of Made-in-India materials and equipment, indigenous technologies, and Indian skills and expertise, the project represents a major step towards achieving Aatmanirbharta in defence manufacturing and reinforces Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi-led Government’s commitment to Make-in-India.

2331406.title: Monthly Production and Dispatch from Captive and Commercial Mines in October 2026
2331406.body_html:
Ministry of Coal
Monthly Production and Dispatch from Captive and Commercial Mines in October 2026
Posted On: 02 NOV 2026 11:37AM by PIB Delhi

Coal production from Captive and Commercial mines during October 2026 of FY 2026–27 stood at 22.03 million tonnes (MT) increasing from 15.49 MT in October 2025 (~42 % YoY growth), while coal dispatches reached 21.11 MT increasing from 15.48 MT in October 2025 (~36 % YoY growth). The sector registered robust year-on-year growth, with coal production increasing from 105.33 MT to 117.23 MT at 11.30% and dispatch increasing from 111.95 MT to 124.86 MT at 11.53% compared to the period April to October of the previous year, reflecting sustained momentum in mining operations.

These encouraging results underscore improved operational efficiency, enhanced mining productivity, and more effective utilization of mining capacities across the captive and commercial coal mining sector.

The accompanying graph illustrates the data on production and dispatch in (Million tonnes).

In a further boost to the sector, the Lohari coal mine in Jharkhand, obtained Mine Opening Permission in October 2026. The mine had been awaiting operationalisation for several years, and its approval reflects the impact of Ministry's Ease of Doing Business reforms. With this, the number of operational captive and commercial coal mines has risen to 87.

The rising production from these mines is expected to reduce dependence on imported coal, strengthen supply-chain resilience, conserve valuable foreign exchange, and advance the Government’s vision of Atmanirbhar Bharat by enhancing self-sufficiency in a critical raw material for industrial development.

Reaffirming its commitment to fully realise the potential of captive and commercial coal mining, the Ministry will continue to focus on sustaining production growth, addressing supply constraints, improving coal availability through a combination of progressive policy interventions, robust regulatory oversight, and continued stakeholder support and ensuring a reliable contribution towards meeting the nation’s growing energy and industrial requirements.

2331397.title: National Orientation Programme for Tribal Healers on Public Health, Kanha Shanti Vanam, Hyderabad
2331397.body_html:
Ministry of Tribal Affairs
National Orientation Programme for Tribal Healers on Public Health, Kanha Shanti Vanam, Hyderabad
Posted On: 02 NOV 2026 11:28AM by PIB Delhi

Ministry of Tribal Affairs in collaboration with the ICMR–National Institute of Health Research (ICMR-NIHR), Bhubaneswar under the Janjatiya Health Institutional Transformation (JanHIT) initiative, has organised the 1st of its kind National Orientation Programme for Tribal Healers on Public Health on 1–2nd November 2026 at Kanha Shanti Vanam, Hyderabad. The programme was inaugurated at the auditorium of Kanha Shanti Vanam, Hyderabad by Shri. Manish Thakur, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Tribal Affairs and Dr. Sanghamitra Pati, Director, ICMR-NIHR, Bhubaneswar in presence of Shri B. M. Santosh, IAS, Special Secretary and Director, Tribal Welfare, Telangana, Dr. V. Samujwala, Director, Tribal Cultural Research & Training Institute (TCR&TI), Telangana, and other senior officials from Ministry of Tribal Affairs and ICMR-NIHR, Bhubaneswar. The launch of this landmark initiative on the first day of the Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas Pakhwada underscores the shared commitment to honouring and empowering India's tribal communities through inclusive health and capacity-building interventions.

The 1st phase of the orientation programme is being attended by around 550 tribal healers nominated by the State Tribal Welfare departments from nine states and UTs of India (Andhra Pradesh, Goa, Karnataka, Keralam, Maharashtra, Odisha, Tamil Nadu, Telangana, and Dadra and Nagar Haveli). The orientation programme aims to orient tribal healers on key public health issues and strengthen their understanding of common diseases, early identification of danger signs, and appropriate referral for timely medical care. Recognising the important role of healers in tribal communities, the initiative seeks to enhance their awareness of essential health practices and encourage linkages with the formal healthcare system.

The two-day orientation programme will cover three training modules addressing a wide range of public health concerns. These include communicable and vector-borne diseases, skin diseases, non-communicable diseases, metabolic and blood disorders, liver diseases, and mental health conditions. The sessions will also focus on appropriate referral for snakebites, scorpion & other stings, animal bites, injuries, eye and ear disorders; oral health; and newborn and infant care. The training will also include integrated practice, review sessions, a post-training assessment, and participant feedback to reinforce learning and assess the orientation's effectiveness.

Participants from different states will attend the 2 day programme, with state-wise arrangements for training sessions in regional languages to facilitate effective communication and learning. Experts from AIIMS, ICMR, Quality Control of India, MS Swaminathan Foundation, Amrita Institute, Kochi, IIHMR, Bengaluru and Piramal Swasthya, Maharashtra will be delivering sessions in respective languages for the healers. 

By orienting tribal healers on essential health concerns and appropriate referral practices, the programme seeks to promote informed community-level health support and strengthen collaboration between tribal community practices and the formal healthcare system. This structured capacity-building module developed by ICMR-NIHR, Bhubaneswar, with support from MoTA represents a milestone effort to integrate tribal healthcare practices with formal medical systems, particularly as we commemorate Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas.

The programme will conclude on 2nd November 2026 with a closing ceremony and distribution of certificates to participants.

2331390.title: Ministry of Rural Development Notifies Grievance Redressal Rules, 2026 under VB–G RAM G Act
2331390.body_html:
Ministry of Rural Development
Ministry of Rural Development Notifies Grievance Redressal Rules, 2026 under VB–G RAM G Act
Multi-tier mechanism and digital platform for prompt, transparent, and time-bound grievance redressal
Multiple channels for grievance submission, mandatory registration, digital tracking and escalation of unresolved grievances
Enquiry to be completed within 7 working days and grievances to be resolved within 15 days
Posted On: 02 NOV 2026 11:16AM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India, has notified the Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin): VB–G RAM G – Grievance Redressal Rules, 2026, establishing a structured, multi-tier and time-bound mechanism for addressing grievances relating to the implementation of the Scheme. The Rules aim to make grievance redressal more accessible, transparent and accountable, while ensuring that citizens' concerns receive timely attention and appropriate action.

Multi-tier grievance redressal mechanism

The Rules provide for the establishment of a time-bound, multi-tier grievance redressal mechanism by State Governments at the Gram Panchayat, Block and District levels. Designated Grievance Redressal Officers at the appropriate levels will be responsible for receiving, registering, enquiring into and disposing of grievances.

The District Programme Coordinator will oversee grievance redressal at the district level and ensure that grievances are addressed through the designated mechanism and the Digital Public Infrastructure for grievance redressal.

Multiple channels for submission of grievances

To facilitate easy access, any person may submit a grievance relating to any matter arising out of or connected with the implementation of the Scheme. The Rules provide for submission of grievances through multiple channels:

  • In person before the designated Grievance Redressal Officer;
  • Through speed post, with proof of delivery;
  • Through the Digital Public Infrastructure for Redressal of Grievances designated by the Central Government; and
  • Through telephone, designated helplines or any other mode decided by the State Government.

Grievances received in physical form at the Gram Panchayat, Block or District level must be entered and registered on the designated Digital Public Infrastructure on the day of receipt or, where this is not feasible, by the next working day.

Upon registration, the complainant will receive an acknowledgement containing the registration number, date of receipt and designation of the receiving authority. The acknowledgement will be provided electronically in cases of digital submission and in physical form where the grievance is received physically.

Importantly, no grievance can be refused registration on the grounds of its format, language, manner of submission or any procedural deficiency. This provision ensures that citizens can access the grievance redressal mechanism without being hindered by procedural requirements.

Defined timelines for enquiry and resolution

The Rules prescribe clear timelines to ensure prompt examination and resolution of grievances. The designated Grievance Redressal Officer is required to examine every registered grievance and undertake the necessary enquiry. For this purpose, the officer may call for relevant records, registers, documents, reports, electronic data or other information from the concerned authorities or functionaries.

Where necessary, the complainant will be provided a reasonable opportunity to be heard, either in person or through electronic means, before the grievance is disposed of.

The enquiry into a grievance is required to be completed within seven working days from the date of its receipt. Upon completion of the enquiry, the Grievance Redressal Officer will record the findings and take, or cause to be taken, appropriate corrective or remedial action in accordance with the Act and the Rules. The grievance is required to be resolved within 15 days from the date of its receipt.

The findings and action taken will be recorded on the designated Digital Public Infrastructure and communicated to the complainant. Where a grievance has been received in physical form, its outcome and the action taken will also be communicated to the complainant in physical form.

Digital tracking and escalation of unresolved grievances

The designated Digital Public Infrastructure will facilitate end-to-end tracking of grievances, from registration to final disposal. It will also enable electronic recording of the enquiry, findings and action taken, thereby strengthening transparency and accountability in the grievance redressal process.

Any grievance that remains unresolved within the prescribed period of 15 days will be escalated to the next higher level through the grievance redressal mechanism established by the State Government. The authority receiving the escalated grievance will examine the matter and take appropriate action for its disposal. Such grievances will continue to be monitored electronically until their resolution.

Provision for appeals

The Rules also provide for appeals against orders passed under the grievance redressal mechanism. Such appeals will be filed and disposed of in accordance with Schedule I to the VB–G RAM G Act, 2025.

Through these Rules, the Government seeks to institutionalise a citizen-centric, accessible and time-bound grievance redressal framework under VB–G RAM G. The multi-tier institutional mechanism, multiple channels for grievance submission, mandatory registration, defined timelines, digital tracking and escalation of unresolved grievances are expected to strengthen administrative accountability and improve the responsiveness of the Scheme's implementation.

The notification marks an important step towards ensuring that grievances relating to the implementation of VB–G RAM G are addressed systematically, transparently and within prescribed timelines, thereby reinforcing the rights and entitlements of rural households under the Scheme.
